## `vti-specs-core`

## [0.5.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-core-v0.5.0...vti-specs-core-v0.5.1) — 2026-11-14 ### Build & CI - **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708)) * build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph] comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11. ring leaves the VTA and VTC graphs; it stays only under attest-verify. removed from 19 crates; deliberate ones are listed under [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job runs cargo-machete and the lint check. once in [workspace.dependencies]; vta-tee inherits aws-lc-rs. The five crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by check-workspace-version-reqs.py. (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added.

## [0.89.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.88.1...vta-sdk-v0.89.0) — 2026-11-14 ### Added - **rooms**: Load older by version (records/list 0.8, keys/browse 0.6) and host limits in rooms/info 0.5 ([#2727](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2727)) * build(vti-specs-rooms): pin rooms/records/list 0.8, rooms/keys/browse 0.6, rooms/info 0.5 trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1289, for #2294 points 3 and 4. Older versions stay pinned beside them while they are still served or sent. The registry's in-place refresh of rooms/records/put 0.1-0.5 and rooms/keys/list 0.2 (marking them superseded) is left out: adopting put/0.6 is separate work. ### Build & CI - **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708)) * build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by cause. The five crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by check-workspace-version-reqs.py. (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added. ### Changed - **vtc**: One typed routing table for every Trust Task family; routes/ is the HTTP surface only ([#2732](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2732)) * refactor(vtc): route every Trust Task family through one typed AsyncDispatcher #2728 split trust_tasks/mod.rs into handler files but left three routing styles: about sixty direct arms in `dispatch_typed`, thirty-three family modules each keeping a `URIS` list beside a `match` that re-matched it (one `FAMILIES` table arm), and typed `AsyncDispatcher` registration for rooms and git-ns. A hand-kept `DISPATCHED_URIS` (540 lines) had to agree with all of it, and already did not: `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1` was routed but not listed, so discovery never advertised it. - `trust_tasks::routing`: one `AsyncDispatcher` every family registers on, keyed on the generated payload type (`on!(routes, P => handler)`). The URI a handler answers is `P::TYPE_URI`; the served set is the table itself (`routing::served_uris`), and `dispatched_uris()` (that plus discovery) replaces `DISPATCHED_URIS` for the unsupported-version hint, discovery, the size gate and the censuses. - Each family exposes `register(Routes) -> Routes`; every `URIS` constant, every family `dispatch` and the `FAMILIES` table are gone, and the direct arms moved into their handler files' `register`. Families whose verbs share an authority check before the payload is read (backup, website, the administrator's passkeys) route through a small `Op` enum, not a URI match. - Handlers are registered on `Received

`: routed and policed as `P`, but handed the JSON as received, so every handler still reads it against the schema before parsing it and still resolves the signer's authority before reading the payload (a typed downcast in the router would reverse that order and change which refusal a stranger gets). - Censuses: no URI is registered twice (the dispatcher would silently keep the later one), and none is also a rooms or git-ns task. - The URI constants nothing but the removed lists named are deleted; the ones only tests name stay behind `#[cfg(test)]`. Behaviour is unchanged except that discovery and the version hint now list `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`, which was always served. - **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730)) * refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566)) Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them, and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to ~935 unique lines. The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so, and why it costs nothing new. - **vtc**: Vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor ([#2728](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2728)) * refactor(vti-common)!: move the VTC's audit-event vocabulary to a new vtc-audit leaf crate ### Documentation - Operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI ([#2706](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2706)) * fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts ([#2631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2631)): the retired `pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` surface becomes `did-mgmt servers|dids …`, `pnm auth login` (pnm has none) becomes `pnm setup`, `pnm acl delete` takes the DID positionally, `list-domains` sits under `dids`, the backup descriptor hints no longer name `pnm backup save|restore`, and stale doc comments (`pnm passkey-enroll-token`, `vta export-mnemonic`, `cnm community info`) are corrected. A pnm and a vta test parse each remediation command through Cli::try_parse_from. The --template help is derived from vta_sdk::did_templates::BUILTIN_NAMES and no longer lists the retired did-hosting-* template names ([#2635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2635)). The `rooms keys key-package` help gives the 14-day KeyPackage lifetime the code holds ([#2632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2632)), and `rooms prune` no longer says a prune reaches the host only: members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the epoch floor ([#2633](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2633)). ### Fixed - **cli**: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors) ([#2726](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2726)) * fix(cli): a corrupt profile is fatal, saves are atomic, one start-up for pnm and cnm, --version and completions ### Performance - **vta**: Cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages ([#2713](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2713)) * perf(vta-sdk,vta-service): compile each Trust Task payload schema once ([#2622](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2622)) trust-tasks-rs 0.37's against_schema / validate_value parse and compile the schema on every call. vta_sdk::schema_cache keeps the compiled validator by the &'static schema text's address (the same technique as trust-tasks-rs 0.38's SchemaValidator), with the jsonschema release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses so the check and its error text are unchanged. The dispatch spine, the SDK's send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it. trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps SchemaValidator. ### Security - Invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types ([#2710](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2710)) * security(vtc): a wallet admin invitation's entry expires with it until claimed, and goes with a revoke ([#2660](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2660)) vtc/admin/invites/create/0.2 item 3 writes a wallet invitation's administrator entry when the invitation is issued, and the code wrote it permanent: revoking the invitation (which create 0.2 says withdraws the authority it confers) or letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed. The entry is now written to expire with the invitation and recorded beside it (install::InviteGrant, keyed by jti). vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 makes it permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code; vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes, remove it (with its sessions and delegations) if it is still exactly what the invitation wrote. A lapsed or still-provisional entry no longer blocks a new invitation for the same DID. The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the same provisional entry. Deferring the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written at mint.

title: chore(vtc-admin-ui): move lucide-react and lucide-static to 1.70.0 together
body:
Supersedes #2734 (lucide-static 0.469.0 → 1.70.0) and #2736 (lucide-react 0.469.0 → 1.70.0), which each failed alone.

## Why the two must move together

The badge picture builder (`admin-ui/src/components/badge-icons.ts`) joins lucide-react's `icons` to lucide-static's `tags.json` by name, so search can find an icon by what it means ("insect" finds the bug). That only works if both packages come from the same release: 0.469.0 has 1,544 icons and 1.70.0 has 2,029, so bumping either one alone fails `BadgeBuilder.test.tsx` ("expected 1544 to be 2029").

## What changed

- **`chore(vtc-admin-ui)`**: `lucide-react` and `lucide-static` both go to **1.70.0** and are pinned exactly. `lucide-react` used to be `^0.469.0`, and a caret let it move ahead of its tag file on any `npm install`. With 1.70.0, the 2,029 icons and 2,029 tag entries name the same icons, with nothing missing on either side. The builder test now compares the two catalogues' key sets rather than only their sizes. `docs/03-vtc/badges.md` now says "about 2,000" icons instead of 1,500, and the comment in `badge-icons.ts` gives the coupling rule.
- **`ci(dependabot)`**: adds a `lucide` group (`lucide-*`) to the `/vtc-service/admin-ui` npm entry, listed before `minor-and-patch`. lucide bumps of every kind, majors included, now arrive as one PR.

## lucide 1.x and stored badges

lucide 1.0 removed the brand icons and renamed some others. `tsc -b` shows the console imports none of the removed ones. **Stored badges are not affected:** nothing persists an icon name. The builder draws the chosen icon onto a canvas and uploads only the resulting PNG through `vtc/badges/images/upload`, where the community re-encodes it (VTI-BDG-050). Badges hold an image digest, and no lucide name appears in any record, wire type or Rust code. A renamed or removed icon only changes what can be chosen next. No alias map is needed.

## Checks run

- admin-ui (after `npm ci`): `npm run lint` (`wire:check` + typecheck), `npx vitest run` (131 files, 1614 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3754 passed, 1 skipped

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.13.1`) | `0.13.0` → `0.13.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(release): read the newest tag without head, which SIGPIPEs git under pipefail
body:
The `Release PR` job has failed intermittently with exit code 141 since #1312. The error trap from #1313 named the line on the next failure:

```
exit 141 from: tag=$(git tag -l "${TAG_PREFIX}*" --sort=-version:refname | head -1)
exit 141 from: ./scripts/release-bump-ts.sh "$pkg"
```

`head -1` exits after one line. If `git tag` is still writing at that moment, it is killed by SIGPIPE, and under `set -o pipefail` the substitution, and the script, fail. Whether git finishes its writes first is a race, which is why the job failed on some pushes and passed on others, and why it never reproduced locally.

Every `| head -1` in the release scripts (`release-pr.sh` and the three `release-bump-*.sh`) and in `check-go-api-compat.sh` is now `| sed -n 1p`. `sed` prints the first line and keeps reading to the end, so the writer never sees a closed pipe. The output is identical. This is the same fix as #1239 (`changed-paths`) and #610 (`git log | grep -q`).

`npm run test:release-scripts` (33) passes. Running `release-bump-ts.sh @openvtc/trust-tasks` and `release-bump-go.sh trust-tasks-go/specs` against current tags gives the expected notices.

Release notes

Sourced from serde-saphyr's releases.

2.1.1 Optimization and maintenance release

Fixed

  • Fixed 2.1.0 regression empty documents producing errors (#265). Empty document is a valid YAML document. Fix of this regression is the reason of making this release so early.

Performance improvements

  • Significantly reduced allocations when deserializing (#262), thanks @​mat-gas

2.1.0 Minor feature extension, maintenance and performance release

Added

  • Added opt-in Options::reject_tagged_field_names to catch misplaced tags on struct field names, with Error::TaggedStructFieldName diagnostics. Struct field names can only be strings; !!str is still accepted. As other tags can only be ignored, tag on a structure field name is almost for sure placed wrongly. This setting will be default in next major release.
  • Added Options::leading_zero_numbers_as_strings and Options::underscored_numbers_as_strings to preserve numeric spellings such as 0755 and 1_000 as strings in untyped values, including untagged enums and flattened fields (#225). Both default to false; direct typed parsing, explicit numeric tags, and mapping-key comparison keep their existing behavior.
  • Added Error::render_to to append diagnostics to any std::fmt::Write using RenderOptions, without collecting the complete output in an intermediate string (#221).
  • Added DuplicateKeyPolicy::PassThrough to delegate repeated explicit mapping entries to Serde visitors, matching serde_yaml's handling for structs, standard maps, and custom multimap visitors (#226). The default remains Error; merge expansion retains its precedence rules. See the README migration note for the scope of this option.

Deprecated

  • Deprecated SerializerOptions::empty_as_braces. Setting it to false emits YAML null for empty block collections without tags or anchors. These values do not round-trip into collection types. title: feat(go-specs): release the generated specification packages as their own module
body:
Step 3 of #1112. Go core **v0.13.0** is on proxy.golang.org, and it is the first core without `specs/`. So `trust-tasks-go/specs` can require it and build. This PR wires that module's release. Import paths do not change. Anyone who imports a prebuilt package adds the module next to the core with `go get github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs`.

## What changes

- **`trust-tasks-go/specs/go.mod`** requires core `v0.13.0`, and the TODO is gone. `go mod tidy` created `go.sum`, which lists only the core. There is no `replace`. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass in the module (1577 packages), on stable and on go1.22.12.
- **Release wiring.** It matches how #886 wired `capabilityclient`, and `npm run check-release-lists` agrees:
  - `specs/version.go`: `package specs`, next to the generated `extends.go`, with `const Version = "0.1.0"`. This is the seeded initial version, and `CHANGELOG.md` is an empty preamble, as `capabilityclient` and `proof` had.
  - A `verify-go`/`publish-go` matrix leg in `publish.yml` with tag prefix `trust-tasks-go/specs/v`.
  - A `GO_MODULES` entry in `release-pr.sh`.
  - A `release-bump-go.sh` arm. It watches `trust-tasks-go/specs`, `specs/` and `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs`, with scopes `go-specs` and `go-bindings`. `go-specs` is added to commit-lint's `!` scope list.
  - The core's watch still excludes `trust-tasks-go/specs`. It still watches `specs/` and the generator, because they write `trusttasks/extends_index.go`. So a spec change can release both modules.
- **`go.yml`** has a new `specs` job. It runs build, vet, gofmt and `test -race` on 1.22 and stable, and exits early through changed-paths like the other nested modules. `specs` comes off `NOT_BUILT_YET`, and that map is now empty.
- **Smoke test.** It moved from `smoke/testdata/smoke/` to `specs/smoke/smoke_test.go` and is now an ordinary test in the module. It runs against the published core it requires, which is what an importer gets. The core's `smoke/smoke_test.go` driver stays. It now copies the test from `specs/smoke` and still runs it against the checkout's runtime, so the core's `go test ./...` keeps driving generated code through unreleased runtime changes.
- **`build-go-bindings`.** `OUT_DIR_SOURCE_FILES` now also keeps `version.go`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `smoke/`. The generator refuses to write a package onto any of them. `npm run regen` leaves no drift.
- **Other:** Dependabot now watches `/trust-tasks-go/specs`. The docs are updated:
  - `trust-tasks-go/README.md`: the warning is replaced with `go get` instructions, and the nested-module table row now says the module is released.
  - `docs/packages/go.md`: the interim section is replaced.
  - `RELEASING.md`: the module's row and the watch paragraph are updated.
  - The website's Go library summary is updated.

  `docs/runtime-parity.md` does not mention the module.

The `specs` module has no API-compatibility job, just as the other nested modules have none. Changes to its generated packages are already gated by `published schemas change only additively`.

## What happens at merge

No Release PR is needed first. The initial version is seeded in `version.go`, and `publish-go` seeds the first tag itself (RELEASING.md, "The Go module seeds itself").

1. `verify-go` (leg `trust-tasks-go/specs`) sees that `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.0` does not exist. It runs `go build/vet/test ./...` in the module against the published core v0.13.0.
2. `publish-go` pushes the tag **`trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.0`** and warms proxy.golang.org. **This tag is permanent and cannot be retracted.**
3. `release-pr` runs after `publish-go`. For `trust-tasks-go/specs` it finds `v0.1.0` at HEAD and has nothing to release. The other legs (core `v0.13.0`, proof, didcomm, capabilityclient) are already tagged, so they skip.
4. This PR changes `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs` and `trust-tasks-go/smoke/`, which are in the core's watch. So the next Release PR also proposes a **patch** for the core (`v0.13.1`). The title has no `!`.

## Checks run locally

- In `trust-tasks-go`: `gofmt -l .` reports nothing, and `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass. The smoke driver runs; it does not skip.
- In `trust-tasks-go/specs`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass on stable, and build, vet and test pass on go1.22.12.
- `npm run regen` leaves no drift.
- These all pass: `npm run check`, `npm run check-release-lists`, `npm run test:release-scripts`, `node --test scripts/test-checks/release-lists.test.mjs scripts/test-checks/go-bindings-names.test.mjs`, and `actionlint`.
- `scripts/release-bump-go.sh trust-tasks-go/specs` parses the new arm. It stops with the expected "No trust-tasks-go/specs/v* tag exists" error, because `publish-go` writes that tag.

Closes #1112.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: ci(release): name the failing command when a release script exits
body:
Since #1312, the `Release PR` job in `publish.yml` has failed with `Process completed with exit code 141` (SIGPIPE) on every push to main, so no Release PR has been opened. The log ends right after `release-plz update`, with nothing to show which command failed. Running `release-pr.sh prepare` on a fresh clone of the same commit succeeds locally (macOS), so the failure only happens on the Linux runner.

`release-pr.sh` and the three `release-bump-*.sh` scripts now run under `set -E` with an `ERR` trap. When a step fails, the trap prints `::error file=…,line=…::exit N from: <command>`. That points at the failing line here, and it is cheap to keep for the next time a release step fails. Nothing else changes: the trap fires only where `set -e` would already exit.

`npm run test:release-scripts` (33) and `npm run check` pass. The fix for the SIGPIPE itself follows once this names the command.

title: refactor(go-tsp,go-didcomm,go-capabilityclient): share the core's ConsumeReceived and NewURNUUID
body:
The follow-up #1110 planned, now that Go core v0.12.0 (with #1305) is on proxy.golang.org.

## What changes

- **`trust-tasks-go/tsp` and `trust-tasks-go/didcomm`**: `Consume` is now `trusttasks.ConsumeReceived` run with the consumer's configuration (proof, payload and replay policies, `Extends`, `MyVID` = `Transport.Local`, `Now`, `NewID`). Each module's own copy of the inbound body is gone: the raw view, `routingView`, the case-fold refusal, the forward read, `documentWith` and the `asReceived` proof wrapper. The core verifies the proof over `Received` by itself, so the wrapper had nothing left to do.
- **DIDComm's binding §3.1 thread cross-check** is now a `ReceiveOptions.BindingCheck` (`threadCheck`). It runs at the same point as before: after the body parses, before the case-fold check. The refusal messages are unchanged.
- **`NewURNUUID`**: `tsp`, `didcomm` and `capabilityclient` mint ids with `trusttasks.NewURNUUID`, and their private generators are deleted. The exported `tsp.NewURNUUID` and `didcomm.NewMessageID` stay as one-line forwarders, so **no public API changes** and there is no `!`.
- `tsp/memberfold.go` is deleted. `didcomm/memberfold.go` stays, because `checkJOSEStructure` uses it on the JWE envelope and protected header, a layer the core never sees. Its comment now says so.
- `tsp`, `didcomm`, `capabilityclient`, `proof` and `examples/getting-started-go` require core **v0.12.0** (`go get … && go mod tidy`). `consumer-app-go` did not change after tidy.
- Docs: `docs/packages/go.md` and `docs/runtime-parity.md`.

## Behaviour

All existing tests pass unchanged in every touched module, including the size-bound, received-digest, extends-routing and malformed-body tests. No test pinned any of the details below, which were unified with the core and not preserved:

- When the forward read fails, the refusal message is now the core's `MalformedDocumentWireMessage` ("body is not a well-formed Trust Task document") instead of the binding's "envelope body is not a Trust Task document". It is still malformedRequest.
- A DIDComm body that does not parse as a document is now answered **addressed from the routing members that did parse**, as TSP already did. DIDComm used to answer from an empty document. This is one of the drifts #1110 set out to remove.
- If the handler's response cannot be marshalled, `Consume` now returns an error. Before, it returned a nil reply silently.
- `Consume` with a hand-built `Unpacked` whose `Transport.Peer` is empty now returns `trusttasks.ErrNoAuthenticatedSender`. `UnpackTrustTask` always sets `Peer`, so `Receive` is unaffected.

## Checks

`gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass in `tsp`, `didcomm`, `capabilityclient` and `proof`. Both examples pass `go vet` and `go test`. `npm run check-release-lists` and `npm run check-doc-facts` pass.

Merging this releases patches of `trust-tasks-go/proof`, `/didcomm` and `/capabilityclient`. `tsp` is not released yet.

Closes #1110.

title: feat(go)!: move the generated specification packages into their own module
body:
Step 2 of #1112. Go core v0.12.0, which contains #1307, is now on proxy.golang.org. Since #1307 the runtime no longer imports `specs/`.

## What changes

- **`trust-tasks-go/specs/go.mod`** makes the prebuilt packages a separate module, `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs`. Import paths do not change. The core module now holds only `trusttasks`, `cmd/trust-tasks-gen` and `smoke`, so its next release ships without the ~34 MB tree. `go list ./...` in `trust-tasks-go` lists those three packages and nothing else.
- **Breaking for the core** (`feat(go)!`): every `specs/...` package leaves the core module, and `go API compatibility` will report them as removed packages. Anyone importing a prebuilt package must stay on core v0.12.x until the `specs` module is published (step 3). A package that `cmd/trust-tasks-gen` generated needs only the core.
- **`scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs`**: `clean()` now keeps `specs/go.mod` and `go.sum` and wipes everything else. `npm run regen` leaves no drift.
- **Smoke test**: the core's `./smoke` can no longer import generated packages, because they are in another module. The test moved to `smoke/testdata/smoke/smoke_test.go` unchanged except for a header note. The new `smoke/smoke_test.go` copies the three packages it imports into a throwaway copy of the `specs` module, writes a `go.mod` that `replace`s the core with the checkout (as `cmd/trust-tasks-gen`'s `TestGeneratedPackagesCompile` and the examples already do), and runs `go test ./smoke` there. So the core's `go test ./...` still drives real generated code through the real pipeline, under the import paths a consumer uses. It skips when `specs/` is not beside the core, as in a module-cache copy. I chose this over moving the smoke test into the `specs` module because that module has no CI until step 3, and the smoke test would go unrun in the meantime. Step 3 can move it.
- **`cmd/trust-tasks-gen`** never imported `specs/`. The equivalence test reads `../../specs/**/payload.go` from disk, so it is unaffected.
- **Examples**: `consumer-app-go` and `getting-started-go` use consumer-side generation and import no prebuilt package. Both pass `go vet` and `go run`.
- **Release lists**:
  - `:(exclude)$PKG_DIR/specs` is added to the core watch in `release-bump-go.sh` and in `check-go-api-compat.sh`.
  - `:(exclude)trust-tasks-go/specs` is added to the changed-paths lists of the four nested-module jobs in `go.yml`.
  - `scripts/check-release-lists.mjs` gets a `NOT_BUILT_YET` map. `specs` is listed there with its reason, so the "every nested module has a go.yml job" rule skips it and prints a note. The check fails if a listed module disappears or becomes released while still on the list.
  - The core keeps watching the repository's `specs/`, because the generator writes the core's `trusttasks/extends_index.go` from it.
- **Docs**: `trust-tasks-go/README.md` warns importers of prebuilt packages and adds `specs/` to the nested-module table. `docs/packages/go.md` gets a new section with the interim state and the step-3 checklist. `RELEASING.md` gets a "Not released yet" row and the watch note.

## Known breakage until step 3

`specs/go.mod` requires core **v0.12.0**, with a `TODO(#1112 step 3)`. That core still contains `specs/`, so inside the `specs` module every package is found in two modules and the go command refuses it as an **ambiguous import**. `go mod tidy` there fails the same way, so the module has no `go.sum`. This is expected. The module is unreleased, CI does not build it, and the core module builds and tests without it. No version would work today: the only core that fixes this is the one this PR's release produces.

## Step 3, after the first core without `specs/` (the release of this PR) is on proxy.golang.org

1. Point `specs/go.mod` at that core, run `go mod tidy`, and remove the TODO.
2. Remove `specs` from `NOT_BUILT_YET` and add a `go.yml` job that builds, vets, gofmts and tests `trust-tasks-go/specs` on the 1.22 floor and stable.
3. Wire the release:
   - `specs/version.go` (`const Version`)
   - a `GO_MODULES` entry in `release-pr.sh`
   - a `release-bump-go.sh` arm watching `specs/`, `trust-tasks-go/specs` and `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs`
   - a `publish-go` matrix leg with tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/vX.Y.Z`
   - the `RELEASING.md` row
4. Optionally move the smoke test into the `specs` module and drop the driver.
5. Update the docs, then release it. Importers of prebuilt packages then `go get …/trust-tasks-go/specs`.

## Checks

- `gofmt -l .` reports nothing.
- `go list ./...` shows no `specs/` package in the core.
- `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass in `trust-tasks-go`, and so does `go test ./...` under go1.22.12.
- Both examples pass `go vet` and `go run .`.
- `npm run regen` leaves no drift.
- These pass: `npm run check` (which includes `check-release-lists` and `check-doc-facts`), `node --test scripts/test-checks/release-lists.test.mjs scripts/test-checks/go-bindings-names.test.mjs`, and `npm run test:release-scripts`.

title: chore: release 3 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof` | npm | `0.2.2` → `0.2.3` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp` | npm | `0.1.5` → `0.1.6` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client` | npm | `0.2.1` → `0.2.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: ci: group only minor and patch dependency updates, and hold back the codegen migrations
body:
The first weekly Dependabot PRs from #1182 (#1184 npm, #1185 pub, #1186 cargo) all failed. Each group had one or two updates that break something, and they made the whole group fail. This PR changes `.github/dependabot.yml` so that grouped minor and patch updates normally pass, and so that anything needing a deliberate change arrives on its own or not at all.

## What broke, by update

I read the failing job logs and then reproduced each cause locally on the PR heads, holding back the update I suspected and rerunning the check.

| PR | Update | Kind | Failing checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1186 | `schemars` 0.8 → 1.2 (+ `typify` 0.6 → 0.8, which requires it) | major, API break | build, codegen drift, consumer generation, gen-ts equivalence, gen ≡ build-go-bindings, rs API compatibility, cargo test (cli), example application. Each fails at `cannot find type RootSchema in schemars::schema` (`trust-tasks-build/src/generate.rs:163`) |
| #1186 | the other 31 updates (syn 3, prettyplease 0.3, sha2 0.11, serde-saphyr 2, jsonwebtoken 11, affinidi-*, …) | — | none. With schemars/typify held back: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo test --workspace` pass, `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` + `cargo fmt` leaves no diff, `npm run build-bundles` + `check-bundles` pass |
| #1184 | `json-schema-to-typescript` 15 → 16 | major, changes generated output | build-ts-bindings drift and trust-tasks-gen-ts equivalence: both generators reject the output (`counter-suffixed duplicates: DecryptionTarget1, EncryptedCast1, …`) |
| #1184 | `prettier` 3.8.3 → 3.9.10 (direct in trust-tasks-ts-gen, transitive in the root lockfile) | minor, changes generated output | with json-schema-to-typescript held at 15, prettier 3.9 alone reflows union types in 8 generated modules (drift) and the equivalence check reports 8 files that are not byte-identical. Pinning 3.8.3 back gives no drift |
| #1184 | `typescript` 5.9/6.0 → 7.0 | major, API break | trust-tasks-ts-proof, -tsp, -capability-client: `Cannot find name 'TextEncoder'` / `'crypto'`. Their tsconfigs set `lib: ["ES2022"]` and no `types`, and TS 7 no longer loads `@types/node` by default. TS 5.9 with @types/node 26 compiles cleanly |
| #1184 | `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.2 → 0.4 | 0.x "minor", API break | trust-tasks-ts-tsp: `'senderEncryptionKey' does not exist in type 'UnpackKeys'/'PackKeys'`. With vti-tsp-js at 0.2.0, those errors go away |
| #1185 | `lints` 4/5 → 6.1 | major, new lint | trust-tasks-dart-tsp (3.8, stable): `dart analyze --fatal-infos` reports 4 `use_null_aware_elements` infos in `test/support/fixtures.dart` |

The other two expected kinds of cause did not appear. No Dart SDK floor changed: Dependabot widened the `lints` range and left every `sdk:` constraint as it was. No failure was infrastructure flakiness: every failure is deterministic and reproduced locally.

## Changes

- **Every group (`github-actions`, `cargo`, `npm`, `gomod`, `pub`) takes only `update-types: ["minor", "patch"]`.** Majors come as their own PRs. TypeScript 7 (needs `"types": ["node"]` in three tsconfigs) and lints 6 (four lines in one test fixture) are deliberately **not** ignored. Each will arrive as its own PR and needs a small fix-up commit.
- **`ignore`, each with a comment giving the reason**, only where the logs show a deliberate migration is needed:
  - `schemars` majors and `typify` minors+majors. They move together, and `trust-tasks-build`/`trust-tasks-codegen` build on `schemars::schema::RootSchema`.
  - `json-schema-to-typescript` majors. 16 makes both TS generators emit duplicate names.
  - `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` minors+majors. It is 0.x, and 0.4 removes `senderEncryptionKey`.

  Dependabot classes a 0.x step (0.2 → 0.4) as "minor", so grouping by `update-types` cannot keep a breaking 0.x update out of the group. That is why the two 0.x entries also ignore minors.
- **A new `ts-generator` npm group** (`json-schema-to-typescript`, `prettier`) sits ahead of `npm`, so generator updates no longer share a PR with the rest.

## Generator updates still need a regeneration commit

The ts-generator group handles a patch or minor bump of a generator dependency that changes the generated output, as prettier 3.9 does. It does not ignore it. A PR from that group will fail `build-ts-bindings drift` / `trust-tasks-gen-ts equivalence` until someone:

1. moves the root lockfile's `prettier` (a transitive dependency of json-schema-to-typescript) to the version `trust-tasks-ts-gen` pins. The equivalence check compares output from the two generators, so they must format identically.
2. runs `npm run build-ts-bindings` and commits `trust-tasks-ts/src` and `trust-tasks-ts/component-names.lock.json`.

The same applies on the Rust side if a minor/patch of typify's or prettyplease's dependencies ever changes output: run `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` and commit the result. None of the current cargo updates do that.

No version or CHANGELOG changes. Validated with `check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot` and `actionlint`.

title: ci: weekly dependency updates for every ecosystem, and a scheduled advisory check
body:
Adds dependency updates for every ecosystem in the repository and a weekly advisory check, and clears advisory ignores in `deny.toml` that no longer match anything.

## Dependabot

`.github/dependabot.yml` (added in #1160 for `github-actions`) is extended. There is one grouped PR per ecosystem per week:

| Ecosystem | Directories | Title |
|---|---|---|
| github-actions | `/` | `ci:` (unchanged) |
| cargo | `/` (the workspace) | `chore(deps):` |
| npm | `/`, `trust-tasks-ts`, `-proof`, `-tsp`, `-capability-client`, `-gen`, `examples/consumer-app-ts` | `chore(deps):` |
| gomod | `trust-tasks-go` and its `proof`, `didcomm`, `capabilityclient`, `tsp` modules, `examples/consumer-app-go` | `chore(deps):` |
| pub | the six `trust-tasks-dart*` packages, `examples/consumer-app-dart` | `chore(deps):` |

`chore(deps)` passes commit-lint, and `cliff.toml` keeps it out of the changelogs. A note in the file covers two cases. An update inside a package directory still gives that package a patch release. An update that raises a Go module's `go` floor fails CI on purpose.

## Advisories workflow

`.github/workflows/advisories.yml` runs weekly (Monday 04:23 UTC) and on dispatch. It has read-only permissions and does not persist credentials.

- **cargo**: `cargo deny check advisories --all-features`, through the `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action` pin rust.yml already uses. This adds a schedule to the per-PR `cargo deny` job. No new action.
- **npm**: `npm audit`, which reads the lockfile and installs nothing, run in each of the seven lockfile directories. For the five published packages, `npm audit --omit=dev` fails on any advisory in what consumers install. In every directory, `npm audit --audit-level=high` fails on high or critical anywhere in the tree.

Go and Dart get no advisory scan here. `govulncheck` is not used in this repository yet, and adding it is a separate decision. For now they are covered by the Dependabot updates above.

## deny.toml

All eight advisory ignores were stale. `cargo deny check advisories` (cargo-deny 0.19.8) reported each one as `advisory-not-detected`. None of the crates they covered is in `Cargo.lock`: `proc-macro-error`, `rustls-pemfile`, `smallstr`, `clear_on_drop`, `bitmaps`, `im` and `sized-chunks` are absent, and `h2` is only at 0.4.16. The list is now `ignore = []`, and the new `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` setting fails the check when a future ignore stops matching. Without that setting, a stale ignore would stay green if its crate came back. The header comment no longer describes a `notice` downgrade the file does not make.

## Behaviour changes

- New weekly Dependabot PRs for cargo, npm, gomod and pub.
- `cargo deny` now fails on an ignore entry that matches nothing.
- The new `Advisories` workflow is scheduled, not a PR check. Its first run will report what `npm audit` reports today:
  - root tooling: `fast-uri` (high, via the build tooling), which fails the run;
  - `trust-tasks-ts` dev tree: `minimatch` (moderate, via `@microsoft/api-extractor`), which is below the high threshold and only logged.

  The published packages' runtime trees are clean.

## Checks

- `cargo deny check advisories` on `main` before the change: `advisories ok`, with eight `advisory-not-detected` warnings. After: `advisories ok`. Full `cargo deny check`: `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`, exit 0.
- `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` tested by putting one stale ignore back: `error[advisory-not-detected]`, `advisories FAILED`, exit 1.
- `npm audit` run locally in all seven directories, with the results above.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 on `advisories.yml`: clean. `dependabot.yml` parses.

## Checklist (development guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no client code; both jobs have `timeout-minutes`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — an empty ignore list plus `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"`
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the scheduled job fails rather than warns on an advisory that blocks
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutations; the workflow is read-only
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: fix(messaging/mux/ack): notPermitted only for a member whose mail the connection reads (0.1)
body:
Follow-up to #1174 and #1176. `messaging/mux/ack` 0.1 (draft) no longer lets a principal confirm mail it was never shown.

**The problem:** after #1176, rule 3 answers `notPermitted` for any message held for a member the connection carries without `delete`. A member may be carried with only `send` (or another scope that never shows its mail). An id is a hash of the message, so a principal that knows one (it sent the message, say) could ask for it and learn from `notPermitted` vs `notFound` whether that member still holds it.

**Change:**
- **Rule 3:** `notPermitted` only for a member carried with `receive` or `pickup`, whose mail the connection already sees. A member carried with neither is answered `notFound`, the same as a DID the connection does not carry.
- **Security & Privacy → Data carried:** names the sent-message case.
- **`AckRefusal.reason` description** updated to match. Same enum, no schema change beyond the description.

Bindings regenerated (doc comments only). `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` and `check-published-schemas` pass. The reference mediator implements this in a follow-up to affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#231.

title: feat(messaging/mux/ack): acknowledge frames on the mux connection they were delivered on (0.1)
body:
Adds **`messaging/mux/ack` 0.1 (draft)**: a principal acknowledges frames delivered on its mux connection, on that connection, and the mediator deletes each one the principal, or the member it was for, may delete.

**Why:** a raw-TSP `tsp-mux` socket is delete-to-ack, and until now a client acked out of band (a REST delete). Only the connection knows which members it carries and with what scope, so on a clustered mediator a delete landing on an instance that doesn't hold the connection was refused for every member's frame, and those frames were redelivered for ever. Acking on the socket gets the same answer on every instance.

**The task:**
- **Request:** `messageIds`, 1–100 lowercase hex SHA-256 ids (the stored message's hash, as `tsp-ack` and message-pickup deletes already name it).
- **Authority:** a frame the principal owns is deleted as its owner. A member's frame is deleted only while that member is on this connection with the `delete` scope.
- **Response:** `acked`, plus `refused` entries `{ messageId, reason }` with reason `notFound` or `notPermitted`. A refused message is left as it was.
- **Error:** `messaging/mux:notMuxConnection`.
- Declared `mutating`, not `destructive`: only the mediator's copy of frames the principal has already taken goes, and acking again changes nothing.
- Because acking is idempotent, the mediator **MAY** answer on the connection without storing the response, so acks of acks don't pile up.

**`messaging/mux/event` 0.1 (draft):** "Raw-TSP sockets" rule 5 now says a client acknowledges on the socket with `messaging/mux/ack`. `ack` is added to `related`. No schema change.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `check-published-schemas` (nothing released changed) and `check-bindings` pass.

The reference mediator (affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator) and the Rust SDK client (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs) will implement it next.

title: fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof)!: check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default
body:
## Summary

The Go, TypeScript and Dart proof verifiers accepted any non-empty `proofPurpose`, including `keyAgreement`, and no verifier in the four runtimes read a proof's `expires`. The signers also disagreed on the default purpose: Go, TypeScript and Dart wrote `assertionMethod`; Rust writes `authentication`, which SPEC §4.7.3 recommends.

This PR applies the rule `trust-tasks-proof` (Rust) already applies to the other three runtimes, adds the `expires` check to all four, and aligns the signer defaults.

### proofPurpose (Go, TypeScript, Dart)

- `proofPurpose` must be `authentication`, `assertionMethod`, `capabilityInvocation` or `capabilityDelegation`. `keyAgreement` and any other value fail as `malformedProof` before any key is used (SPEC §4.7.3). This is Rust's `ProofPurpose::parse`.
- Go and TypeScript verify `did:key` only, and a `did:key` authorises its key for all four relationships, so the allow-list is the whole rule there.
- Dart `withResolver` (did:web, did:webvh, ...) now applies the rule Rust's `CachedDidResolver` applies. The issuer's DID document must list the exact `verificationMethod` under the relationship `proofPurpose` names (by absolute reference, by a fragment relative to the DID, or embedded). The method must be defined under `verificationMethod`, and its controller must be the issuer. An embedded entry's own controller must be the issuer too. Dart is stricter than Rust in two documented cases: a key embedded only under a relationship (ssi reads keys from `verificationMethod` alone), and `did:scid` with a `?src=` locator (Rust strips it, Dart compares exactly). Both are in the README. ssi's own lookup matches by id or by fragment suffix and ignores relationships. The check also confirms that the method ssi then selects is the one checked. The document is resolved once per verification and shared with ssi, so there is no second fetch.
- New public constants: Go `proof.SigningPurposes`, TS `SIGNING_PURPOSES`, Dart `signingPurposes`.

### expires (all four runtimes)

- When present, `expires` must be a `dateTimeStamp` (`Z` or an explicit `±hh:mm` offset) and must not have passed. No clock-skew allowance applies, because the signer chose the instant.
- After the shared pattern, every runtime checks each field against its range itself: month 1-12, a day the month has (leap years included), hour 0-23, minute and second 0-59 (no leap second), and an offset of at most 14:00 with minutes 0-59. Each language's own date parser accepts or rolls over a different subset. Before this, Rust's chrono accepted `:60`, TS `Date.parse` accepted `2027-02-30` and `24:00`, Go and Dart accepted `+24:00`/`+23:60`, and Dart accepted `+99:00`. Any value outside these ranges, or not a string, fails as `malformedProof`.
- Dart: ssi already compared `expires`, but it read an offset-less value as local time. The verifier now checks it first, with the same rule as the others.
- **Rust refuses every proof that carries `expires`.** `affinidi-data-integrity` 0.8's `DataIntegrityProof` has no `expires` member and drops it when parsing, so the signature Rust recomputes never covers it. A passed or malformed `expires` is refused as such. Any other is refused as unsupported (`UNSUPPORTED_EXPIRES`), not as `signatureInvalid`. Go, TS and Dart accept an unexpired one, and the shared vector `expires-future` records this as a known Rust gap. Closing it needs the member upstream. `Verifier::with_clock` (new) sets the clock `expires` is checked against. No signer in this repo writes `expires`.

### Signer defaults (Go, TypeScript, Dart)

- `proofPurpose` now defaults to `authentication`, matching Rust's `sign_trust_task`. A purpose naming no signing relationship is refused: Go returns an error, TS throws, Dart throws `ArgumentError`. Rust already refused one.

### Ed25519 strictness (Go, TS, Dart)

- **Go:** `crypto/ed25519` accepts a non-canonical public-key encoding and a key of small order. With the identity point as the key and as R, and S = 0, `ed25519.Verify` returns true for any message, so a document "issued" by `did:key:z6MkeXATEjyXENzBXBxgC5EHk2JE5aqd7qMGGtDpLUH1e2Sj` (the identity point's did:key) verified. The verifier now refuses a non-canonical or small-order Ed25519 key, both when it parses the did:key and again right before `ed25519.Verify`. The check is RFC 8032 §5.1.3 decoding plus [8]A ≠ identity, written on `math/big`, so the module still has no third-party dependency. This was already the case on `main`.
- **Dart:** the same keys verified with ssi 3.9.6, the version `package:didcomm` pins; ssi 4 refused them. The relationship check now refuses an Ed25519 multikey that is non-canonical or of small order (BigInt, no new dependency), so the result no longer depends on which ssi resolves.
- **TypeScript:** `ed25519.verify` now passes `{ zip215: false }`. `@noble/curves` 2.4.0's `ed25519` wrapper defaults to ZIP-215, which accepts non-canonical encodings. Strict mode refuses a small-order key, but noble checks the *cofactored* equation, which also accepts an R carrying a small-order component. Go, Rust (`verify_strict`) and Dart check the cofactorless one. TS now also checks the cofactorless equation explicitly, comparing `[S]B − [k]A` with R, so all four refuse the `mixed-order-r` vector.
- Not covered: a small-order **R** with a valid S (only the key holder can produce one). Rust's `verify_strict` refuses it, and the other three do not check it.

### Shared vectors

`fixtures/proof` has new entries, and every runtime runs all of them:

- **Purpose:** `purpose-key-agreement` and `purpose-unrecognised` are both invalid. Their signatures are valid; I checked them with the Go primitives directly.
- **expires, invalid:** `expired`, `expires-february-30`, `expires-hour-24`, `expires-leap-second`, `expires-offset-24-hours`, `expires-offset-minute-60` and `expires-offset-99-hours`. All are correctly signed.
- **expires, valid:** `expires-future` is valid, with an `exceptions.rust` entry for the known gap above.
- **Ed25519, invalid:** `small-order-key` (identity key, R = identity, S = 0), `non-canonical-key` (identity encoded with y = p + 1) and `mixed-order-r` (seed-7 key, R = rB + T with T of order 8, S = r + k·a). I confirmed that noble's cofactored verify accepts `mixed-order-r`.
- Manifest entries may now carry `exceptions.<runtime>`. Each runtime's test applies its own exception and asserts it, so the test fails once the gap closes. Rust also asserts the "not supported" error for `expires-future`.

Before this change, Go accepted `small-order-key` and `non-canonical-key`, and Dart on ssi 3.9.6 accepted both. The byte-for-byte reproduction tests now pass the fixture's `proofPurpose` explicitly, because the fixtures use `assertionMethod`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- Go, TS and Dart verifiers refuse proofs they accepted before: a `proofPurpose` outside the four signing relationships, a passed or malformed `expires`, and (Dart `withResolver`) a key the issuer's DID document does not list under the stated relationship.
- TS refuses Ed25519 signatures that only ZIP-215 decoding, or only the cofactored equation, accepts.
- Rust refuses any proof carrying `expires`. A conforming signer covers `expires`, and Rust never verified such a proof. What Rust accepted before and refuses now is only a proof whose `expires` was not covered by its signature, so the title's `!` does not name the Rust crate. Rust also gains `Verifier::with_clock`, the `Clock` alias and `UNSUPPORTED_EXPIRES` (additive).
- Go and Dart refuse a non-canonical or small-order Ed25519 key (Dart on ssi 3.9 only; ssi 4 already did). TS refuses a signature whose R has a small-order component.
- The Go, TS and Dart signers now write `authentication` when no purpose is given, and refuse a non-signing purpose. A caller that relied on the `assertionMethod` default now gets `authentication`. Rust and the updated verifiers accept both. A third-party verifier that pins `assertionMethod` would not accept the new default.
- Consumers: I searched verifiable-trust-infrastructure, cierge, vti-didcomm-js, pnm-browser-plugin, pnm-relay, vti-message-bridge, affinidi-trust-registry-rs and openvtc. Only the Rust crate `trust-tasks-proof` is used outside this repo (VTI, trust registry, and through lockfiles in cierge, openvtc and vti-message-bridge). For those consumers the only change is the `expires` check. The npm, Go and Dart proof packages have no consumers in those repos.
- `!` is scoped to `go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof`. The TS and Dart public API change is additive (a new constant). The break is behavioural: previously accepted proofs are refused, and the signer default changes.

## Tests

Round 2 (review fixes), all exit 0:
- Go: `gofmt -l` is empty; `go vet`, `go test -race` pass. New tests: `ed25519point_test.go` (the 7 small-order encodings, 4 non-canonical ones, 64 real keys, the base point, and the identity key through `publicKeyFromRaw` and `verifySignature`) and out-of-range and in-range `expires` cases.
- TS: build, `typecheck:test`, `npm test` (80 tests).
- Dart: `dart analyze --fatal-infos`; format check at language version 3.6; `dart test` (116 tests) on ssi 4.3.0 and on ssi 3.9.6. New tests: `test/ed25519_point_test.dart`, `expires` ranges, and an embedded entry with a foreign controller (refused) and with the issuer as controller (accepted).
- Rust: `cargo fmt`; `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-proof`. New: range cases and offset arithmetic for `parse_date_time_stamp`, and the shared-vector exception assertion.

Round 1:

- Go `trust-tasks-go/proof`: `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go vet ./...` (exit 0), `go test -race ./...` (exit 0). New tests: `TestProofPurposeMustNameASigningRelationship`, `TestSignDefaultsToAuthenticationAndRefusesNonSigningPurposes`, `TestExpires`.
- TS `trust-tasks-ts-proof`: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:test`, `npm test` all exit 0 (57 tests). There are new tests for each purpose, for the signer default and refusal, and for the `expires` cases.
- Dart `trust-tasks-dart-proof`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` (no issues), `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --language-version=3.6 .` (exit 0), and `dart test` exit 0 on ssi 4.3.0 and on ssi 3.9.6 (89 tests each). The new `test/purpose_and_expires_test.dart` covers purposes and `expires`, plus `withResolver` documents: listed, relative reference, keyAgreement-only, another relationship, `verificationMethod`-only, foreign controller, document for another DID, and a fragment match on another DID's method. `sign_test.dart` covers the default and the refusals.
- Rust `trust-tasks-proof`: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings` (exit 0), `cargo test -p trust-tasks-proof` (exit 0). There are new unit tests for `check_expires`, and the shared-vector test runs the three new entries.

## Overlap with open PRs

#1167 changes `trust-tasks-dart-proof/lib/src/data_integrity_verifier.dart`, `trust-tasks-proof/src/affinidi/mod.rs` and `trust-tasks-proof/Cargo.toml`. This PR's hunks in those files are separate from #1167's: the Dart purpose/expires checks are before #1167's base58 bound, and the Rust `expires` check is in step 1, not step 3a. The `chrono` line goes under `[dependencies]`, not `[features]`. A rebase should apply cleanly either way. `chrono` was already a dev-dependency and is in the graph through `trust-tasks-rs`, so `Cargo.lock` does not change.

## Checklist (dev guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a, no clients. The Dart verifier still resolves through the caller's resolver, now once per verification instead of possibly twice.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): n/a, no state
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire type changes. The behaviour change is listed above (R3.6), and the consumer search is above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no new config. An unrecognised purpose fails closed.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): failure details name the rule that refused the proof.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: site: render prose through an allow-list, pin marked by hash, and drop the tweaks panel
body:
Four changes to the registry website and its dev server.

**Prose rendering.** Spec, binding and framework-spec (`SPEC.md`) prose is rendered by `marked` and inserted into the page as markup. `marked` passes raw HTML and any link scheme through unchanged. The three call sites in `pages.jsx` now go through `website/assets/markdown.js`, a dedicated `marked` instance (no global `setOptions`) whose renderer hooks:

- keep raw HTML only for an allow-list of inline tags (`a`, `abbr`, `b`, `br`, `code`, `em`, `span`, `sup`, …) and attributes (`id`, `name`, `href`, `title`); a tag outside it is shown as literal text, and every other `<` in a raw-HTML fragment is escaped;
- escape text after an inline `<code>`, `<kbd>`, `<pre>` or `<script>` tag like any other text — marked's inline tokenizer otherwise switches to a raw mode after those tags and emits the following text unescaped, so the renderer wraps that tokenizer to keep the mode off;
- drop `<!-- … -->` comments (they never displayed);
- keep a link or image only when its URL is relative, a fragment, or `http:` / `https:` / `mailto:`, and not protocol-relative (`//host`, or the same with `\`, which browsers read as `/`); otherwise a link renders as its text and an image as its alt text.

With those hooks, the only markup in the rendered prose is what marked writes for markdown syntax, with URLs that passed the check, plus the allow-listed tags rebuilt by the renderer.

No new dependency. A spec's `carries.reference` (`format: uri`, any scheme) becomes a link only when it is `http(s)`; both current references are.

**`marked` pinned by hash.** Its `<script>` tag now carries `integrity`, like the React, ReactDOM and Babel tags. The hash was computed from `marked@12.0.2/marked.min.js` as served by unpkg, and the file is byte-identical to the one in the npm tarball and on jsDelivr. The other three hashes were re-checked and still match. The Google Fonts stylesheet is not hashed: its CSS varies by user agent.

**Tweaks panel removed** (`tweaks-panel.jsx`, its `<TweaksPanel>` block, the `EDITMODE` markers and the unused CSS hook). It was design-tool scaffolding that listened for `postMessage` from a parent frame. The values it defaulted to are now a fixed `SITE_THEME` in `index.html`, so the site looks the same. This covers the "remove the tweaks panel" item of #1157; the rest of that issue is untouched.

**Dev server.** `npm run serve` listens on `127.0.0.1` unless `--host <addr>` or `SERVE_WEBSITE_HOST` names another address (`--host 0.0.0.0` for every IPv4 interface, `--host ::` for every interface on IPv6 and, on most systems, IPv4). The startup log prints the address actually bound.

### Checking that rendering did not change

- Every `spec.md` under `specs/` and `bindings/`, the committed `SPEC.md`, and a fresh `SPEC.md` generated from canonical `main` (1,398 documents; 1,401 counting every tracked `spec.md`) were rendered with marked 12.0.2 both ways in Node. The output is byte-identical apart from the HTML comments in two documents, which are now dropped. No prose uses a protocol-relative link.
- Seven pages were rendered in headless Chrome against a local build, before and after: `/`, `/specification`, `/spec/registry/recognition/0.2` (has `carries`), `/spec/vtc/join-requests/withdraw/0.1` (has a comment), `/spec/did-management/did/register/0.1`, `/binding/https/0.3` and `/binding/didcomm/0.2`. The rendered `<main>` is byte-identical on five of them. On `/specification` and the `join-requests/withdraw` page it differs only by the HTML comment that is now dropped. The body theme attributes and accent are the same on all seven, the tweaks panel is gone, and there are no console errors either way. The `marked` script loads with the new `integrity` attribute.

### Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- Raw HTML in prose outside the allow-list now displays as text instead of rendering; a link or image with another scheme loses its link. No current prose is affected.
- HTML comments in prose no longer appear in the page source.
- The tweaks panel no longer exists, and the page no longer posts or listens for its `postMessage` protocol.
- A protocol-relative link (`//host/…`) in prose now renders as its text. No current prose uses one.
- `npm run serve` is no longer reachable from other machines by default. Use `--host 0.0.0.0` (or `--host ::`) to get the old behaviour.

### Tests

- New `npm run test:website` (`scripts/test/website-markdown.test.mjs`), which `deploy.yml` runs next to `test:infra`. It covers the URL check and the raw-HTML allow-list on their own, and renders markdown end to end through the `marked` build the page loads. That build is not an npm dependency, so the test fetches it from the URL pinned in `index.html` and refuses it unless it matches the `integrity` hash there; `MARKED_JS=<file>` runs it offline against a local copy, with the same check. The end-to-end cases include unclosed inline `<code>` / `<kbd>` / `<pre>` / `<script>` (also carrying into a later paragraph, a heading and a table cell), `javascript:` links, autolinks and reference definitions, protocol-relative links, link titles, and HTML in image alt text. They split the output into tags and check every element, attribute and URL against what the site writes.
- Removing the tokenizer wrap fails the two unclosed-tag tests, and removing the protocol-relative check fails the URL tests.
- `npm run build`, `npm run test:infra` and `npm run test:website` (17 tests) pass locally.

### Pre-merge checklist (development guide §9)

- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()` / bare `fetch()`; all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a, the existing same-origin prose `fetch`es are unchanged
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a

title: fix(runtime)!: digest item 11 over the received document, and check envelope types and nesting depth
body:
## Summary Three consumer-pipeline correctness fixes, all in how a runtime treats the document it actually received. ### 1. Item 11 compares the document as received (Go, Dart, Rust, and their bindings) SPEC §7.2 *Keying and comparison* makes two documents under one `id` the same only when their serializations are identical under RFC 8785. Go, Dart and Rust hashed the **typed re-encoding**, which drops payload members the consumer's type does not model and (Rust) re-renders `issuedAt` / `expiresAt`. A second, different document under a known `id` was then absorbed as a duplicate and answered with the first one's cached response, instead of `idConflict`. TypeScript already hashed the received document; the others now match it. - **Go** — `ConsumeInbound` digests `ConsumeOptions.Received` (canonical form) when it is set **and** `Doc` is a reading of it; otherwise `Doc`'s own re-encoding, as before. The `didcomm` and `tsp` consumers now pass `Received: unpacked.Document`; their core requirement moves `v0.9.3` → `v0.9.6`, the first release with `ConsumeOptions.Received`. - **Dart** — `consumeInbound` digests `received` whenever it is passed and names the same `id` and `type` as `doc` (it did so only for a forward read along `extends`). `trust_tasks_https`'s server and the DIDComm and TSP consumers now pass `received: json`. - **Rust** — `ProofPolicy` gains `RejectIfPresentReceived(&Value)` and `AcceptUnverifiedReceived(&Value)` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is additive), and `with_received` now maps all three policies to their received-carrying form. `consume_inbound` / `consume_dispatched` digest the received JSON under any of them when it is the document being consumed, with or without a proof. Every binding already calls `with_received` (`trust-tasks-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-didcomm-v1` `inbound.rs`), so all of them now digest the received document whatever proof policy the caller chose. The HTTPS server digests the body. New `received_document_digest(&Value)`. **Numbers.** With the received document in the digest, number spelling became visible: Rust and Dart wrote `1.0` / `100.0` where TypeScript and Go write `1` / `100`, so `{"amount":1}` then `{"amount":1.0}` (or `100` then `1e2`) was `idConflict` in two runtimes and `duplicate` in the other two. Rust's `canonical_json` and Dart's `canonicalJson` now read every number as the IEEE 754 double RFC 8785 reads it as, and write an integral value below `1e21` as an integer, as ECMAScript does. All four agree on the new number vectors. **Known remaining difference (not a vector):** Rust and Go order object members by Unicode scalar value, TypeScript and Dart by UTF-16 code unit (JCS's order). They disagree only for member names mixing characters above the BMP with names in `U+E000..U+FFFF`; each runtime orders both documents it compares the same way, so the equality item 11 uses is unaffected. Documented in `fixtures/consume/README.md`. ### 2. TypeScript checks the envelope before anything reads it `JSON.parse(body) as TrustTaskDocument

` checks nothing, and `consumeInbound` used `doc.id` as the item-11 key unchecked: an array `id` compares by object identity, so every resend was "fresh". `consumeInbound` now refuses `malformedRequest`, first, a document that is not an object; lacks `id`, `type` or `payload`; has a non-string `id`, `type`, `threadId`, `parentThreadId`, `issuer`, `recipient`, `issuedAt` or `expiresAt`; a non-object `payload`, `proof` or `ceremony`; or an `@context` that is not a string, array or object. The refusal is addressed only from the members that are strings: with no string `type` it carries no `inResponseTo` (whose `typeUri` the error schema requires), and with neither a string `id` nor a string `type` nothing is emitted (`suppressed`). `validateEnvelope` and `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` are exported. README updated. ### 3. Deep nesting is refused rather than overflowing the stack (TypeScript, Dart) The canonical-form walks recurse. A ~10 KB payload of 5,000 nested arrays threw out of the TypeScript `consumeInbound`; a 200 KB body of 100,000 levels raised a `StackOverflowError` (an `Error`) in Dart — a 500 from the HTTPS server, an escaping throw from the DIDComm and TSP consumers. Both now refuse a document nested more than **128** levels (the document counting as one; the same figure as serde_json's recursion limit, which Rust parses under) with `malformedRequest`, using an iterative check that runs before anything else walks the document — in Dart ahead of the payload validator too, so a recursive validator never sees it. Dart also gets `parseTrustTaskDocument`, which decodes a received value without throwing and returns a `malformedRequest` reason for a mistyped member (`fromJson` throws `TypeError`); the example and README use it. ## Shared vectors `fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json` (with a README), nine cases, each a first and a second document under one `id`: byte-identical and reordered/re-spaced (`duplicate`); extra unmodelled payload member, extra top-level member, `issuedAt` with `.000`, changed modelled member (`idConflict`); `1` vs `1.0` and `100` vs `1e2` (`duplicate`), `1` vs `1.5` (`idConflict`). Run by `trust-tasks-rs/tests/received_digest.rs`, `trust-tasks-ts/test/envelope.test.ts`, `trust-tasks-go/trusttasks/item11_vectors_test.go` and `trust-tasks-dart/test/input_robustness_test.dart`. Rust and Go also pin that, without the received document, the digest is still the typed view; Go pins that a `Received` which is not a reading of `Doc` is ignored. Other new tests: - **Rust bindings** — `trust-tasks-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-didcomm-v1` `tests/replay.rs`: an unmodelled payload member under a known `id`, delivered under `AcceptUnverified`, is `idConflict` and the handler runs once. `trust-tasks-https` `tests/end_to_end.rs`: `.000` on `issuedAt` under a known `id` is 409, and so is an added top-level member. `canonical.rs`: number spellings. - **Go bindings** — `didcomm` and `tsp` `received_digest_test.go`: the same unmodelled-member case through the consumer. It first probes whether the linked core digests `Received`; the published `v0.9.6` does not, so the test skips until the requirement moves to a release containing this change. Verified passing against this branch's core via a local `replace`. - **TypeScript** — every mistyped/missing envelope member, non-object documents (suppressed), the `inResponseTo` addressing rules, the array-`id` resend, 128 levels accepted / 129 refused, 5,000 and 100,000 levels under item 11. - **Dart** — `parseTrustTaskDocument` over the same member cases plus a payload the decoder cannot read; depth boundary; 129 and 100,000 levels through `consumeInbound`; a deep payload is refused before a recursive validator runs and the message names no stack; number spellings. `trust_tasks_https`: an extra payload member under a known `id` is 409; a 100,000-level body is 400. ## Behaviour changes (guide §R3.6) **Breaking (`!`):** consumers now refuse documents they used to accept, which CLAUDE.md counts as a breaking library change. - TypeScript refuses a document with a mistyped or missing envelope member, an explicit `null` for an optional framework member (the framework schema types them as strings/objects), a non-object `payload`, or nesting deeper than 128 levels. A JS producer that serialises `undefined` members is unaffected (`JSON.stringify` drops them). A non-object document, or one with neither a string `id` nor `type`, is now `suppressed` rather than answered. - Dart refuses nesting deeper than 128 levels. - Go, Dart and Rust (core and every binding) answer `idConflict` where they answered `duplicate`, for a second document under a known `id` that differs only in a member the payload type does not model (or, Rust, in a timestamp's spelling). Rust and Dart now answer `duplicate` where they answered `idConflict` for documents differing only in number spelling (`1` / `1.0`), matching TypeScript and Go. - One-off migration effect for a **persistent** replay guard: a resend of a document accepted before the upgrade, within its acceptance window, is compared against a digest computed the old way; where the old and new digests differ (an unmodelled member, a non-integer-spelled integral number), that resend is answered `idConflict` once instead of being absorbed. An in-memory guard is unaffected. - Rust `ProofPolicy::with_received` now returns `RejectIfPresentReceived` / `AcceptUnverifiedReceived` for `RejectIfPresent` / `AcceptUnverified`; code matching on the returned policy needs a wildcard arm (the enum was already `#[non_exhaustive]`). - Go `didcomm` and `tsp` require core `v0.9.6` (was `v0.9.3`). - Additive API: Rust `received_document_digest`, the two `ProofPolicy` variants; TS `validateEnvelope`, `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`; Dart `parseTrustTaskDocument`, `DocumentParse` / `ParsedDocument` / `UnparsableDocument`, `maxNestingDepth`, `exceedsNestingDepth`. - No wire type changes. Grepped verifiable-trust-infrastructure, cierge, vti-didcomm-js, pnm-browser-plugin, pnm-relay, vti-message-bridge and affinidi-trust-registry-rs: none calls these consume pipelines (the only hits are generated doc comments and changelogs). ## Not done here - **Go `didcomm` / `tsp` digests take effect with the next core release.** They now pass `Received`, but the core they require (`v0.9.6`) digests the typed view; the received digest applies once their requirement moves to the release that contains this change. Their new tests detect that and run then. - TypeScript `InMemoryReplayGuard.claim` does not itself refuse a non-string `id`; `consumeInbound`'s envelope check stops one first. Not changed here to avoid colliding with #1163, which rewrites `claim`. - `trust-tasks-ts/README.md`'s "Items 1 and 3 … have already succeeded" paragraph is rewritten by #1162; this PR adds a separate paragraph on the envelope check instead of editing it. ## Rebase notes Merges cleanly with each of #1160, #1162, #1163, #1167, #1168, #1169, and with #1162 + #1163 together (`git merge-tree`, rechecked after the review commit). New tests are in new files or appended to files those PRs do not touch, and edits avoid their hunks; the Dart nesting check sits above `route` so it does not touch #1162's insertion below it. ## Test results (local, exit codes) - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0 - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features acl --all-targets` 0; `cargo clippy` of the same with `-D warnings` 0 - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-https -p trust-tasks-didcomm -p trust-tasks-tsp -p trust-tasks-didcomm-v1 --all-targets` 0; `cargo clippy` of the same with `-D warnings` 0 - `trust-tasks-ts`: `npm test` 0 (163/163), `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 0, `npm run smoke` 0 - `trust-tasks-go`: `go vet ./...` 0, `gofmt -l .` empty, `go test -race ./...` 0; `didcomm` and `tsp` modules: `go vet` 0, `go test ./...` 0 (new binding test skips against published `v0.9.6`; passes with a local `replace` onto this branch's core) - `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` 0, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` 0, `dart test` 0 (184), `dart run example/main.dart` 0 - `trust-tasks-dart-{https,didcomm,tsp,proof,capability-client}`: analyze 0, format 0, `dart test` 0 (64 / 25 / 24 / 57 / 15) Full-workspace `cargo test --workspace` was not run locally (memory); CI runs it. ## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack development guide §9) - [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (guide §R1.2) — no network code touched - [x] No lock held across a network await (guide §R1.3) — n/a - [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (guide §R2.1) — the envelope and depth refusals run before the item-11 claim; nothing is recorded for a refused document - [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (guide §R1.4) — n/a - [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (guide §R1.5) — the Dart consumers and TS pipeline now answer instead of throwing on deep or mistyped input - [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (guide §R1.6) — n/a - [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (guide §R3.*) — no wire type changed; the TS envelope check enforces the existing framework schema's member types - [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (guide §R5.*) — the checks are unconditional - [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (guide §R6.*) — n/a - [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (guide §R2.1) — the only state touched is the replay record, whose claim/settle order is unchanged - [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — the behaviour changes above (guide §R3.6)
