title: refactor(vtc)!: one typed routing table for every Trust Task family; routes/ is the HTTP surface only (#2732)
body:
refactor(vtc)!: one typed routing table for every Trust Task family; routes/ is the HTTP surface only (#2732) * refactor(vtc): route every Trust Task family through one typed AsyncDispatcher #2728 split trust_tasks/mod.rs into handler files but left three routing styles: about sixty direct arms in `dispatch_typed`, thirty-three family modules each keeping a `URIS` list beside a `match` that re-matched it (one `FAMILIES` table arm), and typed `AsyncDispatcher` registration for rooms and git-ns. A hand-kept `DISPATCHED_URIS` (540 lines) had to agree with all of it, and already did not: `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1` was routed but not listed, so discovery never advertised it. - `trust_tasks::routing`: one `AsyncDispatcher` every family registers on, keyed on the generated payload type (`on!(routes, P => handler)`). The URI a handler answers is `P::TYPE_URI`; the served set is the table itself (`routing::served_uris`), and `dispatched_uris()` (that plus discovery) replaces `DISPATCHED_URIS` for the unsupported-version hint, discovery, the size gate and the censuses. - Each family exposes `register(Routes) -> Routes`; every `URIS` constant, every family `dispatch` and the `FAMILIES` table are gone, and the direct arms moved into their handler files' `register`. Families whose verbs share an authority check before the payload is read (backup, website, the administrator's passkeys) route through a small `Op` enum, not a URI match. - Handlers are registered on `Received

`: routed and policed as `P`, but handed the JSON as received, so every handler still reads it against the schema before parsing it and still resolves the signer's authority before reading the payload (a typed downcast in the router would reverse that order and change which refusal a stranger gets). - Censuses: no URI is registered twice (the dispatcher would silently keep the later one), and none is also a rooms or git-ns task. - The URI constants nothing but the removed lists named are deleted; the ones only tests name stay behind `#[cfg(test)]`. Behaviour is unchanged except that discovery and the version hint now list `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`, which was always served. Refs #2579 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * test(vtc): one seed_acl fixture in test_support The ACL-row fixture was written three times (trust_tasks::test_fixtures, git_ns::tests, acl::console_key's tests), each spelling out every field of VtcAclEntry (#2579). test_support now holds the entry the fixtures seed (seeded_acl_entry) and seed_acl(acl, did, role) over the role's implied authority. console_key's tests use it as is; git-ns's adds the member record a git right needs; the trust-task fixture keeps its legacy-context form over the shared entry. Refs #2579 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * refactor(vtc): move the Trust Task operations out of routes/ into their domain modules routes/ was the operations layer for signed documents that have no route (#2574): 34 of its files held only the bodies trust_tasks/ calls, and domain modules (admin_actions, ceremony, join, schemas, directory, elections, acl) imported upward from it. A pure move, bodies unchanged: - acl/ops.rs, auth/admin_passkeys.rs, audit_ops.rs, backup/ops.rs (backup.rs becomes backup/mod.rs), ceremony/listing.rs - community/ops/{branding,config,did_register,join_discovery,profile, requested_attributes,theme} - endorsement_types/ops.rs, endorsements/ops.rs, relationships/ops.rs, schemas/ops.rs - install/ops/{mod,bootstrap,invites}, join/invitations.rs, join/ops/{decide,manifest,present,read,status} - members/ops/{credentials,personhood,read,relationships,remove,renew, request_vmc,rotate,update}, policy/ops/{admin,read} - recognition/{recognise,admin}.rs, registry/admin.rs, vetting/{ops,hidden}.rs, website/ops/{mod,deploy,files,generations} routes/ keeps what it mounts: auth, member_portal, credential_exchange, oid4vp, status_lists, health, did_log, the console's static assets, the Trust Task door, community/did_qr and the public half of community/profile (split out of the moved file), and rooms (left for #2575). Every `crate::routes::` path names the new module. Refs #2574 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * refactor(vtc)!: the operations take the generated payloads; delete the REST-era body types Every one of these tasks validated its document against the generated `vti_specs` payload and then parsed the same JSON again into a REST-era struct of its own, which the operation took — two descriptions of one payload that could drift (#2574). The operations now take the generated payloads, and the parallel structs and their utoipa derives are gone: - members: ListMembersQuery, UpdateMemberRequest, RemoveBody, rotate::{ChallengeBody, FinishBody}, RequestVmcBody (now a parameter) - join: ListJoinRequestsQuery, IssueInvitationBody, SendQueryRequest - policy: ListPoliciesQuery, PolicyStatusFilter, ActiveQuery, UploadBody, TestBody - endorsement types: ListQuery, RegisterBody; endorsements: IssueBody - audit: AuditQuery (its filter rules are a trait on the generated payload); admin invites: CreateInviteRequest; schemas: RegisterSchemaBody Parameter structs that are built, never parsed (PatchRequest, DecideBody, CheckQuery, BootstrapRequest) lose their Deserialize/utoipa derives. Two members the generated type folds — an absent and an empty object read the same — are read from the received JSON (`crate::wire::sent`): `members/update`'s `extensions` (absent leaves them, empty replaces them) and `endorsement-types/register`'s `claimSchema` (the row keeps them apart). That is why the double parse existed; it is now one explicit read. `crate::wire` also reads generated enum members as domain types through their shared wire form. The console: openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated. CreateInviteRequest, IssueInvitationBody, RequestVmcBody and PolicyStatusFilter go (no console code used them); RegisterBody becomes VtcEndorsementTypesRegisterV0_1Payload (new `vta_sdk::openapi::EndorsementTypeRegister01Payload`). Behaviour is unchanged except: `policy/list` accepts an explicit `enabledOnly: false` (the schema default, asking for no filter; it used to be refused with `true`), the dead `status` filter (the 0.3 schema has no such member) is removed, and a few malformedRequest messages for members the schema already constrains are worded differently. Codes are unchanged. BREAKING CHANGE: vtc-service's public module paths moved with #2574's move (`routes::join_requests` → `join::ops`, `routes::recognise` → `recognition::recognise`, `routes::vetting_hidden` → `vetting::hidden`), and the deleted body types are gone from its API. Refs #2574 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * test(vtc): a census that handlers parse payloads as the generated types vta-sdk's generated-wire-types census refuses a hand-written type whose doc summary names a generated task. It already scans vtc-service; what it cannot see is a handler that validates against the generated type and then parses the same JSON into a struct of its own — the pattern #2574 removed. trust_tasks::payload_type_census reads every handler's `let x: T = match parse_payload(&doc)` (and the `without_ext` form) and requires a generated `…Payload`; a shrink-only baseline names the nine parses still hand-written and why. The SDK census's baseline paths follow the move out of routes/. Refs #2574 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * docs(vtc): the source layout after routes/ stopped being the operations layer vtc-service/CLAUDE.md still described routes/ as every HTTP route handler and left out a dozen modules (#2574). The layout now names each domain module's ops, routes/ as the HTTP surface and its declared exceptions, trust_tasks' routing table, and where a new task's handler and operation go. The operator docs' source paths follow the move. Refs #2574 Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * test(vtc): the secret-Debug census names hidden vetting's new path PublishHiddenVettingBody moved from routes/vetting_hidden.rs to vetting/hidden.rs with the operations (#2574); its NOT_SECRET entry follows. title: refactor(vta)!: decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing
body:
The structural refactors from the 2026-11-11 architecture review, one commit per issue. Breaking for published crates (hence the `!`): `vta-service` loses `test_support::MockVta`/`StubWebvhHost` (now in the new `vta-test-support` crate) and `auth::credentials`, and `vtc-service` loses `auth::credentials`.

## #2566: `vta-cli-common` only for the `vta` binary
- `vta-cli-common` and `dialoguer` are optional behind `cli-synthesis`. The `vta` binary already requires that feature, and only its offline-CLI and setup-wizard modules use the two crates.
- `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` went from 981 unique lines to 934. `vta-cli-common`, `vtc-client`, `ratatui`, `crossterm`, `qrcode` and `dialoguer` are no longer in the graph.
- The `vti-rooms` comment said `default-features = false` keeps `storage`/`authz`/`audit` out of the build. That is wrong: `vti-rooms-dtg` verifies through `vti_rooms::authz` and takes `vti-rooms` with its `host` default, so feature unification turns `host` back on. I rewrote the comment to say so. Turning it off would need `vti-rooms-dtg` split into a host half and a member half, and there is no gain: `host` adds only `vti-common`, `tokio`, `uuid` and `tracing`, which are already direct dependencies.
- The decomposition note now records that this gets the `vta-offline-cli` extraction's dependency win without creating the crate.

## #2569: module splits (in-crate, no behaviour change)
`mod.rs` re-exports every submodule in all three splits, so call sites do not change.
- `operations/keys/{records,gates,secret,sign}.rs`, each with its tests beside it. The shared fixtures are in `keys/test_support.rs`.
  - `tests/it/key_custody_census.rs` had one entry, `keys.rs` with 6 sites. It now has three: `records.rs` 3, `secret.rs` 2, `sign.rs` 1. The six sites are unchanged.
- `operations/room_groups/{join,custody,open,advance,migrate,personal}.rs`. Each existing test module moved next to the code it covers. The personal-label reader census and `vta-service/CLAUDE.md` now name the new files.
- `vta-cli-common` `commands/rooms/{records,watch,admin,files,owner,offers,memberships}.rs`. The act/present plumbing stays in `mod.rs`.
  - The `#2588` JSON census read only the top level of `src/commands` and would have silently stopped checking these handlers. It now walks module directories.

## #2570: `vta-test-support`
- New published crate. `openvtc-core` dev-depends on `MockVta` from crates.io (its bootstrap, vault, witness, voting and collection e2e tests), so it has to be published. It follows the new-crate checklist: workspace members and default-members, `Dockerfile.nitro` COPY, `[lints] workspace = true`, the crate map and the counts (now 39 of 50, with #2728's vtc-audit and #2731's vti-rooms-host) in CLAUDE.md, RELEASING.md and the engineering notes.
- What moved there:
  - `MockVta`, the stub DID hosting service and the transport harness with its D6 tests.
  - The `mock_vta` and `vault_release_didcomm` integration tests.
- The crate re-exports everything in `vta_service::test_support`.
- **What stays in vta-service, and why:** the fixtures vta-service's own unit tests build on. A unit test compiles vta-service as its own crate, so it cannot take a fixture from a crate that depends on vta-service without getting a second, incompatible copy of every type.
- **No one-release re-export in vta-service.** The brief asked for one, but vta-service re-exporting a crate that depends on vta-service would be a dependency cycle. Consumers change `vta_service::test_support::MockVta` to `vta_test_support::MockVta`.
- The D6 tests read `TspSender` internals. Those hooks are now `#[doc(hidden)] pub`, only under the test-only `transport-harness` feature: `harness_*` twins of the `pub(crate)` originals, plus the former `cfg(test)` hooks.
- `vta-test-support` is **not** added to `semver-report.sh`'s exclusions. It has a real external consumer, the same reason `vta-service` is kept in that check.

## #2571: shared reject helpers
- The VTA's `trust_tasks::helpers` copies of `parse_payload`, `reject_with`, `reject_with_code`, `success_response`, `acknowledge`, `error_response`, `body_parse_error_response`, `framework_error_type_uri` and the `details` bound are now thin wrappers over `vti_trust_task_server::reject`. They only lift the shared outcome into the VTA's `TrustTaskOutcome`, which also carries `restart`. That field is why the shared functions are wrapped rather than re-exported directly.
- **One `app_error_to_reject`.** The VTA checks its one case of its own first (`ServiceError` 502/504 → `upstream_unavailable`), then falls through to the shared mapping.
  - A new test pins every `AppError` the VTA used to map to the same code and `details.reason` it had before.
  - `StepUpRequired`, `TrustTaskMissing`, `IdempotencyKeyConflict` and `ApprovalRequired` used to go out as `internalError` and now get the shared mapping. As the issue says, the VTA constructs none of these today.
- The VTA's `details` shedding (`consentRequests` → `consentRequestsOmitted`, Keyring VTI-37) moved into the shared bound. **Behaviour change for the VTC:** an oversized consent annex is now shed rather than dropped whole.
- **Issue claim already fixed on main:** the shared mapper already handles `NoMatchingProtocol`.
- **Spine::receive: not adopted.** The VTA's pipeline needs things the shared spine has no place for yet:
  - session-bound `AuthClaims`, including zero-authority ceremony and counterparty claims;
  - the PDP/DTTE consent gate and the operation budgets (VTI-TRN-029), in their order relative to the idempotency record;
  - `restart`, the `wire_v0_2` transforms, and the response-conformance gate.

  The reasons are recorded in the `trust_tasks/mod.rs` module docs, with what the shared pipeline would need first.

## #2572: shared plumbing
- **`vta_sdk::did_key::generate_did_key`** replaces both services' byte-identical `auth::credentials` (removed; the VTA's copy had no caller) and the SDK's private copy. `DidKeyError` gains `Csprng`; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Secrets defaults.** The `vti_secrets::config` defaults are now `pub`, and the VTA wizard and the VTC's `[secrets]` use them.
  - The VTC keeps `keyring_service = "vtc"` and `k8s_secret_key = "secret"`. They differ from the VTA's on purpose, so `#[serde(flatten)]` of `vti_secrets::SecretsConfig` would have changed the VTC's defaults and was not done.
- **`JwtKeys::from_base64_seed`** in vti-common replaces both `decode_jwt_key`s. `vta-backup`'s variant only validates bytes for a backup and returns `Validation`, so it stays.
- **`vti_common::runtime::shutdown_signal`** replaces the copies in vta-service, vtc-service, vti-witness and vti-voting-service.
  - It no longer panics, and no longer returns at once, when a signal handler cannot be installed; it logs and watches the other signal.
  - `vti-mcp-common` keeps its own copy, because that crate has no internal dependencies.
- **`epoch_to_rfc3339`:** both private copies now use `vta_sdk::protocols::auth::epoch_to_rfc3339`. **Wire format change:** VTA consent grants and VTC `acl/*` entries render `…Z` instead of `…+00:00`. Both are RFC 3339.
- **Shared test fixtures:** `init_jwt_provider` and `build_offline_atm` are in `vti_common::test_support` (feature `test-support`), re-exported by both services.
- **Not done:** `send_trust_ping` (the bodies differ in key loading), and the backup-crypto and status-list pairs the issue left unchecked. The status-list pair is remediation-plan D2.

## Checks
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`, `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`, and the two `--doc` runs.

Notes:
- `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features` already fails on main (`app_state` and `restore` are unresolved). This PR does not touch that.
- vta-service built with only `test-support,rest,didcomm` (what `vta-test-support` takes) had three dead-code warnings: `webs_store::did_key`, `WebsTarget`'s fields, and the collector's TSP-only `profile`. CI's `-D warnings` VTC job hit them once vtc-service reached vta-service through `vta-test-support`. They are now gated on `webs` / `tsp`.
- The moves left unused dependencies, which `cargo machete` found and which are removed: vta-service's `jsonwebtoken` and `trust-tasks-https`, vtc-service's `vta-service` dev-dependency, and `vta-test-support`'s `tracing`.

title: refactor(vta)!: decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing (#2730)
body:
refactor(vta)!: decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing (#2730)

* refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis (#2566)

Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them,
and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so
vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer
or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to
~935 unique lines.

The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host
half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which
verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so,
and why it costs nothing new.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta): split keys, room_groups and pnm rooms into module directories (#2569)

In-crate module splits, no behaviour change; mod.rs re-exports every
submodule so call sites are unchanged.

- operations/keys/{records,gates,secret,sign}.rs: record CRUD, the
  capability gates other modules import (ensure_may_*,
  require_key_nameable), secret release, and the signing oracle, each
  with its tests; the shared fixtures in keys/test_support.rs.
- operations/room_groups/{join,custody,open,advance,migrate,personal}.rs,
  each existing test module moved beside the code it covers.
- vta-cli-common commands/rooms/{records,watch,admin,files,owner,offers,
  memberships}.rs, the act/present plumbing staying in mod.rs.

The key-custody census pins raw seed access per file, so its single
keys.rs entry becomes three (records 3, secret 2, sign 1 — the same six
sites). The json census now walks module directories, so splitting
rooms.rs does not take its handlers out of the census; the personal-label
reader census names room_groups/personal.rs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta)!: move MockVta into a vta-test-support crate (#2570)

`vta_service::test_support` had grown to 4.5k lines inside the published
library. MockVta, the stub DID hosting service and the transport harness
(with their tests, and the mock_vta / vault_release_didcomm integration
tests) move to a new published crate, `vta-test-support`, which depends
on vta-service and re-exports its `test_support` fixtures.

The rest of `test_support` stays: vta-service's own unit tests build on
it, and a unit test cannot take a fixture from a crate that depends on
the crate under test without a second, incompatible copy of every type.
For the same reason vta-service cannot re-export the new crate (that
would be a dependency cycle), so this is a clean move rather than a
one-release shim: consumers switch `vta_service::test_support::MockVta`
to `vta_test_support::MockVta` (openvtc-core, the one external user).

The transport harness's D6 tests reach TspSender internals; those hooks
become `#[doc(hidden)] pub` under the test-only `transport-harness`
feature (`harness_*` twins for the production pub(crate) methods), and
`supersede_webvh_keys_for_version` wraps the crate-private webvh helper.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta): answer Trust Tasks through the shared reject helpers (#2571)

The VTA's trust_tasks::helpers held a second copy of
vti_trust_task_server::reject (parse_payload, app_error_to_reject,
reject_with, reject_with_code, success_response, acknowledge,
error_response, framework_error_type_uri, body_parse_error_response,
the details bound). They are now thin wrappers that lift the shared
outcome into the VTA's TrustTaskOutcome (which also carries restart).

The two app_error_to_reject mappings merge: the VTA checks its one case
of its own first (ServiceError 502/504 -> taskFailed
upstream_unavailable) and falls through to the shared mapping. A test
holds every AppError the VTA mapped to the code and details.reason it
had; StepUpRequired, TrustTaskMissing, IdempotencyKeyConflict and
ApprovalRequired, which the VTA's copy sent out as internalError, now
get the shared mapping (permissionDenied, malformedRequest,
taskFailed/conflict, taskFailed/<code>). The VTA does not construct any
of the four today.

The VTA's details shedding (consentRequests -> consentRequestsOmitted,
Keyring VTI-37) moves into the shared bound, so the VTC sheds too
instead of dropping a consent annex whole.

The VTA spine does not adopt Spine::receive: its session-bound claims,
PDP/consent gate, operation budgets, idempotency record, restart and
wire_v0_2 transforms have no place in the shared pipeline yet. The
reasons are recorded in trust_tasks/mod.rs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta)!: one copy of the service plumbing the VTA and VTC shared (#2572)

- did:key minting: vta_sdk::did_key::generate_did_key (OS CSPRNG,
  (did, private_key_multibase, signing_key)) replaces the byte-identical
  auth::credentials modules of vta-service and vtc-service (removed;
  the VTA's had no caller) and the SDK's private copy in session.rs.
  DidKeyError gains Csprng (the enum is non_exhaustive).
- Secrets defaults: vti_secrets::config's serde defaults are public, and
  the VTA setup wizard and the VTC's [secrets] use them. The VTC keeps
  its own keyring_service ("vtc") and k8s_secret_key ("secret"), which
  differ from the VTA's on purpose, so its SecretsConfig is not
  flattened into vti_secrets'.
- JwtKeys::from_base64_seed in vti-common replaces both services'
  decode_jwt_key (vta-backup's, which only validates bytes for a backup
  and answers Validation, stays).
- vti_common::runtime::shutdown_signal replaces the copies in vta-service,
  vtc-service, vti-witness and vti-voting-service. It no longer panics
  when a handler cannot be installed, and never resolves on a failed
  Ctrl-C handler: it logs and watches the other signal. vti-mcp-common
  keeps its own (it has no internal dependencies).
- epoch_to_rfc3339: both private copies use
  vta_sdk::protocols::auth::epoch_to_rfc3339. Wire change, format only:
  the VTA's consent grants and the VTC's acl/* entries now render
  timestamps as 2023-11-14T22:13:20Z rather than +00:00 (both RFC 3339).
- init_jwt_provider and build_offline_atm move to vti_common::test_support
  (feature test-support), re-exported from both services' test_support.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Updates `wrangler` from 4.157.0 to 4.160.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.160.0

Minor Changes

  • #16760 cb9534f Thanks @​petebacondarwin! - Support forwarded Wrangler development server options in the experimental cf-wrangler delegate

    cf dev can now forward options such as --inspector-port 9229, --ip, --var, and --persist-to to the Wrangler development runtime. The delegate reuses Wrangler's dev option definitions and validation while retaining project config discovery, --mode environment selection, local development, and its .cloudflare/state default. Invalid option combinations produce a single-line usage error and exit code 2 before starting the server.

    Place server options that overlap cf's global options after --, for example cf dev -- --local --persist-to "custom state". Config and script overrides, whole-worker remote development, and Wrangler's global options remain unsupported.

  • #16739 6af492e Thanks @​GregBrimble! - Add custom Cloudflare API headers through CLOUDFLARE_API_HEADERS

    Set CLOUDFLARE_API_HEADERS to a JSON object such as {"X-Custom-Header":"value"} to add headers to Cloudflare API requests. Custom headers override existing unprotected request headers, body and transport headers are protected, and header values outside the diagnostic allowlist remain redacted regardless of log sanitization settings.

Patch Changes

  • #16810 cdc970b Thanks @​dependabot! - Update DEFAULT_COMPAT_DATE to 2026-11-10

    Use the bundled workerd release's compatibility date by default when scaffolding new projects or when no compatibility date is configured.

  • #16810 cdc970b Thanks @​dependabot! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

    The following dependency versions have been updated:

    Dependency From To
    @​cloudflare/workers-types ^5.20261109.1 ^5.20261110.1
    workerd 1.20261109.1 1.20261110.1

  • #16709 022ee9d Thanks @​petebacondarwin! - Keep local Container images available for upload retries

    Keep prebuilt local image tags available until the caller finishes uploading the Worker and deploying its Container applications, so a later failure can be retried without rebuilding. When image push commands request cleanup, remove the source tag only after the push succeeds.

  • #16740 44b39b0 Thanks @​GregBrimble! - Redact header values outside a safe diagnostic allowlist, regardless of log sanitization settings.

    Apply the same filtering to request, response, and request-options diagnostics. Strip X-Auth-Key alongside Authorization when forwarding local artifact Git requests.

  • #16758 325dc69 Thanks @​petebacondarwin! - Fix JavaScript configuration parsing for Svelte projects using object spread

    Use a parser that supports object spread when updating JavaScript configuration files. This prevents configuration failures for Svelte projects using Drizzle or Better Auth and other framework configurations containing modern JavaScript syntax.

    Vite autoconfiguration reports a configuration error when an object spread, computed property, or accessor after the plugins array could override the Cloudflare plugin. Place the effective plugins array after these properties before retrying autoconfiguration.

title: refactor(rooms)!: share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine
body:
Three structural refactors of the rooms hosts and the host services' receive paths, one commit (or two) per issue.

## #2575 — one `rooms/*` handler layer for both hosts (`vti-rooms-host`)

The handler layer was implemented twice: room-host's hand `match` over `TrustTask<Value>` plus a hand-kept `is_consequential` list, and the VTC's typed `AsyncDispatcher`, kept in step by parity tests named after the other host. Re-verified against current main (after #2712 and #2727): still true, about 3.5k lines of non-test handler code on each side.

- **New crate `vti-rooms-host`** (published, because `vtc-service` is). It holds every handler body and one `AsyncDispatcher`. `served_uris` and `is_consequential` are both read off the registrations: a handler is registered with `.read()` or `.write()`, so the read/write split is declared where the task is.
- **`RoomHost`**, an object-safe async trait, is what each host lends the handlers:
  - its keyspaces, file host, watches and the verifier's resolver;
  - `host_limits`, which `rooms/info/0.5` advertises;
  - `refuses_rewrites_by_others`;
  - `charge`, which is the VTC's `charged(..)` / `admit_room`;
  - `register`, which is the VTC's `govern_creation` plus the write, or room-host's creator rules and ceilings held under one lock across the write;
  - `owner_changed`;
  - `audit`.
- **The per-host differences are unchanged:**

  | | VTC | room-host |
  |---|---|---|
  | Record document limit (`rooms/info/0.5`) | 64 KiB | its body cap |
  | Registration | the `rooms` policy | creator list and ceilings |
  | Charging | per-room charge | none |
  | Audit | hash-chained trail | `tracing` |
- **What stays in each host:** `vtc-service/src/rooms/handlers.rs` is now only the VTC's `RoomHost`; `room-host/src/lib.rs` keeps its `RoomHost`, receive path and state. Both pass the shared dispatcher the signer their spine proved.
- **New-crate checklist:**
  - workspace `members` and `default-members`;
  - `Dockerfile.nitro` COPY;
  - `[lints] workspace = true`;
  - `scripts/check-docs.py --write` (crate map, plus the 37 of 48 count in the three documents that state it);
  - semver-report exclusion;
  - a row in the crate table and a README.
- **Docs:** `vtc-service-decomposition.md` now records the rooms extraction as done.

Two answers now agree where the hosts used to differ:
- A declared error code carries the `retryable` flag its specification declares. The VTC always sent `false`, even for codes declared `retryable: true`.
- room-host now answers a known task at a version it does not serve with `unsupportedVersion` and the versions it does serve, as the VTC already did, instead of `unsupportedType`.

Also: `rooms/signal-delay/set` and `rooms/records/retention/set` are checked against their generated type before anything else, as room-host already did. The five tasks in #2581 accept a spec-valid `ext`.

## #2576 — every host service's receive path on `vti_trust_task_server::Spine`

- **room-host:** `dispatch_received`, its hand-written size, freshness, `validate_basic` and accepted-id claim/settle, is replaced by `Spine`:
  - `SpecPolicySource` is `vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for`.
  - A `SizeGate` holds each task to its declared `maxDocumentBytes`.
  - The proof is verified once, over the document as received, and bound to `issuer`.
  - DIDComm and TSP frames carry their authenticated sender, and the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093).
  - The duplicate-id record is `StoreAcceptedIds` (VTI-OPS-025 … 029).
  - A host without a DID still refuses an expired document: `before_proof` applies the expiry check that the skipped recipient binding would have.
- **vti-voting-service:**
  - Spec policy from `spec_policy_for`.
  - `needs_proof`, `from_slug`/`slug` and the versions table are deleted. One `SERVED` table names each version by its generated payload's `TYPE_URI`, and a test holds it equal to the pinned `voting/*` set.
  - The duplicate-id record is `StoreAcceptedIds` in `<data_dir>/store`.
  - The did:key cast rule, the issuer-is-sender check and the served-type check are in `SpineHooks::before_proof`.
  - The HTTPS door's resolver selection and the verification deadline (answered `unavailable`) are a per-request `ProofVerifier`.
  - An answer that cannot be signed is still not sent.
- **vti-witness:** `src/replay.rs` is deleted in favour of `StoreAcceptedIds`; its stated reason was stale, because the type moved to `vti-trust-task-server`. `dispatch.rs`'s own steps 3 to 8 are now the Spine's.
- **`vti-trust-task-server`**, both changes additive and non-breaking:
  - `ProofVerifier::refusal` is a new provided method, so a verifier can answer `proofInvalid` or `unavailable` instead of `permissionDenied`.
  - `Spine::accepting_unsigned_optional_over_messaging()` is a new opt-in.

**One claim in the issue is wrong:** "`VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` is never applied" in the voting service. Main applied it through `within_window` for communities' and trustees' requests. That rule is kept: casts and reads are exempt, community and trustee requests get the window.

### Behaviour changes
- **room-host:**
  - A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now `proofInvalid`, as at the VTC, instead of `permissionDenied`.
  - An internal error's message is opaque.
  - `notFound` and `conflict` carry `details.reason`.
  - A body over its declared size, or one that is not a document, gets the spine's unrouted refusal.
- **Voting:**
  - HTTP statuses follow the HTTPS binding's table: `proofRequired`, `proofInvalid`, `expired` and `unsupportedVersion` are 422.
  - The same document resent is answered with its first answer, so a cast resent under the same id gets its original `counted` receipt. A replayed read gets `204`. Replays of close, cancel, register and the trustee steps are absorbed by the record instead of reaching the ballot box. The same cast in a new document still gets `alreadyCounted` from the ballot box.
  - A signed document over messaging must be signed by its sender.
  - The body cap is 2 MiB, axum's previous default.
- **Witness:**
  - One record shared by every identity, discovery included.
  - The body cap is 1 MiB.
  - Accepted-id rows from before the upgrade are ignored and swept once they expire. A document accepted in the minutes before the upgrade could therefore run again if redelivered after it; this is a narrow window.

### Spec questions — Appendix F (dtgwg-vti-spec), not edited here
- **Casts outside the acceptance window:** VTI-OPS-024 against VTI-VOT-003/004. This is existing behaviour, now documented: a cast still needs `issuedAt` and may not be future-dated, but has no age limit, so a voter's agent can resend it until voting closes. Voting reads have no age limit either. If VTI-OPS-024 applies to every document, both **need an Appendix F entry**. The voting client sets a cast's `expiresAt` to voting close, which bounds it either way.
- **The anonymous HTTPS cast door (VTI-VOT-004):** unchanged.
- **Follow-up, not changed here:** by default the Spine refuses every unsigned document over DIDComm/TSP, proof-optional ones included. The VTA reads VTI-OPS-021 the same way (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`). The new opt-in exists for a service that wants unsigned public reads over messaging. Whether the default and the VTA agree with the spec deserves its own issue.

## #2581 — `vti_rooms::wire`

- The five literal Type URIs (`rooms/epoch/{mint,commits}`, `rooms/owner/{transfer,claim}`, `rooms/records/curate`, all 0.1) are now `<generated Payload>::TYPE_URI`.
- **Split, for the requests:** every `rooms/*` request is received and dispatched as its generated payload type. The five hand-written bodies that implemented `trust_tasks_rs::Payload` no longer do (**breaking**: the five impls are removed from `vti-rooms`). The hand-written structs are only the host's reading of a payload the generated type has already accepted.
- **Exemption, for the rest:** storage records, the host's reading of a request, and response bodies stay hand-written because a host also stores them. The exemption is recorded in root CLAUDE.md with its obligation, and the `wire.rs` header now says the same.
- **Census:** `vti-rooms/tests/wire_census.rs` fails on any serde `pub struct` in `wire.rs` that `schema_conformance.rs` does not name. All of them are covered today. `CreateRoomTerms` derives no serde and is not a wire type.

## Checks run
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs,voting`
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`
- `cargo check -p vti-rooms-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- `python3 scripts/check-docs.py`, `scripts/check-nitro-copies-every-member.py`, `scripts/check-workspace-version-reqs.py`

Rebased onto origin/main after #2728 (VTC architecture) merged. The VTC's `RoomHost` writes its audit rows through `vtc_audit`. Both test suites were re-run on the rebased tree.

In the vtc-service runs (both feature sets), the only failures are the 12 admin-UI bundle tests (`admin_ui::tests::*`, plus the portal and console serving tests in `routing_modes`, `member_portal` and `member_portal_oob`). These fail whenever `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` is set, which skips the npm build, and are unrelated to this change. Everything else passes.

Closes #2575
Closes #2576
Closes #2581

title: refactor(rooms)!: share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine (#2731)
body:
refactor(rooms)!: share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine (#2731)

* refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine

room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness,
validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step
and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared
Spine the VTC runs (#2576): the size gate holds each task to its declared
maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from
vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over
the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames
carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093),
and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029).

A host without a DID still refuses an expired document: the spine skips
the recipient binding then, so before_proof applies the expiry check.
A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now proofInvalid, as at
the VTC, rather than permissionDenied.

Refs #2576

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(rooms): one rooms/* handler layer for both hosts (vti-rooms-host)

The rooms/* handler layer was implemented twice — room-host's hand
match over TrustTask<Value> plus a hand list for is_consequential, and
the VTC's typed AsyncDispatcher — held in step by parity tests named
after the other host (#2575). Both now run vti-rooms-host: one
AsyncDispatcher whose served_uris and is_consequential are read off the
registrations, over a small object-safe RoomHost trait (keyspaces, the
verifier's resolver, audit sink, charge hook, registration governance,
host limits).

Each host keeps what is its own: the VTC governs registration with its
rooms policy, charges each authorized operation to the presenter's
budget and writes its hash-chained audit trail, and advertises its
64 KiB record document limit; room-host holds its creator list and
ceilings under one lock across the write, logs its trail and
advertises its body cap. Both receive through their own Spine and hand
the shared dispatcher the proven signer.

Two answers now agree where the hosts differed: a declared error code
carries the retryable flag its specification declares (the VTC sent
false), and room-host answers a known task at an unserved version
unsupportedVersion naming the versions it serves, as the VTC did.

Refs #2575

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(voting-service): receive every document through the shared Spine (#2576)

The voting service's dispatcher re-implemented the Trust Task receive
pipeline by hand: a `needs_proof` list beside the pinned specifications, a
slug table written twice and versions a third time, and no duplicate-id
record (VTI-OPS-025 … 029). It now runs `vti_trust_task_server::Spine`:

- each task's proof / recipient / issuedAt requirement comes from its
  pinned specification (`vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for`); the
  routing table names each served version by its generated payload type,
  held equal to the pinned `voting/*` set by a test; slugs are read off the
  Type URI.
- the duplicate-id record is `StoreAcceptedIds` in `<data_dir>/store`
  (`accepted_ids`), swept on a timer. A redelivered document is answered
  with its first answer (a cast's receipt included); a replayed read with
  204; a resend of the same cast in a new document still reaches the
  ballot box, which answers `alreadyCounted`.
- the service's own rules are pieces handed to the pipeline: `Gate`
  (issuer = transport sender, served type, a cast signed by a did:key,
  VTI-VOT-003), `Verifier` (which DIDs are resolved on which binding, a
  15 s verification deadline answered `unavailable`), `freshness_for`
  (VTI-OPS-024's window for a community's or trustee's request; none for a
  cast, which may be resent until voting closes, VTI-VOT-004, nor a read).
- refusal statuses follow the HTTPS binding's table: `proofRequired`,
  `proofInvalid`, `expired` and `unsupportedVersion` are 422 (were 401,
  400 and 404).

vti-trust-task-server, additive only:
- `ProofVerifier::refusal`, a provided method (default
  `app_error_to_reject`), so a verifier can answer `proofInvalid` or
  `unavailable` rather than `permissionDenied`.
- `Spine::accepting_unsigned_optional_over_messaging`: over DIDComm and
  TSP, run a document with no proof anonymously when its specification
  makes the proof OPTIONAL, as HTTPS does (VTI-OPS-021). Off by default.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(witness): receive through the shared Spine; drop the hand-written replay record (#2576)

`src/replay.rs` was the witness's own accepted-id store, kept because "the
VTC's `accepted_ids` is not reusable from this crate" — no longer true:
it moved to `vti_trust_task_server::StoreAcceptedIds` for exactly that
reason. The witness now uses it, and runs its hand-written steps 3 – 9
through `vti_trust_task_server::Spine`:

- `Gate` (`SpineHooks::before_proof`): the in-band issuer against the
  transport-proven sender, and routing, before any proof is read; the
  spec policy is asked only for a served type, so an unserved one is
  still `unsupportedType`, never `proofRequired`.
- `Verifier`: a proof that does not verify is `proofInvalid`.
- `ReplySigner`: every reply, the pipeline's refusals included, is
  addressed from this identity to the proven sender and signed with the
  identity's own key; a reply that cannot be signed is not sent.
- the routing table reads the document's bytes as received, so a session
  document is still kept verbatim for the VWC's task digest.
- discovery is asked unsigned over messaging, its proof OPTIONAL
  (`accepting_unsigned_optional_over_messaging`, VTI-OPS-021).

The record is now shared by every identity of the service (a document `id`
is its producer's), and discovery is recorded too, so its redelivery is
answered with the first reply. `WitnessStore::sweep` also drops the old
record's `did:`-prefixed rows once their retention passes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(rooms)!: receive every rooms/* request as its generated type

vti_rooms::wire hand-wrote the request bodies of five tasks and made
them the dispatched payload types (impl Payload), with their Type URIs
as literals, and its header said the root rule against hand-written
wire types was deliberately not followed (#2581).

- The five Type URIs (epoch/mint, epoch/commits, owner/transfer,
  owner/claim, records/curate, all 0.1) are now each generated
  payload's TYPE_URI.
- vti-rooms-host dispatches those five on their generated payload types,
  as it already did every other task; the hand-written bodies are only
  the host's reading of a payload the generated type accepted. Nothing
  in wire.rs implements trust_tasks_rs::Payload any more (breaking: the
  five impls are removed).
- What stays hand-written — storage records, a host's reading of an
  accepted request, response bodies — is recorded as the one exemption
  in root CLAUDE.md, with its obligation: every serde type in wire.rs
  is validated against the published schema in schema_conformance.rs,
  and the new tests/wire_census.rs fails on one that is not named
  there.

Also regenerates the root crate map for the voting service's and the
witness's new vti-trust-task-server dependency.

Closes #2581

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(e2e): give the ballot box in voting_trustees its duplicate-id record

AppState::new takes the accepted-id keyspace since the voting service
moved onto the shared Spine (#2576); the e2e harness built one with the
old four arguments.

Refs #2576

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): give the in-process ballot boxes their duplicate-id record

AppState::new takes the accepted-id keyspace since the voting service
moved onto the shared Spine (#2576); the election tests under
--features voting built theirs with the old four arguments.

Refs #2576

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(room-host): drop trust-tasks-https, unused since the Spine port

Refs #2576

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: refactor(vtc)!: vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor
body:
Five structural refactors from the vtc-service decomposition plan (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-service-decomposition.md`, #2725), one commit each, in the order the plan gives (#2568 → #2577 → #2578 → #2579 → #2580). No behaviour change is intended. The full vtc-service suite passes with default features and with `--features vetting-pcs,voting`. So do the census tests (spec pin, response conformance, secret-Debug, generated wire types) and clippy on the pinned 1.95 toolchain.

## #2568 — `AuditEvent` out of `vti-common` into a new leaf crate `vtc-audit`

- **What stays in `vti-common`:** the envelope, the hash chain, HMAC actor hashing, the key store, checkpoints and the writer. They are now generic over the event payload: `AuditEnvelope<E>`, `AuditWriter<E>`, `verify_chain<E>`, `ChainVerifier::push<E>`.
- **New crate `vtc-audit`** (depends only on `vti-common`):
  - holds `AuditEvent` and its data structs, moved with `git mv`;
  - provides the `AuditEnvelope` / `AuditWriter` aliases and re-exports the rest of `vti_common::audit`;
  - vtc-service now imports `vtc_audit::` everywhere it used `vti_common::audit::`.
- **`VtaOperation` moved to `vta-audit`:** it is now `VtaAuditEvent::VtaOperation`, with `VtaAuditEnvelope` and `VtaAuditWriter`.
- **Stored chains still verify.** The serialized `type` / `data` tags are byte-identical. `vtc-audit/tests/stored_chain.rs` and `vta-audit/tests/stored_chain.rs` hold chains written by `main` at 792db16a5, before the move. The tests check that those chains verify, re-serialize byte for byte, keep their storage keys, and keep their HMAC actor hashes.
- **New-crate checklist done:**
  - `members` and `default-members`, `Dockerfile.nitro` COPY;
  - crate map, table row and the "37 of 48" counts (`check-docs.py` passes);
  - `publish = true`, added to semver-report `EXCLUDED`, `[lints] workspace = true`;
  - `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` in the crate.
- **"Not checked" in the issue, now checked:** envelope verification does not match on any variant. The chain commits to the payload's `serde_json` encoding only, and chain-head recovery deserializes into each service's own vocabulary, as before.

## #2577 — one bounded regorus engine

- `vti_common::policy_engine` sits behind a new `policy` feature, with regorus as an optional dependency. It holds:
  - the three limits;
  - `CompiledPolicy<Id>`, generic over the id (`Uuid` at the VTC, `String` at the VTA);
  - `compile` and the bounded `evaluate`;
  - the engine tests, now in one place.
- vta-policy keeps `DECISION_QUERY` and `evaluate_decision`.
- vtc-service keeps `validate_purpose_package` and its `Uuid`-keyed `compile`. The paths `crate::policy::engine::*` still resolve.
- **"Not checked" in the issue, now checked:** the two `evaluate` bodies had not diverged below the constants.

## #2578 — typed errors at the source, no message-substring matching

| Site | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/schemas/accepts/register` | `starts_with("invalid DCQL query")` | `AcceptsQueryError::{InvalidQuery, UncheckableTrustedAuthorities, UnregisteredType, Store}` |
| `vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore}` | `contains("terminal")` | `LifecycleError::Terminal`, carried through `LifecycleRecordError` |
| Registry deletes | `contains("registry/record/delete:notFound")` on a formatted string | the reply's `code` compared with the declared `registry/record/delete` `NOT_FOUND` (0.1 and 0.2) |
| git-ns projection | `contains("still paginating")` | `RegistryError::PaginationExhausted` (retriable, same wording) |
| Community-room renewal | `contains("ermission") \|\| contains("orbidden")` | the framework's `StandardCode::PermissionDenied` |

- **Design choice, conservative:** the issue suggested `RegistryError::Rejected { code, message }`. Instead, the `notFound` check now reads the reply document's `code` before it is classified. That gets the same typed match without reshaping every `Permanent` arm.
- **Kept on purpose:** an uncheckable `trusted_authorities` is still answered `unregisteredType`, as it always was. Register 0.x declares no code of its own for it.
- **"Not checked" in the issue, now checked:** the vta-sdk side has the same pattern in `agent_session.rs:408` (`alreadyRegistered`), `provision_client/runner_didcomm.rs:619` (`401`/`403`) and `didcomm_session.rs:789` (`timed out`). Those are outside this issue set and are not changed here.

## #2579 — split `trust_tasks/mod.rs` (partial)

- **Pure move, bodies unchanged:**
  - `join_tasks.rs`, `vetting_tasks.rs`, `hidden_vetting_tasks.rs`, `member_admin_tasks.rs`, `config_tasks.rs`, `step_up_response_tasks.rs` and `personhood_tasks.rs`, each with its test modules;
  - `spine_proof_tests.rs`;
  - `test_fixtures.rs`, holding the signed-document fixtures (`seed_acl`, `signed`, `dispatch`, …) that nine test modules imported from inside `members_admin_tests`.
  - `mod.rs` goes from 9,089 lines to about 2,600.
- **Routing:** the 32 identical `uri if X::URIS.contains(&uri)` arms are now one arm over a `FAMILIES` table. Routing order is unchanged. `no_two_families_serve_one_uri` holds that table order can never decide which family answers.
- **Not done, deliberately:** converting each family's `URIS` + `match` to typed `AsyncDispatcher` registration. It rewrites every handler's entry: typed downcast, spec-policy enforcement and version routing all move into the framework. That is a behaviour change, not a move, and #2574 changes the same bodies.
- **Also not done:** merging the other two `seed_acl` variants (`git_ns/tests.rs`, `acl/console_key.rs`), which have different signatures.
- **"Not checked" in the issue, now checked:** `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri` already pins `DISPATCHED_URIS` to the router.

## #2580 — `AdminActor`

- **The type:** `acl::AdminActor { did, entry, via_console_key }`. It is built only by resolving an administrator's live entry, and exposes `can()` / `require()` and nothing role-shaped.
- **Who uses it:**
  - `admin_signer`, `capable_signer` and `admin_with` return it;
  - about thirty admin helpers and operations take it instead of the synthetic `AuthClaims`.
- **No second reads:**
  - `capable_signer` asks the entry that was already loaded;
  - `members/list` and `join-requests/list` no longer resolve the signer twice;
  - backup asks the actor instead of re-reading the entry.
- **Member and session paths:**
  - `member_signer` returns `MemberSigner { did }`;
  - the session tasks take the DID;
  - `ceremony::role_change_as` is the session-less door, and it reads "not elevated" exactly where the session-less claims did.
- **One documented exception:** `vti_common::backup_transfer::chunked`, which is shared with the VTA, calls `require_super_admin()`. `backup_tasks::chunked_caller` builds that one claim after the VTC's capability check, and it goes nowhere else.
- **Root CLAUDE.md** now says signed admin documents resolve to `AdminActor`, and that VTC code must never be handed administrator `AuthClaims`.
- **"Not checked" in the issue, now checked:** the cookie and bearer extractors in `routes/auth.rs` and `member_portal` keep session claims, which is legitimate.

## Breaking (marked `!`)

- `vti_common::audit::event` and `AuditEvent` are gone; `AuditEnvelope` and `AuditWriter` take the event type as a parameter.
- `vta_policy::engine::CompiledPolicy` is an alias, and `id()` returns `&String`.
- vtc-service: the new `RegistryError` variant, typed lifecycle / accepts errors, and `AdminActor` in public operation signatures.

Closes #2568
Closes #2577
Closes #2578
Refs #2579 — what remains is per-family `AsyncDispatcher` registration (and merging the other two `seed_acl` variants)
Closes #2580

title: refactor(vtc)!: vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor (#2728)
body:
refactor(vtc)!: vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor (#2728)

* refactor(vti-common)!: move the VTC's audit-event vocabulary to a new vtc-audit leaf crate

vti_common::audit::AuditEvent was almost entirely the community's product
vocabulary, living in the layer-0 crate every VTA subsystem and the enclave
depend on; the VTA used one variant. Every VTC feature that added an event
republished vti-common (#2568).

- vti-common keeps the node-neutral half: the envelope, the hash chain, the
  HMAC actor hashing, the audit-key store, checkpoints and the writer, now
  generic over the event payload (`AuditEnvelope<E>`, `AuditWriter<E>`,
  `verify_chain<E>`, `ChainVerifier::push<E>`). Its own tests bring a
  one-variant stand-in vocabulary.
- New leaf crate `vtc-audit` (depends only on vti-common): `AuditEvent` and
  its data structs, moved with git history, plus `AuditEnvelope` /
  `AuditWriter` aliases and re-exports of the rest of `vti_common::audit`.
  vtc-service names `vtc_audit::` where it named `vti_common::audit::`.
  Published (vtc-service is), excluded from the semver report like the VTA
  subsystem crates, workspace members + default-members, Dockerfile.nitro,
  crate map and counts.
- `VtaOperation` moves to `vta-audit` as `VtaAuditEvent::VtaOperation`
  (`VtaAuditEnvelope`, `VtaAuditWriter`).

Serialized `type` / `data` tags are unchanged, so stored chains still verify:
`vtc-audit/tests/stored_chain.rs` and `vta-audit/tests/stored_chain.rs` hold
chains written by main at 792db16a5 (before the move) and check they verify,
re-serialize byte for byte, keep their storage keys and actor hashes.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vti_common::audit::event` and `AuditEvent` are gone
(`vtc_audit::AuditEvent`, `vta_audit::VtaAuditEvent`); `AuditEnvelope` and
`AuditWriter` take the event type as a parameter.

Closes #2568

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-policy,vtc-service)!: one bounded regorus engine in vti-common (feature `policy`)

vta-policy and vtc-service each carried a copy of the regorus wrapper — the
same three limits (250 ms CPU budget, 1000-unit check interval, 256 KiB input
cap), POLICY_MODULE_PATH, CompiledPolicy with the same Debug impl, compile,
and the bounded evaluate (#2577). The VTC copy guards an unauthenticated path
(join submit), and a tightening applied to one copy silently skipped the
other. Below the constants the two `evaluate` bodies had not diverged: the
VTA's differed only in querying its fixed decision rule and decoding the
result.

- `vti_common::policy_engine` (new feature `policy`, regorus optional): the
  limits, `CompiledPolicy<Id>` (generic over the id: `Uuid` at the VTC,
  `String` at the VTA), `compile` and the bounded `evaluate`, with the engine
  tests (bounds, errors, hashing) moved there once.
- vta-policy keeps `DECISION_QUERY` and `evaluate_decision` (the
  PolicyInput / PolicyDecision mapping) over the shared `evaluate`.
- vtc-service keeps `validate_purpose_package` and the Uuid-keyed
  `compile`; `crate::policy::engine::{compile, evaluate, CompiledPolicy}`
  still resolve for every caller.

Behaviour is unchanged: same limits, same error variants and messages.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_policy::engine::CompiledPolicy` is now an alias of
`vti_common::policy_engine::CompiledPolicy<String>`; `id()` returns `&String`.

Closes #2577

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service)!: type the errors Trust Task codes are chosen from, at their source

Five places chose a wire error code, or decided a delete had succeeded, by
reading the words of an error message (#2578). Rewording a message would have
changed a declared code or turned an idempotent delete into a permanent job
failure, with no test or type to notice. Each now matches on a type:

- `schemas::accepts::validate_accepts_query` returns `AcceptsQueryError`
  (`InvalidQuery`, `UncheckableTrustedAuthorities`, `UnregisteredType`,
  `Store`); `vtc/schemas/accepts/register` picks `invalidQuery` /
  `unregisteredType` from the variant instead of `starts_with("invalid DCQL
  query")`. An uncheckable `trusted_authorities` keeps the unregistered-type
  code it has always been answered with (the specification names none).
- `LifecycleLog::record` returns `LifecycleError` (`OutOfOrder`, `Terminal`,
  `AlreadySuspended`, `NotSuspended`); `record_lifecycle_event` /
  `record_lifecycle_as` return `LifecycleRecordError`, and
  `vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore}` answer `terminal` from the variant
  instead of `contains("terminal")`.
- The registry delete paths tolerate an absent record on the reply's `code`
  compared with the declared `registry/record/delete` `NOT_FOUND` (0.1 and
  0.2), not on `contains("registry/record/delete:notFound")` in a formatted
  string.
- `RegistryError::PaginationExhausted` (retriable, same wording as
  `Transient`) replaces `contains("still paginating")` in the git-ns
  projection.
- Community-room renewal compares the VTA's refusal code with the framework's
  `permissionDenied` instead of `contains("ermission") || contains("orbidden")`.

Every type converts into the `AppError` it used to be, message unchanged, so
callers that only propagate are untouched. Behaviour is unchanged.

BREAKING CHANGE: `RegistryError` gains `PaginationExhausted`; `LifecycleLog::record`,
`record_lifecycle_event` and `validate_accepts_query` return typed errors.

Closes #2578

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service): split trust_tasks/mod.rs into its handler groups; one routing table for the families

`trust_tasks/mod.rs` was 9,089 lines: the spine glue, the router, about
forty handlers and 4,600 lines of tests (#2579). A pure move, bodies
unchanged:

- join_tasks.rs — submit, manifest, status, supplement, withdraw, self-leave,
  decide (+ join_discovery_tests, join_decide_profile_tests)
- vetting_tasks.rs — statement withdrawal, vetter grant and profiles
  (+ vetter_grant_console_key_tests)
- hidden_vetting_tasks.rs — the `vetting-pcs` handlers
- member_admin_tasks.rs — members/{credentials,update,admin-remove,purge},
  members/vmc (+ members_admin_tests)
- config_tasks.rs — profile update, config export/import, DID hosting,
  endorsement types, backup export (+ config_pair_tests,
  endorsement_type_tests, backup_export_tests)
- step_up_response_tasks.rs, personhood_tasks.rs
- spine_proof_tests.rs — the spine's proof tests, as a file
- test_fixtures.rs — the signed-document fixtures (`seed_acl`, `signed`,
  `dispatch`, `error_code`, …) nine test modules imported from inside
  `members_admin_tests`, hoisted to one shared module.

mod.rs keeps the spine, `admin_signer` / `capable_signer` and the router, now
2,600 lines.

The 32 identical `uri if X::URIS.contains(&uri) => … unreachable!` arms are
one arm over a `FAMILIES` table (`family!(module)`), so adding a family is one
line, and `no_two_families_serve_one_uri` holds that the order the table is
asked in can never decide which family answers. Routing order relative to the
other arms is unchanged.

Not done here: converting each family's `URIS` + `match` to typed
`AsyncDispatcher` registration (as rooms and git-ns are). That rewrites every
handler's entry (typed downcast, spec-policy and version routing move into the
framework) and is behaviour, not a move; the decomposition note orders it after
the files move, with #2574 changing the same bodies.

Refs #2579

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service)!: authorize signed admin documents as an AdminActor, not synthetic super-admin claims

`admin_signer` / `capable_signer` returned a synthetic
`vti_common::auth::extractor::AuthClaims { role: Admin, allowed_contexts: [] }`.
A VTC entry holds no contexts, so every such value read as unscoped — a
super-admin — to the shared `vti_common` helpers: an `is_super_admin()` or
`require_super_admin()` on it compiled and passed for every administrator, an
`auditor` included. The rule that no VTC gate is a claims check was held by a
doc comment (#2580).

- `acl::AdminActor { did, entry, via_console_key }`, built only by resolving an
  administrator's live entry (`AdminActor::resolve`, the refusals
  `resolve_auth_role` gave), exposing `can()` / `require()` and nothing
  role-shaped. `admin_signer`, `capable_signer`, `admin_with` and every admin
  helper and operation they feed (about thirty signatures across
  `trust_tasks`, `routes`, `step_up_*`, `ceremony`, `admin_actions::queues`)
  take it instead of claims.
- `capable_signer` asks the entry `admin_signer` already read instead of
  reading it again, and `members/list` and `join-requests/list` no longer
  resolve the signer twice (`admin_with` then `capable_signer`); the backup
  family asks the actor rather than re-reading the entry.
- `member_signer` returns `acl::MemberSigner { did }`; the session tasks
  (`routes::auth::{list_sessions_for, revoke_sessions_task}`) take the DID.
- `ceremony::role_change_as` is the session-less door for an `AdminActor`
  (`members/update`); `role_change_via_pipeline` keeps the session for its
  bearer callers. Both read "not elevated" exactly where the session-less
  claims did.
- One synthetic claim remains, documented and built after the capability check:
  `vti_common::backup_transfer::chunked` (shared with the VTA) asks
  `require_super_admin` of its caller, so `backup_tasks::chunked_caller` hands
  it the administrator value it was always given.
- Root CLAUDE.md: signed administrative documents resolve to `AdminActor`; never
  hand VTC code administrator `AuthClaims`.

Behaviour is unchanged: the same refusals, worded alike
(`require_answers_as_require_capability_does` holds `require` to
`require_capability` for every capability).

BREAKING CHANGE: the public `ceremony` / `routes` operations that took
`&AuthClaims` for an administrator take `&acl::AdminActor`;
`routes::auth::{list_sessions_for, revoke_sessions_task}` take the actor's DID.

Closes #2580

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service): regenerate the console's OpenAPI document after the vtc-audit move

A `ConfigSource` doc comment now names `vtc_audit::ConfigSource` (#2568);
openapi.json and wire.ts carry it.

Refs #2568

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service): name AdminActor's console key by its DID

`via_console_key` read as key material to the secret-Debug census; the field
holds the console key's public `did:key`, so it is `console_did` (#2580).

* build(vta-policy): drop hex and sha2, unused since the engine moved to vti-common

Left behind by the shared regorus engine (#2577); cargo machete flags them.

title: feat(rooms)!: load older by version (records/list 0.8, keys/browse 0.6) and host limits in rooms/info 0.5
body:
Adopts the rooms versions merged upstream in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1289, which answer points 3 and 4 of #2294.

## Pins (`vti-specs-rooms`)

`trust-tasks -C vti-specs-rooms update` with the arrays extended, older versions kept pinned while they are still served or sent:

| Type URI | |
|---|---|
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/records/list/0.8` | beside 0.1 – 0.7 |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/keys/browse/0.6` | beside 0.3 – 0.5 |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/info/0.5` | beside 0.1 – 0.4 |

The registry had also changed some draft bundles in place (prose and the new `deprecation` notes). I kept those changes only for the three families above (their older versions now read "superseded by …"). I reverted the `rooms/records/put/0.1 – 0.5` and `rooms/keys/list/0.2` refreshes, which mark them superseded by put/0.6 and list/0.3. Adopting put/0.6 is separate work, and the refresh would have deprecated types across the workspace. `trust-tasks check` passes.

## Hosts (room-host and vtc-service, through `vti-rooms`)

- **`rooms/records/list/0.8`.** `beforeVersion` is an exclusive upper bound under either order. When `beforeVersion <= sinceVersion + 1` the page is empty, not an error. The read is `vti_rooms::storage::list_records_bounded`, a seek on the version index from #2712: newest first starts the scan below `min(cursor, beforeVersion)`, oldest first stops the walk at `beforeVersion`. A page costs the rows it returns.
- **Cursor binding.** A cursor is bound to `order`, `sinceVersion` and `beforeVersion`. The shape is 0.7's `v<N>`/`n<N>` with `s<since>` and `b<before>` appended. A listing with neither bound issues exactly 0.7's cursor. A cursor offered under any other order or bounds is the declared `invalidCursor` (`CursorError::OtherBounds`, a new variant of a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum). The cursor is checked in `record_tasks::list_v8_parts` before any read.
- **One read path for both hosts.** The two hosts each had their own `ListAt` enum and a three-way response match. Both are replaced by `vti_rooms::record_tasks::{ListAt, list_page, list_response}`, so the page a version reads and the schema it is answered under are chosen in one place. This is a step toward merging the two handler layers.
- **`rooms/info/0.5`.** `vti_rooms::signal_delay::info_v5` takes the host's own `HostLimits`:
  - The VTC states `maxRecordDocumentBytes: 65536`. That is its size gate's limit for `rooms/records/put` (no served put version declares `maxDocumentBytes`, so the spine default applies). It is below put/0.6's 2,097,152, so the spec says it MUST be stated.
  - Both hosts state `maxChunkSize: 262144`. Since #2515 an upload chunk is admitted at its own size on every transport, so this is the transfer ceiling.
  - room-host states no `maxRecordDocumentBytes`. Nothing in its dispatch refuses a record by size, and its HTTP body limit (axum's 2 MiB) equals the bound put/0.6 declares.
- **Older versions.** 0.4 and list/0.5 – 0.7 are still served. Their uses are now `#[allow(deprecated)]`.

## VTA: `rooms/keys/browse/0.6`

- `beforeVersion` is passed through to the host's `rooms/records/list/0.8`.
- At a host without list/0.8:
  - A browse naming `beforeVersion` is `hostRefused`, carrying the host's `unsupportedType`. It is never listed without the bound.
  - A browse naming none falls back to list/0.7, then 0.6, exactly as 0.5 does.
- A listing bounded by `beforeVersion` is never compared against `recordCount`.
- `nextCursor` is returned as in 0.5.
- Classified `RetrySafe` in `vta_sdk::retry_safety` (a read that stores nothing), listed in the operation budget's host-calling set, and given a conformance witness.
- Every declared code is asserted by a test (`hostRefused`, `hostUnreachable`, `notAMember`).

## SDK and clients

- **`VtaClient::room_browse`** sends browse/0.6. `RoomBrowse` gains `before_version` (breaking: a new field on a public struct, hence the `!`) and `needs_v0_6()`.
  - A VTA without 0.6 is asked browse/0.5, but only for a browse naming no `before_version`. The existing 0.4/0.3 fallback is unchanged.
  - The return type and `RoomListOrder` move to the browse/0.6 generated types. The response is the same shape as 0.5's.
- **`vtc_client::VtcClient::room_info`** asks info/0.5, then 0.4, then 0.3 on `unsupportedType`. `RoomInfoResponse` is now the 0.5 type, so callers see `max_record_document_bytes` and `max_chunk_size`.
- **pnm.** `pnm rooms list --newest --before-version N` and `pnm rooms read --newest --before-version N` load older from a version.
  - Each `--newest` page prints the page before it two ways: `--cursor` (repeating the page's `--prefix`, `--since-version` and `--before-version`, which the cursor is now bound to) and `--before-version <lowest version on the page>`.
  - Refusals name the command to run instead: a VTA without browse/0.6, or a host without list/0.8, gets the cursor command.

## Docs

`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`:
- the host limits paragraph (§5, next to the 64 KiB note);
- *Loading older from a version* (§9, after *Opening a conversation at its head*);
- §12 rows for `rooms/records/list/0.8`, `rooms/info/0.4` (missing before) and `rooms/info/0.5`, and browse 0.6 in the member-VTA table.

`vta-service/CLAUDE.md`'s *Room records* flow names the new invariants.

## Tests

- `vti-rooms` storage:
  - load older newest first, with no cursor kept;
  - oldest first bounded above;
  - the empty band;
  - cursor binding: other since or before → `OtherBounds`, other order → `OtherOrder`, malformed → `NotIssued`, unbounded → 0.7's shape.
- `vti-rooms` schema_conformance: the two new dispatched URIs.
- room-host end to end: list/0.8 load-older plus `invalidCursor` under changed bounds; info/0.5 limits.
- vtc-service end to end: list/0.8 and info/0.5 (`maxRecordDocumentBytes` 65,536).
- vta-service against a real room-host:
  - browse/0.6 load-older;
  - `hostRefused` at a host without list/0.8, and fallback to 0.7 without the bound;
  - `notAMember` and `hostUnreachable`.
- pnm: clap parsing of `--before-version`.

Refs #2294. Points 3 (`beforeVersion` paging) and 4 (limits in `rooms/info`) ship here. Points 1, 2, 5 and 7 are still open proposals, and point 6 (doc drift) is a separate PR. This PR does not close the issue.

## Open question (not decided here)

The VTC's own per-record limit stays at the spine's 64 KiB document default, now advertised through `maxRecordDocumentBytes`. Whether it should rise toward records/put/0.6's 2 MiB bound is asked on #2294.

Updates `trust-tasks-rs` from 0.37.2 to 0.37.7
Release notes

Sourced from trust-tasks-rs's releases.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.7

Added

  • vtc/badges: Member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1) (#1052)

  • feat(vtc/badges): member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1)

    A new family for the VTI Community Badges chapter (VTI-BDG-001 – 095): pictures with a name a member earns, holds and shows on their directory card.

    • A community badge is backed by a community group: create creates the group as vtc/groups/create does, its managers are the badge's owners, its members the holders; requests reuse vtc/groups/join and requests/decide, owners reuse managers/add and remove. The shared Group record gains an optional badgeId (additive).
    • An award is an offer until its recipient accepts (awards/offer → mine/accept or mine/decline); mine/accept issues the badge credential as the group's DID first and records the membership after. mine/accept states the credential profile: an Open Badges 3.0 OpenBadgeCredential with the community as the Achievement's creator and endorser, one evidence entry per award; short-lived with no status inside the community, long-lived with a slot in the community's own status set where holders may show it outside.
    • Hidden is portal-only (mine/hide, mine/show): walls, holders/list and counts leave a hidden holder out; awards/list shows owners the hidden mark.
    • Kudos badges (kudos/give, kudos/list): given by any member to any other within per-giver limits, each giving an award of its own; promote turns one into a community badge.
    • settings/show and settings/update hold the community's switches and limits.
    • images/upload and images/get mirror the directory's picture pipeline.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.6

Added

  • vtn/registry: Check a party against the network's trust registry through the network, and the registry status for administrators (#1050)

vtn/registry/check/0.1 lets anyone ask a network to ask its trust registry whether a party is published as its member, returning the registry's own signed answer verbatim, so a verifier with no DIDComm or TSP session (a browser, or a registry that serves no HTTPS) can still check the registry rather than take the network's word for it. Unreachable is indeterminate, never not a member.

vtn/registry/status/0.1 lets an administrator read the registry, the writer and whether it is connected, the last reconcile, and every record compared with what the entries project (ok, missing, stale, wrong).

  • vta/collection: Settings/show and settings/set — collection by default per trust context, stored and changed at run time (#1049)

Collection by default was one operator setting, off unless enabled (VTI-NTF-093). The VTI specification withdraws that in favour of a setting of each trust context, enabled unless disabled there (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098):

  • vta/collection/settings/show/0.1: a party with standing in a context reads its setting, who last changed it and when, and whether the VTA's operator has suspended collection by default everywhere (VTI-NTF-096).
  • vta/collection/settings/set/0.1: a party with administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022) enables or disables it; stored, audited, applied
