body:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 26.1.0 to 31.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v31.0.0

Breaking changes

  • Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from canvas to @napi-rs/canvas. Install @napi-rs/canvas v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing canvas alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the canvas migration guidance. Added WebP serialization through canvas.toDataURL() and canvas.toBlob(). Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing load, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only ctx.canvas, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous null results from canvas.toBlob() for empty canvases or encoding failures. (@​Brooooooklyn)
  • Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, @scope, custom-property substitution and registration through @property and CSS.registerProperty(), typed attr(), conditional if(), shadow-tree styling with :host, ::slotted(), and ::part(), pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with document.adoptedStyleSheets and shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
  • Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The JSDOM constructor, JSDOM.fromURL(), and JSDOM.fromFile() can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for DOMContentLoaded for the finished tree, or the window's load event for load-delaying resources, checking document.readyState first in case the event has already fired. XML syntax errors encountered after asynchronous parsing resumes are reported through the virtual console as "xml-parsing" errors.

Other changes

  • Added window.reportError(), which dispatches an error event and reports uncanceled errors to the virtual console. (@​sarankumar1325)
  • Added element.ariaBrailleLabel and element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription. (@​Kjubikstronk)
  • Fixed page-completion load events to fire only on the window. Use window.addEventListener("load", ...) or window.onload instead of listening on the document.
  • Fixed document.open(), including implicit calls from document.write(), to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
  • Fixed document.write() to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until document.close().
  • Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect script.async = false execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
  • Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and <style> elements in shadow trees now fire load events.
  • Fixed window.stop() to cancel pending subresource and XMLHttpRequest requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
  • Fixed repeated document.close() calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
  • Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
  • Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and element.blur() can release it immediately.
  • Fixed document.hasFocus() returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
  • Fixed \<template> parsing and template.innerHTML serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. (@​b84330808)
  • Fixed rect.toJSON() and performance.toJSON() to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.

v30.1.3

  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle() and computed CSS property reads, including with stylesheets containing attribute selectors. (@​scttcper, @​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed slowdowns when focusing elements and running interaction tests, which regressed in v30.1.2. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest reusing credentials supplied to xhr.open() after cross-origin redirects, including in response to authentication challenges from the destination.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest incorrectly sending and accepting cookies after cross-origin redirects back to the document's origin when xhr.withCredentials is false.
  • Fixed exceptions from malformed CSS math functions, such as calc(0px - @submenu_space), while parsing documents, stylesheets, and style declarations. (@​rnavarro)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring style rules nested inside multiple @media rules.
  • Fixed CSS shorthands overwriting longhands with higher priority or specificity during style computation, including declarations containing CSS variables.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning unresolved or inconsistent shorthand values, including for 'background', 'border', 'flex', 'font', 'margin', and 'padding', and incorrect shorthand defaults and inheritance.
  • Fixed computed background positions to resolve font-relative lengths using the final font size and handle multiple image layers correctly.
  • Fixed computed 'color' values depending on property read order, including unresolved color-mix() results, which regressed in v29.0.2.
  • Fixed currentcolor border colors incorrectly becoming transparent when 'color' uses light-dark() or relative color syntax.
  • Fixed CSS calculations that reduce to a percentage incorrectly producing pixel values, which regressed in v30.0.0.
  • Fixed numeric font weights in the 'font' shorthand incorrectly setting 'line-height'.
  • Fixed selector matching involving XML namespaces, and selectors such as [data-a|=""] failing to match empty values and values beginning with -. (@​asamuzaK)

v30.1.2

  • Updated URLs to support Unicode v18.0.0 in internationalized domain names.
  • Reduced package size and memory use for CSS property definitions. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed severe slowdowns when building large DOM trees, including SVG charts with D3, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​cmdcolin)
  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.

Updates `korthout/backport-action` from 4.7.0 to 4.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v4.7.1

What's Changed

Thanks to a contribution by @​jrasm91, backports no longer fail when you combine auto_merge_enabled: true with experimental.conflict_resolution: draft_commit_conflicts. Previously, when a cherry-pick conflicted, the action created the draft backport pull request and then tried to enable auto-merge on it. GitHub doesn't allow auto-merging of drafts, so the backport was reported as an unexpected failure, was_successful was false, and the draft backport pull request didn't receive instructions on how to resolve the conflict.

Now the action doesn't attempt auto-merge on a draft backport pull request and logs it. The backport is reported as drafted with conflicts, and the draft receives the conflict-resolution instructions as usual. With comment_style: summary, that looks like this:

Target Status
stable/8.7 :warning: Drafted with conflicts #612

Auto-merge stays off for the draft. You can enable it once you've resolved the conflicts.

title: fix(cli)!: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors)
body:
The CLI / operator-UX sweep: pnm-cli, cnm-cli, vta-cli-common, room-host, vta-mcp, vtc-mcp and the vta / vtc setup wizards. I re-checked every issue against current `main`; each claim held unless noted below. One commit per issue or theme.

**Breaking (`!`)** for the published `vta-cli-common`: `cmd_acl_delete`, `cmd_acl_update`, `cmd_key_revoke` and `cmd_seeds_rotate` take new arguments (`reason`, `yes`, a `Zeroizing` mnemonic). The `vta-sdk` additions are additive: `delete_acl_with_reason`, `update_acl_with_reason`, `invalidate_key_with_reason`.

## Per issue

**#2582 A corrupt config.toml.** A `config.toml` that exists but does not parse now stops pnm and cnm with exit 4. The message names the file, gives the parser's line and column, and gives the `mv <path> <path>.broken` command to move it aside. Before, the file was downgraded to an empty profile, and `setup` then overwrote it. A missing file is still a first run. Saves are atomic in both CLIs: temporary file (0600), fsync, rename, then fsync of the directory, through `vta_cli_common::config_file`. The issue's "not checked" item no longer matters: no command can save after a failed load, because the load now ends the process.

**#2583 Confirmations and `--reason`.** One rule, `vta_cli_common::confirm`:
- `--yes` proceeds without asking.
- On a terminal, the command asks `[y/N]`.
- With no terminal and no `--yes`, it refuses with exit 2 (`NotConfirmed`). This is the `rooms prune` rule.

It applies to:
- pnm: `acl delete`, `keys revoke`, `keys rotate-seed`, `did-mgmt dids delete`, `did-mgmt servers delete`, `did-templates delete`, `webs delete`, `vault purge`, `cred-vault purge`, `device wipe`, `did-mgmt agent-names remove` and `external delete`.
- cnm: `acl delete`, `keys revoke`, `keys rotate-seed` and `did-templates delete`.

`acl delete` prints the entry first, and warns when it is the session's own DID.

`--reason` on `acl delete`, `acl update` and `keys revoke` now reaches the wire. I checked the pinned schemas: `acl/revoke/0.3`, `acl/update/0.3` and `keys/revoke/0.1` all carry `reason`.

One server-side gap: the VTA parsed `keys/revoke`'s `reason` and dropped it. It now goes into the `key.revoke` audit row's `detail`. `vta/seeds/rotate/1.0` has no `reason` member, so `rotate-seed` takes only `--yes`.

Not checked: whether the server refuses deleting your own entry or the last super-admin. The CLI warns about your own entry; the server-side guard is a separate question.

**#2584 Mnemonics on the command line.** `keys create` and `keys rotate-seed` (pnm and cnm) take `--mnemonic-file <path|->`. With `-` on a terminal, the phrase is asked without echo. `--mnemonic` stays for one release, hidden, and prints a warning that argv is readable by every process. In transit the mnemonic rides the Trust Task over TSP / DIDComm authcrypt or TLS, as before.

**#2585 Unattended backups.** `backup export` and `backup import` read the password from `--password-file <path|->`, then `PNM_BACKUP_PASSWORD` / `CNM_BACKUP_PASSWORD`, then a no-echo prompt. With none of these and no terminal, they fail with a message naming `--password-file`. The import's "Type 'yes'" prompt is replaced by the shared confirmation, with `--yes`. pnm now says "<file> is not a valid backup file", as cnm did.

**#2586 Hints that name pnm.** Hints now use `{bin}`:
- **Auth:** pnm keeps `pnm setup`. cnm gets `cnm setup` or `cnm auth login --credential-bundle …`.
- **Forbidden:** names the session's own DID (`render::set_session_did`).
- **Network:** pnm keeps `pnm vta info`. cnm gets `cnm community list` / `cnm --url <url> health`.
- **Other hints:** the did-templates, keys and sealed-bundle hints use `{bin}`. The attested-bootstrap hint names `pnm bootstrap connect` only under pnm. The key-deletion warning no longer names `pnm backup export`.

A test holds the cnm-reachable modules to no literal `` `pnm `` command. A new cnm test parses every hint through `Cli::try_parse_from`, and the pnm remediation test is extended.

**#2587 cnm start-up.** One start-up for both CLIs (`vta_cli_common::startup::init_output`):
- JSON when stdout is not a terminal, or under `--json`.
- Colour only on a terminal and never under `NO_COLOR`.
- The banner is shown only when stderr is a terminal, and cnm's banner honours `NO_COLOR`.

Exit codes move to `vta_cli_common::exit`, so cnm now exits 3 / 4 / 5 like pnm instead of 1 everywhere.

On `-v` / `-V` I took the conservative route. In pnm, `-v` is `--vta` and `-V` is `--verbose`, and both stay. cnm keeps `-v` and also accepts `-V` for verbose, so `-V` means verbose in both CLIs. `--version` is long-only in both.

**#2588 JSON output.** These reads now print the SDK response as JSON:
- **pnm and shared commands:** `acl get`, `contexts get`, `keys get` (including `--secret`), `keys seeds`, `config get`, `audit` retention, `approvals explain`, `services didcomm drain list`, `services report` (JSON wins over its table default), `did-mgmt servers list`, `did-mgmt dids list` / `get` and `rooms offers list`.
- **cnm:** `actions list` (every page in one array), `actions show` (still verified first) and `audit verify` (exit status unchanged).
- **Mutations:** `acl delete`, `keys revoke` and `keys rotate-seed` print their result as JSON.

A census (`vta-cli-common` `commands::json_census`) checks the handler sources rather than the clap enums. It holds every read-named `cmd_*` handler in `vta-cli-common/src/commands` to a JSON path. There are four exemptions, each with a reason, and another test checks that every exemption still names a real handler. The `--json` help now reads "Emit output as JSON".

Not done: an audit of every cnm-only module (persona, the rest of rooms, networks and so on) beyond the three above. Those modules mostly use the shared handlers or already emit JSON (boards, elections, git and rooms do), but I did not read each one.

**#2589 Durations.** Every flag measured in seconds now takes `N[s|m|h|d|w]` through `duration::secs_arg` (`external bind --max-ttl`, `external issue --ttl`, `services didcomm --drain-ttl`, `collection claim --duration`). A bare integer is still seconds.

A grant that lapses is `--expires` everywhere, with the old name kept as a visible alias:
- pnm `rooms owner invite` / `issue-membership` / `issue-authority` (was `--valid-for`).
- cnm `rooms members add` and `member endorse` (was `--valid-for`).
- cnm `git grant` (was `--expires-in`).
- cnm `vetting vetters grant` and `vetting bootstrap` (was `--validity`).

cnm access's private parser is deleted. The two grammars differed: the shared one also accepts bare seconds, and it rejects 0 and negative values.

Left as they are:
- `cnm access authorize-key` keeps `--valid-for` beside `--expires`, because there they are two different times.
- `rooms watch --lease` is a watch lease and already takes the suffix grammar.
- `--validity-hours` takes a float, so renaming it would change its unit.

**#2590 Rooms.** Per-room host, host DID and signing-key id are kept in the profile's `rooms.toml` (atomic save), and are applied at parse time as clap defaults:
- A flag on the command line always wins.
- A flag with nothing stored is still required, exactly as before.
- `--help` shows the default in force.

They are recorded at `rooms owner register`, `rooms offers accept` (the community as host) and `rooms keys welcome`, and by the new `pnm rooms use <room> [--host] [--host-did] [--signing-key] [--forget]`. `use` also sets the default room, and bare `pnm rooms use` lists what is stored.

Also:
- `owner invite --subject` is now `--member`, with `--subject` as a visible alias.
- `--visibility` and `--retention-policy` are checked by clap against their allowed values.
- The bare `--room` / `--host` / `--host-did` args on `rooms get`, `rooms prune` and `owner group-add` have help.

Not checked: whether the host can be derived from the room's DID document. The stored-profile approach makes that unnecessary for this issue.

**#2591 Argument shapes.**
- `acl create` and `acl change-role` take the DID positionally; `--did` is kept, hidden.
- pnm and cnm `acl get` / `create` / `delete` also answer to `show` / `grant` / `revoke`, as `cnm access` does.
- `webs --expect-version` is now `--expected-version`, with `--expect-version` as an alias.
- The did-mgmt publish prompts take `--yes` / `-y`, with `--no-confirm` as an alias.
- Commands that already had a hidden `--force` alias for `--yes` keep it. New commands get none.

**#2592 Versions and completions.**
- `--version` on pnm, cnm, room-host, vta-mcp and vtc-mcp.
- The usage line now reads `pnm` / `cnm`.
- `pnm completions <shell>` and `cnm completions <shell>` via `clap_complete` 4.6, the same line as clap 4.6, so no duplicate versions for cargo-deny.

Not done: `--url` stays a top-level flag. Several subcommands have their own `--url` or a positional `url` (`services rest|webauthn enable --url`, `config resolver-url <url>`, `cnm networks preview <url>`), and a global `--url` would collide with them. The `--url` help now says to put it before the subcommand.

**#2593 Setup wizard without a terminal.** The `vta` and `vtc` setup wizards refuse to start when stdin is not a terminal. vta names `vta setup --from <setup.toml>` and `docs/02-vta/non-interactive-setup.md`. vtc names `vtc setup --setup-key-out <key-file>` then `vtc setup --from <setup.toml>`, and `docs/03-vtc/non-interactive-setup.md`. `vti-witness` and `vti-voting-service` never prompt, so they need no guard.

**#2594 MCP errors as tool results.** A failed operation in vta-mcp or vtc-mcp now comes back as a tool result with `isError: true` (`vti_mcp_common::tool_error`), with a body of `{error, message, next?, details?}`:
- In vta-mcp, `error` follows the `VtaError` variant (`forbidden`, `notFound`, `consentRequired`, `notServed`, `rateLimited`, `transport`, …), each with a `next` hint.
- In vtc-mcp, a community's refusal is kind `refused` and carries the community's own code.
- Guard refusals are `deniedByLocalPolicy` / `declinedByOperator`, keeping their guidance text.

`McpError` is now kept for malformed requests only.

`vta_call` and `vtc_call` check the URI against the discovery answer first, and answer `notServed` instead of waiting out the timeout. vta-mcp asks discovery once and remembers the answer, and never asks when local policy denies discovery. vtc-mcp checks against the discovery answer it gets at connect. When discovery cannot be asked, the call goes through as before.

The vtc-mcp parked and step-up results are unchanged. The `vta_supported_tasks` description and both MCP operator pages are updated.

## Overlap with #1758

PR #1758 (feat/pnm-control-master) also changes `pnm-cli/src/cli.rs`, `pnm-cli/src/main.rs`, `pnm-cli/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. The edits here in those files are confined to the start-up block, the `Cli` struct header, the variants listed above and the dispatch table, so a rebase of either should be mechanical.

## Tests

Local runs on the pinned 1.95.0 toolchain, all passing:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`
- `scripts/check-docs.py`

The vtc-service suite was run only for the new wizard test. Its full nextest job is left to CI.

Closes #2582
Closes #2583
Closes #2584
Closes #2585
Closes #2586
Closes #2587
Closes #2589
Closes #2590
Closes #2591
Closes #2593
Closes #2594
Refs #2588: the reads named in the issue are done and the census holds them; the cnm-only modules other than actions and audit were not read one by one.
Refs #2592: `--version` and completions are done; `--url` is not global, because of the subcommand `--url` collisions above.

title: fix(cli)!: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors) (#2726)
body:
fix(cli)!: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors) (#2726)

* fix(cli): a corrupt profile is fatal, saves are atomic, one start-up for pnm and cnm, --version and completions

#2582: pnm and cnm no longer downgrade an unparseable config.toml to a
warning and an empty profile — that pointed the operator at `setup`, which
then overwrote every other VTA / community. A file that exists but does not
parse is fatal (exit 4) with the move-it-aside command; a missing file is
still a first run. Saves are atomic in both CLIs (temporary file, fsync,
rename, directory fsync) via vta_cli_common::config_file.

#2587: the start-up block (JSON off a terminal or under --json, colour only
on a terminal and not under NO_COLOR, the binary name in hints, the banner
gated on stderr) is vta_cli_common::startup::init_output, used by both.
Exit codes move to vta_cli_common::exit; cnm now exits 3 / 4 / 5 like pnm
instead of 1 everywhere. cnm's banner honours NO_COLOR. -V is accepted for
--verbose in cnm too (in pnm -v is --vta, so -V stays verbose there).

#2592: --version on pnm, cnm, room-host, vta-mcp and vtc-mcp; the usage
line reads pnm / cnm; `pnm completions <shell>` and `cnm completions
<shell>` via clap_complete 4.6 (same line as clap 4.6). --url stays a
top-level flag: several subcommands have their own --url / url argument,
which a global one would collide with.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-cli-common): shared hints name the binary the operator ran

#2586: print_cli_error told a cnm operator to run `pnm setup`, `pnm acl
get <your-did>` and `pnm vta info` (cnm has no `vta`). The Auth, Forbidden
and Network hints are now per-binary: cnm re-authenticates with `cnm setup`
or `cnm auth login --credential-bundle …`, checks its VTA with `cnm
community list` / `cnm --url <url> health`; the Forbidden hint names the
session's own DID (render::set_session_did, set by both CLIs once
connected). The did-templates, keys and sealed-bundle hints use {bin}; the
attested-bootstrap hint names `pnm bootstrap connect` only under pnm, and
the key-deletion warning no longer names `pnm backup export` to a cnm
operator. A test holds the cnm-reachable modules to no literal pnm command.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(cli)!: irreversible commands confirm, revocations carry a reason, secrets stay off argv, backups run unattended

#2583: one rule for irreversible commands, vta_cli_common::confirm: --yes
proceeds, a terminal is asked [y/N], no terminal and no --yes refuses
(exit 2) — the rule rooms prune set. Applied to acl delete, keys revoke,
keys rotate-seed, did-mgmt dids delete, did-mgmt servers delete,
did-templates delete, webs delete, vault purge, cred-vault purge, device
wipe, did-mgmt agent-names remove and external delete (cnm: acl delete,
keys revoke, keys rotate-seed, did-templates delete). acl delete prints the
entry first and says so when it is the session's own identity. --reason on
acl delete, acl update and keys revoke reaches the wire (acl/revoke/0.3,
acl/update/0.3 and keys/revoke/0.1 all carry it): new additive SDK methods
delete_acl_with_reason, update_acl_with_reason, invalidate_key_with_reason.
The VTA parsed keys/revoke's reason and dropped it; it now lands in the
key.revoke audit row's detail.

#2584: keys create and keys rotate-seed take --mnemonic-file <path|->
(- at a terminal is asked without echo). --mnemonic stays one release,
hidden, with a warning that argv is readable by every process.

#2585: backup export / import take --password-file <path|->, then
PNM_BACKUP_PASSWORD / CNM_BACKUP_PASSWORD, then the no-echo prompt; with
none and no terminal they fail naming the flag instead of a dialoguer I/O
error. import's "Type 'yes'" becomes the shared confirmation with --yes,
and pnm says "<file> is not a valid backup file" as cnm did.

#2591: acl create / change-role take the DID positionally (--did kept,
hidden); acl get/create/delete answer to show/grant/revoke as cnm access
does; webs --expect-version is --expected-version (old spelling an alias);
the did-mgmt publish prompts take --yes (--no-confirm an alias).

Breaking for vta-cli-common: cmd_acl_delete, cmd_acl_update,
cmd_key_revoke and cmd_seeds_rotate take the new arguments.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(cli): one duration grammar and one name for a lapsing grant

#2589: every flag measured in seconds (pnm external bind --max-ttl,
external issue --ttl, services didcomm --drain-ttl, collection claim
--duration) now takes N[s|m|h|d|w] through vta_cli_common::duration::secs_arg;
a bare integer is still seconds, so existing invocations mean what they did.
A grant that lapses is --expires everywhere: pnm rooms owner invite /
issue-member / issue-authority, cnm rooms members add, cnm member endorse,
cnm git grant, cnm vetting vetters grant and vetting bootstrap, with
--valid-for / --expires-in / --validity kept as visible aliases. cnm
access's private duration parser is gone; it uses the shared one (which
also accepts bare seconds). Runtime hints name --expires.

Not changed: cnm access authorize-key keeps --valid-for beside --expires,
because there they are two different times (how long the document may
wait vs the delegation's lifetime); --lease on rooms watch is a watch lease
and already takes the suffix grammar; --validity-hours (a float) is left,
renaming it would change its unit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(cli): every read answers in JSON under --json or off a terminal

#2588: acl get, contexts get, keys get (with and without --secret), keys
seeds, config get, audit retention, approvals explain, services didcomm
drain list, services report (its table default yields to JSON), did-mgmt
servers list, did-mgmt dids list / get and rooms offers list printed prose
whatever the destination, so `pnm acl get <did> | jq .role` got a table.
Each now prints the SDK response as JSON. In cnm, actions list (all pages
in one array), actions show (still verified first) and audit verify (exit
status unchanged) do too. acl delete, keys revoke and keys rotate-seed
print their result as JSON.

A census (vta-cli-common commands::json_census) holds every read-named
cmd_* handler to a JSON path, with four reasoned exemptions. The --json
help now says "Emit output as JSON" and that it is automatic off a
terminal.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(pnm): rooms remember their host, host DID and signing key

#2590: every `pnm rooms …` verb re-asked for --room, --host, --host-did and
--signing-key, copied from scrollback. They are now kept per room in the
profile's rooms.toml (atomic save) and applied at parse time as clap
defaults: a flag on the line always wins, a stored value fills one that is
absent, a flag with nothing stored is required exactly as before, and
--help shows the default in force. The room is the one --room names, else
the default room.

Written where they become known: `rooms owner register` (room -> host
DID), `rooms offers accept` (the community as host), `rooms keys welcome`
(the room), and the new `pnm rooms use <room> [--host] [--host-did]
[--signing-key] [--forget]`, which also sets the default; bare `pnm rooms
use` lists them. Local only: no session is needed.

Also: `owner invite --subject` is `--member` (as group-add names the same
person; --subject a visible alias); --visibility and --retention-policy are
checked by clap against their values; the bare --room/--host/--host-did on
rooms get, rooms prune and owner group-add have help.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-mcp,vtc-mcp): return operation failures as tool results the model can read

Every VTA failure and every local-guard refusal used to be a JSON-RPC
protocol error: `to_mcp` mapped Forbidden, NotFound, Validation,
RateLimited and Auth alike to `-32603 internal error`, and the guard's
refusals (with their "restart with --allow" guidance) to
`invalid_request`. Hosts render those as a bridge fault, and some never
show the message to the model. vtc-mcp did the same for a community's
refusal and every other client error.

A failed operation is now a tool-execution error (`isError: true`, and
input the tool itself finds wrong too, per SEP-1303), carrying a small
JSON body `{ error, message, next, details }`:

- vti-mcp-common gains `tool_error` (`ToolError`, `CallFailure`), shared
  by both bridges; `CallGuard::finish` / `refuse` return it as
  `CallToolResult::error`, and `ErrorData` stays only for requests the
  bridge cannot parse and unknown resources.
- vta-mcp keys the kind on the `VtaError` variant (`forbidden`,
  `notFound`, `invalidRequest`, `consentRequired` with the code to
  approve, `rateLimited`, `notServed` with the served versions,
  `transport`, `notConnected`, ...), each with what to do next.
- `vta_call` checks the URI against the VTA's discovery answer (asked
  once and remembered, or taken from an unnarrowed
  `vta_supported_tasks`; never asked past a policy denying discovery)
  and answers `notServed` instead of waiting out the reply timeout.
  The answer is derived from the VTA's dispatch table, so absence is a
  fact; when discovery cannot be asked, the VTA answers as before.
- vtc-mcp: a community's refusal is kind `refused` with its own code and
  document; sign-in, enrolment and action-decision failures are tool
  results too; `vtc_call` refuses a URI the community's discovery answer
  (learned at connect) does not list, before sending.

Refs #2594

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service,vtc-service): refuse the interactive setup wizard without a terminal, naming setup --from

`vta setup` / `vtc setup` with no flags went straight to the dialoguer
prompts, so in a Dockerfile, systemd unit or CI they died at the first
prompt with a terminal I/O error that said nothing of the unattended
path. Both wizards now check stdin first and fail with the command to run
instead: `vta setup --from <setup.toml>`, and for the VTC its two phases
(`--setup-key-out`, then `--from`), each naming its
docs/0x-*/non-interactive-setup.md.

vti-witness and vti-voting-service setups were checked: neither prompts
(both are flag/file driven), so neither needs the guard.

Refs #2593

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: pnm/cnm READMEs and the did-webs / did-webvh guides name the new flags

--mnemonic-file and --yes on keys rotate-seed, --password-file / --yes and
PNM_BACKUP_PASSWORD on backup, --expected-version on webs, --yes on the
did-mgmt publish prompt (#2584, #2585, #2591).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(pnm): the rooms profile stores a signing key id, named as one

The secret-Debug census read RoomEntry.signing_key as key material; it is
the room's signing key *id* (#2590), so the field is signing_key_id.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: perf(vta): cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages
body:
Performance sweep over the VTA's per-request and per-tick hot paths. No published API breaks (every new field is on a `#[non_exhaustive]` struct or a struct with private fields; everything else is additive), and every storage change reads what an older build wrote — no migration step a TEE restart could lose.

## #2622 — payload schemas compiled once

`trust_tasks_rs::validate::against_schema` / `validate_value` (0.37) parse and compile the schema on every call. New `vta_sdk::schema_cache` keeps the compiled validator keyed by the `&'static` schema text's address (the technique trust-tasks-rs 0.38's `SchemaValidator` uses), compiled with the **same** `jsonschema` release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses (0.46, as the renamed workspace dep `jsonschema-trust-tasks`), so the verdict and the error text are unchanged — a test checks both against `against_schema` for every pinned schema. Used by the dispatch spine, the SDK's send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting (incl. its `$defs` sub-schemas) and the VTA's per-handler payload checks.

**Why not the bump:** trust-tasks-rs 0.38/0.39 moves in lockstep with `affinidi-tdk` / `affinidi-messaging-sdk` (see the root `Cargo.toml` notes), which is a release train of its own. When the workspace takes it, `schema_cache` becomes a thin wrapper over `SchemaValidator` and the renamed dep goes.

## #2623 — policy set compiled once per change

`vta_policy::PolicyCache` (held in `AppState::policy_cache`) keeps the compiled enabled policy set under the policy keyspace's `cache_ticket()`: served only while nothing has been written since it was read, cached only if no write raced the read. Upsert, delete, enable, the approvals row and a restore all move the ticket, so nothing invalidates by hand. Compilation and evaluation run under `spawn_blocking` (evaluation can take up to `POLICY_EVAL_TIME_LIMIT` per policy). Test: compiled once while unchanged, every write seen.

## #2624 — one parse, one proof verification per DIDComm/TSP document

- `bind_document_to_sender` now returns a `VerifiedDocument` typestate (received JSON, its parse, the verified signer), constructible only by verifying; `accept_from_proven_sender` dispatches it via `dispatch_verified_core`, so the spine neither re-parses nor re-verifies. The spine records the verified signer with the received JSON, and `received::verify_trust_task_proof` returns it for that exact document (same function, same JSON, same resolver) instead of verifying again.
- The reply-waiter check is lazy: `PendingReplies::is_waiting` first, and the proof is verified for it only when a waiter holds the thread (REST included).
- The received document's parse is taken once per dispatch rather than at every verification; `TrustTask` is deserialized from the `Value` by reference (no clone).
- Not done: keeping the handler's response as a `Value` until after signing (the response side) — left for the trust_tasks refactor in flight elsewhere.

## #2625 — intrinsic session row written at the REST granularity

`resolve_did_session` writes only when `last_seen` is `LAST_SEEN_GRANULARITY_SECS` stale or an elevation lapsed (always persisted). Test covers both. Nothing depends on second-level `last_seen` (it only feeds the 24 h idle TTL).

## #2626 — sweeps bounded, expiry-indexed where rows carry responses

- New `vti_common::store::expiry_index`: one empty row `…-exp:{deadline:020}:{record key}` per record write (written before, or in the same batch as, the record). A sweep reads the index in bounded pages up to `now` and stops. Records written before the index are indexed by the first sweep that finds no marker row — ordinary store state, re-run if interrupted. Used by the accepted-id record (`vti-trust-task-server`) and the idempotency cache. Tests: legacy records swept, moved deadlines, multi-page walks.
- Audit retention pages forward from `log:` and stops at the cutoff (O(expired), not O(retained)).
- Sessions (all six passes), vault/credential, consent, ACL and app-state tombstone sweeps read through `scan_pager`.
- Census: `vta-sweepers` fails if a sweeper calls `prefix_iter_raw` / `prefix_keys` outside its tests.
- No new keyspace; index and marker rows live in the record's own keyspace (both are already in the backup partition as they were).

## #2627 — list pages cost a page

- `keys/list`: range read from `key:{cursor}`, stopping one record past the page.
- `vault/list`: new `vti_common::vault::list_vault_entries_page` — range read from `vault:{cursor}`, and rows are decoded **without the secret** (the `secret` member is skipped by the parser, never materialised).
- app-state / memory snapshot list: range read from the cursor key; change feed seeks past `index_key(since)` and resolves records only as taken. `list_all_live` (memory) therefore costs O(N), not ⌈N/200⌉·N.
- Cursors are unchanged on the wire (same encodings, same bindings).
- **Remaining (Refs):** `acl_v0_3` list, `webs` list, `device` list, `policy` list, `auth/sessions` list + revoke-session's own-session lookup, and `find_key_by_public_multibase` still scan. Each wants its own index or cursor shape and is left to a follow-up.

## #2628 — collector candidate set cached

`collection::cached_candidates` keeps the candidate set under the write tickets of the webvh, ACL, contexts and collection keyspaces plus the configured identities it reads; `kick()` drops it. A quiet store costs one comparison per 30 s tick instead of an ACL scan plus three reads (one a whole DID log) per DID. `find_candidate` uses the cached set. Behaviour preserved: a DID created, an ACL change, a context removed, a provisioned mark or a claim is seen on the next pass exactly as before — the issue's "rebuild only on kick" would have missed DID and ACL changes, which don't kick. Test: built once while unchanged, rebuilt on kick, on a new DID and on an ACL change.
- Not done: a per-DID log summary (reading only the tail entry) — the set is now rebuilt only when a log changes, which removes the per-tick cost; a summary row would be a storage change for the webvh subsystem.

## #2629 — idempotency response body as base64

`CacheEntry.response_body` serializes as a base64 string through a serde adaptor that still reads the old array-of-numbers form. Test covers both. The second copy of the response in the accepted-id record is left as is (different keyspace and lifetime; deduplicating them is a design change).

Closes #2622
Closes #2623
Closes #2624
Closes #2625
Closes #2626
Refs #2627
Closes #2628
Closes #2629

title: perf(vta): cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages (#2713)
body:
perf(vta): cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages (#2713)

* perf(vta-sdk,vta-service): compile each Trust Task payload schema once (#2622)

trust-tasks-rs 0.37's against_schema / validate_value parse and compile the
schema on every call. vta_sdk::schema_cache keeps the compiled validator by
the &'static schema text's address (the same technique as trust-tasks-rs
0.38's SchemaValidator), with the jsonschema release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses
so the check and its error text are unchanged. The dispatch spine, the SDK's
send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and
the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it.

trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging
SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps
SchemaValidator.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): write an intrinsic session's last_seen at the REST granularity (#2625)

resolve_did_session rewrote the session row on every DIDComm/TSP message.
It now writes only when last_seen is LAST_SEEN_GRANULARITY_SECS stale or an
elevation lapsed, as touch_last_seen already does for REST.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-service): verify and parse a DIDComm/TSP Trust Task once (#2624)

bind_document_to_sender returns a VerifiedDocument typestate (the JSON as
received, its parse, the verified signer); accept_from_proven_sender hands
it to the spine through dispatch_verified_core, which neither re-parses nor
re-verifies it. The spine records the verified signer beside the received
JSON, and received::verify_trust_task_proof answers with it for that exact
document. The reply-waiter check verifies a proof only when a waiter holds
the document's thread (PendingReplies::is_waiting), on every transport.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-policy,vta-service): compile the policy set once per change, evaluate off the executor (#2623)

The PDP listed the policy keyspace and parsed and compiled every active Rego
module for each gated Trust Task. vta_policy::PolicyCache (AppState
policy_cache) keeps the compiled enabled set under the keyspace's
cache_ticket, so any write through any path is seen on the next decision.
Compilation and evaluation run on the blocking pool.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-service): rebuild the collector's candidate set only when its inputs change (#2628)

current_plan walked every ACL entry and every did:webvh record, reading each
DID's whole log, every 30 s. The set is now kept under the write tickets of
the webvh, ACL, contexts and collection keyspaces and the configured
identities it reads, and dropped by kick(); find_candidate reads it too. A
DID or ACL change (neither of which kicks) is still seen on the next pass.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common,vta-sweepers): bound every sweep; expiry-index the records that carry responses (#2626, #2629)

Over vsock a prefix_iter_raw is one response frame, so a sweep of a
keyspace past 16 MiB failed on every tick and nothing was pruned.

- vti_common::store::expiry_index: one row per record write, keyed by
  deadline, read in bounded pages up to now. Records written before it are
  indexed once by the first sweep without the marker row. Used by the
  accepted-id record and the idempotency cache.
- Audit retention pages from the oldest key and stops at the cutoff.
- Session, vault, credential, consent and ACL sweeps read bounded pages;
  vta-sweepers fails a census on prefix_iter_raw/prefix_keys outside tests.
- CacheEntry.response_body is stored as base64 and still reads the old
  array-of-numbers form (#2629).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-service,vti-common): list pages read a page, not the keyspace (#2627)

keys/list, vault/list and the app-state / memory snapshot list and change
feed read a range from their cursor (the change feed seeks past sinceVersion)
and stop one row past the page. vault/list decodes rows without their secret
(list_vault_entries_page). The app-state tombstone sweep pages too. Cursors
are unchanged on the wire.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-service): box the verified document the spine is handed (#2624)

Keeps SpineInput a pointer wide (clippy large_enum_variant) and the
dispatch future's frame small (VTI-08).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(deny): name vta-sdk's schema_cache as a holder of jsonschema 0.46 (#2622)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): track the webvh keyspace in the collector's cache only when it exists (#2628)

AppState.webvh_ks is #[cfg(feature = "webvh")]; candidate_inputs read it
unconditionally, so a build without webvh (rest,didcomm) did not compile.
Without webvh there are no did:webvh records and no candidates, so there is
nothing to track.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: read the Feature combos job block without a pipe into grep -q

Under set -o pipefail, grep -q exits on its first match while echo is still
writing a block larger than the pipe buffer; echo then fails with EPIPE and
the pipeline reports failure, so 'which builds this change can affect'
failed at random and skipped every downstream job. Here-strings give grep
the whole input with no writer to break.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): name the proof type the bytes door starts with (#2624)

In a rest-only build SpineInput has no Verified variant, so nothing else
fixes the type of the None the bytes path yields and inference fails
(E0282 in Feature combos, rest only).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Release notes

trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.7

Added

  • vtc/badges: Member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1) (#1052)

  • feat(vtc/badges): member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1)

    A new family for the VTI Community Badges chapter (VTI-BDG-001 – 095): pictures with a name a member earns, holds and shows on their directory card.

    • A community badge is backed by a community group: create creates the group as vtc/groups/create does, its managers are the badge's owners, its members the holders; requests reuse vtc/groups/join and requests/decide, owners reuse managers/add and remove. The shared Group record gains an optional badgeId (additive).
    • An award is an offer until its recipient accepts (awards/offer → mine/accept or mine/decline); mine/accept issues the badge credential as the group's DID first and records the membership after. mine/accept states the credential profile: an Open Badges 3.0 OpenBadgeCredential with the community as the Achievement's creator and endorser, one evidence entry per award; short-lived with no status inside the community, long-lived with a slot in the community's own status set where holders may show it outside.
    • Hidden is portal-only (mine/hide, mine/show): walls, holders/list and counts leave a hidden holder out; awards/list shows owners the hidden mark.
    • Kudos badges (kudos/give, kudos/list): given by any member to any other within per-giver limits, each giving an award of its own; promote turns one into a community badge.
    • settings/show and settings/update hold the community's switches and limits.
    • images/upload and images/get mirror the directory's picture pipeline.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.6

Added

  • vtn/registry: Check a party against the network's trust registry through the network, and the registry status for administrators (#1050)

vtn/registry/check/0.1 lets anyone ask a network to ask its trust registry whether a party is published as its member, returning the registry's own signed answer verbatim, so a verifier with no DIDComm or TSP session (a browser, or a registry that serves no HTTPS) can still check the registry rather than take the network's word for it. Unreachable is indeterminate, never not a member.

vtn/registry/status/0.1 lets an administrator read the registry, the writer and whether it is connected, the last reconcile, and every record compared with what the entries project (ok, missing, stale, wrong).

  • vta/collection: Settings/show and settings/set — collection by default per trust context, stored and changed at run time (#1049)

Collection by default was one operator setting, off unless enabled (VTI-NTF-093). The VTI specification withdraws that in favour of a setting of each trust context, enabled unless disabled there (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098):

  • vta/collection/settings/show/0.1: a party with standing in a context reads its setting, who last changed it and when, and whether the VTA's operator has suspended collection by default everywhere (VTI-NTF-096).
  • vta/collection/settings/set/0.1: a party with administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022) enables or disables it; stored, audited, applied

Changelog

Sourced from vti-vetting-pcs's changelog.

Changelog

Released versions are recorded below, newest first.

This file is frozen. It records everything released up to the adoption of release-plz in #938.

Current entries live in each published crate's own CHANGELOG.md (vta-sdk/CHANGELOG.md, vti-common/CHANGELOG.md, …), generated from conventional commits when a release is cut. The changelog.d/ fragment directory is gone.

Writing an entry: you don't. Write a conventional-commit PR title and a real commit body — see CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/RELEASING.md.

Unreleased

Repository — the changelog convention is signposted, enforced, and current (#935)

No crate versions change. Recorded here because it changes where contributors are told to write changelog entries and what CI does about it — exactly the kind of process change changelog.d/README.md asks for a fragment about.

CHANGELOG.md opened with a ## Unreleased section that stopped at #876, while every entry since — 52 fragments — lived in changelog.d/ with nothing in the file saying so.

Signposting. CHANGELOG.md gains a note above ## Unreleased: unreleased entries live in changelog.d/ until a release is cut, this file lags that directory by design, and reading both is how you see everything pending. Above the heading deliberately — collate-changelog.sh inserts fragments immediately after the ## Unreleased line, so a note underneath would sink below the newest entries on every release. CONTRIBUTING.md's PR checklist asked for "CHANGELOG.md updated for user-facing changes" — the one thing the convention forbids, told to every contributor at the moment they were about to do it; it now asks for a fragment, beside a new Changelog section. README.md names both locations.

Enforcement. scripts/check-changelogs.sh gains two rules, because the convention had been documented in four places and enforced in none — and the cost of ignoring it never lands on the author, it lands on every other open PR as a conflict they did not cause:

  • A fragment a PR adds must name that PR, in its filename and in its ### heading. The heading half is the easy mistake — you write the fragment before the PR exists, guess the next number, and lose the race — and it is the worse one, because a wrong number survives collation and permanently points readers at an unrelated PR. Only files this PR adds are checked; the directory holds every open PR's fragment.

Changelog

Sourced from vti-voting's changelog.

vta-sdk 0.21.0 / vta-keys 0.2.0 / vta-service 0.14.0 — the workspace moves to curve25519-dalek 5 (#887)

ed25519-dalek 2 → 3, x25519-dalek 2 → 3, curve25519-dalek 4 → 5 and hpke 0.13 → 0.14. These shipped together on 2026-07-06 (hpke on 07-09) and bring the next-generation RustCrypto stack with them: rand_core 0.10, signature 3, ed25519 3, aead 0.6.

vta-sdk was the single reason curve25519-dalek 4 could not leave the affinidi-tdk-rs graph. It pinned curve25519-dalek = "4" directly, plus ed25519-dalek 2, x25519-dalek 2 and hpke 0.13, and every TDK consumer inherits that through the mediator.

  • vta-sdk: breaking. Dalek types sit in public signatures — protocols::acl_management::swap::build_swap_presentation takes &ed25519_dalek::SigningKey — so callers must move to ed25519-dalek 3 in step. sealed_transfer::hpke loses its hand-rolled OsCsprng adapter, which existed only to bridge getrandom onto hpke 0.13's rand_core 0.9 traits; hpke 0.14 ships OS-CSPRNG variants of single_shot_seal / gen_keypair backed by UnwrapErr(SysRng), the same panic-on-CSPRNG-failure posture the adapter documented. The sealed-transfer wire format is unchanged and the randomness posture is unchanged.
  • vta-keys: ephemeral X25519 wrapping-key generation moves to rand::rng(). rand 0.10 renamed OsRng → SysRng and made it fallible (TryRng<Error = SysError>), so it no longer satisfies dalek's CryptoRng bound; rand_core 0.10 has no OsRng at all.
  • vta-service: two sites passed an ed25519-dalek-bip32 SigningKey straight into a workspace slot. That crate (0.3, last released 2023-08) still pins ed25519-dalek 2 and has no v3, so its SigningKey is now a different type — they cross the boundary as raw bytes, which is what every other derivation site here already did.

ed25519-dalek-bip32 keeps a dalek-2 subtree in vta-service, vta-keys and didcomm-test. It is contained: the crate is absent from vta-sdk's dependency tree, so it never reaches TDK consumers. Removing it means reimplementing SLIP-0010 ed25519 derivation — security-sensitive, and tracked separately rather than folded into a dependency bump.

Version-pin fan-out. vta-sdk's minor bump moves the version = "0.20" requirement every dependent carries, and a changed requirement has to publish or the registry keeps resolving the old one. Those crates are otherwise untouched — their own APIs do not change — so they take patch bumps: cnm-cli 0.11.14, pnm-cli 0.11.17, vta-audit 0.1.2, vta-backup 0.1.5, vta-cli-common 0.10.23, vta-support 0.2.3, vta-tee 0.1.5, vta-vault 0.1.2, vta-webvh 0.1.3, vtc-client 0.3.1, vtc-service 0.11.50, vti-common 0.11.32, vti-secrets 0.1.9.

Updates `korthout/backport-action` from 4.7.0 to 4.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v4.7.1

What's Changed

Thanks to a contribution by @​jrasm91, backports no longer fail when you combine auto_merge_enabled: true with experimental.conflict_resolution: draft_commit_conflicts. Previously, when a cherry-pick conflicted, the action created the draft backport pull request and then tried to enable auto-merge on it. GitHub doesn't allow auto-merging of drafts, so the backport was reported as an unexpected failure, was_successful was false, and the draft backport pull request didn't receive instructions on how to resolve the conflict.

Now the action doesn't attempt auto-merge on a draft backport pull request and logs it. The backport is reported as drafted with conflicts, and the draft receives the conflict-resolution instructions as usual. With comment_style: summary, that looks like this:

Target Status
stable/8.7 :warning: Drafted with conflicts #612

Auto-merge stays off for the draft. You can enable it once you've resolved the conflicts.

title: feat(messaging): wake a device through its own mediator, and end-to-end delivery receipts
body:
Spec layer for two VTI issues: waking a task-consent approver that has no ACL entry on the requester's VTA (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2663), and confirming a durable send to a recipient on another mediator (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2553). Both rest on the id the recipient's mediator stores a message under.

## Waking a device through its own mediator

- **`messaging/wake/set/0.1`** (new): an account gives its own mediator the opaque `WakeHandle` its gateway issued, or clears it (absent = clear). The mediator never holds a platform token. Response `{ wakeCapable }`. `local` capability gate, proof RECOMMENDED, retention durable.
- **`messaging/wake/request/0.1`** (new): a sender that has just queued mail for a DID asks that DID's mediator to ring, naming up to 8 queued messages by stored id. Contentless (no type, reason or content). The mediator rings (`push/wake` as itself) only if: the account has a handle; every id is queued for it, fresh (10 min) and undelivered; the stored sender is the requester where the envelope reveals one; the requester is not blocked by the access list; the account is offline; no id has rung before (no re-ring of a pending request); and the per-(sender, addressee) and per-addressee limits hold. A request may arm for 120 s. **The response is always `{}`**, the same for every outcome, so it cannot be used to learn whether a DID is registered, wakeable or online. Proof REQUIRED (the request usually arrives relayed or on an anonymous session).
- **`push/register/0.3`** (new version): `selfControl { allowedTriggers }` lets a device with no controller VTA register as its own controller, naming its mediator as a trigger, under gateway policy (`push/register:selfControlRefused`). Exactly one of `controllerVtaDid` / `selfControl` (schema `oneOf`). Not declared `extends: "0.2"`, since a 0.2 reader would drop `selfControl` and record no controller.
- **Push binding 0.1** (draft, amended in place): new §3.5 "Sender-requested, mediator-triggered wake" (contentless; no re-ring of a pending request; holding a handle grants no authority to wake), self-controlled handles in §3.3, and the two tasks in the §3.2 table.

## End-to-end delivery receipts

- **`messaging/receipt/0.1`** (new, fire-and-forget): `{ confirms }`, sent by the recipient's delivery layer to the transport-authenticated sender once it durably holds a message that asked for a receipt. It is requested, never automatic. The recipient may decline. A receipt settles only when it comes from the party the message was addressed to, and it is never answered. A transition section accepts the earlier `https://affinidi.com/delivery/1.0/receipt` body alongside it, under the same rules.
- **TSP binding 0.2** (new): optional `deliveryId` envelope member requests a receipt. The envelope type is unchanged, so 0.1 and 0.2 interoperate (a 0.1 consumer ignores the member). Registered in `bindings.js`.
- **DIDComm binding 0.2** (draft, amended in place): §2.1, a `delivery_id` header requests a receipt. It does not use `thid`, because §3.1 gives `thid` to `threadId`.

## Housekeeping

- Stale `push/register/0.2` references moved to 0.3 (`push/provision/0.2` prose, CONTRIBUTING-SPECS worked examples). Removed the `push/register/0.2` spec-examples baseline entry. `tsp/0.2` names `trust-task-discovery/0.4`.
- Regenerated the Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`), TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

## Checks run locally

`npm run check` (validate, check-bindings, published-schemas, version-edits, spec-lifecycle, sibling ranges, dart packages, release lists, doc-facts, withdrawal readiness, ceremonies), `check-framework-spec`, `build`, `build-bundles`, `check-bundles`, `test:checks`. All passed. Also `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,messaging,push --test conformance`, `go build/vet/test ./...`, `tsc --noEmit` + `npm test` (trust-tasks-ts), and `dart analyze --fatal-infos` + `dart test`.

title: feat(messaging): wake a device through its own mediator, and end-to-end delivery receipts (#1297)
body:
feat(messaging): wake a device through its own mediator, and end-to-end delivery receipts (#1297)

Two gaps in getting a document to a device that is on another mediator
or has no agent of its own.

Waking (messaging/wake/set 0.1, messaging/wake/request 0.1):
- messaging/wake/set: an account gives its own mediator the opaque
  WakeHandle its push gateway issued, or clears it (absent = clear). The
  mediator never holds a token. Response { wakeCapable }.
- messaging/wake/request: a sender that has just queued mail for a DID
  asks that DID's mediator to ring, naming the queued messages by their
  stored ids (<= 8). Contentless. The mediator rings (push/wake, as
  itself) only when the account has a handle, every id is queued for it,
  fresh (10 min) and undelivered, the stored sender is the requester
  where the envelope reveals one, the requester is not blocked, the
  account is offline, no id has rung before, and per-(sender, addressee)
  and per-addressee limits hold. Requests may arm for 120 s. The response
  is always {} so it is not a presence oracle. Proof REQUIRED.
- push/register 0.3: `selfControl` lets a device with no controller VTA
  register as its own controller, with an initial allowlist (normally its
  mediator), under gateway policy (push/register:selfControlRefused).
  Exactly one of controllerVtaDid / selfControl.
- push binding 0.1 (draft, in place): §3.5 sender-requested,
  mediator-triggered wake; self-controlled handles in §3.3.

Receipts (messaging/receipt 0.1, TSP binding 0.2):
- messaging/receipt: a fire-and-forget Trust Task { confirms } the
  recipient's delivery layer sends to the transport-authenticated sender
  once it durably holds a message that asked for a receipt. Requested,
  never automatic; may be declined; settles only from the addressed
  party; never answered. A transition section accepts the earlier
  https://affinidi.com/delivery/1.0/receipt body alongside it.
- TSP binding 0.2: optional `deliveryId` envelope member requests a
  receipt; envelope type unchanged, so 0.1 and 0.2 interoperate.
- DIDComm binding 0.2 (draft, in place): §2.1, a `delivery_id` header
  requests a receipt (not `thid`, which §3.1 gives to threadId).

Regenerates the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

title: perf(rooms)!: indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes
body:
Four performance issues in the room host (`vti-rooms`, used by `room-host` and `vtc-service`) and the voting service. Each claim was re-checked against current `main` before it was fixed.

**Breaking (`!`):** `vti_rooms::blobs::BlobHost::read_snapshot` and `records_lock` now take the room id (`read_snapshot(&room_id)`, `records_lock(&room_id)`). `vti-rooms` is published.

## #2595: record get/list rescanned and re-hashed the whole room under a host-wide lock

Confirmed. Every `get` and every `list` page scanned the room, decoded every record, canonicalised it (JCS) and hashed it, and did all of that under the one `BlobHost` mutex.

- **Record indexes** (`vti-rooms/src/storage/index.rs`). Three new row kinds sit in the records keyspace, next to the records:
  - `room_leaf/v1:` holds each record's version and leaf hash;
  - `room_by_version/v1:` orders the room by version;
  - `room_head/v1:` caches the room's tree head.
  
  Every `put`, mirrored store, curate, prune removal and erasure writes the record and its index rows in **one atomic `Batch`**.
- **Head cache that can't go stale.** Every write replaces the head row with a `stale` marker that carries a fresh nonce. A reader computes the head from the leaf rows and caches it with `require_unchanged(marker)`. So a head computed before a write can never be cached after it. A head-only read with a fresh head costs one row read.
- **Paging seeks.** `since_version` and the cursor (either order) now seek through `ScanOpts::after`/`newest_first`. A page reads the version rows it walks and the records it returns.
- **Byte-identical commitment.** The leaves are the same, in the same key order, and go through the same `merkle::root_of`/`inclusion_proof`. `storage::index_tests` checks the head, every trace and every page (both orders, prefixes, watermarks, page sizes) against the old full-scan computation. It does this after every kind of write, and also for a room that has no index yet.
- **No migration step.** A room counts as indexed when its head row exists. The first read or write of an older room builds the index from its records: rows first, head last, so an interrupted build is finished by the next caller. `migrate_room_keys` drops a room's head in the same batch as each record it moves, and `purge_room_rows` removes the index rows. A new `storage::reindex_room` covers a host that rewrites a record row directly.
- **Per-room locks.** `BlobHost` now has striped per-room `RwLock`s. Reads take the room lock shared, so reads never wait on each other or on another room. Record writes take it exclusive.
- **Hashing runs on `spawn_blocking`**, both the one-off index build and root/trace computation. `vti-rooms` gains tokio's `rt` feature for this.
- **Not O(log n), and why.** The issue asked for an O(log n) trace. That isn't reachable for *this* commitment. The leaves are ordered by key and the tree shape depends only on the leaf count, so inserting a key shifts every later leaf's position, and no incremental frontier reproduces the root. A root or trace is now O(n) 64-byte node hashes over 40-byte rows. The per-record decode + JCS + SHA-256, which was the expensive part, is gone from reads.
- **Not checked by the issue:** `get_v2_response` / `list_v6_response` add one `refs` row read per row. They don't scan, and were left as they were.

## #2596: proxied commit held the host lock and the process-wide chunk lock across the whole-file hash and the upload

Confirmed, including the `commit_direct` case (`direct_finish` is a remote call) that the issue hadn't checked.

- `commit_as` and `commit_direct` take the host lock only twice, briefly:
  1. to read the upload and mark it `committing_at`;
  2. to record the blob and convert the reservation.
- The whole-file verification (`finalize_precheck_for`) and `store.put` / `direct_finish` now run outside the host lock, under a **per-upload lock** that `abort_as` also takes.
- The sweeper leaves an upload alone for `COMMIT_HOLD_SECS` after its `committing_at`, so a slow commit is never released under itself. A commit that died is released after that window.
- A purge that aborts the upload mid-commit is detected on re-read. Any object just written that nothing names is deleted.
- Content-addressed keys keep two uploads of one blob correct: the second to record finds the first's entry and charges nothing, as before.
- `chunk_lock` in `vti-common` is now per bundle (64 stripes). A finalize's whole-file hash no longer stalls other transfers, backups included.
- Record writes (`prepare_record` / `prepare_release`) still take the host lock between their check and apply. That keeps reference counts and limit checks exact. The lock is now short, because nothing slow is ever held under it. A prune's `records_lock` holds only its room, and takes the host lock just for `release`.
- `migrate.rs` lock holders were left as they are. They copy blob bytes under the host lock and need their own restructuring. Noted, not done here.
- **Tests** (`blobs::lock_tests`): a commit blocked inside `store.put` doesn't hold up record reads and writes in its own room or another, another upload's begin/chunk/commit, or a sweep. Reads in a room share its lock, and a write in one room doesn't hold up another room.

## #2597: per-chunk work was O(chunk count)

Confirmed.

- **Upload / backup chunks.** The chunk plan (up to 4,096 digests) is written once, at initiate. Progress is now a separate bitmap row (`chunks-done:<id>`, ≤512 bytes), so a chunk no longer rewrites the plan. The per-chunk path reads the plan from an in-process cache: its digests are immutable and bundle ids are never reused.
- **Bundles opened before this change** have no bitmap row. Their first chunk reads the progress their plan recorded, so resumption is unchanged. `get_plan` still returns the plan with current progress, so the public `chunked` API is unchanged. `abort` and `delete_plan` remove the bitmap row as well.
- **Downloads.** `read_chunk` no longer decodes the stored manifest and re-runs `Manifest::parse` (including the `blob_ref` JCS-hash) for each chunk. It reads the blob's location without its manifest, and takes the parsed manifest from a small cache keyed by `blob_ref`, which names the manifest's own digest. `put_chunk_as` reads the upload record without its manifest.
- **Expiry sliding unchanged.** It still slides on every chunk: the bundle and download records are small, and changing when the expiry moves would change resumption semantics.

## #2604: casts fsynced the journal on a runtime thread under one all-communities mutex

Confirmed, including the issue's "not checked" item: an open cast writes a board entry *and* a receipt, so two `sync_data` calls.

- **Per-election sharding** (`vti-voting-service/src/boxes.rs`). Each election is a `BallotBox` of its own, under its own lock. A task names an election that isn't held here? It's answered by an empty box, so the refusal stays exactly the same (`electionUnknown`, after the payload checks).
- **Registration** runs under a registration lock that reads the community's unfinished count across shards, so quotas still hold.
- **Restore** rebuilds each journalled election into its own box.
- **Locked sections run on `spawn_blocking`.** That covers the dispatch, the cast pre-check and `names_party`. A journal write no longer stalls a tokio worker.
- **Durability unchanged.** Within one election, a task holds that election's lock from start to answer, and the journal writes `sync_data` before returning. An acknowledged cast is on disk, and no head covers an entry a crash could lose. No group commit was needed: elections are parallel to each other.
- **Journal handles.** `FileJournal` keeps each election's directory and log handles open, under a per-election lock, instead of opening and `create_dir_all`-ing on every append. A failed append is cut back off, so the next record never follows a torn one.
- **Provisional tally cache.** `vti-voting` caches the provisional tally, keyed by board length. Only a cast changes what's counted, and every cast appends. The type is private, so there is no API change.
- **Test.** An election whose lock is held doesn't hold up another election's `show`. A task on the held election waits for it. A restart gives each election its own box.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-rooms -p room-host -p vti-voting -p vti-voting-service`
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -E 'test(backup_transfer)'`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(room)'`
- the workspace `nextest` run, excluding VTC
- `cargo check -p vti-rooms --no-default-features --features mls --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- `cargo check -p vti-rooms-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`

Closes #2595
Closes #2596
Closes #2597
Closes #2604

title: perf(rooms)!: indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes (#2712)
body:
perf(rooms)!: indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes (#2712)

* perf(vti-common): per-bundle chunk lock and a progress bitmap apart from the plan

A chunked transfer's lock is striped by bundle id, so one bundle's finalize
(a whole-file hash) no longer stalls every other transfer (#2596). Progress
is a bitmap row beside the immutable plan, read from a per-process cache, so
a chunk no longer re-reads and rewrites a plan of up to 4,096 digests (#2597).
A bundle opened before the bitmap row existed keeps the progress its plan
recorded; get_plan still returns the plan with its progress.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-rooms)!: record indexes, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock

#2595: each record's leaf hash, the room's version order and its cached tree
head are kept beside the records and written in the record's own batch. A
read no longer decodes, canonicalises and hashes the whole room; a page
seeks by version. The head cache is invalidated with a fresh nonce on every
write and cached only over the marker it was computed after, so it is never
stale. The commitment is byte-for-byte the scan's (tests hold it through
every kind of write and for a room indexed lazily on first use). Record
reads hold a striped per-room lock shared.

#2596: a commit verifies the staged file and writes it to storage (or
finishes a direct upload) under its own upload lock, taking the host lock
only to mark the upload committing and to record the blob.

#2597: a served chunk reads the blob's location without its manifest and a
parsed manifest from a cache keyed by blob_ref; an uploaded chunk reads the
upload record without its manifest.

BREAKING: BlobHost::read_snapshot and records_lock take the room id.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-voting-service): one lock per election, journalled on blocking threads

#2604: each election is a ballot box of its own under its own lock, and the
locked section runs on spawn_blocking, so a cast's sync_data holds up only
its own election and never a runtime worker. Durability is unchanged: a task
holds its election from start to answer and the journal syncs before
returning. The journal keeps each election's files open under a lock of its
own, and the provisional tally is cached by board length.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): build the in-process ballot box service from Boxes

The voting-feature integration test still handed the voting service a single
BallotBox; the service now holds one box per election (#2604).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: docs(vtc-service): decomposition plan and where it stops
body:
Docs only. Adds `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-service-decomposition.md`, indexes it in `docs/README.md`, and points to it from `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`.

## #2573

All numbers re-measured on `origin/main` at `6cf8ad034`:

- 274,735 lines in `src/` (412 files, ~72k of them in-file tests) and 89,118 in `tests/`, so 363,853 in total.
- `AppState` has **87** public fields, not the 83 the issue counted. 52 of them are `*_ks` handles. The struct is built as a literal twice (`server.rs:1096`, `test_support.rs:769`), and `run` is 1,576 lines.
- 214 of 412 files name `AppState`.

**Corrections to the issue:**
- **The keyspace leaf already exists inside the crate.** `src/store/keyspaces.rs` has 61 names and the backup partition (37 backed up, 24 excluded) with its census. Step 1 is therefore an *extraction* of that file. Two complications:
  - seven of the names are `vti-rooms` re-exports, which a dependency-free leaf can't hold;
  - `all_matches_app_state_keyspace_count` asserts a literal 61, and its comment is stale ("48 top-level fields"; there are 52).
- **`registry/` is not a zero-coupling module.** Only one of its files names `AppState`, but `syncer`/`messaging`/`tail` need `members`, `directory`, `outbound`, `messaging`, `hooks` and `trust_tasks`. Only its pure half (~2.8k lines) is a candidate.
- **`recognition/` and `status_list/` need enabling moves.** They depend on `credentials::{proof_set, vm_resolver}`, `registry::TrustRegistryClient`, and `LocalSigner`, which in turn reaches `setup::bundle`.
- **`acl` ↔ `git_ns` is a cycle.** `acl/resource_grant.rs` and `acl/storage.rs` use `git_ns::model::{Right, BreakGlassMark, SingleAdminMark}`.

**Plan in the note:**
- **Step 0:** a `--timings` baseline. The VTA program never had one.
- **Step 1:** the `vtc-keyspaces` leaf.
- **Step 2:** per-subsystem store structs inside the crate. The census becomes structural and replaces the 38-arm `backed_up_handle` match. `run` is split into phases.
- **Step 3, in order:**
  - `vtc-policy`, after #2577;
  - the `acl` data core, after #2580, with the git-ns rights types moved down;
  - the registry pure half;
  - recognition and status_list, only if still wanted;
  - rooms through #2575's shared crate (no `vtc-rooms`);
  - the git-ns pure core, only on measured evidence.

**Issue order:** #2568 (to a leaf `vtc-audit` crate, not into `vtc-service`, or it blocks every extraction) → steps 0–2 → #2577 → #2579 → #2574 → policy → #2580 + acl → registry → (#2575 in parallel) → git-ns core.

**Publishing:**
- Every new crate must publish, because `vtc-service` publishes. Each also goes in `semver-report.sh`'s `EXCLUDED`.
- `policies/` moves with `vtc-policy`.
- The `fuzz` crate consumes `credentials::exchange`.
- The note lists the per-crate CI tripwires: members, Dockerfile.nitro, the crate map and count via `check-docs.py`, and the version requirements.

**Stopping point:** about 25k lines, under 10% of `src/`, can leave the crate, against the VTA's 23%. The spine stays: `trust_tasks`, `routes`, `ceremony`, `admin_actions` and the product features. Non-goals are listed in the note.

`python3 scripts/check-docs.py` passes.

Closes #2573
