title: perf(vtc-service)!: index and seek the VTC's hot full-keyspace scans (ACL authority, VRC digest, audit, members, rooms fingerprints, directory)
body:
Six performance findings in `vtc-service` (and one console setting), each a full-keyspace scan on a hot or repeated path. Every new index row is written in the same store batch as the row it describes, and boot (and a backup import) backfills it for data written before it existed.

## #2602 — admin-actions reads: an authority index instead of full ACL scans

- New `acladmin:<did>` index in the `acl` keyspace naming every entry that holds authority beyond membership (`acl::holds_authority`: any admin role or act/approve scope, any resource grant, any group grant — decided on stored fields only). Written in the entry's own batch by `store_acl_entry`, `delete_acl_entry` and the new `move_acl_entry`, which replaces the raw `move_if_unchanged` (`acl/swap-key`) and `swap` (member rotation) moves so a rotated administrator never drops out of the index. The git grant-holder index moves with it too; before this, a rotation left the new DID out of it.
- `list_authority_entries` reads through the index (resolved like `list_acl_entries`). Used by `live_admins`, `ViewCtx`, `approvers_for`, `role_assigners`, `routes::acl::other_unrestricted`, the board facilitator check and the `groups` fingerprint. A superset is harmless (readers re-check the rule); a subset is not (VTI-APV-009 counts), which is why every writer goes through the batch helpers.
- `refresh_locked` reads the live administrators once per pass instead of once per acknowledge item.
- `rebuild_authority_index` runs at boot and after a backup import. Tests: index follows store/promote/demote/grant/delete; a move is one journal record and maps refusals the way `move_if_unchanged` did; rebuild backfills raw rows and drops stale ones; the index always agrees with a full scan.
- Not done: "leave settling to the sweeper, not every read". That changes how fresh the action list is (up to a minute stale), which is a behaviour decision rather than a performance fix. With the index each settle costs O(administrators), not O(members).

## #2603 — relationship publish

- `relhash:<digest>` → id, in the **primary** `relationships` keyspace so it shares the row's batch (`store_relationship`); `delete_relationship` removes it in its batch. `find_by_hash` is one lookup and checks the digest of the row it names.
- `supersede_prior_edges` read every relationship on every publish too. It now reads the issuer's edges through the existing by-DID index.
- `rebuild_hash_index` at boot and after import. Checked the issue's "not checked" item: the by-DID index is **not** rebuilt at boot today (its writes are best-effort across two keyspaces). This PR does not change that.
- Left as is: `credentials::witness::resolve_binding` still recomputes against every stored VRC. It deliberately does not trust a stored digest column (its comment says why), so an index on that column is not a substitute.
- Left as is: the admin graph read (`list_all` + `list_members`). It is one admin-only read of the whole edge set by design.

## #2599 — audit log reads

- Hook relay `walk_audit_tail` seeks to the cursor (`range_from_raw("<ts>:")`) as `registry::tail` does, so a tick costs the rows written since the last one.
- `audit/list` pages newest-first with a reverse `scan_pager` from the cursor and stops one match past the page. The cursor is unchanged on the wire, so older cursors still resume.
- `effect_audited` (reconciling an interrupted action) seeks to the action's `created_at` (less an hour's margin) instead of reading the whole log.
- `git-ns/activity/list` and the namespace admin-record history read through a new **audit index** (`audit_index` keyspace, `crate::audit_index`), which names the `GitNsOperation` rows. Design choice: envelopes are written by `vti_common::audit::AuditWriter`, which is shared with the VTA, into a keyspace where every row must be an envelope (chain-head recovery reads the last key; verify counts any other row as unparseable). So index rows cannot ride in the writer's batch. Instead the index is a projection with a cursor: each catch-up writes its index rows **and** the advanced cursor in one batch, and every reader catches up first, so the index is exact up to the moment of reading. Boot catches up, which backfills an existing log. A backup import clears the index, which is excluded from backup and is rebuilt from the log. Lock-free: the cursor is advanced conditionally, and the loser of a race resumes from the winner's cursor. Tests: backfill, rows written later, reset/rebuild, racing catch-ups.
- `measure_chain`: the issue's reading of "O(log size)" was a misreading (it meant linear in the log). **No persisted chain-head/count pointer**, deliberately. The count is what a checkpoint attests, and the truncation check compares it with the rows. A pointer stored beside the rows is as rewritable as the rows by the store-level adversary checkpoints exist to catch, so the count must come from the rows. The doc comment now says this. What changed: `audit/verify` used to read the whole log three times (verify, measure, `find_entry_hash`). It now reads it twice, because `measure_chain_finding` returns the checkpoint's anchor from the measuring walk.

## #2601 — member and ACL lists

- `vtc/members/list/0.2`: seek paging from the cursor (`scan_pager`), with one ACL lookup per member row read. It no longer decodes every member and every ACL entry per page. The cursor is unchanged (last member key), so older cursors still resume. `totalEstimate` is counted once per walk, on the first page, from keys alone (plus each entry's role when a role filter is given). The first page is where the console count reads it (`limit: 1`). The count is carried in the signed cursor's opaque `snapshotId` to every later page, so a full walk costs one count, not one per page. A member admitted mid-walk shows up in the next walk's count. A cursor issued before this change carries the old unfiltered row count, which serves as the estimate until the walk ends.
- `acl/list` (`routes::acl::list_entries` / `page`) and `list_acl_entries_paginated`: seek paging, reading chunks only until the page and one further match are found. The cursor is unchanged.
- **Needs a spec change, not done:** server-side `q` and sort parameters. `vtc/members/list/0.2` defines only `role`, `cursor`, `limit` and `ext`. Adding search needs a new task version in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first, so the console still reads every page for its in-browser search. Each page is now linear, not quadratic.
- Console: the console-wide name book (which walks every `acl/list` page) is fresh for 5 minutes instead of 1. A labels endpoint or lazy per-DID naming would also need a spec change.

## #2598 — admin-console live channel

- The caller-independent `rooms` and `communityRooms` fingerprints are computed **once per bus position**, shared by all open streams (`shared_print`: a `tokio::sync::OnceCell` per position, keyed also by the service instance; no lock across the computation, per R1.3). A slot whose clock-driven wake has passed is recomputed. Before, each of up to 256 streams scanned every blob once a second during uploads.
- The `groups` fingerprint finds group managers through the authority index instead of the whole ACL.
- Not done: having `config_holdings` read the per-config usage counters. That is in `vti-rooms`, and the counters do not count what `config_holdings` reports (orphaned and moved copies, pending-delete bytes), so swapping one for the other would change the reported numbers. With the shared fingerprint it now runs once per change, not once per stream.

## #2600 — directory browse/search and dynamic groups

- `directory::read::subjects` reads members, the ACL, the cards with their `entry:` index and the `mg:` memberships in one scan each and joins them in memory. Before, it made about four store round trips per member.
- `groups::dynamic::recompute_all` reads the subjects once per pass (and not at all while no dynamic group exists). It no longer reads them once per group.
- `kick()` is debounced (2 s, coalescing every kick in the window into one pass), so a bulk admission is one recompute.
- Not done: recomputing only the changed entry, paging the directory from a sorted index, and `badges::rule_counts` per-subject scans. Each is a larger redesign; this PR removes the N+1 and the per-group multiplier.

Closes #2598
Closes #2600
Closes #2602
Closes #2603
Refs #2599 — all reads named in the issue are fixed. The chain-head pointer is declined for the security reason above, and `audit/verify` stays linear (it verifies every row).

* perf(vtc-service): an ACL authority index for approver and administrator reads (#2602)

acladmin:<did> names every entry holding authority beyond membership,
written in the entry's own batch (store, delete, and the new
move_acl_entry used by both key rotations), rebuilt at boot and after a
restore. live_admins, approvers_for, role_assigners, the action view and
the board facilitator check read it instead of the whole ACL; a refresh
pass reads the live administrators once. acl/list pages by seek (#2601).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vtc-service): a VRC digest index for idempotent publish (#2603)

relhash:<digest> is written in the relationship row's batch and removed
with it; find_by_hash is one lookup, supersession reads the issuer's
edges through the by-DID index, and boot and a restore backfill it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vtc-service): stop reading the whole audit log on list, tail and git-ns reads (#2599)

The hook relay seeks to its cursor; audit/list pages newest-first by a
reverse seek; effect reconciliation seeks to the action's creation; the
git-namespace reads go through an audit index (a cursor projection whose
rows and cursor commit in one batch, caught up before every read and at
boot); verify finds the checkpoint anchor in its measuring walk.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vtc-service): seek-paged member list, counted once per walk (#2601)

vtc/members/list reads one chunk of member rows and their ACL rows per
page from the cursor; totalEstimate is counted from keys on the first page
and carried in the signed cursor. Boot and backup import rebuild the new
indexes. The console's name book stays fresh for five minutes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vtc-service): share room fingerprints across streams, bulk directory subjects (#2598, #2600)

The rooms and communityRooms fingerprints are computed once per bus
position for every open stream; the groups fingerprint reads the
authority index. Directory subjects are four scans joined in memory, a
dynamic-group pass reads them once, and kicks are debounced.

* perf(vtc-service): acl/list pages by seek and swap-key moves the index rows (#2601, #2602)

acl/list reads the ACL in chunks from the cursor until the page and one
further match are found, instead of decoding and sorting every entry per
page; the cursor is unchanged. acl/swap-key moves the entry with its
authority and grant-holder rows (move_acl_entry), and the attrition count
reads the authority index.

title: security(vtc-service): setup writes the admin key to an owner-only file, never stdout
body:
## #2703: setup printed the admin private key

Verified on current main: `print_setup_summary_interactive` offered (default-no confirm) to print the long-term admin DID's `DidKeyMaterialV2` JSON to stdout, with `TODO(#2703)`. `setup --from` never printed it but also never kept it, and told the operator to "re-run interactively", which provisions again.

**Fix.** One hand-over in the shared `apply` effect path, used by both front-ends:

- The key goes to `<data_dir>/keys/admin-key.json` through `vti_common::secure_file::write_secret_file`. The file is created new with mode `0600` and synced, and the directory is `0700`. This happens before the install token is minted.
- Setup prints only the path: an `Admin key:` line in the wizard summary and `admin_key_file=<path>` in the terse block.
- An existing `admin-key.json` is never overwritten, since it may be the only copy of an earlier key. A re-run writes `admin-key.<timestamp>.json` beside it.
- `SetupOutcome.admin_key_json: Option<String>` became `admin_key_file: Option<PathBuf>`, so the key never sits in the outcome. The type is crate-private, so no API change.

**Why a file and not the OS keyring or a sealed transfer.** It is the pattern this setup already uses for key material that has to outlive the run: `--setup-key-out` (`EphemeralSetupKey::persist_to`, 0600) and `vtc keys request` (`<data_dir>/keys/…`, 0600). A keyring write would need an agreed service/entry format with a consumer, and none exists. `cnm`/`pnm` keep their own identities and do not import this key. A sealed transfer needs a recipient DID the operator does not have at this point. Design question for review: if a consumer later wants the key in the keyring, add that beside the file and don't print the key again.

**Docs:** `docs/03-vtc/{getting-started,non-interactive-setup,bootstrap-runbook}.md` and the historical note in `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-console-signing.md`. `scripts/check-docs.py` passes.

**Tests:** new `admin_key_is_written_owner_only_and_never_overwritten` (round-trips the material, checks 0600/0700 and no overwrite). `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service` passed 3677/3677. `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

Closes #2703

## Not in this PR: #2702 (step-up approval performs no user verification)

I left #2702 open. The VTI specification has no requirement for this RP step-up approval token: it is an interop artefact with the did-hosting verifier, and no requirement says what user verification it must carry. The issue's own options are a CLI confirm, a passkey at the VTA, a push to the principal's approver device, or a divergence-register entry. Choosing one is a design decision, and the register entry would land in the spec repository. Neither is a contained fix here.

title: build(https)!: jsonwebtoken 11 in trust-tasks-https, jsonschema 0.60 in trust-tasks-rs
body:
Dependency alignment requested by OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2655. VTI builds two `jsonschema` majors and two `jsonwebtoken` majors because of these crates:

| Crate | Dependency | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks-rs` (`validate`) | `jsonschema` | `0.49` (VTI's lock resolves 0.46.10 through trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2) | `0.60` |
| `trust-tasks-https` (`jwt`) | `jsonwebtoken` | `10` | `11` |

The versions match VTI's `jsonschema = "0.60"` and `jsonwebtoken = "11"`. `jsonschema` 0.61 is out, but this PR targets 0.60 so the two workspaces share one copy.

**No source changes were needed.** The only API `trust-tasks-rs` uses, `options().with_draft(Draft202012).build()` and `iter_errors`, is unchanged across 0.49→0.60. jsonwebtoken 11 keeps `decode`, `DecodingKey`, `Validation` and the `aws_lc_rs` feature.

## Why the `!`

- **`jsonschema` is private to `trust-tasks-rs`.** No jsonschema type appears in its public API (`ValidationError` is its own type), so this bump is not a break.
- **`jsonwebtoken` is public.** `trust-tasks-https` exposes it through `JwtBearerAuth::new(key: DecodingKey, validation: Validation, …)`. A consumer that builds those values with jsonwebtoken 10 no longer compiles, so the `jwt` feature's API breaks.
- `cargo-semver-checks` does not report this kind of break (a dependency's type changing major), so the title declares it: `build(https)!`.
- Under `release-plz.toml`'s `core` group, the `!` marks the next release of the whole group as breaking (0.39 → 0.40). No other breaking change has merged since `trust-tasks-rs-v0.39.0`, so this PR alone causes that bump. If that is unwanted, the alternative is to split the `jsonwebtoken` half out and hold it for the next batch of breaking changes; the `jsonschema` half is non-breaking on its own.

`deny.toml`: one comment no longer names jsonschema 0.46.

## #2622: cached compiled validator

VTI's #2622 asks for a `compiled_for(type_uri)` accessor. **None is added here, because the cache already exists.** `trust_tasks_rs::validate::SchemaValidator` (released in 0.38.0, #1215) compiles each schema once and caches it by the schema text's address, confirmed against its content. VTI gets the requested behaviour with:

```rust
static VALIDATOR: SchemaValidator = SchemaValidator::new();
VALIDATOR.check(vti_specs::schema_index::schema_for(uri)?, &payload)
```

VTI is on 0.37.x, which has only the per-call `against_schema`; its fix is to take 0.38+ and switch to `SchemaValidator`. A `compiled_for` inside the `schema_index` that `trust-tasks-build` generates would pull `jsonschema` into every consumer's generated crate, even ones that only want type lookups. It would also duplicate a cache the runtime already has.

## Checks run locally

All pass:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with and without `--all-features`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate,all-specs --all-targets`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --features trust-tasks/all-specs`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-https --features jwt --all-targets`
- `consumer-app` run and test, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-build --all-features`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-cli`
- `cargo deny check`
- `npm run check-version-edits`, `check-release-lists`, `test:checks`
- `scripts/check-rs-api-compat.sh`: reports no undeclared break.

title: feat(rooms): load-older paging by version (records/list 0.8, keys/browse 0.6) and host size limits in rooms/info 0.5
body:
Spec additions requested by a wallet integrator in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2294 (points 3 and 4).

## New versions

| Type URI | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/records/list/0.8` | `beforeVersion`: an exclusive upper bound on `version`, the counterpart of `sinceVersion`, under either `order` |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/keys/browse/0.6` | passes `beforeVersion` through to the host's `records/list/0.8` (sealed rooms' read path) |
| `https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/info/0.5` (`extends: "0.4"`) | optional `maxRecordDocumentBytes` and `maxChunkSize` in the response |

### records/list 0.8 and keys/browse 0.6

`order` (`oldestFirst` default / `newestFirst`) and the cursor that continues in the requested order already shipped in records/list 0.7 and keys/browse 0.5 (#1088), so the enum is untouched. The integrator also asked for a `beforeVersion` bound, so a client can "load older" by passing the lowest version it holds. That works without keeping the host's short-lived cursor, which is lost on an app restart.

- `beforeVersion` is exclusive and applies on every page, alongside `sinceVersion`. If `beforeVersion <= sinceVersion + 1` the page is empty, not an error.
- A cursor now belongs to the `order`, `sinceVersion` and `beforeVersion` it was issued under. Under any other it is refused with `invalidCursor`.
- The newest-first guarantee is restated within the band: a page with bound `B` and lowest version `V` holds every record whose current version lies in (V, B). A record edited since has moved above `B`, and the reader finds it from its watermark.
- `beforeVersion` makes a listing non-comparable against `recordCount`. The count rule is updated in both specs.
- Neither version declares `extends`. A previous-version host that pruned the bound away would answer "load older" with the room's head, the same reasoning 0.7 used for `order`. keys/browse 0.6 answers `hostRefused` instead of dropping the bound.
- records/list 0.8 gains request and response examples, so its 0.7 baseline entry is removed from `spec-examples-allowlist.json`.

### rooms/info 0.5

- **`maxRecordDocumentBytes`** is the largest `rooms/records/put` document the host accepts, measured the way `maxDocumentBytes` measures it. The host MUST state it when it keeps a per-record limit of its own (refused with `recordTooLarge`). It is never above the declared bound, which is 2,097,152 bytes at records/put 0.6.
- **`maxChunkSize`** (`$ref` `ChunkSize`, 16,384–262,144) is the largest proxied chunk the host admits at its own size, without refusing it or charging it to a stricter budget. A 262,144-byte chunk fits `rooms/blobs/upload/chunk/0.2`'s 360,448-byte document bound. A direct transfer is not bound by it.
- File limits and per-member quotas were already in the response from 0.1 (`limits`: `RoomLimits`, and `usage.member.limits`). The spec now says so explicitly instead of duplicating them.

### records/put `maxDocumentBytes`

This PR does not touch it. records/put 0.6 (#1252, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.39.0) already declares `maxDocumentBytes.request: 2097152`. A 64 KiB or 360,448-byte bound would make records some hosts store today non-conforming, which is what #1252's rationale rejects. The figure a client needs (a host's own smaller per-record limit, such as the VTC's 65,536-byte default) is what `rooms/info/0.5`'s `maxRecordDocumentBytes` now advertises.

## Other changes

- `npm run fix-stale-references` rewrote prose links from list 0.7 and browse 0.5 to the new versions in eight current rooms specs. Text only, no wire pins.
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.6` targets framework `0.6.0` (0.5 targeted `0.5.0`), and its `ext` `$ref`s point at `_framework/0.4`, whose `Ext` is identical to `_framework/0.1`'s.
- All four bindings are regenerated: `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`, `npm run build`
- `npm run check-bindings`: 1400 specs agree across Rust, TS, Go and Dart.
- `npm run build-bundles` then `npm run check-bundles`: 1394 bundles verified.
- `npm run check-spec-lifecycle`, `check-framework-spec`, `check-doc-facts`, `check-release-lists`, `check-dart-packages`, `check-sibling-core-ranges`, `check-version-edits`, `test:checks`
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: the eight released files changed additively (prose only).
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features rooms,validate --all-targets`, `go build ./... && go vet ./specs/rooms/...`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos lib/specs/rooms`, `tsc --noEmit` in `trust-tasks-ts`

body:

rooms/records/list 0.8 adds `beforeVersion`, an exclusive upper bound on

cursor is the host's, short-lived and lost with the client's state. It
applies under either order, and a cursor now belongs to the bounds as well
as the order it was issued under. Not `extends: "0.7"`: a 0.7 host that
pruned the bound would answer "load older" with the room's head.

rooms/keys/browse 0.6 passes `beforeVersion` through for a member whose
surface reaches the room only through their key holder, and answers
`hostRefused` rather than drop the bound against a host without
records/list 0.8.

rooms/info 0.5 (`extends: "0.4"`) adds two optional response members so a
client can refuse before it writes: `maxRecordDocumentBytes`, the largest
rooms/records/put document the host accepts (its own per-record limit,
refused with `recordTooLarge`, never above put 0.6's declared 2 MiB), and
`maxChunkSize`, the largest proxied chunk it admits at its own size. File
limits and the member's allowance were already in the response (`limits`,
`usage.member.limits`).

Requested by a wallet integrator (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2294,
points 3 and 4). `order` itself shipped in records/list 0.7 / keys/browse
0.5 (#1088) and put's `maxDocumentBytes` in records/put 0.6 (#1252).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix(rs,https,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document that marks an unrecognized ext namespace critical (#1256)
body:
fix(rs,https,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document that marks an unrecognized ext namespace critical (#1256)

* fix(rs,https,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document that marks an unrecognized ext namespace critical

SPEC §4.5.2 rule 4: a consumer that does not recognize a namespace named in
extCritical MUST NOT process the document and MUST reject it with
unsupportedExtension. No runtime read the member, so a document whose payload
type does not model it was processed as if the namespace were absent.

Each runtime gains a check (check_critical_extensions, checkCriticalExtensions,
CheckCriticalExtensions) that walks the payload as received alongside its
schema, applies rules 1, 2 and 4, and runs in every consume pipeline after
the proof and per-specification checks and before the item-11 record. The
recognized namespaces are a new consume-checks option, empty by default.
Shared vectors in fixtures/consume/ext-critical.json pin the four together.

title: ci: harden CI and the build: pinned toolchain, image digests, release-token checks, advisories, fuzzing, tooling lint
body:
CI and build hardening from the 2026-11-11 review of `main` (CI, build and dependencies area). One commit per issue or theme.

## Required checks (#2647) — what to configure

Add these job names as required status checks on `main` (alongside `DCO` and `branch rules`):

| Check name | Workflow | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Format` | ci.yml | always runs |
| `lockfile resolves` | ci.yml | always runs |
| `lockfile self-pins` | ci.yml | always runs |
| `cargo-deny` | ci.yml | always runs |
| `authorization-context types` | ci.yml | always runs |
| `commit lint` | pr-title.yml | runs on every PR event incl. title edits |
| `Clippy` | ci.yml | skipped by its `affects` gate on prose-only PRs; a job-level skip reports as passing |

None of the workflows that carry these has a workflow-level `paths:` filter, so every PR gets a result for every one of them. New tier-0 job `scripts and workflows` (below) is a good eighth candidate once it has a few green runs.

Root `CLAUDE.md` ("A merge is not evidence…") now states the required set. `CODEOWNERS` is kept as is: code-owner review may be enabled later. `docs/04-reference/workspace-engineering-notes.md` and `RELEASING.md` now say the same.

## Per issue

**#2658 items 4 and 5 — toolchain pin, Dependabot gaps.** `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `1.95.0` (= workspace `rust-version` = the Dockerfiles' Rust image). Every job now runs `scripts/install-rust-toolchain.sh` instead of `rustup toolchain install stable` + `rustup default stable`. Deliberate exceptions: the MSRV job (sets `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=$MSRV`: `rustup default` would have been overridden by the toolchain file, so the first toolchain bump would have made "MSRV" silently check the pin), the three cargo-semver-checks jobs (semver report, release bump guard, release-branch prep: `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable`, because the latest cargo-semver-checks reads a window of recent rustdoc JSON formats) and fuzz (dated nightly). `scripts/check-toolchain-pins.sh` fails when the pin is below the MSRV or a Dockerfile hides its Rust version in an ARG, and warns when a Dockerfile's Rust drifts from the pin. Dependabot gains `rust-toolchain`, `npm` (`vtc-service/admin-ui`) and `cargo /fuzz` entries.
  Clippy 1.95 is stricter than the stable CI had been running in two lints (`nonminimal_bool`, `collapsible_match`), so 13 places in 12 files change to pass it: De Morgan rewrites (`!x.is_some_and(p)` → `x.is_none_or(!p)`, checked line by line), two `Option::take().map` rewrites in vta-persona, and one `#[allow(clippy::collapsible_match)]` on `vti_voting::audit::check_order`, where turning the `if` into a match guard would let a failing guard fall through to later arms. Verified: `cargo +1.95.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and the narrowed feature-combo clippy builds are clean; `cargo fmt` under 1.95 is clean.

**#2649 — nextest.** Installed through the pinned `taiki-e/install-action` as `cargo-nextest@0.9.150` (checksummed; a version that action release lists). `check-workflow-action-pins.sh` now also fails on any workflow line that pipes `curl` into `tar`/`sh`/`bash`.

**#2659 — tooling lint.** New tier-0 job `scripts and workflows`: `shellcheck -x -S warning` over every tracked `*.sh`, `actionlint` 1.7.12 (versioned download, `sha256sum -c`), `py_compile` of `scripts/*.py`, `deploy/nitro/deploy-common.test.sh`, and the toolchain-pin check. `scripts/ci-affects.test.sh` holds `ci-affects.sh` to a 22-row path → answer table and runs first in the `affects` job (a `CI_AFFECTS_TEST_CHANGED` hook replaces the diff for the test). The inline apt-with-retry blocks (ci.yml ×4, publish.yml ×2) now call `scripts/install-build-deps.sh`. shellcheck found a real bug: `deploy-enclave.sh --pcr0/--pcr8` were parsed and never read, so a caller passing them got no check; they now compare against `nitro-cli describe-eif` before anything starts.

**#2644 — join_didcomm soak.** Builds `--test it`, selects `.target.name == "it"`, runs `join_didcomm::didcomm_join_round_trips_…` with `--exact`, uses `install-build-deps.sh` and `./.github/actions/rust-cache` (saves from main only). `Feature combos (mediator-backed)` now builds the same binary and asserts the test is still listed, so the soak cannot rot again.

**#2652 — Docker build cache.** BuildKit registry cache on `ghcr.io/openvtc/vti-buildcache:{vta,vta-nitro}`, `mode=max`. Pull requests and nightly read it (`packages: read`); only the new `image-main` job (push to main) writes it and is the only one with `packages: write`. The build steps moved into `.github/actions/docker-image` so the two jobs share them. The plain `Dockerfile` cooked into `RUN --mount=type=cache` directories, which a registry cache cannot carry (the cook layer would be empty on every runner), so its cook and build now write into the layer, as `Dockerfile.nitro` already did. The stale "~10 GB" comment is replaced (the allowance is 25 GB and full; ghcr is outside it). The first main push creates the package; if org policy blocks GITHUB_TOKEN from creating an org package, `image-main` will fail at the cache export and the package has to be created once by an admin.

**#2653 — base image pins.** Every `FROM` is `image:tag@sha256:…`; the Rust version is inline (`rust:1.95.0-bookworm@…`) so Dependabot sees it. The Nitro runtime's apk packages are pinned to exact v3.24 versions, dependencies included; when Alpine replaces one, the build fails instead of silently changing PCR0 (the Dockerfile says where to look up the new versions). `libc6-compat` was dropped from the list: in 3.24 it is only a name `gcompat` provides. Reproducibility: new job `Nitro image is reproducible` in docker.yml (`scripts/check-nitro-reproducible.sh`) builds Dockerfile.nitro twice on fresh builders with `--no-cache`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and `rewrite-timestamp=true`, and compares the manifests layer by layer. It runs weekly and on dispatch, not per PR: two cold enclave builds are about an hour of runner time. Its first result is the first measurement; I could not run it locally (no Docker daemon here). `deploy/nitro/build-vta.sh` does not set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, so an operator-built EIF is not yet byte-reproducible even if this check passes; left for a follow-up.

**#2646 — release token.** New `.github/actions/release-token`: uses a GitHub App installation token when `vars.RELEASE_APP_ID` and `secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` exist (`actions/create-github-app-token` v3.3.0), else `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`, else (where a degraded token is acceptable) `GITHUB_TOKEN`; either way it calls `GET /repos/{repo}` first and fails with `::error::<name> is invalid or cannot see <repo>`. Used by publish.yml (one token per publishing pass, since an App token lives an hour), backport.yml (no fallback: a backport PR must trigger CI), nightly.yml and release-branch.yml (minted again before the push, after the long semver step). ci.yml's release-bump raise step validates its PAT the same way. release-branch.yml runs from the release branch's own copy, so existing branches (eucalyptus) pick this up only when cut again.
  Backport re-run: no PR merged between 2026-11-10 10:06Z and 22:41Z (#2547, #2548, #2549, #2551, #2552, #2554, #2557, #2527) ever carried a `backport release/*` label (checked the label events), so nothing was dropped and nothing needed re-running.
  **Admin step remaining:** create a GitHub App for the org with Contents: write, Pull requests: write, Workflows: write (if release PRs touch workflows), Metadata: read; install it on this repository; set repository variable `RELEASE_APP_ID` and secret `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Then `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` can be retired. Note the DCO exemption in `.github/dco.yml` relies on the release commit being authored by an org member; an App-authored release commit is not, so check the Release PR's DCO result on the first App-token run (the fix-up commits carry `Signed-off-by` already).

**#2648 — advisories on a schedule.** New `advisories.yml`: daily, a matrix over `main` and every `release/[a-z]+` branch, each checked out at its tip with its own `deny.toml`, `cargo deny check advisories` over the root, `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy` and `fuzz` manifests where present; on failure it opens (or comments on) an issue labelled `advisory-scan`. Baseline, run locally against `release/eucalyptus` (6caec1bdc): **19 advisories in the root lock** (RUSTSEC-2026-0346/0347/0348/0349/0367/0368/0369/0374/0381/0382/0383/0385/0386/0387/0429/0441/0457/0461/0462) and 9 in enclave-proxy; fuzz clean. The first scheduled run will open the issue. CI could not be dispatched on `release/eucalyptus`: its `ci.yml` has no `workflow_dispatch` trigger (and a dispatch uses the branch's own file), so the baseline is the local scan above.

**#2645 — fuzz.** Correction to the issue: there is no tracked `fuzz/Cargo.lock` on `main` (`fuzz/.gitignore` excludes it), so the 0.13.1 entry was a stale local file. That stays the design: a committed lock would record this workspace's own versions and break on every release; CI copies the root `Cargo.lock` in instead, so third-party versions match what the workspace tested. Five new targets: `fuzz_sealed_transfer_armor` (`armor::decode` + `open_bundle_with_policy`), `fuzz_bootstrap_request` (`BootstrapRequest::verify_value`), `fuzz_sd_jwt_presentation`, `fuzz_vp_token` (`flatten_vp_token` then `parse_sd_jwt_presentation` per entry) and `fuzz_oid4vci_proof` (`verify_oid4vci_proof`, fixed audience and clock); the last three call `vtc_service::credentials::exchange` (no default features, so no npm build), since those parsers exist nowhere else. New `fuzz.yml`: builds every target on PRs/pushes touching `fuzz/`, `vta-sdk/` or `vtc-service/src/credentials/exchange/`, and nightly runs each target 300 s over its seeds, uploading `artifacts/` on a crash; nightly pinned to `nightly-2026-10-16`, cargo-fuzz 0.13.2. The ci.yml cargo-deny job scans `fuzz/` too. READMEs list every target. All seven targets build locally (`cargo +nightly fuzz build --release`) and each ran 30 s over its seeds with no crash (43k–244k executions each). Found on the way: `vtc-service` does not compile with `--no-default-features` (`url`, `website` and `seal_trust_task_tsp` are used outside their feature gates, 14 errors); the harness therefore enables `setup,website,tsp` (no `admin-ui`, so no npm). No CI job builds that combination; worth an issue of its own.

**#2650 — VTC suite twice.** Measured before choosing (`cargo nextest list -p vtc-service`, default vs `--features vetting-pcs,voting`): 3,667 vs 3,769 tests; **102 exist only under the features** (election_tasks 22, board_tasks 21, hidden_vetting_tasks 18, vetting::pcs* 27, routes::join_requests::manifest 5, the rest elections:: / notifications::election), none only in the default build. The features are not purely additive (`cfg(not(feature = "voting"))` arms in board_tasks, `cfg!(feature …)` assertions in join_requests, trust_task_manifest, conformance, vm_resolver, vetting), so option 2 (full suite only under the features) would drop the default build's behaviour, and option 1 alone could miss a gated path. Chosen: on a **pull request** `Test (VTC, vetting-pcs)` still runs clippy for the feature set but nextest only over a filterset naming every gated module (468 tests, all 102 feature-only ones included); on **push** (main, nightly, release/**) it runs the full suite and doctests as before. Coverage on main is unchanged; the PR saving is the run time of ~3,300 repeated tests (the feature build itself still has to compile).

**#2651 — Release PR pushed twice.** Refs only. Both routes the issue suggests are blocked here: (1) release-plz has no hook between its version computation and its push, and `release-pr` rebuilds from a fresh copy, so the fix-up cannot be applied before the first push; (2) running release-plz with the default token so only the fix-up push triggers CI does not work in this repository: `can_approve_pull_request_reviews` is `false`, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot open the Release PR, and its commit would be authored by `github-actions[bot]`, which is not an org member, so the `.github/dco.yml` exemption the release commit relies on would no longer apply and DCO (required) would fail. The superseded run is cancelled within about a minute by ci.yml's PR concurrency group, so the cost is roughly a minute of the tier-0 jobs per merge. Revisit if release-plz gains a pre-push hook or the DCO exemption changes.

## Verification

- Rebased onto main after #2706/#2707/#2710 (one conflict, `fuzz/seeds/README.md`; the Format job keeps #2706's `check-docs.py` step). After the rebase: clippy 1.95 `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and the `vetting-pcs,voting` set clean (#2710 needed no changes), `cargo fmt` and `check-docs.py` clean, fuzz targets build.

- `actionlint` (1.7.12, with shellcheck) clean over every workflow; `shellcheck -x -S warning` clean over every tracked script; `bash scripts/ci-affects.test.sh` 22/22; `deploy-common.test.sh` 11/11.
- `cargo +1.95.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, plus the feature-combo clippy sets; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- Fuzz: all seven targets build on nightly and ran 30 s each over their seeds, no crash.
- Tests for the crates whose Rust changed, locally under the pin: vta-persona, vti-voting, vta-mobile-core, vta-service 2878/2878; vtc-service + vtc-client 3724/3736, the 12 failures all `admin_ui` / portal-bundle tests that fail only because the run set `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` (CI's `Test (VTC)` builds the bundle and passed).
- **The pin moved one test.** `vta-service`'s VTI-08 stack test (`contexts/create` must fit a debug worker stack) overflowed its 768 KiB budget on CI under 1.95 x86_64: older Rust lays debug frames out larger. Its failure now reports how much the build needs (this one: 768–896 KiB), and the budget is 960 KiB, still under the >1 MiB a regression of VTI-08 takes.
- CI on this PR (run 43465347288, all jobs green incl. the soak-target check in Feature combos (mediator-backed)): every ci.yml job, both Docker images (digest-pinned bases and the pinned apk set build; the registry-cache read degrades to a cold build as intended) and `Fuzz targets build` passed.
- Not run locally: the Docker builds and the reproducibility job (no Docker daemon here), `--all-features` clippy (needs libtss2 on Linux). CI's own run on this PR covers the first and the last.

Closes #2644
Closes #2645
Closes #2648
Closes #2649
Closes #2650
Closes #2652
Closes #2653
Closes #2659
Refs #2646 — remaining: an org admin creates the release GitHub App and sets `RELEASE_APP_ID` / `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (above).
Refs #2647 — remaining: add the seven checks above as required on `main` (repository settings / ruleset).
Refs #2651 — not changed; why above.
Refs #2658 — items 4 and 5 here; items 1–3 (lints, `unsafe_code`, publish comments) are in another sweep PR; item 6 (stale branches, the probe workflow) not in scope; the probe workflow is already `disabled_manually`.

title: ci: harden CI and the build: pinned toolchain, image digests, release-token checks, advisories, fuzzing, tooling lint (#2709)
body:
ci: harden CI and the build: pinned toolchain, image digests, release-token checks, advisories, fuzzing, tooling lint (#2709)

* build: pin the Rust toolchain to 1.95.0 and pass clippy 1.95 (#2658)

rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.95.0, the workspace rust-version and the Dockerfiles' Rust image. CI jobs install it with scripts/install-rust-toolchain.sh instead of a floating stable, so a new Rust release's lints can no longer turn main red with no code change; Dependabot proposes the next one as a PR. scripts/check-toolchain-pins.sh keeps the pin at or above the MSRV and the Dockerfiles in line.

Clippy 1.95 is stricter than the stable CI ran in nonminimal_bool and collapsible_match: De Morgan rewrites at eleven call sites (behaviour unchanged), Option::take().map in vta-persona, and one allow on vti_voting::audit::check_order, where a match guard would fall through to later arms.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(docker): digest-pin every base, pin the Nitro apk set, and cache builds on ghcr (#2652, #2653)

Every FROM is image:tag@sha256 with the Rust version inline, so Dependabot moves tag and digest. The Nitro runtime's apk packages are pinned to exact versions, dependencies included, so PCR0 moves only with a commit. A weekly job builds Dockerfile.nitro twice on fresh builders (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, rewritten timestamps) and compares the manifests layer by layer.

Builds read a BuildKit registry cache on ghcr.io/openvtc/vti-buildcache (mode=max); only the main-push job writes it and holds packages: write. The plain Dockerfile's cook and build now write into the layer rather than cache mounts, which a registry cache cannot carry.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: validate the release token first, and use a GitHub App token when one is configured (#2646)

A new release-token action picks an App installation token (vars.RELEASE_APP_ID + secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY), else RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN, else GITHUB_TOKEN where that is acceptable, and fails with an explicit error when the token cannot see the repository. Release-plz, Backport, Nightly and release-branch prep use it; the publish passes and the release-branch push each mint their own, since an App token lives an hour.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: scan main and every release branch for advisories daily (#2648)

cargo deny check advisories over the root, enclave-proxy and fuzz manifests of each ref, with that ref's own deny.toml; a failure opens or updates an advisory-scan issue.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: build the fuzz harness on every relevant change, run it nightly, and add the five missing targets (#2645)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: point the join_didcomm soak at the `it` test target (#2644)

vtc-service has one integration-test target, `it`; the soak still built `--test join_didcomm`, which no longer exists. It now builds `it`, runs join_didcomm::didcomm_join_round_trips_… with --exact, installs packages through install-build-deps.sh and caches through the repository's rust-cache wrapper (saved from main only). Feature combos (mediator-backed) builds the same binary and checks the test is listed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: lint the CI's own tooling, pin nextest, split the VTC feature rerun, and require the cheap gates (#2647, #2649, #2650, #2659)

New tier-0 job `scripts and workflows`: shellcheck over every tracked script, actionlint (versioned, checksummed), py_compile, deploy-common.test.sh and the toolchain-pin check; ci-affects.sh is held to a path -> answer table in the affects job. The inline apt blocks call install-build-deps.sh. shellcheck found deploy-enclave.sh's --pcr0/--pcr8 parsed and never read; they now check the EIF's measurements.

cargo-nextest comes from the pinned taiki-e/install-action at a fixed version, and the pin check refuses a download piped into tar/sh/bash.

Test (VTC, vetting-pcs) runs the feature-affected tests on a pull request (468 of 3,769; all 102 feature-only tests among them) and the full suite on push.

cargo-deny scans fuzz/. Dependabot covers the admin UI's npm lockfile, fuzz/ and rust-toolchain.toml. CLAUDE.md states the required checks.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci(fuzz): build vtc-service with the features it compiles under

vtc-service does not build with no features (url, website and the TSP sealing are used outside their gates); the harness takes setup, website and tsp, still without the admin-UI npm build. All seven targets build and ran 30 s each over their seeds with no crash.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: install the toolchain from the repository root in the enclave-proxy job

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): say how much stack contexts/create needs when the VTI-08 budget is exceeded

Debug frame sizes move between Rust releases and targets: under the pinned 1.95 on x86_64 the 768 KiB budget overflowed where newer stable fits. The failure now reports the smallest of 896/1024/1280/1536/2048 KiB that does fit, so it tells the >1 MiB regression this test exists for from a compiler that lays frames out larger.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): give the VTI-08 stack test the budget the pinned 1.95 needs (960 KiB)

Under rust-toolchain.toml's 1.95 on x86_64, contexts/create needs between 768 and 896 KiB in a debug build (measured by the previous commit's report in CI). 960 KiB fits it with room and still fails the >1 MiB regression the test exists for.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: name the required checks in the engineering notes and RELEASING.md (#2647)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: install the pinned toolchain in the manifest hygiene job

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe
body:
Dependency and manifest hygiene from the 2026-11-11 CI/build audit. Re-verified against `origin/main` at 17f913de7.

## #2654 — `deny.toml` gets `[sources]` and `[bans]`

- `[sources]`: `unknown-registry = "deny"`, `unknown-git = "deny"`.
- `[bans]`:
  - `deny = [rsa (wrappers: pgp), openssl (wrappers: webauthn-rs-core, webauthn-attestation-ca)]`, so a second user of either fails CI. Verified with `cargo tree -i`: those are today's only parents.
  - `wildcards = "deny"`, with `allow-wildcard-paths = true`. Versionless dev-only path deps are deliberate, for release-plz ordering.
  - `multiple-versions = "deny"`, with a `skip` list seeded from today's duplicates in the root graph and the enclave proxy's graph. There are 108 entries in 8 groups, each with a comment giving its cause: the previous RustCrypto generation, rand, jsonschema/schemars, jsonwebtoken, the webauthn-rs 0.5 stack, the HTTP stack (tungstenite/tower-http/base64), build-time proc-macros, and small-crate churn. Each entry's `reason` names the immediate dependents. Entries use version requirements (`name:<X`), so a patch release on an old line does not fail CI.
- Advisory ignores: `cargo deny` (all features) reported two as `advisory-not-detected`, `RUSTSEC-2026-0381` (webpki-roots 0.26) and `RUSTSEC-2024-0436` (paste). Both are removed.
- `crypto-bigint` 0.7.6 was yanked (a `cargo deny` warning). The lock now has 0.7.11, and the RUSTSEC-2026-0387 note is updated.
- The stale `[graph]` comment is rewritten. The lock no longer has hyper 0.14, h2 0.3 or rustls 0.21. The comment now says why `all-features` is still needed (`tee`, `mls`, `*-secrets`).
- The file header now describes all four checks.

`cargo deny check advisories bans sources licenses` (0.20.2, the version the action ships) passes on the root workspace and on `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy` with `--config deny.toml`. That scan reads the same file, so it reports most skip entries as `unmatched-skip` (warnings only). The comment says so.

## #2655 — duplicates (in-workspace parts only)

- The duplicates are now enforced and listed with their causes (above).
- `jsonschema` 0.46 (trust-tasks-rs) and `jsonwebtoken` 10 (trust-tasks-https) stay as skip entries pointing at those crates. The bumps are being done in that repository.
- `vta-sdk`'s `x509-parser` now inherits the workspace entry (`verify-aws`) instead of `verify` (the ring path). `ring` is now only a direct dependency under `attest-verify`, for the COSE_Sign1 check. `cargo tree -i ring` is empty for `vta-service` and `vtc-service`.
- `rand` 0.8 stays as a direct dependency of `vti-vetting-pcs`, `vti-voting` and `cnm-cli` (dev), as dependabot.yml documents.
- `Refs` rather than `Closes`: the upstream bumps remain.

## #2656 — unused dependencies

I installed `cargo-machete` and ran `cargo machete --with-metadata`. Every hit was checked by grep for `ident::` / `use ident` and by building. Removed:

- `vta-cli-common`: `aes-gcm`, `hkdf`, `reqwest`, `x25519-dalek`
- `vta-service`: `affinidi-status-list`, `argon2`, `aws-lc-rs`, `axum-extra`, `fjall`, `libc`, `regorus`, `serde_ignored`, `subtle`, `trust-tasks-proof`. `aws-lc-rs` and `libc` were also dropped from the `tee` feature.
- `vtc-service`: `aws-smithy-runtime-api`, `axum-extra`, `bip39`, `keyring-core` (and from the `keyring` feature), `tokio-util`, `trust-tasks-https`
- `vta-sdk`: `x25519-dalek` (and from `sealed-transfer`)
- `vti-common`: `affinidi-data-integrity`, `bytes` (normal and dev)
- `vti-secrets`: `google-cloud-auth` (and from `gcp-secrets`)
- `vta-external`: `trust-tasks-rs`, `tracing`, `vta-keyspaces`, `tempfile` (dev)
- `vti-witness`: `affinidi-messaging-core`, `futures-util`, `rand`, `trust-tasks-didcomm`
- `vta-enclave`: `serde_json`, `sha2`, and `vti-common`. The issue guessed `vti-common` was feature activation, but `vta-service` already enables `vti-common/encryption` unconditionally, so it is redundant.
- `pnm-cli`: `base64`, `sha2`, `tracing`; `cnm-cli`: `tracing`
- `vta-backup`: `subtle`, `vta-webvh` (dev); `vta-sweepers`: `uuid` (dev); `room-host`: `getrandom` (dev); `didcomm-test`: `multibase`; `tests/e2e`: `affinidi-messaging-didcomm`, `url`

Kept, under `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored`, each with its reason:

- `vti-specs-*`: `trust-tasks-build` and `trust-tasks-rs` (used by `build.rs` and the generated code)
- `vti-secrets` and `vta-tee`: `aws-smithy-types` (resolver bound)
- `vta-service`: `affinidi-tdk-common` (version floor)
- `vti-witness`: `affinidi-tdk` and `affinidi-messaging-sdk` (their `tsp` features)

None of the removed crates was re-exported, so no public API changes.

CI: a new tier-0 `manifest hygiene` job runs `cargo machete --with-metadata` (installed by `taiki-e/install-action`, pinned by SHA) and the lint check below. I did not add it to the tier-1 `needs` lists (ci.yml is being edited elsewhere); its comment says so.

## #2657 — dependency declarations

- Every external dependency used by two or more members is now in `[workspace.dependencies]`, and members inherit it with `{ workspace = true }` plus their own `features` / `optional`. That covers 32 new entries (async-trait, tempfile, zeroize, getrandom, tower, affinidi-messaging-didcomm, affinidi-messaging-test-mediator, p256, bip39, argon2, predicate-credential-system, metrics, rmcp, …) and 172 declarations.
- Where one member turns default features off (curve25519-dalek, rcgen, object_store), the workspace entry is `default-features = false` and the other members ask for `features = ["default"]`, so no member's feature set changes.
- The re-declarations of existing workspace entries now inherit: `hmac`, `futures-util`, `serde_json_canonicalizer`, `base64`, `hex`, `dirs`, `time`, `coset`, `x509-parser`. The `url` re-declaration was in `tests/e2e`, where it was unused and is removed.
- `vta-tee` → `aws-lc-rs.workspace = true`. `vta-service`'s `aws-lc-rs` turned out to be unused and was removed.
- Not hoisted: `rand` 0.8 (deliberately behind the workspace's 0.10).
- Crypto floors are now real minimum patches, each the patch the lock held: `ed25519-dalek = "3.0.0"`, `hpke = "0.15.1"` (moved into the workspace table), `jsonwebtoken = "11.1.0"`, `aes-gcm = "0.11.1"`, `aws-lc-rs = "1.19.0"` (was `1.16`).
- `scripts/check-workspace-version-reqs.py` (already in CI) now fails on any requirement on those five crates that is not `^X.Y.Z`. I verified this by setting `aes-gcm = "0.11"`, which it rejected.
- Packaged manifests checked: `cargo package -p vta-sdk` renders inherited deps with their versions and features.

## #2658 items 1–3 — lints, `unsafe_code`, `publish = false` comments

1. Added `[lints] workspace = true` to the 15 crates listed in the issue. All 47 members are covered, and clippy is clean. `scripts/check-workspace-lints.py` (run by the new job) fails on a member that does not inherit.
2. `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"`. `forbid` cannot be lowered by an inner `#[allow]`, and a member cannot inherit the table and override one lint. So the crates that need `unsafe` restate the workspace table with `unsafe_code = "deny"` and put `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on each `unsafe` statement, next to its SAFETY comment. The script holds those tables equal to the workspace's apart from that one lint, and the list can only shrink. That leaves four crates, not five:
   - `vta-sdk`'s three `unsafe { s.as_bytes_mut() }` were test-only ASCII byte flips. They are rewritten as safe `String::replace_range`, so `vta-sdk` forbids `unsafe`.
   - `vti-common`: `umask` and `env::set_var` in tests. `vta-service`: `AsyncFd::register` and `env::remove_var`. `vta-tee`: the NSM / SEV-SNP ioctls. `pnm-cli`: `env::set_var`.
   - Also checked: `vti-rooms-wasm` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (wasm-bindgen output) and `vta-mobile-core` (UniFFI scaffolding) build under `forbid`.
3. Added the missing `publish = false` comments to `didcomm-test` and `vta-mcp`.

Items 4–6 (toolchain pin, Dependabot, stale branches and probe workflow) are owned by other PRs, hence `Refs`.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 7471/7472 passed. The exception, `audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, hit nextest's 300 s limit on a shared macOS host. It builds a fresh store per task and is fsync-bound (149 s on CI for main). It passes under `cargo test` in 54 s.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`
- `cargo check` of feature sets touched by removals: `vta-service --features tee,keyring`; `vtc-service --features keyring,gcp-secrets,aws-secrets`; `vti-secrets --features gcp-secrets,aws-secrets,keyring`; `vta-sdk --features sealed-transfer,attest-verify,x509-issuers,client`; `vti-witness` and `vti-rooms` with `--all-features`; `vti-rooms-wasm` on wasm32
- `cargo machete --with-metadata`, `cargo deny check` (root and enclave proxy), and the three manifest scripts

Closes #2654
Refs #2655 (the jsonschema / jsonwebtoken bumps are upstream in trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-https)
Closes #2656
Closes #2657
Refs #2658 (items 1–3 here; items 4–6 are in other PRs)

title: feat(chat/direct): a message from one person to another, rewritable by its author (chat/direct/message/0.1) (#1066)
body:
feat(chat/direct): a message from one person to another, rewritable by its author (chat/direct/message/0.1) (#1066)

* feat(chat/direct): a message from one person to another, rewritable by its author (chat/direct/message/0.1)

chat/direct/message/0.1: a fire-and-forget message from one pairwise identifier to another. The author names it with a fresh 43-character messageId and rewrites it under the same messageId with a greater revision: an edit carries editedAt, an empty body withdraws it, and a reaction is a message of kind reaction naming its target in inReplyTo. Only the authenticated original author rewrites (notAuthor); a conflicting copy of a held revision is revisionConflict; a rewrite that changes kind, writtenAt or a reaction's inReplyTo is rewriteInvalid; stale and unknown revisions are handled silently. proofRequirement OPTIONAL, with producers restricted to binding modes that permit omitting proof under SPEC 9.1.1. kind, writtenAt and editedAt $ref rooms/_shared/0.1 so the content vocabulary is the rooms one; chat/direct/_shared/0.1 holds MessageId, MessageRevision, MessageReference and MessageBody. The chat category blurb in data.js now names both families.

Libraries regenerated: cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all; npm run build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings, build-dart-bindings.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(chat/direct): address review of message/0.1

- revisionConflict applies only to the current held revision; a lower
  revision is stale and ignored silently, whatever its payload (R2, R3.1,
  acceptance window, error-code meaning).
- R5: keep the R2 key and a digest of the RFC 8785 canonical payload for
  the acceptance window.
- R1.1: the author of a message the consumer's own user sent is that user.
- Every messageId lookup is scoped to the conversation (the issuer/recipient
  pair): R1.2, R2's key, R4 and notAuthor, so no answer confirms a messageId
  held in another conversation.
- maxDocumentBytes 131072 -> 262144, covering encoders that escape all
  non-ASCII text.
- A reader ignores an inReplyTo naming the message's own messageId.
- New invalid example: a reaction rewrite without inReplyTo.

Libraries regenerated: cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all;
npm run build-ts-bindings, build-go-bindings, build-dart-bindings.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(chat/direct): order late messages by writtenAt (R6)

A direct conversation has no host and two parties, and its messages are composed offline and delivered late up to the acceptance window. R6 now orders by writtenAt within the acceptance window instead of applying the rooms backdating rule, keeps the five-minute future bound, adds a floor at the acceptance window, and shows a late arrival as late.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

title: chore: release 3 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof` | npm | `0.2.1` → `0.2.2` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp` | npm | `0.1.4` → `0.1.5` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client` | npm | `0.2.0` → `0.2.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: security!: invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types
body:
Security hardening sweep: eight audit findings across `vtc-service`, `vti-vtn`, `vta-sdk`, `vti-common` and `vta-service`. One commit per issue (#2621 and #2567 share one).

## #2660: a wallet admin invitation's entry outlived a revoke or a lapse

**Spec check.** `vtc/admin/invites/create/0.2` item 3 says a wallet invitation's administrator entry is written **when the invitation is issued**, and `vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3` item 7 relies on that ("whose administrator entry the invitation wrote"). Moving the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict both. So I took the fallback.

**What changed.** The entry is still written at mint, but it now expires when the invitation does. It is recorded beside the invitation (`install::InviteGrant`, `install:invite_grant:<jti>`).
- `vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3` makes it permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code.
- `vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1` removes it, along with its sessions and delegations, and audits `AclRevoked`. The void after five wrong claim codes does the same.
- Both act only on the entry exactly as the invitation wrote it. If someone has changed the entry since, it is left alone.
- An entry that has lapsed, or is still provisional, no longer blocks a new invitation for the same DID.
- The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the same provisional entry.
- Tests cover: claim makes it permanent, revoke before claim leaves no admin, revoke leaves a rewritten entry alone, and lapse leaves no admin.

**Design question.** Under create 0.2 the invited DID can still act as an administrator *before* it claims, until the invitation expires. If that is not intended, the fix belongs in the spec (defer the write to the claim for wallet invitations too). I did not change it here.

## #2661: HSTS, CSRF bearer skip, dead exemptions, cookie names

- **HSTS.** The check `request.uri().scheme_str() == Some("https")` was never true behind a TLS proxy, so HSTS was never sent. HSTS is now decided from `public_url` by `routing::security_headers::HstsPolicy` and set on every response by an outer layer in `server.rs`. Browsers ignore HSTS received over plain HTTP, so this is safe even when the proxy forwards plain HTTP. I used `public_url` alone; I did not add `X-Forwarded-Proto` trust. The deployment docs did not mention HSTS before; `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` now does.
- **CSRF bearer skip.** The gate now decides "carries a bearer" with `vti_common::auth::extractor::bearer_token`, which is exactly what the extractors accept. The member extractor uses it too; it used to match `Bearer ` case-sensitively.
  - The routes that read their cookie whatever the request carries are never exempted by a bearer: `/v1/auth/{refresh,sign-out}` and `/v1/member/{auth/refresh,sign-out}`.
  - Before this, a malformed header such as ` Bearer x` beside a session cookie skipped CSRF, and the request then authenticated by the cookie.
- **Dead exemptions removed.** `/v1/auth/challenge`, `/v1/auth/`, `/v1/install/claim/{start,finish}`, `/v1/admin/bootstrap`, and also `/v1/join-requests` with its `/accept` and `/status` suffixes. The issue did not list the join-requests ones, but those routes are gone as well; they are Trust Tasks now. `every_csrf_exemption_names_a_live_route` holds every exemption to a live route through the real router.
- **`__Host-` cookie names.** The console's session, refresh and `csrf` cookies, and the portal's CSRF cookie, are now written under `__Host-` names. The old names are still read for one release, and refresh and sign-out expire them. The admin SPA and portal read the new CSRF name first and fall back to the old one.
  - The portal's session and refresh cookies keep their names. They are `Path=/v1/member`, and `__Host-` requires `Path=/`.

## #2662: vti-vtn status-list fetch

- `VtnClient::get_url` (the `statusListCredential` fetch) now:
  - vets the URL with `vta_sdk::http::guard_peer_endpoint`;
  - fetches through the hardened foreign-fetch client (no redirects, no proxy, resolved addresses vetted at connect time);
  - reads the body with `read_body_capped`.
- Private and loopback targets are opt-in, through `VtnClient::allow_private_endpoints` or `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`. Metadata and link-local addresses are always refused.
- The status-list cache is bounded at `MAX_CACHED_LISTS`. Lapsed entries are evicted first, then the oldest.
- **Layering.** `vti-vtn` already optionally depends on `vta-sdk`. `vta-sdk` gains an additive `http` feature (`client` implies it), so `vti-vtn`'s `client` feature gets `vta_sdk::http` without pulling in the TDK.
- **Already fixed on main, no change:** an out-of-range status index is already a RANGE_ERROR (indeterminate), and the body was already capped.
- **Not checked:** which constructor the VTN service uses; that code is in another repository.

## #2618: x509_issuer path validation

**Validator choice.** I looked at `rustls-webpki` first. It does not fit EUDI / swiyu issuer chains: it checks a chain against a TLS-style EKU, has no secp256k1, ignores keyUsage `keyCertSign`, and does not handle URI name constraints. So the checks are added to the existing chain walk instead. They apply to every CA on the path, **the trust anchor included**:
- `pathLenConstraint`.
- `keyCertSign`, when keyUsage is present.
- `nameConstraints` against the leaf's `dNSName` and `URI` names.
  - `dNSName` subtrees are also applied to a URI's host, so a sub-CA constrained by DNS name cannot certify an issuer URL outside its subtree.
  - Constraint forms this code does not evaluate (`directoryName`, `iPAddress`, …) refuse the chain rather than being ignored.
- Unprocessed critical extensions are refused, and any extension that does not parse is a refusal. This includes the leaf's keyUsage, which previously passed on a parse error.
- **Answering the issue's "not checked" item:** `x509-parser` verifies SHA-1 RSA signatures, down to 1024-bit keys. SHA-1 signatures are now refused. Revocation is still not checked.
- Each rule has a test.

## #2619: zeroize vault secrets, redact session Debug ⚠ breaking

- `VaultSecret`, `TotpSeed` and `CustomField` overwrite their secret fields on drop.
- `CookieJarEntry`, `RequestHeader` and `StorageEntry` overwrite their `value` on drop, and they and `SessionBlob` have hand-written redacting `Debug`.
- The password-post driver builds its body from `Zeroizing` copies and returns it `Zeroizing`. The HTTP client's own copy of the body is out of reach.
- The secret-Debug census matches fields by name, so a cookie's `value` slipped past it. It gains `SECRET_BY_ROLE`: types that must never derive `Debug`, whatever their fields are called.
- **Breaking:** the `Drop` impls stop callers moving fields out of these `vti-common` types by destructuring. `build_request_body` now returns `Zeroizing<String>`.
- I found no log site that formats these types today.

## #2620: passkey login amr

- Passkey login now issues `amr=["passkey"]` (still `aal2`), and the misleading comment is corrected.
- **Consumers of `amr`:** nothing in the workspace gates on `"did"`. The policy input passes `amr` through to Rego, where an operator's rule could read it.

## #2621 + #2567: generated payload types, `deny_unknown_fields`, census

- **consent/\*.** The six handlers (`request`, `decision`, `revoke`, `list`, `approver-set`, `approver-list`) now parse the generated `vti_specs::consent::*` payloads. Those are `deny_unknown_fields`, so a mis-cased member is refused instead of silently defaulting.
- **vault/\* and vault/credentials/\* bodies.** These stay hand-written: the `wire_v0_2` edge transform rewrites a 0.2+ payload into 0.1 casing before parsing, and the generated types would refuse that.
  - They are now `deny_unknown_fields`, accepting `ext`, and `stepUpProof` where the schema declares it.
  - `assert_reads_exactly_the_schema_members` holds each one to its pinned schema: every declared member is read, an undeclared one is refused.
  - `vault/{archive,unarchive,restore,purge}/0.1` are not pinned, so this is their only gate.
- **Census.** `vta-service/tests/it/payload_type_census.rs` uses `syn` to find every `parse_payload::<T>` and typed `let … = (match) parse_payload(..)` under `src/trust_tasks/`. It resolves `T` through the `use` items in scope, including function-local `use … as t;`, and requires a `vti_specs` type or a baseline entry.
  - The baseline is 97 types and only shrinks. `vta_sdk::protocols::*::*Body` types and tasks pinned nowhere are among them.
  - `CredentialQuery` (defined in `vta-vault`) is baselined, not changed.
- **Not done:** defaulting `require_payload_schema` to true. That needs the census baseline empty first.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`

Closes #2660
Closes #2661
Closes #2662
Closes #2618
Closes #2619
Closes #2620
Closes #2621
Closes #2567

title: security!: invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types (#2710)
body:
security!: invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types (#2710)

* security(vtc): a wallet admin invitation's entry expires with it until claimed, and goes with a revoke (#2660)

vtc/admin/invites/create/0.2 item 3 writes a wallet invitation's administrator
entry when the invitation is issued, and the code wrote it permanent: revoking
the invitation (which create 0.2 says withdraws the authority it confers) or
letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed.

The entry is now written to expire with the invitation and recorded beside it
(install::InviteGrant, keyed by jti). vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 makes it
permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code;
vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes,
remove it (with its sessions and delegations) if it is still exactly what the
invitation wrote. A lapsed or still-provisional entry no longer blocks a new
invitation for the same DID. The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the
same provisional entry.

Deferring the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict
create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written
at mint.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vtc): send HSTS from public_url, align the CSRF bearer skip with the extractors, __Host- cookies (#2661)

- HSTS: the security-headers layer sent Strict-Transport-Security only when
  request.uri().scheme_str() was https, which an origin-form HTTP/1.1 request
  behind a TLS proxy never is. It is now decided from public_url and attached
  to every response by an outer layer (routing::security_headers::HstsPolicy).
- CSRF: the bearer skip matched the scheme case-insensitively and after
  leading whitespace, while the extractors read only a header TypedHeader
  accepts, so a malformed Authorization header beside a session cookie
  skipped CSRF and then authenticated by the cookie. Both now use
  vti_common::auth::extractor::bearer_token (the member extractor too), and
  the routes that read their cookie whatever the request carries (cookie
  refresh and sign-out, console and portal) are never exempted by a bearer.
- Dead exemptions removed: /v1/auth/challenge, /v1/auth/,
  /v1/install/claim/{start,finish}, /v1/admin/bootstrap, /v1/join-requests and
  its accept/status suffixes no longer exist as routes. A test pins every
  exemption to a live route.
- Cookies: the console's session, refresh and csrf cookies and the portal's
  csrf cookie take the __Host- prefix. The old names are still read for one
  release and are expired by refresh and sign-out. The portal's session and
  refresh cookies are Path=/v1/member, which __Host- does not allow, so they
  keep their names.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vti-vtn): fetch credential-named status lists through the guarded client, bound the cache (#2662)

StatusChecker fetched a credential's statusListCredential (before checking its
issuer or proof) with VtnClient's own reqwest client: default redirects, no
public-address guard. VtnClient::get_url now vets the URL with
vta_sdk::http::guard_peer_endpoint, fetches it through the hardened
foreign-fetch client (no redirects, no proxy, resolved addresses vetted at
connect time) and reads the body with read_body_capped. Private and loopback
targets are opt-in (VtnClient::allow_private_endpoints, or the workspace's
VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS); metadata and link-local never.

The status-list cache is bounded at MAX_CACHED_LISTS (lapsed entries evicted
first, then the oldest).

vta-sdk gains an `http` feature (`client` implies it) so vti-vtn's `client`
can use vta_sdk::http without the TDK.

Already fixed on main: the out-of-range status index is a RANGE_ERROR
(indeterminate), and the body was already capped.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vta-sdk): x509_issuer enforces pathLen, keyCertSign, name constraints and critical extensions (#2618)

The x5c chain walk checked validity, CA-ness, issuer/subject linkage and
signatures only. It now also holds every certification authority on the path,
the anchor included, to what RFC 5280 §6 delegates:

- pathLenConstraint against the CA certificates below it;
- keyUsage, when stated, must allow keyCertSign;
- nameConstraints on the leaf's dNSName and URI names (dNSName subtrees are
  applied to a URI's host too, so a DNS-constrained sub-CA cannot certify an
  issuer URL outside them); a directoryName, iPAddress or other constraint
  form this does not evaluate refuses the chain rather than being ignored;
- a critical extension not processed here refuses the certificate, and an
  extension that does not parse is a refusal, not a pass (the leaf's keyUsage
  included);
- SHA-1 signatures, which x509-parser verifies down to 1024-bit RSA for
  legacy use, are refused.

A vetted path validator was considered: rustls-webpki is in the graph, but it
verifies a chain for a TLS-style EKU, has no secp256k1, ignores keyUsage
keyCertSign and does not constrain URI names, so it does not fit EUDI / swiyu
issuer chains. Revocation remains unchecked, as before.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vti-common)!: zeroize vault secrets and proxied session material, redact the session types' Debug (#2619)

VaultSecret, TotpSeed and CustomField now overwrite their secret fields
(passwords, private keys, tokens, TOTP seeds, passphrases, secure notes,
custom values) when dropped, and CookieJarEntry, RequestHeader and
StorageEntry their values. SessionBlob and those three no longer derive
Debug: a hand-written one reports every value as <redacted>.

vta-service's password-post driver builds its form/JSON body from Zeroizing
copies and returns it Zeroizing (the HTTP client's own copy of the body is
beyond reach).

The secret-Debug census matches fields by name, so a cookie's or a header's
`value` escaped it; it gains SECRET_BY_ROLE, a list of types that must never
derive Debug whatever their fields are called.

BREAKING CHANGE: the Drop impls mean these types' fields can no longer be
moved out by destructuring; borrow them instead.
vta_service::operations::vault::password_post::build_request_body returns
Zeroizing<String>.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vta): passkey login records amr=["passkey"], not a DID-key proof it never asked for (#2620)

passkey_login_start takes a bare DID and checks only that it is in the ACL;
finish verifies the WebAuthn assertion and nothing else. The session was
nonetheless issued amr=["did","passkey"], recording a factor that was not
exercised, and the comment claimed a DID-key challenge that does not exist.
It is now amr=["passkey"]; acr stays aal2 on the user-verified passkey.

No consumer in the workspace gates on amr containing "did" (the policy
input passes amr through to Rego, where an operator rule could).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vta): consent/* read the generated payload types; vault bodies refuse unknown members; census of parsed payload types (#2621, #2567)

- consent/{request,decision,revoke,list,approver-set,approver-list} parse the
  generated vti_specs::consent::* payloads (all six are pinned) and convert to
  the store's types, instead of six hand-written structs the
  generated-wire-types census could not see. A mis-cased or unknown member is
  now refused rather than defaulted (R3).
- The vault/* and vault/credentials/* bodies that stay hand-written (the
  wire_v0_2 edge transform hands them 0.1-cased payloads the generated types
  would refuse) are deny_unknown_fields, accepting ext (and stepUpProof where
  the schema declares it). A test holds each to its pinned schema: every
  declared member is read, an undeclared one refused. vault/{archive,
  unarchive,restore,purge}/0.1 are not pinned, so this is their only gate.
- tests/it/payload_type_census.rs reads every parse_payload site under
  src/trust_tasks/ with syn, resolves the type through the use items in scope,
  and requires a vti_specs type or a baseline entry. The baseline (97 types)
  only shrinks.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta): hold cred_vault's receive body to the refusing contract; clippy fixes for #2618 / #2621

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
