title: docs: operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI
body:
Documentation-accuracy sweep for the audit findings #2630 – #2643, plus a CI check (`scripts/check-docs.py`, in the Format job) so the crate map, crate counts, docs index and links cannot drift again. Every claim was re-checked against current `main` (17f913de7) before anything changed. The CLI command trees were dumped from the built `pnm`, `cnm` and `vta` binaries and every backticked command in `*.rs` / `*.md` / `*.html` was checked against them.

## Per issue

**#2630 — stale commands in operator guides.** Each one now names the current command (`pnm contexts …`, `pnm did-mgmt dids get-log`, `pnm did-mgmt servers add`, `pnm did-mgmt dids create/list`, `pnm did-templates create --file`, `cnm member relationships …`, `cnm member revoke-personhood`). Some commands have no CLI equivalent, so those blocks now point at the surface that does exist:
- `cnm website …` / `cnm admin build-info` → the `/v1/website/*` endpoints and `/admin/build-info.json`
- `cnm policies upload|activate` → the console's **Policies** page, or `policy/upsert/0.3` + `policy/activate/0.1`
- personhood challenge/assert → the wallet's `vtc/members/personhood/{challenge/0.1,assert/0.2}`
- `pnm keys sign` → the `keys/sign` Trust Task through the SDK
- `pnm auth login` → pnm has no credential import, so the README says so
- `pnm vta add --mediator-did` → the config field `pnm setup` writes
- `vta tee recover --mnemonic` → no TEE mnemonic recovery exists. The Nitro DR rows now say to restore a backup into a fresh enclave (`pnm backup import --replace-identity`).

Step 4/5 of `03-vtc/getting-started.md` (`cnm join approve`, a `submit/1.0` curl) was stale in the same way. It now describes join criteria and the `vtc/join-requests/*` Trust Tasks.

**#2631 — remediation strings.** Fixed every string the issue lists, plus the others the scan found:
- `pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` in `register_server.rs`, `webs_backing.rs`, `server.rs`, `provision_integration/{mod,webs,webvh}.rs` and comments
- backup descriptor hints naming `pnm backup save|restore`
- `vta export-mnemonic`
- `pnm passkey-enroll-token` (the routes take an admin JWT; there is no enrolment token)
- `cnm community info`
- `vta-sdk` `session.rs`'s `<cli> auth login <credential-string>`

New tests `remediation_commands_in_error_and_help_strings_parse` (pnm-cli and the `vta` binary) parse each remediation command through `Cli::try_parse_from`.

**#2632 — KeyPackage lifetime.** It is 14 days in `data-rooms.md` and in `pnm rooms keys key-package --help`. The table now cites `trust_tasks::room_group::KEY_PACKAGE_V0_2_LIFETIME_SECS`. `vti-rooms-wasm` / `vti-rooms` apply no lifetime of their own.

**#2633 — `pnm rooms prune --help`.** The help now says members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the floor and refuse to derive below it, names `rooms/epoch/prune/0.2`, and says nothing already read is recalled. Verified that `apply_epoch_floor` runs on every chain walk in `operations/room_groups.rs`.

**#2634 — removed DIDComm surface.** `didcomm-protocol.md` is now a short superseded stub. It describes the binding envelope + plumbing that `messaging/router.rs` serves and points at `tsp.md` and the Trust Task design notes. Also fixed:
- `CONTRIBUTING` (the `auth_from_message` rule and its index entry)
- the `integration-guide` sign-request sentence
- the `provision-integration` "dual check": relayer and holder may differ, and the doc now says only 0.3 is served
- `session.rs:621`

**#2635 — retired `did-hosting-*` template names.** `--template` long help on `pnm bootstrap provision-request` and `vta bootstrap provision-request` is now built from `vta_sdk::did_templates::BUILTIN_NAMES`, with a test that it lists every built-in. `did-templates init` help lists the role aliases. Runtime error text and `provision-integration.md` examples now use `did-host-*`, including the two TSP shapes. The `ProvisionAsk` table now has the seven real constructors. The `vta-service/CLAUDE.md` built-in list was missing `room`, `room-host` and `trust-registry`.

**#2636 — published-crate counts.** `RELEASING.md` now holds the one authoritative list of the eleven `publish = false` members (36 of 47 publish). The engineering notes defer to it. Corrected the root `Cargo.toml` comments on `vti-vetting-pcs` / `vti-voting` and the `vti-voting-service` manifest comment. The check script holds every "N of M" and the list to the manifests.

**#2637 — crate map.** The root `CLAUDE.md` dependency layers are now generated from `cargo metadata --no-deps` between markers (`python3 scripts/check-docs.py --write`). The spine is described as the chain it is: `vti-specs → vta-sdk → vti-common`. Other changes:
- ten missing table rows added, and the table is checked both ways
- four → five `schema_index` tables
- the `vta-keyspaces` row
- `README` diagram edges flipped; it points at the full map
- dead paths fixed in root, `vta-service` and `vtc-service` `CLAUDE.md` (`routes/did_templates.rs`, `tests/key_custody_census.rs`, `send_oneway`, `didcomm_websocket_status`, `routes/contexts.rs`, `operations/provision_integration.rs`, `routes/did_webvh.rs` handlers, `routes/git_ns.rs`, the REST `/did-templates` claim)

**#2638 — broken links.** Fixed every link in the issue and the dead backticked paths outside design notes. `CONTRIBUTING` now states the DCO gate instead of linking a CLA and Code of Conduct that don't exist. The checker (GitHub slug rules, code fences ignored) passes over all tracked `*.md`. I used Python rather than lychee, which avoids a third-party action and any cache.

**#2639 — docs index.** `docs/README.md` now lists every page under `01–04`, `06`, `07`, plus the design notes `CLAUDE.md` treats as required reading. It says the design-note list is a selection and links the directory. The vtc-mcp label is now "implemented". The root `README` documentation section is corrected. The index check is in the script.

**#2640 — design-note statuses.** Status lines updated after checking the code: `vta-external-accounts` (partly: s3-presign only), `tsp-enablement`, `vtc-member-directory` (all but introductions), `tee-anti-rollback-anchor`, `oid4vp-wallet-verifier`, `pnm-setup-deferred-vta-did`, `tsp-outbound-send` (partly), `vti-webauthn-crate-design`, `phase5-cutover` (implemented: the encode/decode methods are gone), and the credential-architecture trio. The ten notes without a status now have one. `tee-dual-unlock` was checked and is still unbuilt. `credential-architecture-presentation.html` is now linked from its note.

**#2641 — `degraded_threshold_seconds`.** Removed it. `registry_status` follows probe/dispatch outcomes (`registry::health`), not a lag threshold. `drift_check_interval_seconds` is added to the example, and `trust-registry-deployment.md` is updated.

**#2642 — `data-rooms-guide.html`.** Deleted.

**#2643 — leftover references and TODOs.**
- `trust_tasks_rs::specs` in three docs → `vta_sdk::specs` / `vti_specs`.
- Service ids: see the correction below.
- Filed #2702 (step-up UV), #2703 (wizard prints admin key), #2704 (gateway wake allowlist) and #2705 (TSP relationship reset, D4), and cited them in the four TODOs.

## Claims found wrong or partly wrong
- **#2643 / root CLAUDE.md, service ids.** `#vta-rest` / `#vta-didcomm` are not stale. The VTA's own document still emits them (`operations::protocol::document`, `operations::did_webvh::document`); only DID templates emit `#tsp` / `#didcomm` / `#rest`. The root `CLAUDE.md` claimed the emitted convention is `#tsp/#didcomm/#rest`, which is now corrected. The docs now name services by `type`.
- **#2631.** The issue's list was incomplete: about ten more operator-facing strings named retired commands (listed above).
- **#2641.** Beyond the dead key, the prose claim "flips when the queue is ≥1h behind" was also wrong.
- **#2634 "not checked".** The `vta_sdk::protocols::key_management` URI constants are now used nowhere in the workspace; only `tests/e2e/tests/didcomm_session.rs` uses the literal URIs. I did not remove them: they are public, and removing them would be breaking. Separate issue if wanted.
- **#2643 related placeholders.** `vtc-service/src/registry/upstream.rs` "not yet implemented in M3.x" was not checked or changed.

## Not done / judgement calls
- Design notes are listed as a selection, not all ~100.
- The `cnm`/`vtc` subcommand scan covered backticked commands. Flag values inside long examples were checked only where I rewrote them.
- `ci.yml` change is four lines in the Format job. `cargo metadata --no-deps --offline` needs no registry, and was verified with an empty `CARGO_HOME`.
- The root `CLAUDE.md` "The only required check on main is DCO" line was left alone, as instructed.

Closes #2630
Closes #2631
Closes #2632
Closes #2633
Closes #2634
Closes #2635
Closes #2636
Closes #2637
Closes #2638
Closes #2639

title: docs: operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI (#2706)
body:
docs: operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI (#2706)

* fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse

Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now
names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts (#2631): the retired
`pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` surface becomes `did-mgmt servers|dids …`,
`pnm auth login` (pnm has none) becomes `pnm setup`, `pnm acl delete`
takes the DID positionally, `list-domains` sits under `dids`, the backup
descriptor hints no longer name `pnm backup save|restore`, and stale doc
comments (`pnm passkey-enroll-token`, `vta export-mnemonic`, `cnm community
info`) are corrected. A pnm and a vta test parse each remediation command
through Cli::try_parse_from.

The --template help is derived from vta_sdk::did_templates::BUILTIN_NAMES
and no longer lists the retired did-hosting-* template names (#2635). The
`rooms keys key-package` help gives the 14-day KeyPackage lifetime the code
holds (#2632), and `rooms prune` no longer says a prune reaches the host
only: members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the epoch floor (#2633).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore: cite tracking issues on the four open security/correctness TODOs (#2643)

#2702 step-up user verification, #2703 the setup wizard's admin key on
stdout, #2704 the push gateway's wake allowlist, #2705 the trust-registry
TSP relationship reset (D4).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: operator guides name commands, templates and surfaces that exist

#2630: every stale pnm / cnm / vta command in the operator guides is
replaced by the current one, or — where no CLI exists (cnm website, cnm
policies, cnm admin, personhood challenge/assert, vta tee recover) — by the
console page, the Trust Task, or the real recovery path (backup restore).
Join requests in getting-started now describe criteria and Trust Tasks.

#2634: didcomm-protocol.md is a superseded stub pointing at the Trust Task
surface and tsp.md; CONTRIBUTING, integration-guide and provision-integration
no longer cite auth_from_message or key-management/1.0/sign-request.

#2635: provision-integration uses the did-host-* built-ins, including the two
TSP shapes, and the real ProvisionAsk constructors.

#2632: the data-rooms KeyPackage lifetime is 14 days, citing the real
constant. #2641: trust-registry drops the unread degraded_threshold_seconds
and shows drift_check_interval_seconds. #2642: the stale, unreferenced
data-rooms-guide.html is removed. #2643: doc samples use vta_sdk::specs /
vti_specs, and services are named by type (the VTA's own document still
emits #vta-rest / #vta-didcomm, so the ids are not stale). CONTRIBUTING
drops the CLA / Code-of-Conduct links to files that do not exist: the gate
is DCO.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: generate the crate map from the manifests and check it, the published count and links in CI

#2637: the root CLAUDE.md dependency layers are now generated from
`cargo metadata --no-deps` (normal + build deps, optional included) between
crate-map markers, the spine is described as the chain it is (vti-specs →
vta-sdk → vti-common), the crate table gains the ten missing members, "four"
schema_index tables becomes five, and dead paths in the root and per-crate
CLAUDE.md files are fixed. README's diagram draws edges dependency →
dependent and points at the full map.

#2636: RELEASING.md holds the one authoritative list of the eleven
publish = false members (36 of 47 publish); the engineering notes defer to
it, and the root Cargo.toml / vti-voting-service comments no longer call
published crates unpublished.

scripts/check-docs.py checks the crate map and crate table, every
"N of M crates publish", the internal-crates list, that every page under
docs/0[1-4,6,7]-* is in docs/README.md (#2639), and every relative Markdown
link and anchor (#2638). It needs no build and runs in the Format job.

Also: the root CLAUDE.md said the emitted service ids are #tsp / #didcomm /
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
#rest; templates emit those, but the VTA's own document still carries
#vta-didcomm / #vta-rest (#2643).

* docs: fix broken links, complete the docs index, and correct design-note statuses

#2638: the relative links and anchors that pointed at moved or missing files
(tee-architecture, Nitro README step anchors, bip32-paths sources,
RELEASING.md, the framework SPEC.md, an edit walkthrough that never existed)

title: fix(vtc-admin-ui): console and member portal UX sweep (error boundaries, confirmations, modals, a11y, session expiry, dates, toasts)
body:
The 13 UX findings from the review of `vtc-service/admin-ui` (the operator console and the member portal). There is one commit per issue. Each claim was checked against current `main` first. Everything lives in the admin-ui package, apart from two Rust test assertions on the console's page title.

## Per issue

**#2605: error boundaries.** Adds `components/ErrorBoundary`, a class boundary shared by both bundles.
- Console: `PluginHost` wraps each screen in a boundary keyed by plugin. It resets when the route changes, so the top bar and sidebar survive a throw. `main.tsx` adds one at the root as a last resort.
- Portal: each signed-in page is wrapped, and resets when the hash route changes. `members/main.tsx` adds a root boundary too.
- Fallback: an error card (an alert in the portal) with the message, the route and a "Reload this page" button.
- Not checked in the issue: third-party custom-element plugins render outside React, so a throw from one cannot reach a boundary. Confirmed.

**#2606: Sessions on a failed read.** A failed read now shows an error card with a Retry button. The count, the filter toolbar and the empty state appear only once the list has loaded.

**#2607: portal confirmations.**
- The portal now mounts the console's `ConfirmDialogProvider` with a new `look="portal"`, which uses the portal's `.btn` classes. The scrim, dialog and `btn-danger` styles are in `members.css`. The dialog stays in a `Protected` shadow root, whose root carries the body's `.vtc-signin`.
- Confirmed acts: remove passkey, leave group (as a member, not when withdrawing a pending request), unlink a forge account, withdraw an idea or note, withdraw a badge request, and decline a badge award.
- A failed passkey list now shows an alert with "Try again" instead of "No passkeys yet."

**#2608: election and board acts.**
- "Close early", "Close and end voting" and "Archive" now ask first, with `destructive: true`. The board's tooltip text becomes the dialog message.
- The cancel confirmation moved out of `mutationFn` into the click handler. Its cancel button is labelled "Keep it", so backing out no longer shows a "Not cancelled" refusal card.
- Recognition's "Discard" uses the shared dialog instead of `window.confirm`.
- Not changed: `storage.tsx`'s inline "Send for approval" reason form. It is a form, not a confirmation, and the issue proposed no change for it.

**#2609: forms that discarded input.** The role define form and the directory-field form now close only when `parkedOf(err)`. Any other failure keeps the form and what was typed. The directory prefix is now always "Change failed": `pushFromError` already ignores the prefix for a parked act. A grep for other `onError`-then-close sites found none beyond the two that were already correct.

**#2610: one modal contract.**
- `plugins/repos/ui.tsx`'s `useModal` moves to `components/useModal.ts`, and repos re-exports it. It traps Tab, closes on Escape (not while `locked`), and returns focus to the opener.
- Additions:
  - `initialFocus`, so a confirmation starts on Cancel.
  - `returnTo`.
  - The opener is found through shadow roots (`deepActiveElement`), so focus returns to the right button when the opener sits inside a `Protected` surface.
  - A stack of open modals, so Escape in a confirmation opened from the idea drawer closes only the confirmation.
- Used by `ConfirmDialog` (which now also returns focus), `TypedConfirmDialog` (which now traps Tab and is locked while busy), `DidQrButton`, `BadgeBuilder`'s icon browser, and the portal's idea drawer and Propose dialog.
- `CommandPalette` is unchanged: it already traps and restores focus by making `#root` inert, which is stronger.
- `WalletSignIn`'s `role="alertdialog"` is an inline confirmation in the page flow, not an overlay. Non-modal is correct there, so `aria-modal` was not added.
- The design note §7 now lists `useModal` and `ErrorBoundary`.

**#2611: Policies editor and click-only rows.**
- Rule editor:
  - The `rule-x` span is now a `<button aria-label="Remove condition: …">`.
  - The route name, effect value, and move/remove buttons are labelled.
  - The tool buttons are 24px, the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size.
  - `.rule-name` gets the focus ring back.
- The Rego and facts-JSON `<textarea>`s are labelled.
- `Toggle` (`button role=switch`) is replaced by the shared `Switch`. This also removes its `transition: all`.
- The board, badge and group name cells are now `<Link>`s, and the row click stays as a convenience.
- **Not done: `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`.** The package has no ESLint at all. Adding it means eslint 9, a flat config, a TypeScript parser and the plugin: new dev dependencies and a regenerated `package-lock.json`, which has known npm-version churn in CI. It would also flag every scrim `onClick` across the dialogs. That is a separate change; the listed controls are fixed here.

**#2612: portal session expiry.**
- `memberFetch` dispatches `MEMBER_SESSION_EVENT` on a 401 after the one renewal, or on a 403, except for `/v1/member/me` itself. So does the directory `send` (`K_b`-signed tasks).
- While signed in, `Portal` then re-reads `/v1/member/me`. If the session is gone, sign-in shows "Your session ended. Sign in again to continue." A 403 only triggers a re-check, so an ordinary refusal does not sign anyone out.
- **Not done (console):** keeping drafts of long forms across a session expiry, or warning before the deadline. The portal half, which is the reported defect, is done.
- The optional scheduled renewal from `accessExpiresAt` was not added.

**#2613: dates.**
- `lib/format.ts` gains `parseTime`, `formatDate` ("Nov 12, 2026") and `formatDateTime`, which always includes `timeZoneName: "short"`. It uses component options because `dateStyle` cannot be combined with `timeZoneName`.
- `formatIso` and `formatEpoch` now go through `formatDateTime`. The claim was correct: their `try/catch` fallback never fired, because an invalid date formats as "Invalid Date" instead of throwing. Both now return the raw input.
- Every listed private formatter and inline `toLocale*` call now uses these. The one exception is the board schedule's weekday/time slot form, which keeps its own options.
- **Not done:** a `<time>` component. The deadlines now carry their zone in the text.

**#2614: DIDs.** The portal's three `shortDid` copies and `Home`'s full DID now use `shortenDid`. The note author (`MemberNotes`, which kept only the head) and recognition's discard toast use `shortenDid`. In the Sessions dialogs, the message uses `NamedDid` and the title uses `shortenDid`.

**#2615: wording.**
- Passkey guidance says "your wallet".
- The home page's sign-in method reads "Your VTA" (no "(SIOPv2)").
- The console is called "Operator console" in the loading card, the `<title>`, the install copy and the two ACL audit reasons.

**#2616: narrow screens.**
- `DataTable` renders a `.data-table-wrap`. At 720px and below it scrolls the table sideways in place, and row actions stack.
- Above 720px the wrapper does nothing. An `overflow-x` box is a scroller on both axes, so making it scroll on wide screens would break the sticky header (the issue's open question).
- The 720px breakpoint is documented in `tokens.css`, copied byte-for-byte to `website-default/tokens.css`.
- Per-screen breakpoints (600–1100px) are left as they are.
- The ceremonies flow SVG has a fixed `viewBox` but is `width: 100%`, so it scales down rather than overflowing.

**#2617: toasts.**
- The bare status is dropped from the text and kept as a `title` ("HTTP 403").
- The live region is always mounted.
- A parked-act notice stays until dismissed.
- `lib/messages.ts` exports one `messageOf(err)`, now used at all 12 listed sites in both bundles. It also fixes `e instanceof Error ? … : String(e)` reading a plain `ApiError` as "[object Object]".

## Checks
- `npm run lint` (wire check + typecheck): passes.
- `npm test`: 131 files, 1614 tests. New tests cover each fix.
- `npm run build` and `npm run build:members`: pass.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 3736 tests. Four failed, each asserting the old `<title>VTC Admin</title>` (`admin_ui::tests`, three `routing_modes` tests). They were updated in the last commit and pass on rerun.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- One unrelated timing flake seen once under load: `MemberNotes.test.tsx` "shows nothing…" asserts an empty host immediately after the mock is called. It passed on rerun and alone.
- `package-lock.json` is untouched. The only Rust change is in tests: the two title assertions.

Closes #2605
Closes #2606
Closes #2607
Closes #2608
Closes #2609
Closes #2610
Refs #2611 — controls fixed; `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` not added (see above)
Refs #2612 — portal done; console draft preservation and pre-expiry warning remain
Closes #2613
Closes #2614
Closes #2615
Closes #2616
Closes #2617

title: trust-tasks-cli-v0.2.1
body:
### Build & CI

- Catch superseded versions and drifted counts in the docs ([#1268](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1268))

The stale-references check now reads every *.md outside specs/ (READMEs,
  guides, docs/, the latest version of each binding) and every
  examples/**/trust-tasks.toml [tasks] pin, as well as the registry. A
  reference may be a link, a mention, a path through a mirroring directory
  (specs/…, src/…), a generated module path (acl::grant::v0_2,
  acl/grant/v0_2) or a Type URI. CHANGELOGs, SPEC.md and ADRs are history;
  other deliberate references are listed with a reason under `documents` in
  stale-references-allowlist.json. `npm run fix-stale-references` rewrites the
  text references in documents too.

  Fixed what it found: README examples in trust-tasks-rs, -https and -proof
  on acl/grant 0.1; the push binding's links to push/* and device/set-wake
  0.1; CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md's examples; consumer-side-generation.md, which
  said examples/consumer-app pins acl/grant/0.2 and keys/list/0.2 (it pins
  0.3 and `latest`).

  New scripts/check-doc-facts.mjs (`npm run check-doc-facts`, in `npm run
  check` and a `documented facts match the tree` job in checks.yml) checks
  the facts the docs still state in prose: RELEASING.md's package table
  against the manifests and release-pr.sh's lists, the crates DEVELOPMENT.md
  says do not depend on trust-tasks-rs, the layout table, the Node floors,
  and the current framework version.

- **cli**: Attach prebuilt trust-tasks binaries to each CLI release ([#1260](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1260))

publish.yml calls the new cli-binaries.yml with the tag release-plz reports
  for trust-tasks-cli (a tag pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow). It
  builds Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/aarch64 and Windows x86_64, and
  attaches the archives, .sha256 files and SHA256SUMS to the GitHub Release.
  cargo binstall metadata names the same assets. GETTING-STARTED and the TS,
  Go and Dart READMEs gain an install section and a what-you-bring table.



### Fixed

- **build,cli**: Require a spec slug and version for every locked task, and the canonical path for every index entry ([#1245](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1245))

An official lockfile entry's slug and version were checked only against a Type URI built from the same strings, then used as path segments of the vendored bundle's location. Each entry's slug and version must now have their SPEC form, whichever registry it comes from. The CLI now also requires an index entry's path to be <slug>/<version>/bundle.json, the only form the registry publishes.

title: trust-tasks-build-v0.2.0
body:
### Added

- **rs,build**: A generated file names the runtime contract it needs ([#1253](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1253))

trust-tasks-rs gains a hidden __private::ABI_V1, and every file
  trust-tasks-build generates for an application opens with
  const _: () = ::trust_tasks_rs::__private::ABI_V1; under a comment naming
  the trust-tasks-build version. A runtime too old for the generator, or one
  that has moved to a newer contract, now fails on that line with an error
  naming the contract, instead of on whichever hidden door the generated code
  reaches first ([#1101](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1101)). The in-repo prebuilt tree is unchanged.

- **rs,build,ts,ts-gen,go,dart**: Emit only the $defs each schema constant reaches ([#1243](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1243))

* feat(rs,build,ts,ts-gen,go,dart): emit only the $defs each schema constant reaches

  Each generated request and response schema constant now keeps only the root $defs its root reaches: the request drops Response and what only the response uses, the response document drops what only the request uses. Registry bundles are unchanged, so no pinned digest moves. Types are still generated from the whole schema.

  trust-tasks-rs packages at 10,037,990 bytes (9.57 MiB) against 10,349,753 (9.87 MiB) before.

- **rs**: No prebuilt specification families by default ([#1240](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1240))

`trust-tasks-rs` and the `trust-tasks` facade now have `default = []`. A
  plain dependency compiles the runtime and the framework's own
  `trust-task-*` modules, not every deprecated prebuilt family (a ~17 GB
  build). A consumer that still uses `specs::<family>` enables
  `features = ["all-specs"]`, or the one family it uses.



### Fixed

- **build,cli**: Require a spec slug and version for every locked task, and the canonical path for every index entry ([#1245](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1245))

An official lockfile entry's slug and version were checked only against a Type URI built from the same strings, then used as path segments of the vendored bundle's location. Each entry's slug and version must now have their SPEC form, whichever registry it comes from. The CLI now also requires an index entry's path to be <slug>/<version>/bundle.json, the only form the registry publishes.

title: trust-tasks-tsp-v0.39.0
body:
### Added

- **rs,tsp,didcomm,didcomm-v1**: One guarded consumer for the binding crates; answer an authenticated unparsable body ([#1241](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1241))

The TSP, DIDComm v2.1 and DIDComm v1 consumers each carried the same wrapper
  (record, freshness policy, consume/consume_dispatched). It now lives once in
  trust-tasks-rs as GuardedConsumer; each binding consumer dereferences to it and
  keeps only its unpack and its envelope check (the DIDComm thread headers).

  receive now answers an authenticated body that fails to deserialise, or fails
  the thread cross-check, with ConsumeOutcome::Rejected(malformedRequest),
  addressed to the transport-authenticated sender and refused before the item-11
  record is written, as binding section 4 requires and the Go and Dart bindings
  already do. It used to return Err with nothing to answer.

- **rs**: No prebuilt specification families by default ([#1240](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1240))

`trust-tasks-rs` and the `trust-tasks` facade now have `default = []`. A
  plain dependency compiles the runtime and the framework's own
  `trust-task-*` modules, not every deprecated prebuilt family (a ~17 GB
  build). A consumer that still uses `specs::<family>` enables
  `features = ["all-specs"]`, or the one family it uses.



### Fixed

- **rs,ts,ts-tsp,proof,didcomm,didcomm-v1,tsp,dart-didcomm,dart-tsp,go-didcomm,go-tsp**: Message bindings enforce document size bounds; shared extends routing vector ([#1263](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1263))

Size bounds ([#1121](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1121)). GuardedConsumer::consume_body and
  consume_body_dispatched, the inbound half of the DIDComm, DIDComm v1 and
  TSP consumers, now hold a body to its specification's declared
  maxDocumentBytes (SPEC §12.4) and refuse a larger one malformedRequest. The
  refusal comes after the envelope has authenticated the sender, goes to that
  sender, and is made before the item-11 record is written. The size is the
  body's compact JSON text, because those stacks hand over a decoded body. A
  specification that declares no bound gets no default bound.
  consume_inbound and consume_dispatched used to hold a document read forward
  along extends to the implemented version's bound. They no longer do, because
  a later version may declare a larger bound. The Dart DIDComm and TSP
  consumers and the TypeScript TSP consumer now apply the same rule. The
  TypeScript consumer reads SPEC.maxDocumentBytes defensively, since core
  0.29.0 does not carry it yet.

  Extends ([#1117](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1117)). trust-tasks-go/didcomm and trust-tasks-go/tsp now require
  the published core v0.11.0, use ReadForSpecWith, and take an optional
  Consumer.Extends lookup that is passed through to ConsumeOptions.Extends.
  They already pass the received bytes as ConsumeOptions.Received, so size
  bounds take effect there once they require a core that carries #1251's
  check, which v0.11.0 predates.
  A new shared vector, fixtures/consume/extends-routing.json, is run by all
  four runtimes. It found that TypeScript's readForSpec refused the
  implemented version's own #request Type URI as unsupportedType; that is now
  fixed.

  Proof ([#1092](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1092)). verify_raw no longer clones the whole document (or the
  proof) to drop `proof`. It serialises a borrowed view without that member.
  The byte-for-byte fixtures still pass.

- **tsp,ts-tsp,go-tsp**: Open a TSP message only when it names this consumer's VID ([#1247](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1247))

The receiver VID in a TSP envelope is written by the sender; the HPKE seal only shows the message was encrypted to the recipient's key. The Rust and TypeScript bindings took that VID as the transport recipient, so a message sealed to our key but naming another VID passed the recipient check and was answered as that VID. Both now refuse a message whose receiver VID is set and differs from the configured one, and take the configured VID as the transport recipient. The Go binding's upstream library already refuses it; Go now takes the configured VID as the transport recipient too and keeps its own check. Dart's upstream library already refuses it.

title: trust-tasks-https-v0.39.0
body:
### Added

- **rs,https**: Build the HTTPS server on consume_dispatched; async handlers and auth ([#1244](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1244))

* feat(rs,https)!: build the HTTPS server on consume_dispatched; async handlers and auth

  HttpsServer now runs every framework check through

  The checks only it had become ConsumeChecks options (require_attribution,

  AsyncAuth trait every Auth satisfies, extends forward routing with
  unsupportedVersion, and per-type maxDocumentBytes enforcement with a body
  limit derived from the registered tasks.



### Build & CI

- **proof, didcomm**: Affinidi-crypto 0.3 and the matching Affinidi releases ([#1265](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1265))

* build(proof,didcomm): affinidi-crypto 0.3 and the matching Affinidi releases

  trust-tasks-proof requires affinidi-crypto 0.3, affinidi-data-integrity
  0.8.7, affinidi-did-common 0.4.7 and affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk
  0.8.53, the releases built on affinidi-crypto 0.3, so its KeyType is the
  one those crates use. The trust-tasks-didcomm dev dependencies move to
  affinidi-crypto 0.3 and affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.14, and the
  affinidi-secrets-resolver dev dependencies to 0.5.18.

  The mediator integration test leaves the tree for now: the published
  test-mediator 0.16 / messaging-sdk 0.32 build on affinidi-crypto 0.2 and
  no longer compile beside affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.14.

- Catch superseded versions and drifted counts in the docs ([#1268](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1268))

The stale-references check now reads every *.md outside specs/ (READMEs,
  guides, docs/, the latest version of each binding) and every
  examples/**/trust-tasks.toml [tasks] pin, as well as the registry. A
  reference may be a link, a mention, a path through a mirroring directory
  (specs/…, src/…), a generated module path (acl::grant::v0_2,
  acl/grant/v0_2) or a Type URI. CHANGELOGs, SPEC.md and ADRs are history;
  other deliberate references are listed with a reason under `documents` in
  stale-references-allowlist.json. `npm run fix-stale-references` rewrites the
  text references in documents too.

  Fixed what it found: README examples in trust-tasks-rs, -https and -proof
  on acl/grant 0.1; the push binding's links to push/* and device/set-wake
  0.1; CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md's examples; consumer-side-generation.md, which
  said examples/consumer-app pins acl/grant/0.2 and keys/list/0.2 (it pins
  0.3 and `latest`).

  New scripts/check-doc-facts.mjs (`npm run check-doc-facts`, in `npm run
  check` and a `documented facts match the tree` job in checks.yml) checks
  the facts the docs still state in prose: RELEASING.md's package table
  against the manifests and release-pr.sh's lists, the crates DEVELOPMENT.md
  says do not depend on trust-tasks-rs, the layout table, the Node floors,
  and the current framework version.



### Fixed

- **rs,https,dart-https**: Run the attribution gate before the route lookup ([#1246](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1246))

Both HTTPS servers looked the route up before the attribution gate, so a sender with neither a bearer token nor a proof could tell a registered type (proofRequired) from an unregistered one (unsupportedType).

  The Rust server now runs on consume_dispatched_answer, so the reorder is made there: the checks that read only the envelope (expiry, recipient, freshness, identity) and the attribution gate move out of consume_core into envelope_checks, which consume_inbound and consume_dispatched_answer both run ahead of their item-3 type check. The route lookup still precedes the DID-method screen and proof verification, so an unregistered type never reaches a resolver.

  The Dart server runs the same checks before the route lookup and before decoding the payload.



### Performance

- **rs,https**: Hash, compare and route each inbound document once ([#1259](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1259))

* test(rs,https): time the inbound path and pin the item-11 digest values

  The capability clients matched a reply to a request by thread id and slug alone. All four ports gain request-bound classifiers (classify_git_trust_reply_to / parse_capability_reply_to and their TS, Go and Dart counterparts) that also require the reply's issuer to be the request's recipient, its recipient to be the request's issuer, and its type to be the request's own #response or the framework error type, as the HTTPS clients do. The thread-only classifiers now read trust-task-error and family responses only under the registry's authority, and a toggle or listing reply missing a required member is no longer read as reporting defaults. TypeScript parses a body as a document only when its payload is an object. Rust adds try_build_document for a caller-supplied Type URI.

* feat(rooms/records/put): 0.6 declares a 64 KiB document bound

  rooms/records/put/0.6 extends 0.5 and changes no member. Its front matter
  declares maxDocumentBytes.request: 65536, the bound a deployed host already
  enforces, so hosts stop disagreeing on the largest record and a room can move
  between them without stranding records; larger content goes through files.
  Adding the bound to 0.5 in place would have narrowed what a 0.5 host must
  accept. The response declares no bound.

  Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart regenerated; earlier versions now carry
  "superseded by rooms/records/put/0.6".

- **rs,build**: A generated file names the runtime contract it needs ([#1253](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1253))

trust-tasks-rs gains a hidden __private::ABI_V1, and every file
  trust-tasks-build generates for an application opens with
  const _: () = ::trust_tasks_rs::__private::ABI_V1; under a comment naming
  the trust-tasks-build version. A runtime too old for the generator, or one
  that has moved to a newer contract, now fails on that line with an error
  naming the contract, instead of on whichever hidden door the generated code
  reaches first ([#1101](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1101)). The in-repo prebuilt tree is unchanged.

  Each generated request and response schema constant now keeps only the root $defs its root reaches: the request drops Response and what only the response uses, the response document drops what only the request uses. Registry bundles are unchanged, so no pinned digest moves. Types are still generated from the whole schema.

  trust-tasks-rs packages at 10,037,990 bytes (9.57 MiB) against 10,349,753 (9.87 MiB) before.

  build). A consumer that still uses `specs::<family>` enables

- **messaging/mux**: Admin-list, admin-revoke and admin-revoke-all for operators ([#1234](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1234))

Adds three administrator tasks (0.1, draft) for DID multiplexing, the
  operator side of the mediator design's §7.8:

  - messaging/mux/admin-list: list stored grants by principal DID, member
    DID or both (one is required), paged, in every state, without the
    signed statements; with `member`, the member's current epoch.
  - messaging/mux/admin-revoke: revoke grants of other accounts by
    principal, member, both, or member + grantIds; a bounded batch per
    request (`limit`), with an exact `remaining` count; synchronous detach,
    replay floors raised, detached events and grantsRevoked notices with
    reason `admin`.
  - messaging/mux/admin-revoke-all: advance a member DID's epoch without
    its signature, naming the current epoch so a replay is inert; same
    state change as revoke-all, reported with reason `admin`.

  messaging/mux/connections does. The two destructive tasks admit admin and
  rootAdmin only, and refuse an admin whose target member or principal is a
  rootAdmin account with <slug>:protectedAccount, as messaging/account/remove
  protects root admins. No shared-schema change: DetachReason,
  MemberChangeReason and the grantsRevoked notice already carry `admin`.
  Regenerates the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

- **messaging/monitor**: Opt-in mux membership events (event 0.3, subscribe 0.2) ([#1235](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1235))

  MembershipFilter whose presence opts a subscription in to mux membership
  events (none are sent without it), and `traffic: false` for a

  to, as for traffic.

  member, wire didcomm|tsp, source grant|attach, reason, optional
  sessionId) mirroring each messaging/mux/event member change, and
  `membershipDropped`. MonitorEvent and the closed TrafficStage are
  unchanged: a membership change is not a step in a message's life.

- **rs,ts,go,dart,go-didcomm,go-tsp,ts-tsp**: Settle the open runtime parity rows ([#1251](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1251))

* fix(rs,ts,go,dart): settle the open runtime parity rows

  Replay guard: a capacity below one takes the default capacity in all four
  libraries. Rust's InMemoryReplayGuard::new(0) no longer panics and the
  TypeScript constructor no longer throws RangeError; Go and Dart already
  defaulted. Moving the two to the default only relaxes them.

- **rs,https,dart-https**: Run the attribution gate before the route lookup ([#1246](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1246))

Both HTTPS servers looked the route up before the attribution gate, so a sender with neither a bearer token nor a proof could tell a registered type (proofRequired) from an unregistered one (unsupportedType).

  The Rust server now runs on consume_dispatched_answer, so the reorder is made there: the checks that read only the envelope (expiry, recipient, freshness, identity) and the attribution gate move out of consume_core into envelope_checks, which consume_inbound and consume_dispatched_answer both run ahead of their item-3 type check. The route lookup still precedes the DID-method screen and proof verification, so an unregistered type never reaches a resolver.

  The Dart server runs the same checks before the route lookup and before decoding the payload.

- **rs,ts,go,dart**: Issue an error response as the consumer, not as the rejected document's recipient ([#1249](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1249))

SPEC §8.1 makes an error response's issuer the consumer that emitted it. All four runtimes copied the rejected document's in-band recipient into it, which is unchecked for a refusal raised before item 5 and, under wrongRecipient, is by definition another party. The transport-level reject now sets the issuer to the transport's own identity where it has one; with none, it keeps the in-band recipient except under wrongRecipient, where it leaves the issuer out.



### Performance

- **rs,https**: Hash, compare and route each inbound document once ([#1259](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1259))

* test(rs,https): time the inbound path and pin the item-11 digest values

build(proof, didcomm): affinidi-crypto 0.3 and the matching Affinidi releases (#1265)

* build(proof,didcomm): affinidi-crypto 0.3 and the matching Affinidi releases

trust-tasks-proof requires affinidi-crypto 0.3, affinidi-data-integrity
0.8.7, affinidi-did-common 0.4.7 and affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk
0.8.53, the releases built on affinidi-crypto 0.3, so its KeyType is the
one those crates use. The trust-tasks-didcomm dev dependencies move to
affinidi-crypto 0.3 and affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.14, and the
affinidi-secrets-resolver dev dependencies to 0.5.18.

The mediator integration test leaves the tree for now: the published
test-mediator 0.16 / messaging-sdk 0.32 build on affinidi-crypto 0.2 and
no longer compile beside affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.14.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(proof,didcomm): lock the affinidi-crypto 0.3 releases

cargo update moves affinidi-crypto to 0.3.1 and the Affinidi crates
built on it (data-integrity 0.8.7, did-common 0.4.7,
did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.53, messaging-didcomm 0.15.14,
messaging-didcomm-v1 0.2.4, secrets-resolver 0.5.18). The removed entries
are the test-mediator / messaging-sdk dev graph.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(proof): define every member in the RDFC sign test's context

affinidi-data-integrity expands RDFC documents in JSON-LD safe mode since
0.8.2, so a member the active context does not define fails signing
instead of being left out of the signed dataset. The test document adds
an inline @vocab beside the credentials context.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(proof): define the RDFC sign test's members through a context URL

The verifier compares the proof @context with the document's and supports
only string entries, so the inline @vocab object did not survive the round
trip. The credentials examples context supplies the @vocab instead.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(https): time only the request in the blocking-handler test

The fast request built its reqwest client inside the timed window, and
building one loads the TLS root store, which on a CI runner can take a
large share of the 250 ms budget. The client is now built before the
clock starts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(proof): sign both copies at one pinned time in the wrapper comparison

title: feat(messaging/queue/purge): 0.1 gains storedBefore and selectedAt to pin a confirming purge to its dry run
body:
## Why
affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#122: the mediator console's two-step purge (dry run → confirm count → real purge) also removed messages that arrived between the preview and the confirmation, which the operator never saw. `queue/purge/0.1` acts on the selection at execution time and gave a producer no way to pin it.

## Change (additive, in place — optional members only)
- Request: `storedBefore` (RFC 3339 date-time) — only messages stored at or before this instant. Consumer rule 7 narrows by it; rule 9's audit record names it.
- Response: `selectedAt` (RFC 3339 date-time) — the instant the mediator took the selection; a consumer SHOULD return it on a dry run.
- Producer conformance: an interactive producer SHOULD send the dry run's `selectedAt` as `storedBefore` on the confirming purge.
- Prose, Definitions, a confirming-purge example, and an invalid example (`storedBefore` as Unix seconds).
- Regenerated Rust / TS / Go / Dart bindings and the Rust conformance test.

`check-published-schemas`: every released file changed only additively.

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.68.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.67.0...vta-sdk-v0.68.0) — 2026-10-13 ### Added - **keys**: Serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2057](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2057)) Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames caller bytes under the opaque signing domain. keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256, EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload; payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test. - **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056)) * feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part. The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756): - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest, vetter/show - **vtc**: Credential issuers known by an X.509 chain — x5c trust anchors for EUDI PID and Rulebook credentials ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2053](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2053)) An EUDI credential (the PID, or one a Rulebook governs) is issued by an https URL whose JWS names its key by an x5c chain, not by a DID. The VTC now trusts such an issuer only through operator-configured anchors, never by the chain alone. vta-sdk (feature `x509-issuers`): `x509_issuer` — `X509TrustAnchors`, `x5c_issuer_key` (validity, CA flags, chain signatures, ends at an anchor or a certificate an anchor signed, leaf key usage, leaf SAN URI = iss or dNSName = its host; P-256, secp256k1, Ed25519) and `issuer_jws_key`. Token Status Lists signed the same way verify through `verify_status_list_token_with_anchors` / `resolve_token_status_with_anchors`.

## [0.44.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.43.0...vti-common-v0.44.0) — 2026-10-13 ### Added - **keys**: Serve keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr — a verifier key that never leaves the VTA ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2057](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2057)) Custody B for the OpenID4VP verifier, VTA side. A VTC signing request objects with a VTA-held key, or obtaining an EUDI access certificate for one, needs the VTA to produce a JWS or a PKCS#10 request; keys/sign cannot, since it frames caller bytes under the opaque signing domain. keys/sign-jws/0.1 (tt-tf #749): the VTA sets alg from the key (ES256 for P-256, EdDSA for Ed25519), refuses alg/crit/b64/jwk/jku/x5u, checks the registered header members' types and that an x5c's first certificate carries the named key, and builds the signing input itself (RFC 8785 header and payload; payloadBase64Url checked canonical; integers beyond 2^53 refused). The specification's example signing input and its digest are reproduced in a test. - **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056)) * feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part. The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756): - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest, vetter/show - **vtc**: Storage configs — where a community keeps its rooms' files, changed only with consent ([#2052](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2052)) Phase P4 (first part) of docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7.

## `vti-vetting-pcs`
## [0.0.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/releases/tag/vti-vetting-pcs-v0.0.0) — 2026-10-13 ### Added - **vta**: The VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS ([#2056](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2056)) * feat(vta)!: the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — vta/pcs/* for clients that cannot run PCS A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge proof that distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and applicant holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a client linking the PCS library, so a mobile wallet (Keyring) could not take part. The VTA now holds those keys and runs every member-side operation (design vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §13 C7); the client carries messages and never holds a key. Twelve Trust Tasks (trust-tasks-tf #756): - applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove - vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest, vetter/show - **vtc**: Join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) ([#1907](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1907)) A community's join criteria are its join rules, and the VTC now decides a submission by them as vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 specifies (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#710, trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1). Nothing in the service assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any combination are all criteria an administrator registers. - Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission` (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`. `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`. - The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement. - A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the first it meets, else the first published. No criteria → `notAccepting`; an unpublished digest → `criterionUnknown`. Superseded versions are kept and govern while their `requirementsGrace` lasts. - The host verifies the presentation's embedded credentials (proof set, validity window, revocation, subject = applicant) and matches the query, applying DCQL `type_values`, which the matcher alone ignores. - The host holds the policy to the criterion: unmet → never admitted or referred (requestMore naming what is missing); met review → refer; met automatic → the policy's verdict. Policy may tighten, never loosen. The default join.rego follows the criterion. - A new community is seeded once with `invited` (automatic) → `member-credential` (automatic) → `review`. - The criterion and version that governed are recorded beside the request; a supplement re-decides under it. - DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope ([#1859](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1859)) * feat(vta-sdk)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role credentials are VACs Conform the SDK's vetting artifacts to the DTG Credentials Core Specification (v1 context, `issuerScope`) and the DTG VSC predicate registry, following the regenerated vetting specifications (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance). Vetting Statement (vetting/session/0.1): no longer an EndorsementCredential. `sign_statement` builds a StatementCredential with `new_vetted_vsc` under `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`; the body is `credentialSubject.object.value`, with no `type` member. `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are both read from the `vetting/session` document, which `StatementDraft::session` now carries in place of `task_context`, and `StatementDraft::issuer_scope` is `directed` or `public` (pairwise is refused by the profile). `verify_statement` parses through `dtg-credentials`, so the v1 context, the one-subtype rule and the profile are checked by the code that issues them; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_session` binds a statement to the session document by id and task digest. - `IdentityVettingEndorsement` -> `VettedObjectValue` (no `type`; digests and commitment must be base58btc, as the registry schema requires). - `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` -> `VETTED_PREDICATE`. - `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` -> `value()`; new `issuer_scope()`, `task_digest_multibase()`. Vetter role credential (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1, vetting/request/0.1): a community-issued VAC, `issuerScope` public, `authority` { scope: , actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }. `eligibility::community_role` -> `community_roles`, returning every `role:` of a VAC the community issued in its own scope with no parent; `verify_eligibility_vp` parses the VAC strictly and refuses a non-public scope or an attenuation. - `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` removed; new `ROLE_ACTION_PREFIX`, `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`, `role_action`, `role_of_action`. - `protocols::members::ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` removed; new `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`. - `VerdictWith::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (wire `roleVac`).

Changelog

All notable changes to this workspace are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the workspace crates follow Semantic Versioning.

Per-crate version history is summarised here; for the full code history see git log.

[Unreleased]

Removed

  • The mediator moved to its own repository, affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator. affinidi-messaging-mediator, affinidi-messaging-mediator-common, affinidi-messaging-mediator-config, affinidi-messaging-mediator-processors, affinidi-messaging-mediator-setup, affinidi-messaging-test-mediator, affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin and affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui are no longer workspace members here; their history was extracted to the new repository, which releases them in lockstep from 0.42.0. Consumers move from mediator 0.41 / mediator-common 0.17 / test-mediator 0.22 / admin and tui 0.11 to 0.42. The mediator Docker image, composed test stack and their workflows went with them. affinidi-messaging-mediator-types (the protocol contract) stays here beside the SDK. affinidi-messaging-didcomm-service 0.21.1 loses the four end-to-end tests that ran against the embedded test mediator; they moved too.

Added

  • IETF Token Status List. affinidi-status-list 0.1.7. A token module implementing draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21, the status mechanism SD-JWT VCs and the EUDI / swiyu profiles reference: 1/2/4/8-bit ZLIB lists with a decompression cap, the status-type registry, strict status.status_list references, and VerifiedStatusListToken::verify, which checks a statuslist+jwt signature (caller-supplied) before reading typ, sub = the referenced uri, iat and exp, and only then decompresses. Additive; the CWT form is not implemented.
  • Rate limits inside handlers, on any key. affinidi-rate-limit 0.1.4. KeyedRateLimiterState<K> limits on any hashable key (RateLimiterState is its IpAddr alias), per_window(max, window) and per_period(period, burst) state limits as requests per window or one per period, charge refuses with only the retry time, with_max_tracked_keys bounds a limiter's keys, with_limiter_name names the limit that fired in the refusal body, refuse gives handlers the layer's refusal response, and a public ClientIpExtractor gives handlers the key the layer charges, /64 grouping included (RateLimitLayer::ipv6_prefix). The layer now logs a client's first refusal per window rather than every one, a proxy's invalid X-Forwarded-For is logged once a minute wherever it is met, and Retry-After rounds up.

title: chore(deps): Bump syn from 2.0.117 to 3.0.6
body:
Bumps [syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn) from 2.0.117 to 3.0.6.
Release notes

Sourced from syn's releases.

3.0.6

  • Fix parsing interpolated lifetime at statement start (#2082)

3.0.5

  • Report correct span for lex errors from LitStr::parse_with (#2080, thanks @​sunshowers)

3.0.4

  • Allow safe fn in impl Parse for ForeignItemFn (#2078)

3.0.3

  • Documentation improvements

3.0.2

  • Add Error::new_range(start..end, "msg") (#2068, #2070)
  • Add Cursor::prev_span

3.0.1

  • Parse const traits (#2056, #2057, #2058, #2063, #2064)
  • Parse unsafe binder types (#2065)
  • Parse impl restrictions (#2066)

3.0.0

This release contains adjustments to the syntax tree to account for ongoing Rust language development from the 3 years since syn 2.0.0 and to anticipate some in-flight Rust language RFCs.

These include: default values in fields, pinned type sugar, raw lifetimes, generator blocks and functions, unnamed enum variants, attributes in tuple types and tuple patterns, named arguments in parenthesized generic argument lists, lightweight clones, const traits, const function pointers, mutability restricted fields, supertrait auto implementation, final associated functions, trait implementability restrictions, const blocks in path arguments, item-level const blocks, return type notation, never patterns, function delegation, mutable by-reference bindings, in-place initialization, field projections, explicitly dyn-compatible traits, view types, file-level frontmatter, generic const arguments, guard patterns, lazy type aliases, explicitly safe foreign items, super let, unsafe fields, pattern types, heterogeneous try-blocks, function contracts, async function trait bounds, static closure coroutine syntax, unsafe binder types, move expressions, for-await loops, and postfix keywords.

Breaking changes

Modifiers

To reserve more room for language evolution, there are 10 new non-exhaustive structs in the syntax tree having the following commonality:

  • Name ending in Modifiers. {BlockModifiers, ClosureModifiers, ConstModifiers, FieldModifiers, FnModifiers, ImplModifiers, LocalModifiers, TraitBoundModifiers, TraitModifiers, TypeModifiers}

  • Each implements Default. The default value is guaranteed to comprise no tokens.

  • Non-exhaustive. Can only be instantiated by Syn's parser or by creating and then mutating ▁▁Modifiers::default().

  • Does not implement Parse. When parsing, they are parsed by the enclosing syntax tree node.

  • Does not implement ToTokens. In some cases the syntax that these nodes might hold in the future is not necessarily contiguous tokens.

  • Provides .require_empty() -> Result<()> which returns a meaningfully spanned error if the modifiers are different from the empty default. This enables a caller to reject syntax it does not recognize without knowing what that syntax may be.

title: fix(rs,ts,ts-tsp,proof,didcomm,didcomm-v1,tsp,dart-didcomm,dart-tsp,go-didcomm,go-tsp): message bindings enforce document size bounds; shared extends routing vector (#1263)
body:
fix(rs,ts,ts-tsp,proof,didcomm,didcomm-v1,tsp,dart-didcomm,dart-tsp,go-didcomm,go-tsp): message bindings enforce document size bounds; shared extends routing vector (#1263)

Size bounds (#1121). GuardedConsumer::consume_body and
consume_body_dispatched, the inbound half of the DIDComm, DIDComm v1 and
TSP consumers, now hold a body to its specification's declared
maxDocumentBytes (SPEC §12.4) and refuse a larger one malformedRequest. The
refusal comes after the envelope has authenticated the sender, goes to that
sender, and is made before the item-11 record is written. The size is the
body's compact JSON text, because those stacks hand over a decoded body. A
specification that declares no bound gets no default bound.
consume_inbound and consume_dispatched used to hold a document read forward
along extends to the implemented version's bound. They no longer do, because
a later version may declare a larger bound. The Dart DIDComm and TSP
consumers and the TypeScript TSP consumer now apply the same rule. The
TypeScript consumer reads SPEC.maxDocumentBytes defensively, since core
0.29.0 does not carry it yet.

Extends (#1117). trust-tasks-go/didcomm and trust-tasks-go/tsp now require
the published core v0.11.0, use ReadForSpecWith, and take an optional
Consumer.Extends lookup that is passed through to ConsumeOptions.Extends.
They already pass the received bytes as ConsumeOptions.Received, so size
bounds take effect there once they require a core that carries #1251's
check, which v0.11.0 predates.
A new shared vector, fixtures/consume/extends-routing.json, is run by all
four runtimes. It found that TypeScript's readForSpec refused the
implemented version's own #request Type URI as unsupportedType; that is now
fixed.

Proof (#1092). verify_raw no longer clones the whole document (or the
proof) to drop `proof`. It serialises a borrowed view without that member.
The byte-for-byte fixtures still pass.

title: feat!: approve a relying party's session step-up without its tokens
body:
## Summary

The did-hosting console no longer hands the wallet a session's access and refresh tokens to step it up (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#445). The console opens the step-up itself with the session key its login bound, and asks the wallet only for the one thing a session key can never give: the holder's signed approval of the RP's challenge.

**New page method:** `window.vtaWallet.approveSessionStepUp({ rpDid, approveRequest })` → `{ approveResponse, holderDid }`.

- `approveRequest` is the RP's signed `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.5`, exactly as the page got it back from its own `auth/step-up/start/0.2`: a single-use challenge bound to that session and subject, with a short TTL.
- The background refuses the call unless `rpDid` is the RP DID the origin is pinned to by an approved login (`pageStepUpBindingRefusal`, now RP-DID-only: the wallet contacts no one for a step-up, so the base URL pin no longer applies to it).
- The offscreen runs core's `performRpStepUp`: verify (proof by an enrolled executor that is `rpDid`, `authentication` purpose, addressed to and naming the active holder, not lapsed, `didSigned` accepted) → consent prompt on the verified reason (unchanged `RUNTIME_STEP_UP_CONSENT`, minus `baseUrl`) → sign `approve-response/0.7` (`assertionMethod`). The page sends it and renews the session itself.
- The wallet makes no network request for a step-up and never sees a session token.

**Removed:** `stepUpVta` (page method, runtime/offscreen messages) and core's `stepUpVtaStart` / `stepUpVtaFinish` / `performStepUpVta`. Per this repo's rule, no compatibility fold: the console and the wallet cut over together (the console PR never calls `stepUpVta`). The only consumer of `stepUpVta` in the workspace was the did-hosting console.

A side note on the old flow: it signed `auth/refresh/0.2` with the holder's key, which the control plane refuses with `auth/refresh:sessionKeyProofRequired` for a session that bound a session key — the console's own renewal uses the bound key.

`demo/index.html`'s step-up button now explains the flow instead of calling the removed method (the demo holds no session key to open a step-up with).

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- Page bridge contract: `stepUpVta` → `approveSessionStepUp` (different params and result). Breaking for any page calling `stepUpVta`.
- A step-up is allowed for an origin pinned by a DIDComm login (no base URL), since none is used.
- Core exports renamed as above (core CHANGELOG, BREAKING).

## Tests

- `core/tests/rp-login.step-up.mjs`: `verifyRpStepUpRequest` accepts the RP's request for this holder and refuses another subject, another recipient, a lapsed request, another enrolled executor, a page-altered request and no document; `performRpStepUp` shows consent the verified reason and returns an `assertionMethod` approve-response addressed to the RP, signs nothing on decline, and never prompts for a refused request. Existing `buildStepUpApproval` / `verifyStepUpApproveRequest` tests kept.
- `extension/tests/page-rp-binding.test.mts`: step-up binding by pinned RP DID, another RP refused, DIDComm-seeded pin (no base URL) allowed, missing/non-DID `rpDid` refused, unpinned origin refused.
- `page-task-policy` / `approver-policy` tests updated for the method name.

No suites were run locally; CI runs lint, build and tests.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — the step-up now makes no fetch at all.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the wallet commits nothing; it returns a signed document.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — Trust Task documents unchanged; bridge params are camelCase; the one consumer is updated in affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#445.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no pin → refused; anything but an explicit consent → nothing signed.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — refusals surface to the page with the reason.

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart,go-didcomm,go-tsp,ts-tsp): settle the open runtime parity rows
body:
Settles the open rows of `docs/runtime-parity.md` as the maintainer decided (#1130), adds the TypeScript and Go halves of `maxDocumentBytes` generation (#1121), and closes the `Proof.created` question (#1119).

## Runtime parity (#1130)

| Row | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `InMemoryReplayGuard` capacity 0 | Rust panics, TS throws `RangeError`, Go/Dart default | default (100,000) in all four |
| `extends` chain bound | 256 / unbounded / 64 / seen-set | strictly decreasing MINOR (unchanged) **and** at most 64 links in all four |
| Prune recursion depth | 128 / 64 / 256 / 128 | 128 in all four. Every library counts payload levels and schema `$ref`/branch steps together, so Go's 256 measured the same thing. |
| Read-as name | todo | deliberately different, naming only |
| Bundled validator (TS, Dart) | todo | deliberately no, as Go |
| Discovery responder outside Rust | todo | still todo, low priority |

The two `extends` bounds are added to `check-bindings`' runtime-defaults comparison (read from the source; they stay private constants). The capacity rule is pinned by a test in each library. No public signature changes.

## `maxDocumentBytes` in TypeScript and Go (#1121)

- The prebuilt generators (`build-ts-bindings.mjs`, `build-go-bindings.mjs`) and the consumer-side generators (`trust-tasks-ts-gen`, `trust-tasks-go/cmd/trust-tasks-gen`) each emit the per-variant bound, independently, only where declared: `SPEC.maxDocumentBytes` / `Spec.MaxDocumentBytes`.
- `SpecPolicy` gains an optional `maxDocumentBytes` (TS) and a `MaxDocumentBytes int` field (Go, 0: none). Both are additive.
- `check-bindings` compares TS and Go with the front matter, as it does Rust and Dart: 70 bounds each.
- Enforcement: Go's `ConsumeInbound` refuses a document of `Spec`'s own version over the bound with `malformedRequest` (`DocumentTooLargeWireMessage`) when given its bytes as `ConsumeOptions.Received`. A document read forward along `extends` is never held to the implemented version's bound. The TS runtime never sees the bytes, so its transport enforces it. The Rust HTTPS server already enforces it (#1244).
- Regenerated: 48 TS and 48 Go modules gain the member. The Go and TS consumer-side equivalence runs pass against freshly built bundles.

TS API note: a generated `SPEC` const that gains `maxDocumentBytes` changes its `as const` type text, which `ts API compatibility` reports as a change. The TS core is already taking a breaking release since its last publish (#1236, `feat(ts, ts-gen)!`), so the job lets it through. The change itself is additive.

## Forward routing in the Go and TypeScript binding consumers (#1117)

The Go DIDComm and TSP consumers (`trust-tasks-go/didcomm`, `trust-tasks-go/tsp`) and the TypeScript TSP consumer (`trust-tasks-ts-tsp`) now re-read a document with `ReadForSpec` / `readForSpec` before decoding it, as the Rust binding consumers and the Dart bindings already do:

- A later version whose registry `extends` chain reaches the implemented one is consumed with its payload pruned to the implemented schema, and answered as the received version.
- An unreached version of the same slug is `unsupportedVersion`. Another slug is `unsupportedType`. Both are routed to the authenticated sender.
- The proof and the item-11 digest stay over the document as received.

Each module has a test that uses `rooms/records/put` 0.5 → 0.4 from the registry. The Go nested modules require a published core (v0.10.23) that has no `ReadForSpecWith`, so they follow the registry's chain only. The Rust HTTPS server already routes forward (#1244).

## `Proof.created` (#1119)

It stays required. Each proof package's README (`trust-tasks-proof`, `-ts-proof`, `go/proof`, `-dart-proof`) now says so and why, and the parity page records it.

## Checks run locally

`npm run check`, `npm run check-bindings`, `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --features acl --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features acl --lib`, `trust-tasks-ts` `npm test`, `trust-tasks-ts-gen` `npm test` + `scripts/equivalence.mjs`, `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go`, `didcomm` and `tsp` + `cmd/trust-tasks-gen` equivalence, `trust-tasks-ts-tsp` `npm test`, `dart test` (extension, replay), and TS/Go regeneration is drift-clean.

Closes #1130
Closes #1119
Part of #1121
Part of #1117


Merged `origin/main` (#1243, #1244, #1250, #1253): resolved `docs/runtime-parity.md` against #1244 (Rust HTTPS now routes along `extends` and enforces size bounds); `npm run regen` is drift-free.

title: fix(rs,https,dart-https): run the attribution gate before the route lookup (#1246)
body:
fix(rs,https,dart-https): run the attribution gate before the route lookup (#1246)

Both HTTPS servers looked the route up before the attribution gate, so a sender with neither a bearer token nor a proof could tell a registered type (proofRequired) from an unregistered one (unsupportedType).

The Rust server now runs on consume_dispatched_answer, so the reorder is made there: the checks that read only the envelope (expiry, recipient, freshness, identity) and the attribution gate move out of consume_core into envelope_checks, which consume_inbound and consume_dispatched_answer both run ahead of their item-3 type check. The route lookup still precedes the DID-method screen and proof verification, so an unregistered type never reaches a resolver.

The Dart server runs the same checks before the route lookup and before decoding the payload.
