title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.38.0
body:
### Added

- **messaging/mux/ack**: Acknowledge frames on the mux connection they were delivered on (0.1) ([#1174](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1174))

* feat(messaging/mux/ack): acknowledge frames on the mux connection they were delivered on (0.1)

- **vta/dids**: Key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians ([#993](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/993))

* feat(vta/dids): key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians

  Key roles were all-or-nothing: every key-role identity needed an external
  recovery key, and an identity without roles was not served at all. The VTI
  specification now gives every service DID a key assurance level its operator
  chooses (VTI-KEY-194): 1 single key, 2 role-separated, 3 recoverable.

  - vta/dids/create/1.1: `assuranceLevel` (2 or 3) is required;
    `recoveryCommitment` is required at level 3 and refused at level 2; a level-3
    identity under a method with witnesses needs one (witnessRequired); a
    template MAY set a level floor (assuranceLevelBelowTemplate). create/1.0 is
    released, so the changed shape is a new version rather than an in-place edit.
  - vta/dids/upgrade/1.0 (new): raise an identity's level in place, from 1 to
    2 or 3 or from 2 to 3, with fresh keys for every tightened role; never lower.
    `previousKeys` is retire (RECOMMENDED), revoke, or, from level 1, keep.
  - _shared/0.1 (additive): KeyAssuranceLevel, RecoveryCustodian and its kind,
    ThresholdRecoveryCommitment (a condition over whole keys, VTI-KEY-210–221),
    the declareAssuranceLevel change, the roleKeysInBackups warning; CONVENTIONS
    §3.4 (levels and the `keyAssurance` member), §3.5 (raising), §5.6–§5.7
    (recovery custodians, threshold custodians), §19, two family error codes
    (assuranceLevelMismatch, witnessRequired), and level-scoped custody, witness
    and approval rules.
  - 1.0 tasks, additively: keys/rotate gains `useRecoveryKey` and
    `recoveryProof`; keys/list reports `assuranceLevel`; keys/revoke
    `scope: boundary` and recover are level 3 only; update refuses
    `keyAssurance` and the removal of a level-3 identity's last witness.
  - Method profiles: did:webvh names the recovery commitment in
    `state.keyAssurance`; did:webs maps the levels onto its next-key threshold,
    every rotation exposes K and commits a fresh K′.
  - vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 now links vta/dids/create/1.1.

  Rebased onto main as one commit (was five, including a merge of main).
  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

- **vta/webs/dids/create**: DID classes, service DIDs and DID templates (0.2) ([#1159](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1159))

create 0.2 takes a required didClass (relationship, persona or service,
  VTI-KEY-190 - 193) and records it. A service did:webs - the durable identity
  of the VTA, a VTC, a VTN, a host service or an integration - is allowed at
  level 1 as an optional, alpha method (VTI-KEY-001 / VTI-KEY-003 as being
  amended, dtgwg-vti-spec#120), enabled separately in the VTA's configuration
  (serviceDidNotPermitted when it is off); didClassConflict holds VTI-KEY-193.

  A DID may be shaped by a DID template (template, templateContext,
  templateVars), exclusive of the explicit service and alias members. The VTA
  renders it and maps its document onto the did:webs derivation: one Ed25519
  signing key in authentication and assertionMethod, one designated X25519 key
  agreement key, designated services and aliases; anything else is refused
  with templateNotRepresentable (details.reason, details.members), and
  templateNotFound / templateVarsInvalid as for the other template consumers.

  Family conventions move to vta/webs/_shared/0.2 (CONVENTIONS.md section 1
  rewritten for classes and service DIDs, section 9 the template mapping;
  webs-records adds WebsDidClass and an optional didClass on the record).
  0.1 is unchanged and now superseded.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and Dart.

- **rooms/watch**: A live watch for an open conversation (0.2), and rooms/keys/watch 0.2 ([#1087](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1087))

* feat(rooms/signal-delay/set): a room may turn off the watch signal's randomised delay (0.1), served by rooms/info 0.4

  A host waits a randomised few seconds before sending a rooms/changed
  signal (producer item 4), so that a signal's time does not mark one
  write. In a room used as a conversation that is a few seconds between
  one member writing and another seeing it, on every message.

  rooms/signal-delay/set/0.1 lets a holder of `admin` set the room's
  signal delay to `randomised` (the default) or `none`. It is the room's
  setting, not a watcher's: an undelayed signal lets a party who sees both
  the write reach the host and the signal leave it match the two, which
  gives away every writer, so one watcher cannot opt out for itself. The
  request carries a reason and a proof; the host audits each change and
  may refuse a setting its governance will not apply
  (`signalDelayNotPermitted`). A room can choose only whether there is a
  delay, never its interval.

  rooms/info/0.4 serves `signalDelay` to every member, always present.
  rooms/changed/0.1 producer item 4 applies the setting the host serves
  and never a watcher's preference, and its Correlation section says what
  `none` gives up. `SignalDelay` is a new definition in
  rooms/_shared/0.2. Links to rooms/info/0.3 move to 0.4.

- **rooms/signal-delay/set**: A room may turn off the watch signal's randomised delay (0.1), set at rooms/create 0.3 and served by rooms/info 0.4 ([#1084](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1084))

* feat(rooms/signal-delay/set): a room may turn off the watch signal's randomised delay (0.1), served by rooms/info 0.4

  A host waits a randomised few seconds before sending a rooms/changed
  signal (producer item 4), so that a signal's time does not mark one
  write. In a room used as a conversation that is a few seconds between
  one member writing and another seeing it, on every message.

  rooms/signal-delay/set/0.1 lets a holder of `admin` set the room's
  signal delay to `randomised` (the default) or `none`. It is the room's
  setting, not a watcher's: an undelayed signal lets a party who sees both
  the write reach the host and the signal leave it match the two, which
  gives away every writer, so one watcher cannot opt out for itself. The
  request carries a reason and a proof; the host audits each change and
  may refuse a setting its governance will not apply
  (`signalDelayNotPermitted`). A room can choose only whether there is a
  delay, never its interval.

  rooms/info/0.4 serves `signalDelay` to every member, always present.
  rooms/changed/0.1 producer item 4 applies the setting the host serves
  and never a watcher's preference, and its Correlation section says what
  `none` gives up. `SignalDelay` is a new definition in
  rooms/_shared/0.2. Links to rooms/info/0.3 move to 0.4.

- **rooms/records/list**: Newest-first listing for a conversation's head (0.7), and rooms/keys/browse 0.5 ([#1088](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1088))

Chat clients open a conversation at its newest messages, but a room
  listing only paged forward from sinceVersion, so a client opening a room
  with tens of thousands of records had to page from the start.

  rooms/records/list 0.7 adds an optional `order` (`oldestFirst`, the
  default, or `newestFirst`), defined once as `ListOrder` in
  rooms/_shared/0.2. Newest first returns rows in descending version;
  sinceVersion still bounds from below; tombstones and lastPrune are
  unchanged; a cursor is valid only under the order it was issued for
  (invalidCursor otherwise). The spec states what makes it correct for chat
  although edits move a record's version: a newest-first listing whose
  lowest version is V holds every record whose current version is above V,
  so every message created since V; a reader orders by createdAt, not by
  row order. A record changed mid-listing moves above the listing's first
  row, so a catching-up reader takes the first page's highest version as
  its watermark, and only after reading to the end.

  rooms/keys/browse 0.5 passes `order` through, and adds `maxPages`,
  `cursor` and response `nextCursor`: a 0.4 recipient always reads the
  host's listing to its end, so order alone would still read the whole
  room before answering. The MemberProfile "Near the room's head" rule
  now says how a newest-first reader finds names (500 rows below the
  earliest record it shows reach at least 500 versions).

- **rooms/keys/read-marker**: A member's read marker kept by their key holder, so every device agrees on unread (0.1), and rooms/keys/list 0.3 ([#1086](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1086))

rooms/changed 0.1 counts unread messages against a read marker that was each
  client's own, so a member's phone and laptop disagreed about what is unread and
  a notification read on one device stayed on the other.

  - rooms/keys/read-marker/set 0.1: a member's client tells their key holder
    where the member has seen a room up to (room version + host createdAt of the
    newest message seen). The marker only moves forward (greater version; at equal
    version, later createdAt) unless `rewind: true` ("mark as unread"); the answer
    is the marker in force and `moved`, so racing devices converge without a
    precondition. Acting as the member, delegates refused, notHeld as for
    rooms/keys/label. Idempotent; retry class two.
  - rooms/keys/read-marker/moved 0.1: one-way, key holder to the member's other
    clients holding a rooms/keys/watch on the room as that member (never the
    setter), so a device can clear a notification.
  - rooms/keys/list 0.3: each entry may carry `readMarker`, returned under
    includePersonal beside the personal label.
  - ReadMarker in rooms/_shared/0.1/read-marker.schema.json.
  - rooms/changed 0.1 (draft, prose): a reader MAY keep its marker with its key
    holder; it is still never sent to the host, the room or another member.

- **messaging/mux**: Connections, an administrator's view of live mux connections ([#1083](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1083))

Adds messaging/mux/connections/0.1: an administrator lists a mediator's live mux connections — principal, wire (didcomm | tsp), openedAt, exact memberCount, and members with source, grantId, scope, expiresAt and deliveryActive — paged by cursor/limit with a per-page member budget that splits a large connection across pages, and a required coverage (allInstances | thisInstance) so a horizontally scaled mediator never implies completeness it lacks. Regenerates the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.



### Build & CI

- Guard version edits, release lists, crate size and released spec policy; one-pass registry dates ([#1213](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1213))

* ci: guard version edits, release lists, crate size and released spec policy; one-pass registry dates

  Pipeline fixes from the 2026-11-11 repository review.

  - Crate size ([#1097](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1097)): the `package` job fails when the trust-tasks-rs .crate
    exceeds 9.9 MiB and warns above 9.5 MiB; CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the
    package. Measured here at 10,308,682 bytes (9.83 MiB) after the exclusion.
  - deploy.yml ([#1133](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1133)): the deploy job joins one `deploy-production`
    concurrency group (never cancelled) and skips a queued deploy whose commit
    main has moved past, so an older run cannot roll the site back.
  - check-published-schemas ([#1134](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1134)): front matter parsed as YAML; the full
    derived per-variant policy (proof and issuedAt request/response,
    parties[].requirement, bearer) is compared; a deleted or renamed released
    file fails. Regression fixtures and tests in scripts/test-checks/.
  - rust.yml ([#1135](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1135)): the path filter covers fixtures/, ceremonies/,
    check-rs-api-compat.sh and release-plz.toml; published-schemas moved to the
    unfiltered checks.yml.
  - build-registry.mjs ([#1136](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1136)): created/updated dates and git authors come from
    one `git log` over specs/, skipped under --validate-only. Build 1m43s -> 6s
    with identical output; validate 2.6s.
  - Release rules ([#1137](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1137)): checks.yml refuses a version-declaration change in
    any PR but the Release PR; commit-lint refuses a BREAKING CHANGE line in the
    commits or description and accepts only an explicit list of `!` scopes.
  - check-release-lists.mjs ([#1139](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1139)): the npm, Go and crate release lists, and
    commit-lint's scopes against the release scripts', held in agreement.
  - timeout-minutes on every job that had none; rust-cache in ts.yml
    gen-equivalence ([#1141](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1141)).
  - `npm run check`, `npm run regen`, .nvmrc, new-spec's closing message, and a
    readable reserved-slug failure ([#1142](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1142)).
  - Drift checks use `git status --porcelain`; release-plz-release has a
    concurrency group; a withdraw re-run updates its existing PR ([#1143](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1143)).



### Documentation

- Fix drifted counts, release runbook, licences and stale examples across the four libraries ([#1224](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1224))

* docs(getting-started): move the worked example to acl/grant/0.3 and stamp issuedAt with issued_at_now()

  The example pinned acl/grant/0.2, superseded by 0.3, and stamped issuedAt
  with chrono::Utc::now(), the full-precision form #970 removed from the
  libraries. The TS consumer example wrote toISOString() milliseconds into
  document fields the same way. The dependency snippet now uses cargo add,
  so it cannot name a stale version, and §4.4 describes the shared version
  group instead of versions from 0.14.



### Fixed

- **runtime**: Bound the work of pruning a payload read forward along extends ([#1209](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1209))

* fix(runtime): bound the work of pruning a payload read forward along extends

  Pruning a later version's payload to the implemented version's schema runs
  before any proof is checked. Its cost could grow exponentially with the
  payload's nesting depth: in TypeScript, choosing a oneOf/anyOf branch pruned
  the whole subtree once per branch, at every level; in all four runtimes, a
  recursive member named from more than one place (properties and an allOf
  branch) was pruned once per place, at every level.

  Each runtime now gives a prune at most 100,000 steps plus 64 per value in
  the payload. readForSpec (TS), ReadForSpec (Go), readForVersion (Dart), and
  read_as, the dispatchers and consume_dispatched (Rust) refuse a payload
  that needs more as malformedRequest, saying why. prunePayload /
  prune_payload on their own return the payload untouched instead.

  TypeScript also remembers, for the rest of a walk, the branch chosen for
  each value and the structural matcher's answers, so a value under nested
  oneOfs is decided once rather than once per enclosing branch, and compiles
  each patternProperties pattern once per walk.

- **rs,build,cli,codegen**: Review fixes — declared guard code, SchemaValidator, keyword slugs, generate --lang rs, registry hints, docs.rs ([#1215](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1215))

* fix(rs): declared acl/revoke code in the guard, a caching SchemaValidator, docs.rs metadata

  - guards::acl::reject_last_authority returns acl/revoke:lastAuthorityProtected,
    the code every acl/revoke version declares (was snake_case); new
    LAST_AUTHORITY_PROTECTED constant, pinned to the generated declarations ([#1093](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1093)).
  - validate::SchemaValidator: a PayloadValidator compiling each schema once,
    cached by the schema text's address and confirmed against its content;
    validate_value and check_details use a shared one; prune_payload reuses a
    parsed-schema cache; PayloadPolicy::accept_unvalidated() ([#1091](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1091)).
  - docs.rs builds trust-tasks-rs with validate + acl and the facade with its
    non-spec features, and trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-https enable doc_cfg
    under docsrs, without which the docs.rs build cannot compile ([#1106](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1106)).

- **ts,go,dart,rs**: Whole-second capability-client issuedAt, tested Dart core floors, TS default export condition, Go schema caching ([#1214](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1214))

* fix(dart-capability-client,go-capabilityclient,go-didcomm): stamp issuedAt in whole seconds and fail on entropy failure

  The Dart capability client stamped issuedAt with toIso8601String (full
  precision); it now uses the core's systemClock. The Go port now stamps
  through trusttasks.SystemClock. The TS port already stamped whole seconds.

  The Go capabilityclient and didcomm UUIDv4 generators ignored crypto/rand
  errors and would mint an all-zero id; they now panic, as tsp's does.

- **dart-https**: Advertise the expiry horizon, and pin all four runtimes' freshness to shared vectors ([#1212](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1212))

* test(runtime): shared freshness vectors run by all four runtimes

  fixtures/consume/freshness.json pins SPEC §7.2's acceptance window (items 4
  and 13, *Bounding the record*): now / policy / issuedAt / expiresAt to a
  verdict and, for an accepted document, the replay record's expiry. It covers
  a stated expiresAt replacing the maximum age, the 30-day expiry horizon and
  its clamp on the record, a zero horizon, the half-open edges to the
  millisecond, skew on both sides, a missing issuedAt with and without
  requireIssuedAt, offsets, fractions and calendar-invalid timestamps, and
  holds each runtime's default and consequential policies to the same values.

  Run by trust-tasks-rs (tests/freshness_vectors.rs), @openvtc/trust-tasks
  (test/freshness-vectors.test.ts), trust-tasks-go
  (trusttasks/freshness_vectors_test.go) and trust_tasks
  (test/freshness_vectors_test.dart). The Rust workflow now runs on a change
  under fixtures/, which its integration tests read.

- **rs,ts,go,dart,proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof**: Refuse out-of-range timestamp fields instead of rolling them over ([#1210](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1210))

issuedAt and expiresAt, and a proof's created, are now read with every
  field range-checked after the shared pattern: month 1-12, a day the month
  has, hour 0-23, minute and second 0-59 (no leap second), and an offset of
  at most 23:59 (14:00 for a proof's dateTimeStamp, as for expires).

  Before, the four runtimes disagreed on the same bytes. TypeScript's
  Date.parse read 2026-02-30 as 2 March and 24:00 as the next day; Dart's
  DateTime.tryParse rolled 2026-13-45T25:61:61Z over into 2027 and took any
  offset; Rust's chrono read :60 as a leap second and accepted a space for
  the T; Go's time.Parse accepted +24:00 and +23:60. In the TypeScript proof
  verifier a regex-valid but unparseable created (month 13) gave NaN, which
  never compares later than the clock-skew horizon, so it was accepted.

  New shared vectors: fixtures/consume/timestamps.json, run by all four
  runtimes, and five correctly signed created-* proof vectors.

- **messaging/mux/ack**: NotPermitted only for a member whose mail the connection reads (0.1) ([#1179](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1179))
- **rs,ts,go,dart**: The in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records ([#1163](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1163))

* fix(runtime): the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records

  InMemoryReplayGuard (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) made room for a new id by
  dropping the least-recently-used record, whether or not that record was
  still inside its retention window. A document whose record was dropped that
  way was then accepted again inside its window, with nothing logged.

  - When every slot holds a live record, a claim for a new id now fails
    (Rust ReplayGuardError, TS ReplayGuardFullError, Go ErrReplayGuardFull,
    Dart ReplayGuardFullException), which the pipeline answers `unavailable`
    (retryable). Records whose window has closed are reclaimed first; a
    record is never dropped to make room. Duplicates and conflicts are still
    recognised while full.
  - The default capacity is 100 000 live records (was 10 000), documented as
    a ceiling on distinct documents per retention window, and exported as
    DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY / DefaultReplayCapacity / defaultReplayCapacity.
  - TypeScript, Go and Dart gain the expiry horizon Rust already had
    (`expiryHorizonMs` / `ExpiryHorizon` / `expiryHorizon`, 30 days in the
    consequential policy): a stated expiresAt bounds the acceptance window in
    place of the maximum age, up to issuedAt + horizon, and the retained
    record's expiry is clamped to the same instant, so a producer can no
    longer pin a record indefinitely with a distant expiresAt.

- **runtime**: Settle or release the item-11 claim on every remaining path ([#1177](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1177))

- Rust: the claim stays armed across a retryable refusal's awaited
    release and is disarmed on the next statement, so a pipeline dropped
    mid-release still releases it. A response or refusal whose `Serialize`
    panics is recorded with no response before the panic continues.
  - HTTPS server: `release_claim` holds a drop guard across its awaited
    release, on both the refusal and the panic branch.
  - `ReplayGuard::release_abandoned` documents that it must not block,
    require a runtime context or panic, and the default's degradation for a
    `release` that suspends, which a test now pins.
  - Go: a `MarshalJSON` panic in `settle` records the claim with no
    response, then the panic continues.
  - Dart: a final refusal that cannot be encoded releases the claim, so a
    resend is evaluated again, before the error is rethrown.

- **messaging/mux/ack**: An id held for a DID off the connection is notFound (0.1) ([#1176](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1176))
- **rs,ts,go,dart**: Refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under ([#1162](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1162))

* fix(runtime): refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under

  The typed consume functions took the document's payload type, or a spec
  policy, as given and never compared the document's `type` with it. A
  document of another specification whose payload happened to fit was run
  under the consumed spec's policy and handler, and answered as its own type.
  SPEC §7.2 item 3 assigns that check to the consumer.

  Each runtime's typed path now checks it before any other step, so a refused
  document never reaches the item-11 record:

  - accepted: the spec's own Type URI (`#request` and no fragment alike), or a
    later version of the same specification and variant whose declared
    `extends` chain reaches it (SPEC §5.2);
  - `unsupportedVersion`: the same specification and variant at any other
    version;
  - `unsupportedType`: anything else — another slug, the same slug under
    another authority or form, the `#response` variant, or a `type` that is not
    a Type URI.

- **runtime**: Release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and end the acceptance window where the record does ([#1175](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1175))

* fix(runtime): release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and close the window where the record expires

  A handler that panicked (Rust, Go) or whose future was dropped mid-await
  (Rust: a request timeout, a client disconnect) left its item-11 claim in
  flight until the record expired, so every resend of the document was
  absorbed as an in-flight duplicate and never ran. The claim is now
  released on those paths exactly once:

  - Rust: `consume_core` holds the claim in a drop guard across the handler
    await. A panic or cancellation releases it through the new defaulted
    `ReplayGuard::release_abandoned` (synchronous, as it runs from a
    destructor); a returned handler settles it as before. The default polls
    `release` once; `InMemoryReplayGuard` releases directly.
  - Go: a deferred release covers a panicking handler without recovering, so
    the panic continues unchanged. Release and settle run on a context
    detached from the request's cancellation (bounded at five seconds), so a
    store-backed guard is not handed an already-cancelled context.
  - Dart: when the response encoder throws after the handler returned, the
    claim is settled with no cached response before the error is rethrown,
    rather than left in flight. The effect happened, so a resend is absorbed.
  - TypeScript already released the claim on a throwing handler.

  The acceptance window over `issuedAt` (and the expiry horizon in Rust) now
  ends exclusively, at the instant `recordExpiry` returns, in all four
  runtimes. A guard drops a record once `retainUntil <= now`, while a
  document was still accepted at exactly `retainUntil`, so at that instant
  it could be accepted with no record and executed again. The window is now
  half-open, as `expiresAt` already was.

  The shared `fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json` vectors gain an optional
  per-case `secondAt` and two boundary cases, run by all four runtimes.

- **runtime**: Digest item 11 over the received document, and check envelope types and nesting depth ([#1171](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1171))

* fix(runtime)!: digest item 11 over the received document, and check envelope types and nesting depth

  Item 11's duplicate-execution digest is now taken over the document as
  received wherever a pipeline holds it, so two documents under one id that
  differ only in a member the payload type does not model, or in the spelling
  of a timestamp, are an idConflict rather than a duplicate:

  - Go ConsumeInbound digests ConsumeOptions.Received when set.
  - Dart consumeInbound digests `received` whenever it is passed (it did only
    for a forward read), and the HTTPS server, DIDComm and TSP consumers pass it.
  - Rust consume_inbound / consume_dispatched digest the received JSON under
    ProofPolicy::VerifyReceived, with or without a proof; the HTTPS server
    digests the body. New received_document_digest.

  TypeScript consumeInbound now checks the envelope before anything reads it:
  member types (string id/type and string-valued optional members, object
  payload/proof/ceremony, @context string/array/object) and a nesting bound of
  128 levels, refused malformedRequest and addressed only from string members.
  validateEnvelope and MAX_NESTING_DEPTH are exported.

  Dart consumeInbound refuses a document nested beyond maxNestingDepth (128)
  with malformedRequest instead of overflowing the stack, and the new
  parseTrustTaskDocument decodes a received value without throwing, returning
  a malformedRequest reason for a mistyped member.

  Shared vectors in fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json run in all four
  runtimes.

- **messaging/mux**: Revoke-all ends session attaches; accountBlocked covers ACLs narrowed below scope ([#1165](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1165))

messaging/mux/revoke-all 0.1 (draft) now ends the member DID's session
  attaches admitted before it, on every connection, before answering, with
  reason epochBumped; a principal that carried the DID only through an
  attach gets the live detached event and no notice. The attach spec lists
  revoke-all and a blocked or removed account among the ways an attach
  ends. DetachReason's description says accountBlocked also covers ACLs
  that no longer cover the member's scope. Bindings regenerated
  (descriptions only).

title: fix(runtime): bound the work of pruning a payload read forward along extends (#1209)
body:
fix(runtime): bound the work of pruning a payload read forward along extends (#1209)

* fix(runtime): bound the work of pruning a payload read forward along extends

Pruning a later version's payload to the implemented version's schema runs
before any proof is checked. Its cost could grow exponentially with the
payload's nesting depth: in TypeScript, choosing a oneOf/anyOf branch pruned
the whole subtree once per branch, at every level; in all four runtimes, a
recursive member named from more than one place (properties and an allOf
branch) was pruned once per place, at every level.

Each runtime now gives a prune at most 100,000 steps plus 64 per value in
the payload. readForSpec (TS), ReadForSpec (Go), readForVersion (Dart), and
read_as, the dispatchers and consume_dispatched (Rust) refuse a payload
that needs more as malformedRequest, saying why. prunePayload /
prune_payload on their own return the payload untouched instead.

TypeScript also remembers, for the rest of a walk, the branch chosen for
each value and the structural matcher's answers, so a value under nested
oneOfs is decided once rather than once per enclosing branch, and compiles
each patternProperties pattern once per walk.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(runtime): keep the recursive-oneOf case inside the walk's depth limit, and test prune_forward directly

title: fix(ceremony): decode the salt as multibase in every build, and compare digests by their decoded bytes
body:
trust-tasks-ceremony read the enactment salt differently depending on a Cargo feature. With affinidi (the default) it was multibase-decoded; with default-features = false it was hashed as the string's bytes. trust-ceremony-receipt/0.1 says the salt is "decoded from its multibase form", so the no-backend build did not conform, and because features unify across a dependency graph, a build that implemented its own Digester saw every digest change as soon as any other crate enabled affinidi.

multibase is now an unconditional dependency (it was already in the lockfile) and decode_salt decodes under every feature set.

Digests are now compared as decoded multihash bytes rather than as strings, in all four places verify compares them: the recomputed step digest against the receipt, a signed prev entry against the receipt, and the definition digest (supplied vs. receipt, and step document vs. receipt). The same digest written in another base (u…, f…) now matches. A value that does not decode only equals itself byte for byte, so a malformed digest can never match a well-formed one; a receipt step digest that does not decode is Invalid. A Digester whose output is not multibase is Error::DigestEncoding, since that is a broken backend rather than a bad receipt.

Security notes from reviewing the diff. Decoding receipt-supplied digests means running multibase decoders, some quadratic in input length, on attacker-controlled strings, which string equality never did; decode_digest therefore refuses anything over 256 characters (a SHA-512 multihash is 91 base58btc or 133 base16 characters) before decoding, mirroring the existing MAX_SALT_CHARS bound, with a timing test. Byte comparison uses a small length-then-XOR-fold helper with black_box rather than a new dependency; the spec says the salt is not secret from receipt holders, so this is defence in depth rather than a load-bearing property. The comparison is over multihash bytes, so the multibase prefix itself carries no meaning, which is what a multibase value means.

The fixture suite previously did not compile without affinidi. It now runs under both configurations, using a stand-in test digester when the backend is absent, and gains tests for the salt decoding, other-base digests at each comparison site, malformed and over-long digests, and a non-multibase digester. The test-single-family job in rust.yml now also runs cargo test and clippy for trust-tasks-ceremony with --no-default-features, since every other job builds it with the backend on.

No public signature changes, so no !. It is a behavioural fix for default-features = false builds only. TS, Go and Dart carry the ceremony.prev type but implement no receipt verification, so there is nothing to change there.

Closes #1094.

A default-features = false build hashed the salt's string bytes, so its digests changed whenever anything else in the graph enabled affinidi. trust-ceremony-receipt/0.1 defines the salt as decoded from multibase; multibase is now an unconditional dependency and the salt is decoded under every feature set.

Step, prev and definition digests are compared as decoded multihash bytes (length-bounded, constant-time over equal lengths), so the same digest in another multibase base matches, and a malformed digest never matches a well-formed one. title: fix(proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof): follow the JCS cryptosuites' @context rule in all four proof backends (#1233)
body:
fix(proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof): follow the JCS cryptosuites' @context rule in all four proof backends (#1233)

Signers copy a document's @context into the proof (eddsa-jcs-2022 /
ecdsa-jcs-2019 section 3.3.1 step 2). Verifiers hash the proof
configuration as received, and refuse a proof whose @context is not
exactly the document's (section 3.3.2 step 4, held to equality because a
ProofVerifier returns no verified document). The Dart verifier no longer
lets ssi copy the document's @context into the configuration, which made
it refuse what the other three signers emit. Documents without @context
get byte-identical proofs. Six shared vectors in fixtures/proof pin the
behaviour in every library.

so it cannot name a stale version, and §4.4 describes the shared version
group instead of versions from 0.14.

* docs(release): describe the one Release PR and the current package set

RELEASING.md still described per-language Release PRs, listed two of the
five version declarations contributors must not edit, called the Dart
capability client unreleased, and kept a one-time migration section for a
tree at trust-tasks-rs 0.14. It now names every published package (the
manifests and release-pr.sh stay authoritative), describes the merge of
the single Release PR per language, and replaces the migration with a note
on release anchor tags.

CLAUDE.md lists the trust-tasks-rs dependants with a command instead of a

and release-bump-ts.sh comments that contradicted the release wiring are
corrected (comments only). new-spec's closing message no longer tells
authors to bump versions; it says to regenerate all four libraries.

README.md states the Node 24 floor and that the libraries are Apache-2.0,
CONTRIBUTING-SPECS's template targets the latest framework version, and
both point the worked example at the latest acl/grant. The consumer-side
generation design doc gets a per-milestone status table.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(rs): fix the facade's stale facts and add READMEs to tsp, didcomm-v1 and capability-client

The trust-tasks facade documented a 0.1 dependency line (the crate
releases at the core group's version), called its crates eight
independently-versioned ones although they share one version, counted 26
spec-family features, and led with a line that compiles every deprecated
prebuilt module. The documented line is now the cargo add form with
default features off. The default feature set itself is unchanged.

trust-tasks-tsp, trust-tasks-didcomm-v1 and trust-tasks-capability-client
had no README, so their crates.io pages were empty; each now has one
describing its API, wired with readme = in Cargo.toml.

trust-tasks-rs's README drops module counts, sizes and a version that had
drifted, and links its licence absolutely so it resolves on crates.io.
The HTTPS, DIDComm and loopback examples stamp issuedAt with
issued_at_now().

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

consume_inbound's docs described "items 2 and 4-8" of an "eight-step"
§7.2 list; it runs items 2-8, 11 and 13 of thirteen, and the freshness
bound is item 13, not "item 4, the other half". validate_basic's table
gains the rows for items 9-13. reject_with said it stamps
trust-task-error/0.1; it points at TRUST_TASK_ERROR_TYPE_URI now, and the
constant's own docs no longer restate the number. freshness.rs said

ConsumeChecks carries. Code names in comments use the lowerCamelCase
spellings. trust-tasks-https's description no longer calls the crate a

map is demo-grade.

title: fix(ts,go,dart,rs): whole-second capability-client issuedAt, tested Dart core floors, TS default export condition, Go schema caching (#1214)
body:
fix(ts,go,dart,rs): whole-second capability-client issuedAt, tested Dart core floors, TS default export condition, Go schema caching (#1214)

* fix(dart-capability-client,go-capabilityclient,go-didcomm): stamp issuedAt in whole seconds and fail on entropy failure

The Dart capability client stamped issuedAt with toIso8601String (full
precision); it now uses the core's systemClock. The Go port now stamps
through trusttasks.SystemClock. The TS port already stamped whole seconds.

The Go capabilityclient and didcomm UUIDv4 generators ignored crypto/rand
errors and would mint an all-zero id; they now panic, as tsp's does.

Refs #1114, #1110

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(go,go-proof): cache parsed schemas and compiled patterns, pick patternProperties deterministically, precompute JCS sort keys

ReadForSpecWith re-parsed the payload schema on every extended document and
matchPattern recompiled every pattern per member, iterating a Go map so the
choice between two matching patterns was nondeterministic. Both are now
cached in sync.Maps and patterns are tried in sorted order.

proof's JCS canonicaliser now encodes each member name to UTF-16 once
instead of twice per comparison; the fixture proofValue test still holds.

Refs #1112

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rs): advertise no acceptance window when the policy's expiry horizon is below one second

AcceptanceWindow::of_policy dropped a zero, sub-second or negative
expiry_horizon but still advertised the window, which reads as "the
maximum age applies to every document" -- wider than the policy, which
holds a document stating expiresAt to that horizon (discovery responder
rule 1). It now advertises no window, as the Dart HTTPS server does.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(dart,dart-https,dart-capability-client): HttpsServer.handle never throws; generator swaps its output in by rename; capability-client example

HttpsServer.handle is documented 'Never throws', but encoding the response
(the caller's encoder, then jsonEncode) ran outside any try. It is now an
internalError reply, and handle has a last-resort catch around the whole
pipeline. consumeInbound already settles the item-11 claim when the
response encoder throws (#1177).

The generator's _replaceOutput deleted the output and copied the new tree
in place, so a failure part-way left a half-written directory. It now
copies into a sibling temporary directory and swaps it in by renames,
restoring the old tree if the second rename fails.

trust-tasks-dart-capability-client gains the example/ the other siblings
have.

Refs #1119

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(dart-proof,dart-https,dart-didcomm,dart-tsp): raise trust_tasks floors to the oldest core each compiles against, and test them

Every sibling declared trust_tasks ^0.9.3, but trust_tasks_https imports
trust_task_discovery/v0_4, which first reached pub.dev in 0.9.23, and the
other siblings' lib/ or example/ need consumeInbound's received: (0.9.6).
Each floor is now the oldest published core its lib/ and example/ compile
against, found by dart pub downgrade + dart analyze over the published
versions: https, didcomm and tsp ^0.9.23, proof ^0.9.6; capability-client
stays ^0.9.3.

dart.yml's packages job gains a downgrade leg per sibling that drops the
in-tree trust_tasks override, resolves every dependency at its floor and
analyzes lib/ and example/. It warns and skips while the floor names an
unpublished core (the Release PR crossing a minor).

Refs #1115

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(ts,ts-proof,ts-tsp,ts-capability-client,ts-gen): export a default condition and declare engines.node >=20.19.0

The exports maps carried only types + import, so require() of the
packages failed with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED even on a Node that can
require ESM. The import condition is now default (types still first),
which import keeps matching. The core's smoke test resolves ./runtime by
package name through both import and require().

Each package now declares engines.node >=20.19.0: the floor @noble/curves
and @noble/hashes 2 set for proof and tsp, and the first 20.x that can
require() ESM. The code itself is ES2022 and needs the global Web Crypto
API (Node 19+). Each README states the floor.

Refs #1108

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci(dart): tell a too-low floor from core API not yet published in the downgrade leg

title: fix(dart-https): advertise the expiry horizon, and pin all four runtimes' freshness to shared vectors (#1212)
body:
fix(dart-https): advertise the expiry horizon, and pin all four runtimes' freshness to shared vectors (#1212)

* test(runtime): shared freshness vectors run by all four runtimes

fixtures/consume/freshness.json pins SPEC §7.2's acceptance window (items 4
and 13, *Bounding the record*): now / policy / issuedAt / expiresAt to a
verdict and, for an accepted document, the replay record's expiry. It covers
a stated expiresAt replacing the maximum age, the 30-day expiry horizon and
its clamp on the record, a zero horizon, the half-open edges to the
millisecond, skew on both sides, a missing issuedAt with and without
requireIssuedAt, offsets, fractions and calendar-invalid timestamps, and
holds each runtime's default and consequential policies to the same values.

Run by trust-tasks-rs (tests/freshness_vectors.rs), @openvtc/trust-tasks
(test/freshness-vectors.test.ts), trust-tasks-go
(trusttasks/freshness_vectors_test.go) and trust_tasks
(test/freshness_vectors_test.dart). The Rust workflow now runs on a change
under fixtures/, which its integration tests read.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(dart-https): advertise the expiry horizon in the 0.4 acceptance window

FreshnessPolicy gained expiryHorizon, and the server enforces it, but its
trust-task-discovery 0.4 window still said the maximum age applies to every
document. It now states expiryHorizonSeconds, rounded down like the other
members, as the Rust responder does. A horizon under one second cannot be
stated without advertising a window wider than the one enforced, so no
window is stated for it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart,proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof)!: refuse out-of-range timestamp fields instead of rolling them over (#1210)
body:
fix(rs,ts,go,dart,proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof)!: refuse out-of-range timestamp fields instead of rolling them over (#1210)

issuedAt and expiresAt, and a proof's created, are now read with every
field range-checked after the shared pattern: month 1-12, a day the month
has, hour 0-23, minute and second 0-59 (no leap second), and an offset of
at most 23:59 (14:00 for a proof's dateTimeStamp, as for expires).

Before, the four runtimes disagreed on the same bytes. TypeScript's
Date.parse read 2026-02-30 as 2 March and 24:00 as the next day; Dart's
DateTime.tryParse rolled 2026-13-45T25:61:61Z over into 2027 and took any
offset; Rust's chrono read :60 as a leap second and accepted a space for
the T; Go's time.Parse accepted +24:00 and +23:60. In the TypeScript proof
verifier a regex-valid but unparseable created (month 13) gave NaN, which
never compares later than the clock-skew horizon, so it was accepted.

New shared vectors: fixtures/consume/timestamps.json, run by all four
runtimes, and five correctly signed created-* proof vectors.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix(release): raise the Dart siblings' trust_tasks floor when the Release PR takes the core across a minor (#1211)
body:
fix(release): raise the Dart siblings' trust_tasks floor when the Release PR takes the core across a minor (#1211)

The Release PR that first took trust_tasks across a 0.x minor (0.9.37 -> 0.10.0,
#1085) could not go green: check-sibling-core-ranges refuses a sibling whose
caret range excludes the core in the checkout, and nothing in the release
scripts moved the siblings' ^0.9.3.

release-pr.sh now passes the core's new version to each sibling's
release-bump-dart.sh, which raises a floor that no longer admits it
(scripts/raise-dart-core-floor.mjs, which changes only that constraint) and
releases the sibling for it even with no other change, with a Dependencies
line in its changelog. The unreleased trust-tasks-dart-tsp has its floor
raised too. Unlike npm this works inside the Release PR, because the Dart
siblings build against the in-tree core through pubspec_overrides.yaml.

title: fix(https,proof)!: verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default
body:
## Summary

**HTTPS client response proofs (`trust-tasks-https`)**
- `HttpsClient` verified a response's `proof` over `TrustTask<Value>` re-serialised, which re-renders framework members (e.g. `issuedAt` written with `+00:00` comes back as `Z`), so a valid signature could be refused. It now calls `DynProofVerifier::verify_received` over the body exactly as received, matching the server side.
- With `with_response_verifier` configured, a non-2xx `trust-task-error` is returned as `ClientError::TrustTaskError` only if its proof verifies over the received body and its `issuer` / `recipient` match the configured `server_vid` / `my_vid`. Otherwise the client returns the new `ClientError::UnverifiedErrorResponse { http_status, reason, error }`, documented as untrusted: the document is kept for diagnostics, but it must not be read as the server's verdict. Without a verifier nothing changes.
- `ClientError` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`, so variants can be added later without a break.

**Server DID-method default (`trust-tasks-https`)**
- A server with `with_verifier(..)` and no explicit DID-method choice now accepts only `did:key` in `proof.verificationMethod` (`DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DID_METHODS`), which never leaves the process. `allowed_did_methods([...])` widens it, and the new `allow_any_did_method()` lifts it. A server without a verifier is unchanged, because it already refuses proof-bearing documents.

**`CachedDidResolver` (`trust-tasks-proof`)**
- Every resolution has a deadline: `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT` (10 s), or `with_timeout(..)`.
- A host policy is applied before the client is called. A DID naming `localhost` or a loopback, private, link-local, shared-address or unspecified IP literal (`did:web`, `did:webs`, `did:webvh`, `src=` locators) is refused. `allow_private_hosts(true)` opts out, and `with_host_filter(|host| ..)` adds an allow-list.
- Note: the resolver cache SDK (0.8.43 in the lock) already has `DIDCacheConfigBuilder::with_host_policy`, which defaults to `PublicOnly` and covers hostnames that resolve to private addresses. This layer screens what the DID names, so the limit still holds when the client was configured `AllowPrivate` or a custom resolver is installed. It also adds the overall deadline that covers multi-fetch resolutions.
- `tokio` (feature `time`) becomes an optional dependency under `affinidi`. It is already in that graph through the resolver SDK and is already in `Cargo.lock` for this crate.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- Client with a response verifier: an unsigned or otherwise unattested error response now surfaces as `UnverifiedErrorResponse` instead of `TrustTaskError`.
- Client with a response verifier: valid proofs over non-canonical timestamp spellings now verify (previously refused).
- Server with a verifier and no `allowed_did_methods`: a non-`did:key` proof is refused `proofInvalid` before the verifier runs. Deployments using `did:web` and similar must call `allowed_did_methods([...])` or `allow_any_did_method()`.
- `CachedDidResolver`: DIDs naming private or loopback hosts are refused by default, and resolutions time out after 10 s.
- Adding a `ClientError` variant and `#[non_exhaustive]` is an API break, hence `!` scoped to `https` and `proof`.

## Tests

- `trust-tasks-https/tests/end_to_end.rs`:
  - `a_response_proof_is_verified_over_the_body_as_received`
  - `an_unsigned_error_response_is_unverified_when_proofs_are_required`
  - `an_error_response_signed_by_another_party_is_unverified`
  - `a_signed_error_response_from_the_server_is_returned`
  - `default_did_method_screen_admits_did_key_only_when_a_verifier_is_set`
  - The stub-verifier fixture now opts into `allow_any_did_method()`, because its `did:web` proofs never resolve.
- `trust-tasks-proof`:
  - unit tests for DID host extraction, the non-public host classification and percent-decoding
  - `cached_resolver_refuses_private_hosts_by_default`
  - `cached_resolver_host_filter_is_applied`

Not run locally; relying on CI.

## Checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the resolver now has a deadline
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire change
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): DID-method default, host policy and response attestation all default closed
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): unattested errors are labelled as such
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(https,proof)!: verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default (#1204)
body:
fix(https,proof)!: verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default (#1204)

* fix(https,proof)!: verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default

HttpsClient verified a response's proof over the parsed and re-serialised
document, so a valid signature over, for example, an issuedAt written with
+00:00 was refused. It now verifies over the body exactly as received, as
the server already does.

With a response verifier configured, a trust-task-error response is now
returned as TrustTaskError only when its proof verifies and its issuer and
recipient match the configured VIDs. Otherwise it is returned as the new
ClientError::UnverifiedErrorResponse, which keeps the document for
diagnostics but marks it as unattested. ClientError is now non_exhaustive.

HttpsServer with a verifier and no explicit DID-method choice now accepts
did:key only (DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DID_METHODS). allowed_did_methods widens it;
the new allow_any_did_method lifts it. A server without a verifier is
unchanged.

CachedDidResolver now gives every resolution a deadline
(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT, 10 s, with_timeout) and refuses a DID naming
localhost or a loopback, private-network or link-local address before the
client is called (allow_private_hosts opts out). with_host_filter adds a
caller-supplied host allow-list.

title: fix(go-proof)!: decode documents as I-JSON and refuse out-of-range ECDSA private keys (#1208)
body:
fix(go-proof)!: decode documents as I-JSON and refuse out-of-range ECDSA private keys (#1208)

The JCS decoder now refuses input that encoding/json would accept only by
rewriting or dropping part of it: invalid UTF-8, an unpaired surrogate
escape, two members with the same name in one object, and data after the
first JSON value. Such input canonicalized to the same bytes as a different
document, so one proof covered both. The verifier reports it as
malformedProof; Sign returns an error.

SignerFromPrivateKey now requires an ECDSA scalar of the curve's exact byte
length in [1, n-1], and derives the public key through crypto/ecdh instead
of elliptic.Curve.ScalarBaseMult. A zero, short, long or out-of-range key
is refused at construction instead of producing a signer.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: chore(release): 0.14.0 — did:webvh resolution as of a time
body: Release 0.14.0: did:webvh (and did:scid:vh:1) resolution as of a `versionTime` (#35). Bumps package.json and the lockfile, and dates the CHANGELOG entry.
author: stormer78

title: feat(did-webvh): resolve a did:webvh as of a versionTime
body:
## What

`resolve(did, { versionTime })` returns a did:webvh's DID document as it stood at an instant: the `state` of the last log entry whose `versionTime` is at or before it (did:webvh v1.0). Works through the resolver, `didWebvh.resolve`, `didWebvh.resolveLog`, and for `did:scid:vh:1` through its did:webvh log.

Consumer: pnm-browser-plugin's `verifyRecordBody` takes a `resolveDidAt` option so a room record's proof is checked against the author's document as of the host's `bodyStoredAt` (`SealedRecordBody`, *Which DID document*, `rooms/_shared/0.2`). Nothing can pass it until this resolver can answer as of a time.

## How

- **The whole log is verified first**, exactly as a current resolution verifies it: SCID, hash chain, every entry's proof under the update keys in force, pre-rotation commitments and witness thresholds. Only then is the entry chosen, and upstream is asked for that version by number, so the document has the same shape as a current resolution (implicit `#files` / `#whois`).
- **Before the DID existed** → `DidVersionNotFoundError`, `code: "E_DID_VERSION_NOT_FOUND"` (both exported). Callers can tell "did not exist then" from "does not resolve".
- `versionTime` is a `Date` or an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset; anything else is a `TypeError`.
- **Cache**: a call with `versionTime` bypasses the resolver cache and in-flight de-dup in both directions. A historical document is never served as current, and the reverse never happens either.
- **did:scid source book**: a historical resolution neither advances the book nor is checked against it. An earlier version is the right answer for its own time, not a stale mirror.
- A deactivated DID still resolves as of before its deactivation.

### Why not `didwebvh-ts`'s own `versionTime` selector

Checked against 2.8.0:

1. It compares strictly (`versionTime > updated` and `< next.versionTime`), so an instant equal to an entry's `versionTime` selects nothing and the call returns `notFound`. The spec rule is "at or before".
2. Once an entry is selected, a later failure in the walk is swallowed. The witness checks run after the walk, so a failure there skips them entirely: a log with a broken entry appended after the selected one would resolve without its witness thresholds ever being counted.

Both deserve upstream issues. This PR works around them rather than vendoring the library.

## Judgement call

A log that fails verification *after* the instant fails the historical resolution too. That is stricter than "verify up to the selected entry", but it matches what current resolution already requires and fails closed.

## Tests

`test/did-webvh-version-time.test.js` (14 tests):
- Rotation: before it, the old key resolves; at exactly the rotation instant, and after it, the new key; a key added after the instant is absent.
- An instant before creation → `E_DID_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`.
- Input parsing.
- Deactivated DID.
- A tampered entry before the instant is refused, and so is one after it.
- Pre-rotation log: history resolves with the update keys in force at that time.
- Witness threshold not met → refused, also as of a time.
- `resolve(did, { fetch, versionTime })` over a stubbed fetch.
- Resolver cache isolation.
- did:scid source book untouched.

`npm test`: 334 pass, 0 fail, 11 skipped (the Rust-fixture tests, as on main). `npm run build:types` clean.

No version bump. The CHANGELOG entry is under Unreleased.

title: feat(vtc): a did:webs VTC takes over the keys its VTA rotated (vtc keys request / refresh)
body:
`pnm webs rotate` replaces a level-1 did:webs VTC's key-state key and with it
the key's id, so the bundle the VTC stored at setup named a key its document no
longer lists, and everything it signed afterwards was material a verifier must
refuse (VTI-KEY-042). The only remedy was setting the VTC up again.

The VTC keeps no VTA credential, so the new keys come by the sealed hand-off
`vtc oid4vp` already uses, over the existing `vta/contexts/secrets` export:

- `vtc keys request [--out]` writes a sealed-transfer request and keeps its
  seed and nonce at `<data_dir>/keys/refresh.request-key` (0600).
- `pnm keys bundle <context> --recipient <request>` seals the DID's current
  keys to it (no VTA change).
- `vtc keys refresh --bundle --digest` opens it (digest pinned), resolves the
  VTC's DID afresh, and keeps each key only if the document publishes it under
  that id for its role (`setup::refresh::successor_bundle`): a bundle sealed
  before another rotation, for another DID, or holding a key the document does
  not publish, is refused before anything is written. The successor carries the
  derivation root (`carry_derivation_root_to`), so the at-rest storage,
  install-token and audit keys are unchanged. Written like setup and restore:
  inline in config.toml for the config backend, `set` otherwise.

At boot, a did:webs VTC whose resolved document no longer lists its signing key
refuses to start, naming the commands (`stale_signing_key`). An unreachable
host only warns. Level-1 (VTI-KEY-146) only; a key-role bundle is refused.

Docs: docs/02-vta/did-webs.md ("Changing it"), the S7 row of
docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md, vtc-service/CLAUDE.md.

title: feat(vtc): a did:webs VTC takes over the keys its VTA rotated (vtc keys request / refresh) (#2699)
body:
feat(vtc): a did:webs VTC takes over the keys its VTA rotated (vtc keys request / refresh) (#2699)

`pnm webs rotate` replaces a level-1 did:webs VTC's key-state key and with it
the key's id, so the bundle the VTC stored at setup named a key its document no
longer lists, and everything it signed afterwards was material a verifier must
refuse (VTI-KEY-042). The only remedy was setting the VTC up again.

The VTC keeps no VTA credential, so the new keys come by the sealed hand-off
`vtc oid4vp` already uses, over the existing `vta/contexts/secrets` export:

- `vtc keys request [--out]` writes a sealed-transfer request and keeps its
  seed and nonce at `<data_dir>/keys/refresh.request-key` (0600).
- `pnm keys bundle <context> --recipient <request>` seals the DID's current
  keys to it (no VTA change).
- `vtc keys refresh --bundle --digest` opens it (digest pinned), resolves the
  VTC's DID afresh, and keeps each key only if the document publishes it under
  that id for its role (`setup::refresh::successor_bundle`): a bundle sealed
  before another rotation, for another DID, or holding a key the document does
  not publish, is refused before anything is written. The successor carries the
  derivation root (`carry_derivation_root_to`), so the at-rest storage,
  install-token and audit keys are unchanged. Written like setup and restore:
  inline in config.toml for the config backend, `set` otherwise.

At boot, a did:webs VTC whose resolved document no longer lists its signing key
refuses to start, naming the commands (`stale_signing_key`). An unreachable
host only warns. Level-1 (VTI-KEY-146) only; a key-role bundle is refused.

Docs: docs/02-vta/did-webs.md ("Changing it"), the S7 row of
docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md, vtc-service/CLAUDE.md.

title: fix(https,dart-https)!: cap HTTPS client responses, keep bearer tokens on https, stop following redirects, and keep response bodies out of errors (#1205)
body:
fix(https,dart-https)!: cap HTTPS client responses, keep bearer tokens on https, stop following redirects, and keep response bodies out of errors (#1205)

* fix(https,dart-https)!: cap HTTPS client responses, keep bearer tokens on https, stop following redirects, and keep response bodies out of errors

Rust HttpsClient and Dart HttpsClient:

- The response body is read up to a cap (256 KiB by default,
  max_response_bytes / maxResponseBytes) and refused beyond it, with a new
  ResponseTooLarge error. A declared Content-Length over the cap is refused
  before reading.
- server_url / base must be https. Plain http is accepted for a loopback
  host, or elsewhere with allow_insecure_http / allowInsecureHttp, but a
  bearer token is never sent over non-loopback http.
- Redirects are not followed by default; a 3xx is returned as an HTTP status
  error so the signed document is never re-posted elsewhere. Rust can opt
  into same-origin redirects with follow_redirects(true); an https client
  never downgrades to http.
- Error text no longer quotes the response body: HttpStatus keeps at most
  512 bytes in its field and leaves it out of Display; decode errors keep
  only the category and position.

Dart only: every error the HTTP client raises (TLS included) is wrapped as
TransportException; the timeout now covers reading the body and cancels the
read when it fires; a responseVerifier requires a serverVid; a platform
client that followed a redirect anyway is detected by its final URL.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(https): keep the client transport-limit tests together at the end of the file

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

v0.12.0

Highlights

  • Restored support for no_std + alloc builds. Use: --no-default-features --features alloc.
  • Added Unicode Script=Unknown property support.
  • Improved correctness for ECMAScript Unicode Sets (v mode), inline modifier groups, and several Unicode case-insensitive matching cases.
  • Hardened parsing against excessively nested expressions, avoiding stack-overflow failures.
  • Reduced downstream binary size by avoiding forced inlining of regex construction and search internals.

Fixes

  • Correctly propagate flags from inline modifier groups.
  • Correct handling of nested and negated character sets in v mode.
  • Correct parsing of invalid \x escapes as identity escapes where ECMAScript permits it.
  • Correctly detect start-anchored alternations.
  • Include the v flag in Flags formatting.
  • Make Regex::find_from clearly panic when given an index that splits a UTF-8 code point.
  • Fix big-endian matching.
  • Avoid overly aggressive loop unrolling.

Performance and implementation

  • Improve PikeVM handling of one-character loops and reduce state allocation overhead.
  • Improve Unicode string-set lowering and longest-match ordering.
  • Improve case-folding/literal lowering internals.
  • Add a safety limit for deeply nested patterns.
  • Allow downstream users to share regex internals rather than duplicating them through inlining.

body:
Bumps [jsonschema](https://github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema) from 0.46.5 to 0.49.4.
Changelog

Sourced from jsonschema's changelog.

[0.49.4] - 2026-08-04

Added

  • Canonicalization of not a string format, which the string leaf carries as barred formats.
  • Canonicalization of not an existential demand, which an array fails exactly when no element matches.
  • Canonicalization of not a string value set, which the string leaf carries as excluded values.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedItems beside contains, where the elements it matches are evaluated and the tail admits either.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluated* beside anyOf or oneOf, where every branch evaluating the same keys or indexes pins what is left over.
  • Canonicalization of not an array element schema, which an array fails exactly when one element violates it.
  • CanonicalSchema::intersect, the values both schemas admit.
  • CanonicalSchema::negate, the values a schema rejects.
  • CanonicalSchema::definition, one reference target by URI.

Fixed

  • An integer past i64 admitted by a fractional bound f64 rounds it onto, such as -10000000000000000000000000 under {"maximum": -10000000000000000000000000.1}.
  • An integer past 2^53 admitted by a bound f64 rounds onto it, such as 9007199254740992 under {"minimum": 9007199254740993}.
  • A contains subschema beside both minContains and maxContains overwriting a sibling keyword of the same name, such as items.

Performance

  • CanonicalSchema hashing and equality cost the node instead of the whole document.

[0.49.3] - 2026-08-02

Added

  • Canonicalization of a recursive schema with no finite witness, which now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef, which resolve through the dynamic scope and stay symbolic like any other reference. A dangling $dynamicRef errors rather than staying Raw.
  • Canonicalization of minContains under uniqueItems, where a demand asking for more matches than its own schema has distinct values now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of a Draft 4 patternProperties coverage closed by additionalProperties: false, spelled as the closed map it was parsed from.
  • Canonicalization of a oneOf whose branches repeat, where a repeated branch can never contribute exactly one match.
  • Canonicalization of a $ref whose target is an empty schema, which now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedItems beside allOf, where every branch must pass and so the indexes they evaluate are known without the instance.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedProperties beside allOf, where every branch must pass and so what they evaluate is known without the instance.
  • Canonicalization of a Draft 4 type list holding integer beside other types with enum, which previously modeled only when spelled as an allOf.
  • Canonicalization of patternProperties patterns matching finitely many keys, such as ^a$ and ^(a|b)$.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems when no in-place applicator sits beside them.

Fixed

  • additionalItems values that are not schemas silently ignored beside an array-form items (they should fail the build like additionalProperties).
  • additionalItems beside a boolean items rejecting every instance, such as {"additionalItems": false, "items": false}.
  • additionalItems beside a non-array items value failing schema compilation with an error blaming additionalItems (the keyword should be ignored).
  • Draft 4 rejecting a size bound at or past 2^64, such as {"maxItems": 18446744073709551616}.
  • An integer past the f64 range admitted by a fractional bound it exceeds, such as 1e400 under {"exclusiveMaximum": 0.1}.
  • A $ref at the root of an $id-bearing subresource dropped as a self-reference when its pointer matched the one that reached that subresource.
  • Canonicalization reusing one definition's body for a same-named definition in another resource, when the name spells a canonical URI.
  • unevaluatedItems counting prefixItems as evaluating elements before Draft 2020-12, where it is not a keyword.

Updates `serde_with` from 3.21.0 to 3.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from serde_with's releases.

serde_with v3.24.0

Added

  • Implement JsonSchemaAs for NoneAsEmptyString, so fields using it compile with the schemars_* features (#1014)

Changed

  • Make with_prefix! and with_suffix! available with the alloc feature, instead of only with std (#1008)

Fixed

  • Handle potential panics in deserialization of chrono and time DateTimes. This was privately reported by @​NotAFlightRisk.

serde_with v3.23.0

Changed

  • Update syn and darling dependencies to use syn v3 (#992)
  • Update dev-dependencies to newer versions (#993)
  • Update base64 to a newer version. This should not have any API change, but some error messages might change. (#993)
  • serde_as can now parse cfg_attr(true, ...) and cfg_attr(false, ...) (#995) true/false are new literals as of Rust 1.88 but need to be parsed explicitly with the syn types. This is used when emitting schemars annotations.

serde_with v3.22.0

Added

  • Add support for jiff v0.2 behind the new jiff_0_2 feature flag (#936) jiff::SignedDuration works with DurationSeconds and its variants. jiff::Timestamp, jiff::Zoned, and jiff::civil::DateTime work with TimestampSeconds and its variants. Deserializing a jiff::Zoned uses the system time zone, like chrono::DateTime<Local>.

Fixed

  • Extend the GHSA-7gcf-g7xr-8hxj fix to the duplicate-key-prevention collections. The rust::sets_duplicate_value_is_error, rust::maps_duplicate_key_is_error, rust::sets_last_value_wins, and rust::maps_first_key_wins adapters created their backing sets/maps with with_capacity_and_hasher using the raw deserializer size_hint, bypassing the size_hint_cautious cap added in #966 (the clippy.toml disallowed_methods lint only covers Vec::with_capacity, not with_capacity_and_hasher, so these sites were not flagged). Attacker-controlled input claiming a huge length could panic with Hash table capacity overflow before a single element was read. All such constructions now route through size_hint_cautious.

title: fix(cli)!: refuse a plain-http registry unless it is on loopback or --allow-http-registry is given (#1203)
body:
fix(cli)!: refuse a plain-http registry unless it is on loopback or --allow-http-registry is given (#1203)

A registry's index supplies the digests a pin records, so over plain http
anything on the network path could choose both the digests and the bundles
they name. Sources were already https-only; the registry now is too, with
a loopback exception for local mirrors and tests and an explicit
--allow-http-registry flag. The https agent refuses http redirects.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: chore(deps): pin prettier at the root to the version trust-tasks-ts-gen uses (#1202)
body:
chore(deps): pin prettier at the root to the version trust-tasks-ts-gen uses (#1202)

The generated TypeScript is formatted by prettier, and the root build resolved
it only transitively, so a ts-gen bump left the root on the old version and the
bindings-drift check failed. Pinning it directly lets one Dependabot
ts-generator PR move both together.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: feat(did-webs): authenticate and encrypt to a did:webs party (JsonWebKey verification methods)
body:
Stacked on #38. A client can now authenticate and encrypt to a did:webs VTA, VTC or mediator, whose documents carry `JsonWebKey` verification methods and keys chosen by role.

**New:** `src/verification-method.js`, built on `jwk.js`.
- `publicKeyOf(vm)` reads `publicKeyJwk` (JsonWebKey / JsonWebKey2020: Ed25519, X25519, P-256) and `publicKeyMultibase` (Multikey, Ed25519VerificationKey2020, X25519KeyAgreementKey2019 / 2020).
- It fails closed on a missing or unknown type, a type and encoding that don't match, an unsupported curve, a JWK with `d`, or a revoked method.
- `selectKey(doc, did, relationship, …)` chooses by verification relationship, never "first Ed25519". With a `kid`, it uses that exact key or refuses.
- `x25519KeyAgreement` returns the X25519 key-agreement key.

**Now used by:**
- `mediator-auth.js` `extractX25519KeyAgreement`;
- `vta-rest-auth.js` `resolveVtaRecipient`;
- `vta-didcomm.js` `resolveX25519KeyAgreement` and `resolveX25519KeyAgreementKey`.

**Behaviour changes** (in the CHANGELOG):
- Packs to the first *X25519* keyAgreement entry, not the first entry. A key-roles VTA may list P-256 first.
- A verification method's `type` is checked, so a type-less method is refused.
- VTA REST auth now follows a relative keyAgreement reference.

**Tests**
- `test/did-webs-auth.test.js` (12 tests) uses did:webs VTA and mediator fixtures made by `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.3, run through the real resolver. It covers mediator auth, VTA REST auth, DIDComm both ways (a `skid` naming the authentication key is refused), and P-256 packing.
- `roundtrip-rust`: Rust `affinidi-messaging-didcomm` unpacks under the did:webs key ids.
- npm test: 404 pass, 4 skipped (as before).

**Follow-ups:**
- pnm-browser-plugin has its own copies of the key-reading code: `trust-tasks/verify.ts` `resolveEd25519Key`, `vta/tsp-vid.ts` `findEd25519`/`derefVm`, `vtc/directory-card.ts`, `vtc/domain-linkage.ts`. It also has `did/verify.ts` `didMethod`, which doesn't know did:webs. After a release of this library, the plugin needs a bump and those ports.
- `vta-rest-auth` resolves the VTA DID without the caller's `netPolicy` (unchanged here).

title: feat(did-webs): authenticate and encrypt to a did:webs party (JsonWebKey verification methods) (#39)
body:
feat(did-webs): authenticate and encrypt to a did:webs party (JsonWebKey verification methods) (#39)

VTI-KEY-003 makes did:webs a method every VTI party resolves, so a client
must be able to authenticate and encrypt to a did:webs VTA, VTC or mediator.
#38 resolves did:webs, but its documents carry keys as `JsonWebKey`
verification methods (`publicKeyJwk`, ids `<did>#<CESR key>`), and every
auth path here read only `publicKeyMultibase` — mediator auth, VTA REST auth
and the VTA DIDComm client (its recipient key and its inbound-sender lookup)
each refused a did:webs party with "no publicKeyMultibase".

`src/verification-method.js` (`./verification-method`, and
`verificationMethod` on the root export) is now the one place a
verification method becomes key bytes, and all four sites use it:

- `publicKeyOf(vm)` reads `publicKeyJwk` (`JsonWebKey`, `JsonWebKey2020`;
  OKP Ed25519 / X25519, EC P-256, through `jwk.js`) and `publicKeyMultibase`
  (`Multikey`, `Ed25519VerificationKey2020`, `X25519KeyAgreementKey2020` /
  `2019`; a compressed P-256 multikey is decompressed, `p256.uncompressedPoint`).
  It fails closed on an unknown or missing type, a type without its encoding,
  both encodings, an unsupported curve (secp256k1, P-384), a curve the type
  contradicts, a JWK with `d`, and a `revoked` method.
- `selectKey(doc, did, relationship, { kid, curves })` chooses by
  verification relationship, through absolute or relative references and
  embedded methods. A did:webs VTA with key roles (VTI-KEY-150 / VTI-KEY-173)
  binds different keys to authentication, assertionMethod and keyAgreement;
  a key is never "the first Ed25519". Without `kid` the first readable entry
  of an accepted curve is used (others are passed over, never used); a key
  named by `kid` — an inbound `skid` — is used or refused, never substituted.
- `x25519KeyAgreement(doc, did, { kid })`: the X25519 keyAgreement key. A
  VTA may list a P-256 key agreement key first; packing used to fail on it.

The `kid` / `skid` written into JWE headers is the document's own id, made
absolute against the DID when written relative. VTA REST auth now also finds
a relative keyAgreement reference (it compared ids exactly).

Tests: `test/fixtures/did-webs/parties/` holds a VTA (key roles: separate
attestation and operational Ed25519 keys; P-256 then X25519 messaging keys)
and a mediator (designated X25519 key agreement and DIDCommMessaging
service) minted by affinidi-did-webs 0.13.3 with known secrets; the README
carries the generator. `test/did-webs-auth.test.js` resolves them through the
did:webs resolver over a mocked network and covers the helper, mediator auth,
VTA REST auth, DIDComm to the VTA and back through the inbound-sender lookup
(a skid naming its authentication key is refused), and P-256 packing; this
library derives the same documents the Rust crate did. `roundtrip-rust`
adds did:webs VTA → did:webs mediator and P-256 to the VTA, unpacked by
affinidi-messaging-didcomm under the documents' key ids.

title: feat: read did:webs (JsonWebKey) verification methods by relationship (VTI-KEY-003)
body:
The VTI spec now requires every party to resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003). A did:webs document carries `JsonWebKey` verification methods, and a key-role VTA keeps a separate key for each relationship. This PR makes the plugin's own DID-document key reads handle that: keys are picked by verification relationship, never "any Ed25519" and never by fragment `endsWith`.

**New:** `packages/core/src/did/vm-key.ts`, a rule-for-rule port of vti-didcomm-js#39 (`publicKeyOf`, `selectKey`, `x25519KeyAgreement`).
- It fails closed on a missing or unknown type, a wrong encoding for the type, an unsupported curve, a JWK with `d`, or a revoked method.
- It is marked to be replaced by the library's `verification-method` export once a release includes it (R4.1).

**Sites**
1. **`trust-tasks/verify.ts`:** the key comes from the required purpose (authentication for step-up, consent and replies; assertionMethod for record bodies and domain linkage), or else the proof's own `proofPurpose`. Both encodings are read and ids match exactly. **Behaviour change:** a proof whose key isn't listed under the purpose it claims no longer verifies.
2. **`vta/tsp-vid.ts`:** the TSP signing key is the first Ed25519 `authentication` key (tsp-enablement D5), with no fallback. `derefVm` is gone, and a JWK with `d` is refused.
3. **`vtc/directory-card.ts`** and **`vtc/domain-linkage.ts`:** assertion keys come through `selectKey`.
4. **`did/verify.ts`:** knows `did:webs`; the host is checked before resolving (`egress-guard.ts`). `derive-signing-key.ts` has no `verificationMethod[]` fallback for did:webs. The extension's confirm screen shows "key event log verified".

**Tests:** `packages/core/tests/did.webs-keys.mjs`, using did:webs VTA and mediator fixtures with real signatures from vti-didcomm-js#39, plus a did:webvh regression and fail-closed cases for each site. `tsp.vid.mjs` is extended. Lint, build, tests, bundle assertions and the store package check all pass locally.

**After vti-didcomm-js ships #38/#39:**
- Bump the dependency and delete `vm-key.ts`.
- With that release, the plugin's default resolver resolves did:webs (#38), and DIDComm/TSP key agreement picks the X25519 key past a P-256 one (#39). Until then a real did:webs fails at resolution, never with the wrong key.
