body:
feat: read did:webs (JsonWebKey) verification methods by relationship (VTI-KEY-003) (#429)

Every party must resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003). A did:webs document
carries JsonWebKey methods (publicKeyJwk, ids <did>#<CESR key>), and a
VTA with key roles (VTI-KEY-173) lists a different key under each
relationship: the attestation key under assertionMethod, the
operational key under authentication, and X25519 key agreement after
a P-256 one. The plugin's own DID-document key readers assumed
publicKeyMultibase, fell back to "any Ed25519 key", or matched ids by
fragment suffix — each of which picks the wrong key for that document.

One reader now serves every site: core/src/did/vm-key.ts (publicKeyOf,
selectKey, x25519KeyAgreement), a port of vti-didcomm-js #39's
verification-method module, to be replaced by that export when the
plugin moves to the release that ships it (R4.1). It fails closed on an
unknown or missing type, an encoding the type does not carry, both
encodings, an unsupported curve, a JWK carrying d, or a revoked method.

- trust-tasks/verify.ts: the proof key is read from the relationship
  the proof is for (the required purpose, else the proof's own
  proofPurpose), in either encoding; no endsWith fallback.
- vta/tsp-vid.ts: the VID signing key is the authentication key only
  (tsp-enablement D5); no "any Ed25519" fallback, exact dereference,
  type checks; rawFromOkpJwk refuses d.
- vtc/directory-card.ts assertionKeys and vtc/domain-linkage.ts
  assertionKey read assertionMethod through the same reader.
- did/verify.ts didMethod knows webs (didWebsDomain, host guarded before
  resolution); deriveSigningKeyId offers no bare verificationMethod ids
  for a did:webs.

Tests use vti-didcomm-js's did:webs party documents (VTA with key
roles, mediator), with a did:webvh regression and fail-closed cases at
each site.

title: feat(did-webs): resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003)
body:
Adds did:webs resolution in pure JS, so browser and Node clients can verify a VTA or VTC whose DID is a did:webs. The VTI spec now requires every node to resolve did:webs (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#123, VTI-KEY-003).

It is a port of the Rust reference `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.3 and is held to it by recorded vectors.

**What it does**
- Four modules: `src/did-webs.js` (identifier, fetch, document, `did.json` check), `src/did-webs-cesr.js`, `src/did-webs-kel.js` and `src/did-webs-designations.js`. Registered in the default resolver, cached like did:webvh, and exported as `./did-webs`.
- Reads KERI 1 and 2 (native and mixed streams), including thresholds (weighted too), pre-rotation, recovery, delegation (`dip`/`drt`), witnesses and deactivation.
- Derives the document with the key-role, key-agreement, service and alias designations, and accepts `did.json` only if it matches.
- A deactivated DID is refused (`kind: "Deactivated"`). `versionId` DID URLs work; `versionTime` is refused.
- Fetching goes through net-guard: both URLs are checked before any request, redirects are refused, each body is capped at 4 MiB, each request times out after 20 s, and stream limits match the Rust crate.
- CBOR and MessagePack bodies are refused.

**Conformance:** 1,749 vectors, all giving the same answer as Rust (the same document, or the same error kind).
- 160 were recorded from the Rust crate's own tests.
- 1,589 were generated: lifecycles at every version, key roles, thresholds, recovery, witnesses, delegation, plus mutation sweeps and `did.json` edits.
- The fixtures README says how to regenerate them. SSRF and cache tests are modelled on did:webvh's.

**Dependency:** `@noble/hashes` (blake3) is now direct. It was already installed through `@noble/curves`.

**Not in this PR:** DIDComm and REST auth with a did:webs VTA. `mediator-auth`, `vta-rest-auth` and `vta-didcomm` read only `publicKeyMultibase`, and did:webs documents carry `JsonWebKey`. That's a follow-up, because the same auth code is copied in the plugin and relay.

npm test: 390 pass, 4 skipped (live infra), on Node 20 and 26.

title: feat(did-webs): resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003) (#38)
body:
feat(did-webs): resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003) (#38)

* feat(did-webs): resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003)

The VTI specification makes did:webs a method every VTI party must resolve
(VTI-KEY-003), so a browser client has to verify a VTA or VTC whose DID is a
did:webs. This adds a pure-JavaScript did:webs resolver, registered with the
default resolver and exported as `./did-webs`.

It is a port of `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.3 and the `affinidi-keri-core`
0.8.1 it verifies with, rule for rule and in the same order:

- CESR: both counter tables (genus 1.x and 2.x, the genus-version counter,
  mixed streams), JSON and native CESR bodies (with keripy's round-trip
  check), indexed signatures including big codes, every attachment group
  the Rust parser reads; strict, so an uninterpretable group fails the
  stream.
- KEL: SAIDs (Blake3-256) and field lists per version; simple, hex and
  weighted thresholds; pre-rotation over exposed digests (nt), partial
  reveal and reordering; witness receipts, attached or in rct messages;
  dip/drt delegation anchored in the delegator's verified log, DND, cycle
  and depth bounds; superseding recovery (P7); EO; abandonment.
- Designations from 1.x TELs and 2.x rip/bup registries, with every
  anchored registry event required in the stream: designated aliases,
  key agreement (X25519, P-256, secp256k1), services, key roles
  (VTI-KEY-173), and critical designations this resolver does not
  implement, which fail resolution.
- KERI endpoint services under BADA order, the DelegatorOOBI service, and
  the converted X25519 key agreement of an AID that designates none.
- The document derived from that state and a did.json, in either form,
  checked against it as the Rust crate checks it; versionId resolution.

0.13.3 rather than 0.13.1: it is the reference on affinidi-tdk-rs main and
carries fixes to 0.13.1 that a client must have. A deactivated identifier
no longer resolves to its last keys (resolve refuses it with kind
"Deactivated"; resolveFromArtifacts reports deactivated and, at the
deactivating version, a document without keys); host and path labels must
decode to a host and single segments; and a stream is bounded in messages,
signatures, witnesses, seals and unimplemented critical schemas, with the
key state at each establishment event computed once rather than replayed
per reply.

Fetching goes through the net-guard egress policy (both artifact URLs
vetted before any request, redirects refused), each artifact is capped at
4 MiB while it is read, and each request has a timeout. Plain http is used
for a loopback host under allowPrivate and for any host under
allowInsecure, as the Rust HostPolicy::AllowPrivate and allow_http do.
versionTime is refused: did:webs history is by key event.

Refused rather than read: CBOR and MessagePack bodies, and non-integer
numbers in messages.

Conformance: test/fixtures/did-webs/rust-vectors holds 1,749 calls the Rust
crate answered (its own test suite, recorded through a shim, and generated
lifecycles, KEL edge cases and mutation sweeps); every one gets the same
answer here, the same document where Rust accepts and the same error kind
where it refuses. @noble/hashes becomes a direct dependency.

title: feat(vtc): a VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID
body:
A VTC can be set up and run with a level-1 did:webs as its own DID (VTI-KEY-001), the same way as a did:webvh VTC. Level 1 is conformant (VTI-KEY-146). Level 2+ (VTI-KEY-196, a SHOULD) waits on `vta/dids/create`, as it does for did:webvh VTCs.

**Template:** `vtc-host-classical` is a built-in derived from `vtc-host.json` when it's loaded. It is `vtc-host` minus the post-quantum slot, which did:webs level 1 can't carry (CONVENTIONS 0.2 §9.2 refuses a second signing slot, and KERI has no ML-DSA). A drift test pins the relationship. `vtc-host` is still refused under did:webs. A did:webs VTC's credentials therefore carry one eddsa proof, which is documented.

**Checker fix:** a whole-value service variable (`SERVICE_TSP` / `SERVICE_DIDCOMM`) keeps `{DID}#frag`, and the did:webs checker now reads that as the DID's own fragment. Previously every template using them was refused.

**Setup** (interactive and TOML `identity_method = "webs"`):
- provisions `vtc-host-classical` with `DID_METHOD=webs` at a did-hosting server;
- writes no `did.jsonl` (the host serves `keri.cesr`);
- refuses a VTA that minted something else, naming the settings it needs.

**Runtime:**
- `VtcKeyBundle::key_role_ids` uses the bundle's own ids, so signing and authentication use the key-state key. Before, every credential, status list, Trust Task and attested response named a missing `#key-0`.
- `pnm webs update --services` keeps the other designated services (the update replaces the whole set), pinning `expectedVersionId`.
- `cnm storage` seals to the community's key-agreement key, chosen by role, as multibase or JWK.

**Tests:**
- VTA end to end: a VTC host provisioned as did:webs.
- VTC first-boot setup against a real level-1 KEL.
- A did:webs VTC's credential, Trust Task request, reply and attested response all verify against its resolved document.
- did:webvh goldens unchanged.

Local: nextest workspace 7468 passed, vtc 3724 passed, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and the no-webs check all pass.

**Known limits:**
- Rotating the VTC's key-state key through the VTA makes its stored bundle stale, so the VTC needs setting up again (documented).
- `pnm` has no flag to add new services.
- No boot-time transport check without a local document.
author: stormer78

title: feat(vtc): a VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID (#2698)
body:
feat(vtc): a VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID (#2698)

* feat(vta-sdk): vtc-host-classical, the VTC template a level-1 did:webs can carry

A level-1 did:webs holds one key-state signing key, and CONVENTIONS.md 0.2
§9.2 refuses vtc-host's second (post-quantum) signing slot as keyAlgorithm and
forbids a VTA to drop what a template describes; the template keys block has no
optional slot (vta/did-templates/* 3.1). So a did:webs VTC (VTI-KEY-001) names a
template that does not ask for the key: vtc-host-classical, vtc-host less the
pq-signing slot, its verification method and its assertionMethod reference.
It is derived from vtc-host when loaded, not shipped as a second file, so the
two cannot drift (pinned by a test rendering both). The §9.2 check is
unchanged: vtc-host stays refused, every other refusal stands.

The §9.2 service rule reads a `{DID}#…` id as the DID's own fragment: a
service supplied whole as a variable (SERVICE_TSP, SERVICE_DIDCOMM) keeps the
placeholder, because a whole-value substitution is not substituted again, and
was refused under did:webs as "not a fragment".

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): a VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID (VTI-KEY-001)

`vtc setup` offers did:webs for the community's own DID: interactively, as a
method prompt before the hosting-server picker (no serverless option), and in
TOML as `identity_method = "webs"`, which requires `[webvh] server_id`, refuses
path `.well-known` and `scid_also_known_as`. Setup provisions through
provision-integration as for did:webvh, naming vtc-host-classical with
DID_METHOD=webs, WEBVH_SERVER/DOMAIN/PATH. Level 1 (VTI-KEY-146), as today's
did:webvh VTCs are; a key-role VTC waits on vta/dids/create.

No did.jsonl is written: the VTA published the keri.cesr stream at the host,
which serves it. Setup checks the bundle carries the stream and that the VTA
minted a did:webs (a VTA ignoring DID_METHOD=webs is refused, naming the
settings it needs), and the reverse for a did:webvh ask.

Keys by the document's ids: a bundle without key roles whose ids are not
#key-0/#key-1 (a level-1 did:webs names its key by itself) now answers
`key_role_ids` with them, signing = authentication = the key-state key, as
NodeKeyIds::from_document reads that document. So credentials, status lists,
Trust Task requests and replies, attested responses, DIDComm/TSP and
`vtc status` sign and decrypt under the ids the document publishes, with no
resolution; before, they named a #key-0 the document does not have. A
did:webvh bundle is unchanged (still None).

`apply` splits into the round-trip and `persist_provisioned`, and
`provision_ask` builds what is sent, so first-boot setup is tested against a
VTA's reply. The did:webs sign-in self-check and OOB fix texts name the VTA
update instead of `dids edit` / `cnm did-log install`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-cli-common): webs update --services keeps every other designated service

`vta/webs/dids/update` replaces the whole service set, and `--services` names
only #didcomm and #tsp, so changing a transport withdrew every other
designated service — a did:webs VTC's VTCRest, VTCStatusList, TrustTaskHTTPS
and SignInPortal. The command now reads the DID's services back, states the
others again as `services.additional`, and pins expectedVersionId to the
version it read (unless one was given), so a concurrent change is a
versionConflict rather than a lost update.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(cnm-cli): seal storage credentials to a did:webs community's key

`cnm storage credentials set` sealed to the community's #key-0, or any
publicKeyMultibase Ed25519 key; a did:webs document publishes its key-state
key as a JWK under its own id, so sealing failed. The key is now found by role
(the signing key NodeKeyIds names, VTI-KEY-150) in either encoding — the key
the VTC opens sealed credentials with.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(did-webs): a VTC as a did:webs; setup, templates and the S7 status

The operator guide gains "A VTC as a did:webs" (provisioning, no post-quantum
key, keys by id, no log to serve, changing it through the VTA); the VTC
first-boot and non-interactive setup guides and the example TOML document
`identity_method`; did-templates lists vtc-host-classical; the design note
marks S7 done at level 1, with what is not.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

This release collects the fixes and small features merged since 15.0.4. Several of them correct types that were previously emitted wrong, so existing schemas may generate different output; hence the major version.

New:

  • e3c7776 Feat: Support OpenAPI 3.0 nullable: true, including next to a $ref; such schemas now emit T | null (#755, fixes #410)
  • ab31f41 Feat: Support draft-3 / Swagger 2 property-level required: true; such properties are now emitted as required (#756, fixes #440, #6)
  • 111c187 Feat: Resolve draft-07 named-anchor $refs ("#name" matching a sibling $id: "#name") instead of crashing (#744, fixes #220)

May change emitted types for existing schemas:

  • efceb64 Bugfix: Multiple patternProperties (or patternProperties with additionalProperties: false) are folded into one index signature typed as the union of their value types, instead of being dropped (#754, fixes #160, #315)
  • b84b3da Bugfix: allOf members made up only of unsupported keywords (eg. if/then, not) no longer add a stray {[k: string]: unknown} to the intersection (#743, fixes #369)
  • d8618e5 Bugfix: properties/patternProperties on a nested schema were dropped when combined with oneOf/anyOf/allOf; they are now intersected with the compound type (#708, fixes #630)
  • 4eee0f1 Bugfix: $refs to definitions with dotted names (eg. #/definitions/v1.ManagedFieldsEntry) were truncated at the first dot (V1); the full name is now used (V1ManagedFieldsEntry) (#705, fixes #645)
  • 7a3dd8e Bugfix: Nested arrays with minItems/maxItems are capped by the cumulative product of their bounds against maxItems, falling back to an unbounded array instead of hanging or emitting enormous tuple unions (#703, fixes #690)
  • 34a692c Bugfix: type: null (the JSON null value) is treated as type: "null" instead of as an untyped object (#702, fixes #667)
  • 0f9d309 Bugfix: unreachableDefinitions now declares definitions even when declareExternallyReferenced is off (#706, fixes #652)
  • 1900e1f Bugfix: With inferStringEnumKeysFromValues, a const is emitted as a literal type again rather than a single-member enum (#701, fixes #666)
  • 606e359 Bugfix: A schema with an array type and properties (eg. type: ['object', 'null']) at the root or as an untitled definition compiled to A & (A | null), making the non-object members unreachable; it now emits A | null (#753, supersedes #672)
  • c73ea75 Bugfix: An empty schema inside allOf (eg. allOf: [{$ref: '#/definitions/User'}, {}]) collapsed the whole intersection to unknown; the empty member is now dropped and User is kept (#752, fixes #654)
  • 9c50776 Bugfix: The description of an inline items schema is no longer dropped; it is added to the JSDoc of the array's declaration as an Items: ... paragraph (#751, fixes #660)

Fixes for crashes and output that did not compile:

  • b25c768 Bugfix: A root-level $ref to a definition that is itself only a $ref no longer crashes with "Refs should have been resolved by the resolver!" (#741, fixes #740)
  • b25c768 Bugfix: A root-level $ref to a definition that refers back to itself (directly or through items/properties) compiles instead of crashing with the same error (#741, fixes #132, #730). The referenced definition is still emitted as its own interface alongside the root type
  • 107dd42 Bugfix: Index signatures from patternProperties/additionalProperties are widened to cover sibling named properties, so the interface typechecks (TS2411). Index signatures that already typechecked are emitted type-equivalent to before (#704, fixes #671)
  • a2234d3 Bugfix: inferStringEnumKeysFromValues no longer produces invalid enum members for non-string, empty or digit-leading values (#694, fixes #657)
  • 377c6a1 Bugfix: A named enum (tsEnumNames) in a position with no name no longer emits a nameless enum declaration; it degrades to a union of literals (#693, fixes #691)
  • c44faed Bugfix: Generated type names can no longer start with a digit or collapse to an empty name (#698, fixes #640)
  • 8d8a141 Bugfix: Recursive schemas that reach the generator without a name (a self-referencing $ref with a sibling keyword such as description, a recursive oneOf under components/schemas, an untitled recursive schema in another file) are given a generated type name instead of overflowing the stack. Schemas that compiled before are unchanged, except that an anonymous recursive union with a {}/true member now keeps its alias (same type, one extra export type) (#760, fixes #482, #614)

Other:

  • bf06bbb Bugfix (CLI): Piping a schema on stdin no longer prints a DEP0187 deprecation warning on Node 24 (#750)
  • 3abde40 Perf: compile() no longer scans every definition once per parsed node; schemas with thousands of definitions compile much faster (schemastore's CloudFormation schema: ~54 s -> ~3 s). Generated output is unchanged (#759)
  • b88891c Perf: Formatting large, mostly quote-free outputs is several times faster (prettier is told the output is a .d.ts, so it skips its JSX-detection scan); a caller's own style.filepath still wins. Generated output is unchanged (#758)
  • 16c2e77 Bugfix (CLI): relative $refs are resolved against each schema file's own directory rather than process.cwd(), so a schema passed by path from another directory finds its siblings; an explicit --cwd still wins (#742, fixes #324, #680)
  • 9219636 Updated runtime dependencies: js-yaml 4 -> 5 (YAML files parse as before, #689), prettier ^3.9 (short unions that fit on one line are no longer wrapped; users on the existing ^3.2.5 range may already see this), @​apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser ^11.9 (#686)
  • a5834aa Removed the is-glob dependency (#643)

Updates `serde_with` from 3.21.0 to 3.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from serde_with's releases.

serde_with v3.24.0

Added

  • Implement JsonSchemaAs for NoneAsEmptyString, so fields using it compile with the schemars_* features (#1014)

Changed

  • Make with_prefix! and with_suffix! available with the alloc feature, instead of only with std (#1008)

Fixed

  • Handle potential panics in deserialization of chrono and time DateTimes. This was privately reported by @​NotAFlightRisk.

serde_with v3.23.0

Changed

  • Update syn and darling dependencies to use syn v3 (#992)
  • Update dev-dependencies to newer versions (#993)
  • Update base64 to a newer version. This should not have any API change, but some error messages might change. (#993)
  • serde_as can now parse cfg_attr(true, ...) and cfg_attr(false, ...) (#995) true/false are new literals as of Rust 1.88 but need to be parsed explicitly with the syn types. This is used when emitting schemars annotations.

serde_with v3.22.0

Added

  • Add support for jiff v0.2 behind the new jiff_0_2 feature flag (#936) jiff::SignedDuration works with DurationSeconds and its variants. jiff::Timestamp, jiff::Zoned, and jiff::civil::DateTime work with TimestampSeconds and its variants. Deserializing a jiff::Zoned uses the system time zone, like chrono::DateTime<Local>.

Fixed

  • Extend the GHSA-7gcf-g7xr-8hxj fix to the duplicate-key-prevention collections. The rust::sets_duplicate_value_is_error, rust::maps_duplicate_key_is_error, rust::sets_last_value_wins, and rust::maps_first_key_wins adapters created their backing sets/maps with with_capacity_and_hasher using the raw deserializer size_hint, bypassing the size_hint_cautious cap added in #966 (the clippy.toml disallowed_methods lint only covers Vec::with_capacity, not with_capacity_and_hasher, so these sites were not flagged). Attacker-controlled input claiming a huge length could panic with Hash table capacity overflow before a single element was read. All such constructions now route through size_hint_cautious.

Updates `jsonschema` from 0.46.5 to 0.49.4
Changelog

Sourced from jsonschema's changelog.

[0.49.4] - 2026-08-04

Added

  • Canonicalization of not a string format, which the string leaf carries as barred formats.
  • Canonicalization of not an existential demand, which an array fails exactly when no element matches.
  • Canonicalization of not a string value set, which the string leaf carries as excluded values.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedItems beside contains, where the elements it matches are evaluated and the tail admits either.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluated* beside anyOf or oneOf, where every branch evaluating the same keys or indexes pins what is left over.
  • Canonicalization of not an array element schema, which an array fails exactly when one element violates it.
  • CanonicalSchema::intersect, the values both schemas admit.
  • CanonicalSchema::negate, the values a schema rejects.
  • CanonicalSchema::definition, one reference target by URI.

Fixed

  • An integer past i64 admitted by a fractional bound f64 rounds it onto, such as -10000000000000000000000000 under {"maximum": -10000000000000000000000000.1}.
  • An integer past 2^53 admitted by a bound f64 rounds onto it, such as 9007199254740992 under {"minimum": 9007199254740993}.
  • A contains subschema beside both minContains and maxContains overwriting a sibling keyword of the same name, such as items.

Performance

  • CanonicalSchema hashing and equality cost the node instead of the whole document.

[0.49.3] - 2026-08-02

Added

  • Canonicalization of a recursive schema with no finite witness, which now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef, which resolve through the dynamic scope and stay symbolic like any other reference. A dangling $dynamicRef errors rather than staying Raw.
  • Canonicalization of minContains under uniqueItems, where a demand asking for more matches than its own schema has distinct values now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of a Draft 4 patternProperties coverage closed by additionalProperties: false, spelled as the closed map it was parsed from.
  • Canonicalization of a oneOf whose branches repeat, where a repeated branch can never contribute exactly one match.
  • Canonicalization of a $ref whose target is an empty schema, which now folds to false.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedItems beside allOf, where every branch must pass and so the indexes they evaluate are known without the instance.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedProperties beside allOf, where every branch must pass and so what they evaluate is known without the instance.
  • Canonicalization of a Draft 4 type list holding integer beside other types with enum, which previously modeled only when spelled as an allOf.
  • Canonicalization of patternProperties patterns matching finitely many keys, such as ^a$ and ^(a|b)$.
  • Canonicalization of unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems when no in-place applicator sits beside them.

Fixed

  • additionalItems values that are not schemas silently ignored beside an array-form items (they should fail the build like additionalProperties).
  • additionalItems beside a boolean items rejecting every instance, such as {"additionalItems": false, "items": false}.
  • additionalItems beside a non-array items value failing schema compilation with an error blaming additionalItems (the keyword should be ignored).
  • Draft 4 rejecting a size bound at or past 2^64, such as {"maxItems": 18446744073709551616}.
  • An integer past the f64 range admitted by a fractional bound it exceeds, such as 1e400 under {"exclusiveMaximum": 0.1}.
  • A $ref at the root of an $id-bearing subresource dropped as a self-reference when its pointer matched the one that reached that subresource.
  • Canonicalization reusing one definition's body for a same-named definition in another resource, when the name spells a canonical URI.
  • unevaluatedItems counting prefixItems as evaluating elements before Draft 2020-12, where it is not a keyword.

Updates `regress` from 0.11.1 to 0.12.0
Release notes

Sourced from regress's releases.

v0.12.0

Highlights

  • Restored support for no_std + alloc builds. Use: --no-default-features --features alloc.
  • Added Unicode Script=Unknown property support.
  • Improved correctness for ECMAScript Unicode Sets (v mode), inline modifier groups, and several Unicode case-insensitive matching cases.
  • Hardened parsing against excessively nested expressions, avoiding stack-overflow failures.
  • Reduced downstream binary size by avoiding forced inlining of regex construction and search internals.

Fixes

  • Correctly propagate flags from inline modifier groups.
  • Correct handling of nested and negated character sets in v mode.
  • Correct parsing of invalid \x escapes as identity escapes where ECMAScript permits it.
  • Correctly detect start-anchored alternations.
  • Include the v flag in Flags formatting.
  • Make Regex::find_from clearly panic when given an index that splits a UTF-8 code point.
  • Fix big-endian matching.
  • Avoid overly aggressive loop unrolling.

Performance and implementation

  • Improve PikeVM handling of one-character loops and reduce state allocation overhead.
  • Improve Unicode string-set lowering and longest-match ordering.
  • Improve case-folding/literal lowering internals.
  • Add a safety limit for deeply nested patterns.
  • Allow downstream users to share regex internals rather than duplicating them through inlining.

  • Add Cursor::prev_span

3.0.1

  • Parse const traits (#2056, #2057, #2058, #2063, #2064)
  • Parse unsafe binder types (#2065)
  • Parse impl restrictions (#2066)

3.0.0

This release contains adjustments to the syntax tree to account for ongoing Rust language development from the 3 years since syn 2.0.0 and to anticipate some in-flight Rust language RFCs.

These include: default values in fields, pinned type sugar, raw lifetimes, generator blocks and functions, unnamed enum variants, attributes in tuple types and tuple patterns, named arguments in parenthesized generic argument lists, lightweight clones, const traits, const function pointers, mutability restricted fields, supertrait auto implementation, final associated functions, trait implementability restrictions, const blocks in path arguments, item-level const blocks, return type notation, never patterns, function delegation, mutable by-reference bindings, in-place initialization, field projections, explicitly dyn-compatible traits, view types, file-level frontmatter, generic const arguments, guard patterns, lazy type aliases, explicitly safe foreign items, super let, unsafe fields, pattern types, heterogeneous try-blocks, function contracts, async function trait bounds, static closure coroutine syntax, unsafe binder types, move expressions, for-await loops, and postfix keywords.

Breaking changes

Modifiers

To reserve more room for language evolution, there are 10 new non-exhaustive structs in the syntax tree having the following commonality:

  • Name ending in Modifiers. {BlockModifiers, ClosureModifiers, ConstModifiers, FieldModifiers, FnModifiers, ImplModifiers, LocalModifiers, TraitBoundModifiers, TraitModifiers, TypeModifiers}

  • Each implements Default. The default value is guaranteed to comprise no tokens.

  • Non-exhaustive. Can only be instantiated by Syn's parser or by creating and then mutating ▁▁Modifiers::default().

  • Does not implement Parse. When parsing, they are parsed by the enclosing syntax tree node.

  • Does not implement ToTokens. In some cases the syntax that these nodes might hold in the future is not necessarily contiguous tokens.

  • Provides .require_empty() -> Result<()> which returns a meaningfully spanned error if the modifiers are different from the empty default. This enables a caller to reject syntax it does not recognize without knowing what that syntax may be.

title: ci: group only minor and patch dependency updates, and hold back the codegen migrations (#1188)
body:
ci: group only minor and patch dependency updates, and hold back the codegen migrations (#1188)

The first weekly grouped PRs (#1184, #1185, #1186) all failed. In each
case one or two breaking updates turned the whole group red:

- cargo: schemars 0.8 -> 1.x (with typify 0.6 -> 0.8, which needs it)
  breaks trust-tasks-build and trust-tasks-codegen
  (`cannot find type RootSchema in schemars::schema`), and every job
  that builds them failed. With those two held back, the other 31
  updates compile, pass `cargo test --workspace`, and leave codegen
  output and the registry bundles unchanged.
- npm: json-schema-to-typescript 16 makes both TypeScript generators
  emit counter-suffixed duplicate names. TypeScript 7 stops loading
  @types/node by default, so three sibling packages lose
  TextEncoder/crypto. @openvtc/vti-tsp-js 0.2 -> 0.4 (a "minor" update
  on 0.x) removes `senderEncryptionKey`. prettier 3.8.3 -> 3.9.10
  reflows the generated unions, so the drift and equivalence checks
  need regenerated output.
- pub: lints 6 adds use_null_aware_elements, which
  `dart analyze --fatal-infos` reports in trust-tasks-dart-tsp's
  test fixtures.

Changes:

- Every group now takes only minor and patch updates. A major update
  comes as its own PR with the fix-up it needs, so it no longer blocks
  the rest.
- Ignore the updates that need a deliberate migration: schemars majors,
  typify minors and majors (0.x), json-schema-to-typescript majors, and
  @openvtc/vti-tsp-js minors and majors (0.x).
- Move json-schema-to-typescript and prettier into their own
  `ts-generator` npm group. A patch to either can change the generated
  TypeScript, so that PR needs `npm run build-ts-bindings` committed
  and the `npm` group stays green without it.

title: fix(vta)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#123 (merged):
- **VTI-KEY-003:** every node resolves did:webs.
- **VTI-KEY-001:** a node never requires a peer to use a particular durable method.
- **VTI-KEY-008:** the `resolvedMethods` gate is withdrawn.

A did:webs node now acts toward any peer exactly as a did:webvh node does. Each party chooses its own DID method.

**Removed**
- The send-side gate: `require_declared` and its callers (VTA `Outbound::send`, VTC `PeerTasks::select` and the trust-registry selection, room-host). `Outbound::from_parts` loses `node_did`.
- `MethodNotDeclared`: the `VtaError` and `AppError` variants, the SDK struct and the reject reason, with all their mappings.
- The declaration: `declare`, `OPTIONAL_METHODS_DECLARED`, the `resolvedMethods` member and `@context` term in VTA documents and in the vtc-host, room-host, dtg-witness and ballot-box templates. The `RESOLVED_METHODS` var leaves the `did-host-*` templates, which are now byte-identical to before #2672.

**Kept**
- `resolvedMethods` in an uploaded did:webs template is ignored, not refused, so old templates still work.
- The VTI-KEY-009 `unsupportedDidMethod` receive refusal. It can't fire for did:webs, because `REQUIRED_METHODS` is now webvh, scid, webs and key, and a test holds that.

**Resolvers:** the enclave proxy resolves the mediator DID, so it moves to cache-sdk 0.8.51 with `did-webs`. Its CI job is the first Linux build of that change.

**Tests:** a did:webs VTA's `Outbound::send`, and a did:webs VTC's `PeerTasks::select`, each succeed toward a peer that declares nothing (`vti_key_003_*`).

**Breaking:** public error variants and functions are removed, and a caller still passing `RESOLVED_METHODS` to a `did-host-*` template is refused as an unknown var.

Local: nextest workspace 7462 passed, vtc 3718 passed, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, the no-webs vta-service check and the vta-enclave `webs` check all pass.

**Also:** `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.1 → 0.13.3 and cache-sdk 0.8.51 → 0.8.52, in the workspace and the enclave proxy. 0.13.3 resolves a deactivated did:webs without keys (0.13.1 returned its last keys) and bounds per-stream verification work.

body:
fix(vta)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008) (#2697)

* fix(vta,vtc)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)

Each party chooses its own identity method and still works with every
other: a did:webs client talks to a did:webvh service, and a did:webs
node reaches any peer. dtgwg-vti-spec#123 makes did:webs a required
method every node resolves, with the key-role designation extension
(VTI-KEY-003); a node never requires a peer to use a particular durable
method (VTI-KEY-001); VTI-KEY-008, the resolvedMethods declaration gate,
is withdrawn with its methodNotDeclared refusal; VTI-KEY-009 keeps only
the receiving side.

Removed:
- the send-side gate: vta_sdk::resolved_methods::require_declared and
  every caller — the VTA's Outbound::send (may_act_toward, and the node
  DID Outbound carried for it: Outbound::from_parts loses its node_did
  argument), the VTC's PeerTasks::select and trust-registry selection
  (PeerError::MethodNotDeclared, LinkError::MethodNotDeclared), and
  room-host's watch signals;
- the refusal: VtaError::MethodNotDeclared, AppError::MethodNotDeclared,
  resolved_methods::MethodNotDeclared, trust_task_reject_reasons::
  METHOD_NOT_DECLARED and their reject/REST mappings;
- the declaration: resolved_methods::{declare, declared,
  OPTIONAL_METHODS_DECLARED, OPTIONAL_DURABLE_METHODS,
  RESOLVED_METHODS_MEMBER, RESOLVED_METHODS_IRI}; the resolvedMethods
  member and its @context term in every document the VTA mints and in
  the vtc-host, room-host, dtg-witness and ballot-box templates; the
  RESOLVED_METHODS variable of the did-host-* templates. The templates
  are back to their shape before the gate.

Kept:
- resolvedMethods in a did:webs template's ignored members
  (DOCUMENT_MEMBERS), so an operator-uploaded template written while the
  gate stood keeps working (tested);
- the VTI-KEY-009 receiving refusal unsupportedDidMethod
  (VtaError/AppError::UnsupportedDidMethod, DiProofError::
  UnsupportedDidMethod). It never fires for did:webs: REQUIRED_METHODS is
  now webvh, scid, webs and key, all in RESOLVED_HERE;
- is_durable_identity, which admits did:webs as a node's durable
  identity (didcomm_light).

Resolution: every resolver the root workspace builds already has
affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk's did-webs feature (the workspace dep).
The enclave proxy, its own workspace, resolves the mediator DID with a
0.8.43 pin and no did-webs; it moves to 0.8.51 with did-webs, the root
lock's versions.

Tests: a did:webs VTA's Outbound::send reaches a peer whose document has
no resolvedMethods (end to end over REST); a did:webs VTC's
PeerTasks::select does too; no built-in template or minted document
carries resolvedMethods. The VTI-KEY-008 tests are gone with the rule.

Docs: did-webs.md, the design note (decision 4 and S5 withdrawn), the
setup and TEE guides, vta-service/CLAUDE.md, and the setup/config
rustdoc no longer tell an operator to declare resolvedMethods or that a
did:webs node reaches only declaring peers.

Breaking: public variants, functions, constants and a constructor
argument are removed (vta-sdk, vti-common, vta-service); a did-host-*
caller passing RESOLVED_METHODS is now refused as an unknown variable.

Refs: VTI-KEY-001, VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008, VTI-KEY-009

title: ci: check the contents of the release manifests a token job commits, and the tarball's install scripts
body:
A follow-up to #1181. It narrows what the release jobs that hold a token accept from the read-only jobs before them.

## Manifest contents (`release-pr.sh open`)

`check-patch-paths.sh` already limits which files a Release PR patch may touch. `open` now also checks what changed inside the manifests. The check runs after `git apply --index` and before the commit, using only git, jq and grep. Any other change is refused, and nothing is committed or pushed.

| File | May change |
|---|---|
| `*/package.json` | `version`, and values in `dependencies` / `devDependencies` / `peerDependencies` / `optionalDependencies` that are version ranges before and after. The comparison uses `jq -S` against HEAD. A new `scripts` entry, a new key, or a dependency moved to a path, URL or git source is refused. |
| `*/version.go` | Only the one `const Version = "…"` line, to another version. |
| `trust-tasks-dart/lib/src/runtime/version.dart` | Only the one `packageVersion` line, to another version. This file was not in the review list; I added it because it is the pubspec's mirror and the release edits it. |
| `*/pubspec.yaml` | Only `version:` at the top level and dependency constraints. Each changed line must stay in place, under the same key, from one version constraint to another. Adding or removing lines is refused, which covers turning a dependency into a `git:`/`path:` map. |

## Patch paths (`check-patch-paths.sh`)

- A path containing a control character is refused, even when it matches the allowlist.
- A new file with mode 100755, or a mode change to 100755, is refused. There is an `allow_exec` list per producer, and both are empty.
- If `git apply --summary` or `git apply --numstat -z` fails, the patch is refused as unreadable. Before, an unreadable patch only failed through the "no files" fallback.

## npm tarball (`publish-npm`)

The check moves into `scripts/check-npm-tarball.sh`, run from the publishing job's own checkout. It now also refuses a manifest with a `preinstall`, `install` or `postinstall` script. No package here has one.

## Behaviour changes

Release PRs and npm publishes that only bump versions are unaffected. The real `prepare` → `open` run below passed every new check.

## Checks

- `npm run test:release-scripts`: 26 of 26 pass, exit 0 (up from 8).
  - **Content:** an accepted bump across package.json, version.go, pubspec.yaml and version.dart. Refused: a package.json `postinstall`, a package.json dependency moved to a git URL, an extra line in version.go, an extra line in version.dart, a pubspec `description` change, a pubspec constraint changed to `any`, and a pubspec dependency turned into a `git:` map.
  - **Paths:** a control character in a path, a new 100755 file, a file made executable, and two unreadable patches.
  - **Tarball:** the expected package is accepted. Refused: a wrong name, a wrong version, a `publishConfig`, and each of the three install scripts.
  - With the new checks disabled, 10 of the 26 fail.
- `release-pr.sh prepare` then `open`, run on a local clone of main with a stub `gh` and a local bare remote. The 40-file, 18-package patch passed the path and content checks and was committed and pushed.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12: clean.
- `shellcheck`: `check-patch-paths.sh`, `check-npm-tarball.sh` and `git-push-with-token.sh` are clean. `release-pr.sh` reports SC2016 infos only: the three already on main, plus two on the deliberately single-quoted regex strings.

## Checklist (development guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the content check runs before the commit and push; a refused run leaves the remote untouched
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types; `release-pr.sh`'s interface is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — an unreadable patch or invalid JSON is refused
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — each refusal names the file and the reason
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no new mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

body:
ci: weekly dependency updates for every ecosystem, and a scheduled advisory check (#1182)

.github/dependabot.yml, which covered github-actions only, now also
covers cargo (the workspace), npm (the root tooling, the five published
packages and the example app), gomod (the core, its four nested modules
and the example app) and pub (the six Dart packages and the example app).
Each ecosystem gets one grouped PR a week, titled `chore(deps):`.

A new `Advisories` workflow runs weekly and on dispatch. It runs
`cargo deny check advisories` through the same pinned cargo-deny-action
rust.yml uses. It also runs `npm audit` against every lockfile: published
packages fail on any advisory in their runtime dependencies, and every
directory fails on a high or critical advisory anywhere in its tree. It
reads lockfiles only and installs nothing.

deny.toml: the eight advisory ignores matched nothing in Cargo.lock
(cargo deny reported each one as `advisory-not-detected`). They are
removed, and `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` now fails the check when
an ignore outlives its reason. The header comment no longer describes a
`notice` downgrade the file does not make.

title: ci: read-only workflow tokens by default, and keep release tokens out of jobs that run package code
body:
Narrows what each workflow job can do with its token, and keeps the release token and OIDC tokens out of the jobs that run third-party package code.

## Read-only by default

Every workflow now declares `permissions: contents: read` at the top (`codegen`, `dart`, `deploy`, `go`, `publish-dart`, `rust` and `ts` had no block and inherited the repository default). A job that needs more asks for it:

| Workflow | Job | Permissions |
|---|---|---|
| `go.yml`, `rust.yml` | `api-compat` | + `pull-requests: read` (reads the PR title through the API) |
| `deploy.yml` | `deploy` | + `id-token: write` |
| `publish.yml` | `publish-npm` | `contents: write`, `id-token: write` (unchanged) |
| `publish.yml` | `publish-go`, `tag-dart` | `contents: write` (unchanged) |
| `publish.yml` | `release-pr-open` | `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` |
| `withdraw.yml` | `open-pr` | `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` (was workflow-wide) |

Every `actions/checkout` now sets `persist-credentials: false`. The jobs that push no longer pass a token to checkout; `scripts/git-push-with-token.sh` gives `$PUSH_TOKEN` to the one `git push` that needs it, through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables (not `.git/config` or argv).

## Release jobs split into an unprivileged job and a privileged job

| Before | Now: runs package code, read-only | Now: publishes or pushes, runs no package code |
|---|---|---|
| `publish-npm` (`npm ci && npm run build` beside `id-token: write`) | `build-npm`: `npm ci`, build, `npm pack`, upload the tarball | `publish-npm`: `npm publish <tarball>` (OIDC, provenance), tag |
| `publish-go` (`go test` beside `contents: write`) | `verify-go`: build, vet, test | `publish-go`: tag, warm the proxy |
| `tag-dart` (`dart pub get` / `dart test` beside the PAT) | `verify-dart`: pub get, analyze, test, dry run | `tag-dart`: push the tag with the PAT |
| `release-pr` (release-plz and git-cliff beside the PAT) | `release-pr`: `release-pr.sh prepare` → patch artifact | `release-pr-open`: `release-pr.sh open` → apply, commit, push, PR |
| `withdraw.yml` `batch` (`npm ci`, cargo, generators beside the PAT) | `batch`: flip and regenerate → patch artifact | `open-pr`: apply, commit, push, PR |

Each pair shares one matrix through a YAML anchor (`&npm-packages` / `*npm-packages`, and likewise for Go and Dart), so the legs line up by construction and `check-dart-packages` still reads the `tag-dart` matrix. The decide step is shared the same way, and the privileged job re-reads the decision from its own checkout. A leg of the privileged job runs only if its own leg of the first job passed: it downloads that leg's artifact, which is uploaded only on success.

`scripts/release-pr.sh` gains `prepare DIR` and `open DIR` subcommands. With no arguments it runs both, as before. `open` checks that the patch was computed against the commit it is applying to.

### What a token job accepts from the job before it

- **Patches** (`release-pr-open`, and `open-pr` in `withdraw.yml`). Before applying, each job checks the patch from its own checkout with `scripts/check-patch-paths.sh` (`git apply --numstat -z` and `--summary`).
  - Allowed for `release`: the files a real `prepare` run changed, which were 40 files from main at 774ccaea6. That means the root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, `<pkg>/Cargo.toml`, `<pkg>[/<module>]/CHANGELOG.md`, `<pkg>/package.json`/`package-lock.json`, `<pkg>/pubspec.yaml`, `trust-tasks-go/<module>/version.go` and `trust-tasks-dart/lib/src/runtime/version.dart`.
  - Allowed for `withdraw`: `specs/` plus the four generators' output trees (the same trees the drift checks compare).
  - Always refused: `.github/`, `scripts/`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`, mode 120000/160000, renames and copies.
  - After `git apply`, nothing from the working tree runs. The push is a function in `release-pr.sh` and inline in `withdraw.yml`, with tracing off.
- **npm tarball.** `publish-npm` extracts `package/package.json` from the tarball. It requires `name` to equal the matrix package and `version` to equal the version the job decided from its own checkout, and it refuses any `publishConfig`.
- **Verify markers.** `publish-go` and `tag-dart` require the marker's recorded commit to equal `$GITHUB_SHA`. I kept the artifact names stable rather than adding `run_attempt`: re-running only a failed publish leg must still find the marker from the earlier verify attempt.
- `git-push-with-token.sh`, now used only on unpatched checkouts, turns tracing off before it reads the token.

`release-plz-release` is unchanged apart from a comment. The libdbus step's comment no longer says that job compiles what it publishes; the step stays for now. It runs the release-plz action beside the crates.io token and `contents: write`, but it compiles nothing (`publish_no_verify = true`), so no dependency build script runs there. Its checkout already persisted no credentials.

## Deploy: GitHub OIDC for AWS

`deploy.yml` uses `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` (same pin, v6.3.0) with `role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}` when that repository variable is set. Until it is set, the existing `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` secrets are used as before, so merging this changes nothing until the role exists. The deploy job now runs in a `website` environment, so the role's trust policy can name it. GitHub creates that environment on the first run. Both jobs have timeouts: build 30 minutes, deploy 15 (recent runs take about 3).

To finish, in this order (also in RELEASING.md, "Setup this depends on"):
1. **In GitHub first:** create the `website` environment (Settings → Environments) and restrict its deployment branches to `main`. The role trusts the environment, not the branch, so this rule is what limits it to `main`, and it must be in place before the role exists.
2. Confirm the repository uses the default OIDC subject template. I checked this today: `gh api repos/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/actions/oidc/customization/sub` returns `{"use_default":true,...}`.
3. In AWS, add the IAM OIDC provider `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` (audience `sts.amazonaws.com`) if the account has none.
4. Create the role.
   - **Trust policy:** allow `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` from that provider with `StringEquals` on `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud` = `sts.amazonaws.com` and `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` = `repo:trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf:environment:website`.
   - **Permissions:**
     - `s3:ListBucket` on `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>`, with `StringLike` `s3:prefix` = `website/*`
     - `s3:PutObject` and `s3:DeleteObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/website/*`
     - an explicit **Deny** of `s3:DeleteObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/website/specs/by-digest/*`, because the by-digest store is append-only
     - `cloudfront:CreateInvalidation` on the distribution
   - No `s3:GetObject` is needed: `aws s3 sync` compares by listing.
5. Set the repository variable `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` to the role's ARN and let a deploy run.
6. Once a deploy succeeds through the role, delete the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` secrets and the IAM user's key, and remove the access-key step from `deploy.yml`.

## Behaviour changes

- A release now runs as two jobs per registry, so the Actions UI shows `Build … for npm`, `Verify … before tagging`, and `Open or update the Release PR` alongside the existing job names. The idempotency of a re-run is unchanged. A re-run now means "Re-run failed jobs", which reruns the failed verify leg and the publish leg that depends on it.
- Dart: all packages are verified before any is tagged. Before, the dependents were verified one at a time after the core's tag. In both cases a dependent that needs core API released in the same merge fails verification, and the remedy is still to re-run once the core is on pub.dev. Now the core is still tagged when a dependent fails.
- The `withdraw.yml` job is now `prepare the withdrawal batch` followed by `open the withdrawal pull request`.
- RELEASING.md now says the release token must be a user PAT, since the scripts already refuse an App token, and recommends a fine-grained one limited to this repository. A fine-grained PAT on a `trustoverip` repository works only if the organization allows fine-grained PATs and an owner approves this one.
- A Release PR or withdrawal batch that touches a file outside its allowlist is now refused. The `open` job fails and names the file, and nothing is pushed. Adding a new kind of file to a release means adding it to `check-patch-paths.sh`.
- New workflow `Release scripts`, which runs `npm run test:release-scripts` on every PR and push to main.
- Nothing in any published package changes.

## Checks

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 on every workflow: clean.
- `shellcheck` on `git-push-with-token.sh` and `check-patch-paths.sh`: clean.
- `npm run test:release-scripts`: 8 of 8 pass, exit 0.
  - `open` is refused, with nothing applied, pushed or sent to `gh`, for a patch that touches `scripts/other.sh`, `scripts/release-pr.sh`, a new `.github/workflows/*.yml`, a `.gitattributes`, a symlink, or a file off the release list.
  - An ordinary release patch is applied, committed with sign-off and pushed.
  - The `withdraw` allowlist takes spec and generated paths and refuses others.
  - With the check commented out, 6 of the 8 fail. On `release-pr.sh`: only the three SC2016 infos already on `main`.
- `node scripts/check-dart-packages.mjs`: lists agree (it reads the `tag-dart` matrix through the alias).
- `release-pr.sh prepare` then `open`, re-run after these changes on a local clone of `main` (774ccaea6), with a stub `gh`, a local bare remote and `PUSH_TOKEN` set.
  - `prepare` exited 0, produced the 18-package, 40-file patch, and left the tree clean.
  - `open` exited 0: all 40 files were on the release allowlist, and it applied the patch, committed as the token owner with sign-off, and pushed.
- The publish, deploy and withdraw jobs cannot be exercised from a PR. Their first real run is the next merge (deploy, and the publish no-op legs), the next Release PR merge, and the next quarterly withdrawal.

## Checklist (development guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no client code; deploy jobs gained timeouts
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — each privileged job re-checks registry/tag state before acting, as before
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — existing bounded loops unchanged
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types. The `release-pr.sh` interface is extended (no-argument behaviour kept), and its only caller is `publish.yml` (R3.6)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no `permissions` means read-only. Without the role variable, deploy keeps today's access-key path, which is a deliberate transition and is listed above.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — a publish leg fails visibly when its verify leg did not pass
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — the publish, tag and push steps are the same idempotent steps as before. A failed `open` leaves the branch as it was, and a re-run recomputes it.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

body:
ci: read-only workflow tokens by default, and keep release tokens out of jobs that run package code (#1181)

* ci: read-only workflow tokens by default, and keep release tokens out of jobs that run package code

Every workflow now declares `permissions: contents: read` at the top, and
a job that needs more asks for it by name: the API compatibility jobs in
go.yml and rust.yml read the PR title (`pull-requests: read`), and the
deploy job requests `id-token: write`. No checkout persists credentials.

The publish and tag jobs in publish.yml are each split in two. The first
(`build-npm`, `verify-go`, `verify-dart`) installs, builds and tests with
read-only permissions and no OIDC token; the second (`publish-npm`,

and runs no package code. The two share one matrix through a YAML anchor,
and a leg of the second runs only if its own leg of the first passed.

The Release PR job is split the same way: `release-pr` runs
`release-pr.sh prepare` (release-plz, git-cliff, the bump scripts) and
uploads the change as a patch; `release-pr-open` runs `release-pr.sh open`,
which applies it, commits and pushes with RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN. withdraw.yml
follows the same shape. scripts/git-push-with-token.sh hands the token to
the single `git push` that needs it through the environment.

deploy.yml takes AWS credentials from GitHub OIDC (`role-to-assume`) when
the AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN repository variable is set, and from the existing
access-key secrets until then. The deploy job runs in a `website`
environment, and both deploy jobs have timeouts.

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records
body:
`InMemoryReplayGuard` — the batteries-included SPEC §7.2 item 11 record in all four runtimes, and the default in the Rust HTTPS/DIDComm/TSP consumers — made room for a new `id` by dropping the least-recently-used record, whether or not that record was still inside its retention window. A document whose record was dropped that way was accepted again inside its window, silently. The default capacity (10 000) was sized for the five-minute window, while a document with `expiresAt` must be remembered for up to 30 days. Separately, TypeScript, Go and Dart retained a record until the producer's `expiresAt` with no upper bound, so a distant `expiresAt` kept a record indefinitely.

## What changes

**Full guard: refuse, don't forget (all four runtimes)**
- When every slot holds a record still inside its window, a claim for a new `id` fails — Rust `ReplayGuardError`, TS `ReplayGuardFullError`, Go `ErrReplayGuardFull`, Dart `ReplayGuardFullException` — which `consume_inbound` / `consumeInbound` / `ConsumeInbound` already answer `unavailable` (retryable, no detail on the wire). Expired records are reclaimed first; a live record is never dropped to make room. Duplicates and conflicts are still answered while full.
- Rust indexes records by retention deadline, so reclaiming is `O(expired · log n)`; TS/Go/Dart track the earliest deadline and only scan when something can have expired.
- Default capacity is now **100 000** live records (≈ five-minute window at ~330 distinct documents/s), exported as `DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY` (Rust, TS) / `DefaultReplayCapacity` (Go) / `defaultReplayCapacity` (Dart), and documented as a ceiling per retention window, with the sizing guidance for consumers that admit long-lived documents (raise it, lower the horizon, or use a shared store).

**One party's share (all four runtimes)**
- No issuer may hold more than a share of the guard: a tenth of the capacity by default, rounded up; configurable (Rust `InMemoryReplayGuard::with_per_issuer_limit`, TS/Dart second constructor argument, Go `WithPerIssuerLimit`). An issuer at its share is refused `unavailable` (retryable) for its *own* new documents only; every other party is unaffected. Without this, one signer sending documents with `expiresAt` = `issuedAt` + 30 days could hold every slot for a month.
- The pipeline passes the issuer it resolved (SPEC §4.8.1) through a new issuer-aware claim, added without breaking existing guards: Rust `ReplayGuard::claim_for` (default method → `claim`), TS optional `ReplayGuard.claimFor`, Go `IssuerScopedReplayGuard` (optional interface, type-asserted), Dart `IssuerScopedReplayGuard` (separate interface, `is`-checked). Documents with no resolved issuer, and direct `claim` calls, share one allowance.
- Limitation, documented on each guard: the share is per identifier. Where anyone can mint identifiers (an unauthenticated transport with `did:key`), one party using many is bounded only by the overall capacity.

**Expiry horizon in TypeScript, Go and Dart (port of Rust's `expiry_horizon`)**
- `FreshnessPolicy` gains `expiryHorizonMs` / `ExpiryHorizon` / `expiryHorizon` (optional; the consequential policy sets 30 days, `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_HORIZON_MS` / `DefaultExpiryHorizon` / `defaultExpiryHorizon`).
- `recordExpiry` clamps a retained record's expiry to `issuedAt + horizon + skew`, as Rust's `record_expiry` does.
- `validateFreshness` follows Rust: a stated `expiresAt` bounds the window in place of the maximum age, up to the horizon; past `issuedAt + horizon + skew` the document is `expired`, so it is never accepted after its record could be dropped.
- Zero horizon means the same in all four: no horizon only when absent (`None` / `undefined` / `nil` / `null`); a zero horizon clamps at `issuedAt`. Go's `ExpiryHorizon` is therefore a `*time.Duration` (unlike `MaxAge`, where zero is "unbounded").

**Documentation**
- Each guard documents its worst-case memory (≈ capacity × (largest `id` + largest cached response)) and that a document with `expiresAt` but no `issuedAt` is not bounded by the horizon under a policy that does not require `issuedAt` (the consequential policy does). I did not cap the stored response size: dropping it would turn a duplicate's answer into silence, so I left that to a decision about the transport's own body limit.
- `GETTING-STARTED.md`: a consumer may keep its record for less than a stated `expiresAt`, provided it stops accepting the document at the same point (SPEC §7.2, *Bounding the record*); the in-memory guard's full and per-issuer behaviour. (`SPEC.md` is generated from the canonical repo, so it is not edited here.)

Refs #1120 — this ports the "`expiresAt` replaces maxAge" rule and the horizon with its record clamp. The issue's shared cross-runtime freshness vector file (including calendar-invalid timestamps) is not in this PR.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
**Breaking (`!`):** a consumer now refuses documents it used to accept (a full guard, an issuer at its share), and the Go/TS/Dart freshness verdicts change. The `go API compatibility` job also needs the `!` for the new exported names.
- An issuer holding a tenth of the guard is refused for its own new documents until its records expire.
- A full in-memory guard now answers new documents `unavailable` instead of accepting them after dropping an older record. With the larger default this needs ~10× the previous concurrent load; deployments with sustained high rates or long-lived documents should size explicitly or use a shared guard.
- Default capacity 10 000 → 100 000: the memory bound rises accordingly (≈ 100 000 × typical cached response size).
- TS/Go/Dart, consequential policy: a document with `issuedAt` older than five minutes but an `expiresAt` still ahead is now **accepted** (as Rust already does); a document stated to expire more than 30 days after `issuedAt` is treated as expiring at the horizon.
- Additive API: the new error types, constants and the optional horizon field/parameter. Nothing removed.

## Tests
- Rust `replay.rs`: full guard refuses (mapped to `unavailable`) and keeps both records; expired records are reclaimed first; one issuer at its share is refused while another issuer and the no-issuer allowance are not, the share frees on expiry, and the limit is configurable. The LRU test is replaced.
- TS `replay.test.ts`, Go `replay_test.go`, Dart `replay_test.dart`: the same two guard cases, a pipeline case (second `id` → retryable `unavailable`, first `id` still a duplicate, one execution), `expiresAt` replacing the maximum age, the horizon clamp for acceptance and for the record, the per-issuer share (same cases as Rust), and (Go, Dart) a zero horizon clamping at `issuedAt`.

Run locally (exit codes):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features acl --all-targets` 0; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-https -p trust-tasks-didcomm -p trust-tasks-tsp -p trust-tasks-didcomm-v1 -p trust-tasks-capability-client --all-targets` 0; `cargo clippy … -D warnings` (trust-tasks-rs acl; the binding crates and capability-client) 0
- `trust-tasks-ts`: `npm test` 0 (131/131), `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 0, `npm run smoke` 0
- `trust-tasks-go`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go test -race ./...` 0
- `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` 0, `dart format` clean, `dart test` 0; `trust-tasks-dart-{didcomm,https,tsp}`: `dart test` 0

Full-workspace `cargo test`/`clippy` were left to CI (memory).

## Not in this PR
- Capping `id` length / storing a digest of oversized ids, capping the cached response size, and keeping records of refused documents from competing with executed ones for capacity.
- An eviction/full counter or callback for metrics.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack development guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the guards hold their mutex only for in-memory work
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — a refused claim writes nothing; the producer's retry is absorbed or executed once capacity frees
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — `unavailable` is retryable by the producer; nothing retries here
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a full guard is a per-document refusal, not a loop failure
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire type changed; all four runtimes changed together
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — a full record fails closed; the consequential policy carries the horizon by default
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the guard error carries the record count for logs; the wire message stays generic
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — in-memory record only; restart loses it as before (documented)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — R3.6 behaviour changes above

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records (#1163)
body:
fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records (#1163)

* fix(runtime): the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records

InMemoryReplayGuard (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) made room for a new id by
dropping the least-recently-used record, whether or not that record was
still inside its retention window. A document whose record was dropped that
way was then accepted again inside its window, with nothing logged.

- When every slot holds a live record, a claim for a new id now fails
  (Rust ReplayGuardError, TS ReplayGuardFullError, Go ErrReplayGuardFull,
  Dart ReplayGuardFullException), which the pipeline answers `unavailable`
  (retryable). Records whose window has closed are reclaimed first; a
  record is never dropped to make room. Duplicates and conflicts are still
  recognised while full.
- The default capacity is 100 000 live records (was 10 000), documented as
  a ceiling on distinct documents per retention window, and exported as
  DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY / DefaultReplayCapacity / defaultReplayCapacity.
- TypeScript, Go and Dart gain the expiry horizon Rust already had
  (`expiryHorizonMs` / `ExpiryHorizon` / `expiryHorizon`, 30 days in the
  consequential policy): a stated expiresAt bounds the acceptance window in
  place of the maximum age, up to issuedAt + horizon, and the retained
  record's expiry is clamped to the same instant, so a producer can no
  longer pin a record indefinitely with a distant expiresAt.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(runtime): give each issuer a share of the in-memory replay guard

One signer could fill the in-memory guard with documents whose records
live to the expiry horizon (issuedAt now, expiresAt 30 days on) at a few
documents an hour per slot, after which every party was refused.

- No issuer may hold more than a share of the guard's capacity: a tenth by
  default, rounded up, configurable (Rust `with_per_issuer_limit`, TS and
  Dart second constructor argument, Go `WithPerIssuerLimit`). An issuer at
  its share is refused `unavailable` for its own new documents only.
- The pipeline passes the issuer it resolved (SPEC §4.8.1) through a new
  issuer-aware claim: Rust `ReplayGuard::claim_for` (default method calling
  `claim`), TS optional `claimFor`, Go `IssuerScopedReplayGuard`, Dart
  `IssuerScopedReplayGuard`. Existing guards are unaffected; documents with
  no resolved issuer, and direct `claim` calls, share one allowance.
- Zero expiry horizon means the same everywhere: none only when absent
  (None / undefined / nil / null); zero clamps at issuedAt. Go's
  `ExpiryHorizon` is now a `*time.Duration` to say so.
- Documented: the share is per identifier; a document with expiresAt and no
  issuedAt is not bounded by the horizon; the guard's worst-case memory; and
  in GETTING-STARTED that a consumer may retain below a stated expiresAt
  (SPEC §7.2, Bounding the record).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: place the record-retention note where it does not overlap the item 3 note

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(runtime): end the clamped expiry window where its record does

With the acceptance window over `issuedAt` now half-open (refused once
`issuedAt + maxAge + skew <= now`), the expiry-horizon clamp in the
TypeScript, Go and Dart runtimes follows suit: a document whose
`expiresAt` lies beyond the horizon is refused from
`issuedAt + expiryHorizon + skew`, the instant `recordExpiry` returns
and a guard may drop the record, rather than one instant later. Rust's
clamp already did.

The horizon tests now accept one millisecond before that instant and
expect `expired` at it, and the shared `fixtures/consume` vectors gain
the clamped-horizon boundary, run by all four runtimes. The
`recordExpiry` docs say "refuses from", as Rust's do, and a redundant
rustdoc link target is dropped.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(keys)!: every node resolves did:webs; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)
body:
Each party chooses its own identifier method, and the stack works whichever it chooses. For example, a did:webs client talks to a did:webvh service, and the reverse.

#121 admitted did:webs as an *optional* method that no peer had to resolve. A did:webs node could then act only toward peers that declared `resolvedMethods` (VTI-KEY-008). That made a party's choice of method limit who it could talk to. This PR reverses the choice:

- **VTI-KEY-003:** did:webs is a required method; every node resolves it, with the key-role designation extension (VTI-KEY-173).
- **VTI-KEY-001:** which durable method a node uses is its operator's choice, and a node must not require a peer to use any one of them.
- **VTI-KEY-008:** withdrawn. There is nothing to declare.
- **VTI-KEY-009:** keeps the receiver's `unsupportedDidMethod` refusal (now for genuinely unsupported methods) and the no-downgrade rule. `methodNotDeclared` is gone.
- **Follow-on edits:** the alpha note, the rationale (rewritten), the level 2/3 open issue under VTI-KEY-173, the DID-class table, the [DID-WEBS] reference and the Appendix F row. The Appendix F row records what implementations still lack: the push gateway and the browser client library don't resolve did:webs yet, and the gate is still in the VTI code.

did:webs stays at alpha maturity.

This touches the same chapter as #122 (the VTI-KEY-184/199/129 narrowing) but different requirements, so either can merge first.

title: fix(keys): narrow VTI-KEY-184 to dependent keys; a next-key threshold stands in for a witness in VTI-KEY-199
body:
Two changes, both prompted by trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#993 (key assurance levels, and the `webs` method profile).

**VTI-KEY-184: narrowed, with the rest as best practice.**
- *Was:* at level 2 and 3, a node MUST NOT publish any X25519 key computed from an Ed25519 key.
- *Now:* it MUST NOT publish a key computed from a key it publishes, or from a key of another role. An X25519 key computed from a *published* Ed25519 key is one such key.
- *New SHOULD:* derive each key agreement key independently of every signing key.
- *Not prohibited:* an X25519 key that is the image of an Ed25519 key derived for it alone, and published and used nowhere else. This is what a key hierarchy that derives on one curve produces; VTI's derives on Ed25519 only.
- The rationale gains a sentence on why: VTI-KEY-071 targets a dependence between published keys or between roles, and this form creates neither.

**VTI-KEY-199 item 3: the VTI-KEY-129 stand-in.**
- *Was:* item 3 capped every unwitnessed level-3 version at level 2, although VTI-KEY-129 lets a next-key threshold stand in for the witness. That stand-in is what a level-3 did:webs (KERI) identity relies on: `nt` over `[R′, K]`, which cannot be met without the recovery key K.
- *Now:* item 3 accepts the stand-in when two things hold: the threshold makes the recovery custodian's signature necessary for every change of the change authority, and the history is published at the one location the identifier names.
- VTI-KEY-129 adds that such an identity SHOULD still be witnessed. A witness also detects a duplicitous history (two histories published for one identifier), which no threshold can.

title: fix(runtime): settle or release the item-11 claim on every remaining path
body:
Follow-up to #1175. It closes the remaining paths on which an item-11 claim could be left neither released nor settled, or settled the wrong way.

## Changes

**Rust core (`trust-tasks-rs/src/consume.rs`)**
- **Cancellation during a retryable-refusal release.** `HeldClaim` now stays armed across `guard.release(..).await` and is disarmed on the very next statement, with no await in between. If the pipeline is dropped while that release is pending, the destructor releases through `release_abandoned`. Before, the claim was disarmed as soon as the handler returned, so a pipeline dropped mid-release left it in flight.
- **A panicking `Serialize`.** The handler returned, so the effect happened. If its response or a final refusal panics while being serialised for the record, the claim is now recorded with no response before the panic continues unchanged, so a resend is absorbed. Before, the claim stayed in flight.

**Rust HTTPS server (`trust-tasks-https/src/server.rs`)**
- `release_claim` is used on the refusal branch and the panic branch. It now holds a small drop guard across its `release().await`, so a request dropped mid-release (a timeout layer, a client disconnect) still releases the claim through `release_abandoned`.

**`ReplayGuard::release_abandoned` docs (`trust-tasks-rs/src/replay.rs`)**
- The method **MUST NOT** block, **MUST NOT** require a runtime context, and **MUST NOT** panic.
- The docs now state the default's degradation: a `release` that suspends is polled once and abandoned, so the record stays until `retain_until`.
- Overriding guidance no longer suggests `tokio::spawn`, which needs a current runtime.

**Go (`trust-tasks-go/trusttasks/consume.go`)**
- A `MarshalJSON` that panics inside `settle` (after the handler returned) now records the claim with a nil response in a deferred block, and the panic continues unchanged.

**Dart (`trust-tasks-dart/lib/src/runtime/consume.dart`)**
- On the non-retryable refusal branch, a refusal that cannot be encoded for the record now **releases** the claim before the error is rethrown. A refusal executed nothing, so the resend is evaluated again rather than answered as a completed duplicate with no body.
- The success branch is unchanged from #1175: there the handler ran, so the claim is settled with no response.

## Tests
- **Rust:**
  - `tests/replay_guard.rs`:
    - a response whose `Serialize` panics → panic propagates, and the resend is a completed duplicate with no response;
    - a pipeline dropped while a retryable refusal's release is pending → the claim is released and the resend runs.
  - `src/replay.rs`: the default `release_abandoned` on a guard whose `release` returns `Pending` → polled exactly once, returns without a runtime, and the record stays.
  - `trust-tasks-https` (new `release_tests` module): a release cancelled mid-await still releases the claim.
- **Go** (`claim_release_test.go`): a response whose `MarshalJSON` panics → panic propagates, and the resend is a settled duplicate.
- **Dart** (`replay_test.dart`): a final refusal whose payload cannot be encoded → the error propagates, the claim is released, and the resend is handled.

Each new test fails on `main` and passes here.

## Behaviour changes
- **Rust:** after a response or refusal `Serialize` panic, a resend is absorbed as a completed duplicate with no response. Before, it was answered "in flight" until the record expired. The panic still reaches the caller.
- **Rust and HTTPS:** a pipeline or request dropped while a claim's release is pending now releases the claim. Before, it was left in flight.
- **Go:** after a response `MarshalJSON` panic, a resend is absorbed as a settled duplicate instead of "in flight". The panic still reaches the caller.
- **Dart:** after a final refusal fails to encode, a resend is evaluated again instead of being answered as a completed duplicate with no body. The encoder error still reaches the caller.
- **No public API change:** documentation only on `release_abandoned`.

## Checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no clients touched.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): unchanged.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the item-11 record is the idempotency record. It is now settled or released on every path the handler's outcome leaves.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added. A claim whose handler returned is never released for a re-run, except a refusal, which executed nothing.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): unchanged.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): no logging changes.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): in-process cancellation and panics now settle or release; a process death still leaves a persistent record until `retain_until`, as before.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.
