title: fix(messaging/mux/ack): an id held for a DID off the connection is notFound (0.1)
body:
Follow-up to #1174. `messaging/mux/ack` 0.1 (draft) no longer lets an ack confirm another DID's mail.

**The problem:** consumer rule 3 said to answer `notPermitted` when "the message is a member's and the member is not on the connection". A message id is the SHA-256 of the message, so a principal could name an id it guessed. A `notPermitted` for a DID the connection doesn't carry would then confirm that someone holds that message, where `notFound` would not.

**Change:**
- **Rule 3:** `notPermitted` only for a message held for a member *this connection carries*, which lacks `delete` (or whose account no longer stands). Everything else is `notFound`, and a message held for a DID the connection does not carry **MUST** be answered as if it did not exist.
- **Security & Privacy → Data carried:** says why.
- **`AckRefusal.reason` description** updated to match. No schema change beyond the description: the same enum and the same members.

Bindings regenerated (doc comments only). `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` and `check-published-schemas` pass. The reference mediator implements the rule as written here (affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator, the `messaging/mux/ack` PR).

title: feat(vta): a TEE VTA can take a key-role did:webs as its own DID at first boot
body:
A TEE (Nitro) VTA can take a key-role did:webs as its own DID at first boot (design note did-webs-in-the-vta, S8).

- **Config:** new `[tee.kms.vta_did_webs]` (`server_did`, `domain`, optional `path`, `server_id`). It needs `[dids] webs_enabled` and the new, off-by-default `webs` feature on vta-enclave (`VTA_ENABLE_WEBS=true` in `build-vta.sh`). Existing images, PCR0 and attested config digests are unchanged. Setting it together with `vta_did_template` is refused. It is not in the fleet tenant overlay.
- **First boot:** `vta_service::tee_webs::maybe_generate_webs_vta_did` mints through `operations::did_webs::create_own_identity`, the same path setup's `create_webs` now uses. That function refuses if the VTA already has an identity and is reachable only from first boot and setup, never from a transport. A refused mint is fatal on Nitro, never a fallback to another identifier (VTI-KEY-009). `server::run` publishes the DID as before.
- **Interrupted boot:** the next boot adopts the identity already minted instead of minting a second one (R2.1).
- **Egress proxy:** allowlists the host and domain. `extract_host_from_did` handles did:webs and now keeps the `%3A` port for did:web and did:webvh (it used to drop it).
- **Restore fix:** `detach_hosted_dids` now also detaches did:webs slots on a cross-identity restore.
- **Refactor:** `build_vta_additional_services` moves into the library (`operations::protocol::document::vta_additional_services`) so the TEE and setup designate the same services.
- **CI:** a `tee_` test step and an enclave `…,webs` check.

Local: nextest workspace all passed (the two known flaky tests pass when rerun alone), vtc 3702/3702, doctests, clippy `-D warnings` (workspace, `tee,rest,didcomm[,webs]`), fmt, and the narrow no-webs check. Not run locally: the Linux `vsock-store` enclave builds; CI covers them.

Open questions for review:
1. Should the fleet tenant overlay be able to set `vta_did_webs`, as it can `vta_did_template`?
2. The proxy assumes the host's endpoint is on the host DID's own domain; if it isn't, the operator adds it to `ALLOWLIST_HOSTS`.
3. A detached did:webs has no command to re-attach it to a server.

title: fix(runtime): release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and end the acceptance window where the record does
body:
Two robustness fixes to the SPEC §7.2 item-11 duplicate-execution record, across the runtimes.

## 1. A handler that does not return releases its claim

When a handler panicked, or the future running the pipeline was dropped while the handler was awaited, the item-11 claim stayed "in flight" until the record expired (five minutes by default, up to the expiry horizon with `expiresAt`). Every resend in that time came back as an in-flight duplicate and never ran. The claim is now released on those paths, exactly once, and a resend runs again.

| Runtime | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Rust (`consume_core`, so `consume_inbound` and `consume_dispatched`) | released only on the two normal returns | the claim is held in a drop guard across the handler await. A panic or a dropped future releases it through the new **defaulted** `ReplayGuard::release_abandoned` (synchronous, because it runs from a destructor). A returned handler settles it as before. |
| Go (`ConsumeInbound`) | a panicking handler skipped the release; release/settle reused the request `ctx`, which was already cancelled when the handler failed for that reason | a `defer` releases the claim if the handler did not return. It does not `recover`, so the panic reaches the caller unchanged with its original stack, and `runtime.Goexit` is covered too. Release and settle run on `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` bounded at 5 s, so a store-backed guard is not handed a cancelled context. |
| Dart (`consumeInbound`) | a throwing response encoder (`responseToJson`, or encoding a non-retryable refusal) after the handler returned left the claim in flight | the claim is settled with no cached response before the error is rethrown. The handler did run, so a resend is absorbed rather than executed a second time. This is what Rust and Go already do when encoding a response fails. |
| TypeScript | already released the claim when the handler throws (and a promise cannot be cancelled) | unchanged; the existing test covers it |

`release_abandoned`'s default polls `release` once with a no-op waker and drops it. That completes for any guard whose `release` does not suspend; `InMemoryReplayGuard` overrides it to release directly and to tolerate a poisoned lock during unwinding. A guard backed by a network store should override it to hand the release to its own runtime (documented on the method). Otherwise its record stays until `retain_until`, which is no worse than before.

`trust-tasks-https`'s server is unchanged here. Its dispatch is synchronous and already releases on panic. *Correction:* cancellation can also interrupt the awaited `release_claim` on its refusal and panic branches, leaving the claim in flight; that, and the same window around the core pipeline's retryable-refusal release, are fixed in the follow-up PR.

## 2. The acceptance window ends where the record does

All four runtimes accepted a document whose `issuedAt + maxAge + skew` equalled `now` (stale only when `< now`), while `InMemoryReplayGuard` treats a record as absent once `retainUntil <= now`, and `recordExpiry` returns exactly that sum. At that one instant a resend passed freshness, found no record, and ran again. The window is now half-open (refused when `bound <= now`), as `expiresAt` already was (`expiresAt <= now` is expired). The same applies to Rust's expiry-horizon clamp. Moving the boundary on the freshness side, rather than in the guard, also fixes custom `ReplayGuard` implementations that drop at `retainUntil <= now`, as the trait contract allows.

## Tests

- Rust (`tests/replay_guard.rs`): panicking handler → resend handled, then absorbed; dropped future → resend handled; a resend while the handler is still running is still an in-flight duplicate; window boundary. `src/replay.rs`: `release_abandoned` through the override and through the default. `src/freshness.rs`: window and horizon boundaries.
- Go (`trusttasks/claim_release_test.go`): panicking handler, with the panic value propagating unchanged; handler failing because its context was cancelled, against a guard that refuses a cancelled context; window boundary.
- Dart (`test/replay_test.dart`): throwing response encoder → claim settled, resend absorbed; window boundary.
- TypeScript (`test/replay.test.ts`): window boundary.
- Shared vectors: `fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json` gains an optional per-case `secondAt` and two cases (one millisecond before the window closes → `duplicate`; at the instant it closes → `expired`). The Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart harnesses all run them, and now report a refusal by its code.

The new claim-release and boundary tests fail on `main` and pass here (checked in Rust, Go and Dart).

## Behaviour changes

- A document arriving at exactly `issuedAt + maxAge + skew` (or, in Rust, at exactly `issuedAt + expiryHorizon + skew` for a clamped `expiresAt`) is now refused `expired`; it was accepted. One instant earlier than before, and consistent with `expiresAt`.
- Rust and Go: a resend after a handler panic, or (Rust) after the pipeline future was dropped mid-handler, now runs the handler again instead of being answered as an in-flight duplicate.
- Dart: after a response-encoder failure, a resend is absorbed as a settled duplicate with no prior response, instead of an in-flight duplicate. The encoder's error still reaches the caller as before.
- Rust public API: one new trait method with a default body (`ReplayGuard::release_abandoned`). Additive; no existing implementation needs to change.

## Checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no clients touched. Go's detached settle/release context is bounded at 5 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): `InMemoryReplayGuard` takes its lock synchronously, as before.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the item-11 record *is* the idempotency record; this makes an abandoned claim releasable, so the producer's bit-for-bit resend proceeds.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added. A claim is released only when the handler did not return; a handler that returned is settled, never released for a re-run (Dart encoder path).
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none. The shared fixture format gains an optional `secondAt`, and all four harnesses read it.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): unchanged; the window boundary moves toward refusing.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): no logging changes.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a process death mid-handler leaves an in-memory record nowhere to go (it dies with it); a persistent guard keeps the claim until `retain_until`, as before. The drop guard addresses the in-process cases: panic and cancellation.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(vta)!: provision an integration as a did:webs
body:
Lets an operator provision an integration (dtg-witness, ballot-box, …) whose DID is a level-1 did:webs of class `service`, from a template (design note did-webs-in-the-vta §4, S7).

- **Selection:** template var `DID_METHOD=webs`, as `DID_METHOD=scid` already works; no new wire member in `provision/integration/0.3`. `WEBVH_SERVER` is required (no serverless did:webs); `WEBVH_DOMAIN` and `WEBVH_PATH` place it. A build without `webs` refuses by name.
- **Mint:** `create_did_webs` with `did_class: Service` and the template, so every CONVENTIONS 0.2 §9.2 check applies and `[dids] webs_service_dids` gates it.
- **Bundle:** stays `SealedPayloadV1::TemplateBootstrap`. A new additive `TemplateOutput::WebsKeriCesr` carries the stream, emitted only for did:webs, so other bundles are byte-identical. `TemplateOutput` becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Integration side:** `DidSecretsBundle::trust_task_signing_key_for(document)` picks the authentication key by role (VTI-KEY-150). vti-witness and vti-voting-service setup accept `did_method = "webs"`.
- **Fix:** `build_did_secrets_bundle` (room-host export) included the KERI pre-rotated successor key for a did:webs. It now holds only the keys the document lists.

Breaking: `TemplateOutput` variant and `#[non_exhaustive]`; `ExportDeps.webs_ks`.

Local: nextest workspace 7449 passed, vtc 3702 passed, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, and the Docker-image feature set without `webs` all clean.

Follow-ups not in this PR: distinct `provision/integration` error codes (`serviceDidNotPermitted`, `templateNotRepresentable`) need a trust-tasks change; VTI-KEY-008/009 send-side checks for host services; the did:webs VTC identity.

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under
body:
SPEC §7.2 item 3 (an unrecognised `type`) was documented in every runtime as "the caller's parse and dispatch — already succeeded by the time you hold a typed document". On the typed paths that is not true: deserialising into `TrustTask

` / `Document[P]` / `TrustTaskDocument

` (or, in TypeScript, nothing at all) never compares `type` with the spec being consumed, and the binding consumers (Rust DIDComm/TSP/DIDComm v1 `receive`, the TS TSP consumer, the Go DIDComm/TSP consumers, the Dart DIDComm/TSP consumers) take one spec and go straight to `consumeInbound`. A document of another specification whose payload happened to fit was therefore run under the consumed spec's policy and handler, and answered as its own type. The Rust dispatched path and the HTTPS servers (exact route lookup) were already correct. ## What changes Each runtime's typed consume function checks the document's `type` first, before the item-11 claim, so a refused document never burns its `id`: | Document `type` | Outcome | |---|---| | the spec's Type URI, `#request` or no fragment | accepted | | a later version of the same spec and variant whose declared `extends` chain reaches it (SPEC §5.2) | accepted (as `read_as` / `readForSpec` / `ReadForSpec` / `readForVersion` already accept it) | | the same spec and variant, any other version | `unsupportedVersion` | | anything else — another slug, the same slug under another authority or form, the `#response` variant, not a Type URI | `unsupportedType` | These are the codes SPEC §8.3 defines for item 3 and the ones each runtime's existing reader (`read_as`, `readForSpec`, `ReadForSpec`, `readForVersion`) already returns. - **Rust** — `consume_inbound` uses the decision factored out of `extension::read_as`. Every binding crate's typed receive goes through it. - **TypeScript** — `consumeInbound`. A `readForSpec` re-reading (recognised through `receivedDocumentOf`) has already been routed with whatever index the caller gave, and is not re-checked. - **Go** — `ConsumeInbound`. New optional `ConsumeOptions.Extends` names the extension lookup for a forward reading (nil: `RegistryExtends`); pass the one given to `ReadForSpecWith`. - **Dart** — `consumeInbound`. New optional `extendsIndex` argument, same purpose. - Module docs, `trust-tasks-ts/README.md` and `GETTING-STARTED.md` no longer say item 3 has already succeeded. ## Review follow-ups (second commit) - **Extension links:** Go `chainReaches` and Dart `extensionChain` now follow a declared link only to a strictly earlier MINOR of the same MAJOR, as Rust (`extension.rs`) and TypeScript (`extendsChain`) already did. A caller-supplied lookup declaring an upward, same-version or cross-MAJOR link no longer routes. Tests in `extends_test.go` and `extension_test.dart`. - **TS re-readings are tied to their spec:** `readForSpec` records the `spec.typeUri` it read for; `consumeInbound` skips its own check only when consuming under that same spec. `readForSpec(raw, A)` then `consumeInbound({ spec: B, doc })` is now checked (test in `extends.test.ts`). - **Custom indexes documented:** Go `ConsumeOptions.Extends` and Dart `extendsIndex` say a caller re-reading with its own lookup/index MUST pass it (otherwise a chain only that index declares is refused `unsupportedVersion`); the TS README says `consumeInbound` reads the generated index plus `declareExtends` tables and takes no index of its own. ## Behaviour changes (R3.6) **Breaking (`!`):** a consumer now refuses documents it used to accept, which CLAUDE.md counts as a breaking library change. All four libraries move together. - A typed consumer now refuses documents of a type other than the spec it consumes under. Callers that consumed a document under a *different* spec on purpose (none in this repo outside tests) must route on `type` first. - Rust `extension::read_as` now answers a `#response` document read as a request type `unsupportedType` (was `unsupportedVersion`), matching TypeScript and Go. - Go `didcomm` / `tsp` require the published core (`v0.9.3`); they pick the check up when that requirement moves to the release containing it. The Rust binding crates and the Dart siblings (path / `pubspec_overrides` deps) get it now. - Additive API only: Go `ConsumeOptions.Extends`, Dart `consumeInbound(extendsIndex:)`. ## Tests Each runtime gets the same negative set — another slug, the same slug under another authority, the `#response` variant, (TS/Go/Dart) a non-Type-URI, and two versions that do not reach the implemented one — plus `#request` ≡ bare, and a refusal-before-claim case (the right document under the same `id` is still handled). Existing tests that consumed a document typed for one spec under another were aligned to consume it under its own. Run locally (exit codes): - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features acl --all-targets` 0; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-https -p trust-tasks-didcomm -p trust-tasks-tsp -p trust-tasks-didcomm-v1 --all-targets` 0; `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features acl --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0; `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-didcomm -p trust-tasks-tsp -p trust-tasks-didcomm-v1 -p trust-tasks-https --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0 - `trust-tasks-ts`: `npm test` 0 (135/135 after the follow-ups), `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 0, `npm run smoke` 0 - `trust-tasks-go`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go test -race ./...` 0 - `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` 0, `dart format` clean, `dart test` 0 (161 after the follow-ups); `trust-tasks-dart-{didcomm,https,tsp,proof,capability-client}`: `dart test` 0 The full-workspace `cargo test --workspace` / `cargo clippy --workspace` were not run locally (memory); CI runs them. ## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack development guide §9) - [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched - [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a - [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the check runs before the item-11 claim; nothing is written for a refused document - [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a - [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a - [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a - [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire type changed; all four runtimes changed together - [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — the check is unconditional; the optional extension lookups default to the registry's - [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — n/a - [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutation precedes the check - [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — R3.6 behaviour changes above

title: fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under (#1162)
body:
fix(rs,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under (#1162)

* fix(runtime): refuse a document whose type is not the spec it is consumed under

The typed consume functions took the document's payload type, or a spec
policy, as given and never compared the document's `type` with it. A
document of another specification whose payload happened to fit was run
under the consumed spec's policy and handler, and answered as its own type.
SPEC §7.2 item 3 assigns that check to the consumer.

Each runtime's typed path now checks it before any other step, so a refused
document never reaches the item-11 record:

- accepted: the spec's own Type URI (`#request` and no fragment alike), or a
  later version of the same specification and variant whose declared
  `extends` chain reaches it (SPEC §5.2);
- `unsupportedVersion`: the same specification and variant at any other
  version;
- `unsupportedType`: anything else — another slug, the same slug under
  another authority or form, the `#response` variant, or a `type` that is not
  a Type URI.

Rust: `consume_inbound` (and so every binding's typed receive) uses the
same decision as `extension::read_as`. `read_as` now answers a variant
mismatch `unsupportedType` rather than `unsupportedVersion`, as the
TypeScript and Go readers already did.
TypeScript: `consumeInbound`; a `readForSpec` re-reading is already routed
and is not checked again.
Go: `ConsumeInbound`, with a new optional `ConsumeOptions.Extends` naming the
extension lookup for a forward reading (nil: the registry's).
Dart: `consumeInbound`, with a new optional `extendsIndex` argument.

The module docs and READMEs that said item 3 had "already succeeded" by the
time a typed document is held are corrected.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(runtime): hold the type check to the spec a re-reading was made for

- Go `chainReaches` and Dart `extensionChain` follow a declared extension
  link only to a strictly earlier MINOR of the same MAJOR, as Rust and
  TypeScript already do. A caller-supplied lookup declaring an upward,
  same-version or cross-MAJOR link no longer routes.
- TypeScript `consumeInbound` skips its own type check only for a
  `readForSpec` re-reading made for the spec it is consuming under; one made
  for another spec is checked like any other document.
- Documented that Go and Dart callers re-reading with their own extension
  lookup must pass it to `ConsumeOptions.Extends` / `extendsIndex`, and that
  TypeScript's `consumeInbound` reads the generated index plus
  `declareExtends` tables only.

* fix(ts): check the document type after the envelope members' types

title: fix(runtime): release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and end the acceptance window where the record does (#1175)
body:
fix(runtime): release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and end the acceptance window where the record does (#1175)

* fix(runtime): release the item-11 claim when a handler does not return, and close the window where the record expires

A handler that panicked (Rust, Go) or whose future was dropped mid-await
(Rust: a request timeout, a client disconnect) left its item-11 claim in
flight until the record expired, so every resend of the document was
absorbed as an in-flight duplicate and never ran. The claim is now
released on those paths exactly once:

- Rust: `consume_core` holds the claim in a drop guard across the handler
  await. A panic or cancellation releases it through the new defaulted
  `ReplayGuard::release_abandoned` (synchronous, as it runs from a
  destructor); a returned handler settles it as before. The default polls
  `release` once; `InMemoryReplayGuard` releases directly.
- Go: a deferred release covers a panicking handler without recovering, so
  the panic continues unchanged. Release and settle run on a context
  detached from the request's cancellation (bounded at five seconds), so a
  store-backed guard is not handed an already-cancelled context.
- Dart: when the response encoder throws after the handler returned, the
  claim is settled with no cached response before the error is rethrown,
  rather than left in flight. The effect happened, so a resend is absorbed.
- TypeScript already released the claim on a throwing handler.

The acceptance window over `issuedAt` (and the expiry horizon in Rust) now
ends exclusively, at the instant `recordExpiry` returns, in all four
runtimes. A guard drops a record once `retainUntil <= now`, while a
document was still accepted at exactly `retainUntil`, so at that instant
it could be accepted with no record and executed again. The window is now
half-open, as `expiresAt` already was.

The shared `fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json` vectors gain an optional
per-case `secondAt` and two boundary cases, run by all four runtimes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(runtime): keep the claim-release change clear of neighbouring edits

Wrap the claim in its drop guard just before the handler runs, keep the
record-expiry doc wording, and move the Go claim-release tests into their
own file.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(runtime): keep the TypeScript record-expiry wording

title: fix(vtc-service)!: keyed list cursors for badges, boards and elections; application and suspended entries read as members do not
body:
Two fixes on vtc-service's read paths: list cursors are keyed, and `application` and suspended entries no longer pass gates meant for members and administrators.

## 1. Keyed list cursors (badges, boards, elections)

The three families paged with `"{offset}.{mac}"` cursors. The "mac" was `SHA-256("vtc/<family>/cursor/v1" ‖ binding ‖ offset)`, truncated and unkeyed, so any caller could compute a valid cursor for any binding and offset. It was compared with `==`. On the five badge lists (`list`, `claims/list`, `awards/list`, `holders/list`, `kudos/list`), `page()` then computed `offset + limit` unchecked, so an offset near `usize::MAX` overflowed. In release it wrapped and sliced `items[len..small]`, which panics. Boards clamped `start` first and did not panic. Elections added the offset to a schema-capped limit with no check.

- New `trust_tasks::offset_cursor`, used by all three families:
  - `mint`: `"{offset}.{hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, family ‖ binding ‖ offset)[..16])}"`.
  - `read`: refuses anything but the canonical decimal offset, then verifies the tag with `verify_truncated_left` (constant time).
  - `key`: the audit writer's active key, as `directory_tasks` / `group_tasks` cursors use. With no audit writer, a random per-process key, so cursors stop verifying at a restart and the client starts the list again. Rotating the audit key does the same.
  - `window(offset, limit, len)`: a page that is always inside the result.
- `badge_tasks`, `board_tasks` and `election_tasks` drop their own MAC functions. The bindings (caller and filters) are unchanged.

## 2. `application` and suspended entries read as members do not

An `application` entry is not a membership (VTI-ACL-037), and a suspended entry may read the action list and nothing else (`vtc-action-list.md` §8.2, VTI-APV-019). Several gates let both through:

| gate | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/relationships/list` (`acting_party`) | any live row | an active member, or an administrator not suspended (`Actor::may_read_as_member`) |
| `member_signer` fallback (badge, board, directory, group, community and session reads) | any live row | a live row that is neither suspended nor `application` |
| `groups::Standing::read` `administrator` | `is_administrator()` | `is_administrator() && !is_suspended()` |
| capability-module list | refused `application` only | also refuses a suspended entry |
| `vtc/join-requests/query` | `as_admin` (any administrative role) | `as_capable(.., vtc.join.decide)`. It is a write: it queues a community-signed credential query to a DID the caller names. |

Checked and already correct: the other `as_admin` reads (vetting show, revocations list, policy list/get) go through `admin_signer` → `resolve_admin_claims`. That path refuses a non-administrator (so an `application` entry) and a suspended entry outside the action-list tasks. Those reads stay open to any administrative role, as designed.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- **Cursors:** every badge, board and election cursor issued before this change is refused as `cursorInvalid` (badges, boards) or `malformedRequest` (elections), so a client mid-list starts again. That also happens after a restart when the community has no audit writer, and after an audit-key rotation. The cursor stays an opaque string, now 32 hex characters after the dot instead of 24. The admin console and portal only echo `nextCursor`.
- **Newly refused** with `permissionDenied`:
  - an `application` entry on `relationships/list` and on every `member_signer` read;
  - a suspended entry (administrator or member) on those reads, on group reads and on the capability-module list. That includes `auth/sessions/list` and `auth/revoke-session` for the suspended entry's own sessions, consistent with "the action list and nothing else";
  - an administrator without `vtc.join.decide` (Auditor, Approver, a custom role without it) on `vtc/join-requests/query`.
- A live `member` row with no member record (or a removed one) no longer reads `relationships/list`. Such an entry is not an active member.
- No wire types change. No JS client sends these as an `application` entry. Git bridges, the `application` holders, use the `git/*` tasks, which are capability-gated and unchanged.

## Tests

- `offset_cursor` unit tests:
  - a cursor reads back for its own binding only (not another caller, family or key);
  - edited cursors are refused: offset, `usize::MAX`, `+50`, `050`, missing, short or long tag, non-hex;
  - the old unkeyed construction is refused;
  - `window` stays in bounds for any input.
- `it::badges::a_list_cursor_is_honoured_only_as_the_community_minted_it`:
  - a real `nextCursor` pages;
  - the old unkeyed cursor at 1 and at `usize::MAX` is refused (before, the second reached the slice);
  - an edited offset is refused;
  - another caller's cursor is refused.
- `it::board_tasks::vti_brd_003_a_list_cursor_is_honoured_only_as_the_community_minted_it` (feature `voting`).
- New `it::standing_gates`:
  - `vti_acl_037_an_application_entry_reads_nothing_members_read`;
  - `a_suspended_administrator_reads_no_relationships_groups_or_badges`, each answered before the suspension;
  - `a_suspended_member_reads_no_badges`;
  - `a_join_query_takes_the_join_decide_capability_not_any_administrative_role`.

Local results:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs,voting --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --features vtc-service/vetting-pcs,vtc-service/voting --no-fail-fast` with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`: 3800 passed, 13 failed, exit 100. 12 of the 13 are the embedded-console tests (`admin_ui::tests::*`, `routing_modes::*`, the member-portal page tests), which need the console bundle that variable skips; they pass with the bundle built (verified on the same base in #2693). The 13th was a test edit of mine that broke an assertion in `arranging_the_wall_pins_within_the_limit_and_never_a_hidden_badge`; it is fixed, and `badges::` now passes 32/32 (exit 0).
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs,voting --doc`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a, read paths only.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. Refusals use the codes each task already declares.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). With no audit writer the cursors are still keyed (per-process key). Every gate changed here fails closed.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). n/a. `join-requests/query` changes only its gate.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vtc-service)!: keyed list cursors for badges, boards and elections; application and suspended entries read as members do not (#2694)
body:
fix(vtc-service)!: keyed list cursors for badges, boards and elections; application and suspended entries read as members do not (#2694)

List cursors

The badge, board and election lists bound their offset cursors to the
caller and the question with an unkeyed SHA-256, which any caller could
compute for any offset. On the badge lists, `offset + limit` was then
unchecked, so an offset near `usize::MAX` overflowed and indexed past the
slice.

`trust_tasks::offset_cursor` is now shared by all three:
- `"{offset}.{tag}"`, the tag being 128 bits of HMAC-SHA256 over the task
  family, the binding and the offset. The key is the audit writer's
  active key, as the directory and group cursors use, or a random key
  made once per process when there is no audit writer.
- The tag is verified in constant time. Only the canonical decimal form
  of the offset is read.
- `window` clamps every page to the result whatever the offset and limit,
  and the election list's next offset uses a saturating add.

Who reads as a member

- `vtc/relationships/list` admitted any live ACL row. It now requires an
  active member or an administrator who is not suspended, so an
  `application` entry (never a membership, VTI-ACL-037) and a suspended
  entry (which may read the action list and nothing else, VTI-APV-019)
  are refused.
- `member_signer`'s fallback for a signer that is not an administrator
  admitted any live row. It now refuses suspended and `application`
  entries. That covers the badge, board, directory, group, community and
  session reads that use it.
- `groups::Standing` counted a suspended administrator as an
  administrator. It no longer does.
- The capability-module list refuses a suspended entry as well as an
  `application` one.
- `vtc/join-requests/query`, which queues a credential query the
  community signs to a DID the caller names, was gated on holding any
  administrative role. It now requires `vtc.join.decide`.

title: fix(vtc-service)!: passkey ceremonies expire and are bounded, and a sign-in naming a subject answers alike whether or not it is enrolled
body:
Two related changes to the VTC's WebAuthn ceremonies: ceremony state now has a lifetime and a bound, and the unauthenticated sign-in start answers the same way for every subject.

## 1. Ceremony state expires, is swept, and is bounded

`vti_common::auth::passkey::store` wrote each in-flight ceremony (`pk_reg:`, `pk_auth:`, `pk_auth_stepup:`, `pk_reg_user:`, `pk_reg_enroll:`) with no timestamp, and nothing removed it unless a finish took it. That caused two problems:
- A sign-in or step-up challenge stayed redeemable however old it was. The 60 s `timeout` in the options binds only the browser.
- Every unauthenticated start (console sign-in, member-portal sign-in) wrote a row, and each row serialised every candidate credential. The rows were never cleared.

The vtc-service host pins beside these rows (`member_reg:`, `revoke_target:`) had the same issue.

Now:
- **TTL.** Every ceremony row is stored as `{ expiresAt, owner?, value }`, five minutes out (`CEREMONY_TTL_SECS = 300`).
  - `take_*` / `take_pending` deletes the row atomically, as before, and answers `None` if it has lapsed. So the row is deleted exactly once and a stale challenge is never honoured.
  - `get_pending` (registration user, portal pin, revocation pin) also refuses a lapsed row.
  - A row in the old layout cannot be read as the new one. It is treated as lapsed: it authorises nothing and the sweep removes it.
- **Sweep.** `sweep_expired_ceremonies(ks, now, extra_prefixes)` deletes lapsed rows. The delete is a `Batch` with `require_unchanged` + `remove`, so a row a finish took (or that was rewritten) in the meantime is left alone. That gives the R1.7-style exactly-once delete between sweep and take, and a test races the two.
  - The existing `RetentionSweeper` runs it on start and every pass for `passkey_ks` (plus `revoke_target:`) and `member_passkey_ks` (plus `member_reg:`). `RetentionSweeper::spawn` gains the two keyspaces.
- **Bounds.** Each ceremony state row is counted by a key-only owner index (`pk_owner:{owner tag}:{state key}`). The owner tag is a digest of the DID, so `did:web:a` never counts against `did:web:a:b`.
  - **8 per authenticated owner** (enrolment, step-up, revocation, portal registration, install claim). Refused with 429.
  - **1,000 anonymous** (unauthenticated sign-in starts, console and portal together per keyspace). Refused with 503.
  - **2,000 in all** per keyspace. Refused with 503.
  - Lapsed rows are swept before a start is refused, so only live ceremonies count. An anonymous flood cannot use up the room authenticated ceremonies need.
  - The count and the write are not one atomic step, so concurrent starts can pass a bound by their own number. That is noted in the code.
- **API (breaking, vti-common):** `store_registration_state` and `store_auth_state` take an `owner: Option<&str>`. New: `store_pending`, `take_pending`, `get_pending`, `sweep_expired_ceremonies`, and the constants above. Every caller in this repository is updated: console sign-in and step-up, admin passkey enrol and revoke, install claim, and portal registration and sign-in. Nothing else in the workspace uses these functions. vta-service does not use this store.

## 2. A sign-in that names a subject answers alike for enrolled and unenrolled subjects

`POST /v1/auth/passkey-login/start` (`purpose: login`, no session) with a `subject` answered a subject with no passkeys with 403 and a subject with passkeys with 200 and a challenge.

Now:
- **Start.** Both get 200 and a challenge of the same shape. For an unenrolled subject, `login_credentials_for` builds 1 or 2 stand-in credentials. Each detail is taken from `HMAC-SHA256(key, subject)`: the count, an id length of 16, 20, 32 or 64 bytes, the id bytes, and the transports (none, or a common set). The key is 32 random bytes kept in `passkey_ks` (`pk_decoy_key`) and made on first use, so the set is the same on every call and across restarts, as a real one is.
  - Both cases take the same path: one lookup, one `start_passkey_authentication`, one stored ceremony.
  - No authenticator holds a stand-in credential, so its ceremony fails at finish.
- **Finish.** `passkey-login/finish` answers every failure before a registered credential is found with the same 401 and the same body: `passkey authentication failed`. That covers no ceremony, a lapsed ceremony, an assertion that does not verify, and a credential that is not registered. Before, three different messages told those cases apart. The detail is logged at warn.
- **Rate-limit refusal.** On `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, a document that claims a signer the community knows is charged the per-address `signed-address` ceiling before verification. Its 429 named that limiter, unlike the `unauth` 429 a stranger gets, so a 429 said whether the named DID was known. It is now the anonymous refusal, name and message alike. The bucket that refused is logged at debug.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- **Newly refused:**
  - a passkey ceremony finished more than five minutes after its start;
  - a ninth concurrent ceremony for one DID (429);
  - a start when 1,000 anonymous, or 2,000 total, ceremonies are pending (503).
- Ceremonies in flight during the upgrade must be restarted, because their rows are in the old layout.
- `passkey-login/start` with an unenrolled `subject`: 403 becomes 200 with a stand-in challenge. The admin console never sends `subject`. No client in this repository, `pnm-browser-plugin`, `cierge` or `vti-didcomm-js` sends it or matches the old 403 message.
- `passkey-login/finish`: the 401 message is now always `passkey authentication failed`. No client matches on the old messages, which were "auth state not found or expired", "credential not registered" and the webauthn-rs detail.
- A pre-verification 429 on the Trust Task door reports `limiter: "unauth"` for both buckets. No consumer branches on `signed-address`. I checked the admin console, `pnm-browser-plugin` and `vta_sdk::rate_limit`.
- Not changed: the console's and the portal's usernameless sign-in still list every registered credential in `allowCredentials`. See "Decision needed" below.

## Decision needed (not in this PR)

The usernameless sign-ins (console with no `subject`, and `/v1/member/passkey-login/start`) still return every registered credential id. That shows how many passkeys exist and gives stable ids for them. The fix is a discoverable challenge with an empty `allowCredentials`, resolving the user at finish (webauthn-rs `conditional-ui` / `start_discoverable_authentication`). But registration today uses `start_passkey_registration`, which does not require a resident key. A credential registered as non-discoverable would then stop working for usernameless sign-in. **Recommendation:** require resident keys for new registrations now, then move both usernameless sign-ins to discoverable challenges once existing credentials have been re-enrolled, or keep the full list only for credentials marked non-discoverable. That needs a product call on re-enrolment, so it is left out.

## Tests

- vti-common `auth::passkey::store`:
  - a lapsed ceremony is not returned and is gone after the take, with its owner count released;
  - a live ceremony is taken once;
  - pre-change rows authorise nothing and are swept;
  - the sweep keeps live rows and removes lapsed ones, including host prefixes;
  - **a sweep racing takes deletes each row exactly once** (20 rounds × 8 rows, 8 threads);
  - per-owner bound (429), with other owners unaffected and the place freed on finish;
  - lapsed ceremonies do not count;
  - the anonymous bound (503) leaves authenticated owners room;
  - a DID's owner prefix never covers a DID that extends it.
- vtc-service:
  - `stand_in_credential_tests`: deterministic per subject and key; accepted by webauthn-rs; the shape of `allowCredentials`.
  - `retention::the_passkey_ceremony_sweep_covers_both_keyspaces_and_the_host_pins`.
  - `trust_task_admission::a_known_signer_claim_is_refused_exactly_as_an_anonymous_document`.
  - `it::passkey_step_up::a_login_naming_a_subject_answers_alike_whether_or_not_it_is_enrolled`: same status and JSON shape, a stable stand-in set, a fresh challenge.
  - `it::passkey_step_up::a_login_finish_refuses_alike_for_enrolled_unenrolled_and_unknown_ceremonies`: same status and body.

Local results:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common --features passkey --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common --features passkey`: 838 passed, exit 0
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`: 3696 passed, 12 failed, exit 100. All 12 are the embedded-console tests (`admin_ui::tests::*`, `routing_modes::*`, the member-portal page tests), which need the console bundle that variable skips. With the console bundle built (no `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD`), those tests (`admin_ui::tests`, `routing_modes::`, the two portal page tests) were re-run: 28 passed, exit 0.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). No locks added.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a. The owner index row is written before the state row, so a crash between the two leaves only an index row, which lapses and is swept.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The sweep logs a failure and runs again next pass.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). Deletes are conditional on the row being unchanged, so each row is deleted once, by its take or by the sweep (R1.7-style ownership).
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. Status and message changes and the consumers checked are listed above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). The bounds are constants. A row without a readable expiry is lapsed.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Refusals and sweep counts are logged; the finish detail stays in the log.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). Answered above for start. A finish still takes before it verifies, as before.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vtc-service)!: passkey ceremonies expire and are bounded, and a sign-in naming a subject answers alike whether or not it is enrolled (#2693)
body:
fix(vtc-service)!: passkey ceremonies expire and are bounded, and a sign-in naming a subject answers alike whether or not it is enrolled (#2693)

In-flight WebAuthn ceremony state (`vti_common::auth::passkey::store`)
had no expiry and no bound. A sign-in challenge stayed redeemable however
old it was; the browser's 60 s timeout is advisory only. Every
unauthenticated start wrote a row that nothing removed.

Ceremony state now:
- carries an `expiresAt` five minutes out (`CEREMONY_TTL_SECS`). A take
  or read of a lapsed row answers `None`, and the take deletes it exactly
  once. Rows written before this change are treated as lapsed.
- is swept by the retention task in the console's and the member
  portal's passkey keyspaces, together with the portal registration pin
  and the revocation target pin. Each delete is conditional on the row
  being unchanged, so a row a finish has just taken is never deleted a
  second time.
- is counted per owner. That is the authenticated DID that started it, or
  one shared anonymous owner for an unauthenticated sign-in. The bounds:
  8 pending per DID (429), 1,000 pending anonymous sign-ins (503) and
  2,000 in all per keyspace (503). Lapsed rows are swept before a start
  is refused. `store_registration_state` and `store_auth_state` take the
  owner; `store_pending` / `take_pending` / `get_pending` /
  `sweep_expired_ceremonies` are new.

`POST /v1/auth/passkey-login/start` with a `subject` and no session
refused a subject without passkeys (403) and challenged one with
passkeys (200). It now answers 200 for both. An unenrolled subject gets a
stand-in credential set derived with HMAC-SHA256 from the subject under a
community-held random key. The set is stable per subject, goes through
the same webauthn-rs start, and is stored as a ceremony that no
authenticator can finish. `passkey-login/finish` answers every failure
before a registered credential is found with the same 401 body ("passkey
authentication failed"). The detail is logged.

A `429` from the Trust Task door's pre-verification ceiling for
documents claiming a known signer now reports the anonymous limiter's
name and message, so it no longer says whether the named DID is known.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof)!: check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default (#1168)
body:
fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof)!: check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default (#1168)

* fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof)!: check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default

The Go, TypeScript and Dart proof verifiers accepted any non-empty
proofPurpose, including keyAgreement, and none of the four read a proof's
expires. They now apply the rule trust-tasks-proof (Rust) already applies
(SPEC §4.7.3):

- proofPurpose must be authentication, assertionMethod,
  capabilityInvocation or capabilityDelegation; keyAgreement and any other
  value are malformedProof.
- Dart's withResolver path checks that the issuer's DID document lists the
  exact verificationMethod under the relationship proofPurpose names (by
  absolute reference, relative fragment, or embedded), defines it under
  verificationMethod, and names the issuer as its controller. The document
  is resolved once per verification and shared with ssi.
- expires, when present, must be a dateTimeStamp (Z or an explicit offset)
  that has not passed; no clock-skew allowance. All four runtimes.
- The Go, TypeScript and Dart signers default proofPurpose to
  authentication, as the Rust signer does, and refuse a purpose naming no
  signing relationship.
- TypeScript verifies Ed25519 with RFC 8032 decoding ({ zip215: false }),
  as Go, Rust and Dart do.

Three shared vectors (fixtures/proof) are correctly signed and must fail in
every runtime: proofPurpose keyAgreement, an unrecognised proofPurpose, and
a passed expires.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof): refuse small-order Ed25519 keys, range-check expires, refuse expires in Rust

Ed25519:
- Go: crypto/ed25519 accepts a non-canonical or small-order public key,
  and with the identity as key and R and S = 0 it verifies any message.
  The verifier now checks the key (on math/big, no new dependency) when a
  did:key is parsed and again before verifying.
- Dart: ssi 3.9 (the version package:didcomm pins) accepted the same keys;
  ssi 4 refused them. The relationship check now refuses an Ed25519
  multikey that is non-canonical or of small order, whichever ssi resolves.
- TypeScript: after @noble's strict check, the cofactorless equation is
  checked explicitly. noble checks the cofactored one, which also accepts
  an R with a small-order component that Go, Rust and Dart refuse.

expires:
- Every runtime checks each field against its range after the shared
  pattern: month, day for the month (leap years included), hour 0-23,
  minute and second 0-59, offset at most 14:00 with minutes 0-59. Each
  language's date parser accepted or rolled over a different subset.
- Rust: affinidi-data-integrity 0.8 drops `expires` when parsing, so the
  signature it checks never covers it. A proof carrying a well-formed,
  unexpired `expires` is now refused as unsupported (UNSUPPORTED_EXPIRES)
  rather than verified without it. Verifier::with_clock sets the clock.

Dart: an embedded relationship entry's controller must also be the issuer.

Shared vectors: small-order key, non-canonical key, mixed-order R, six
out-of-range `expires` values, and a valid future `expires` with a recorded
Rust exception. Manifest entries may carry `exceptions`, which each
runtime's test asserts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(dart-proof): check the Ed25519 key ssi will use, in every key format

ssi verifies with the verification method's asJwk(), which every format
(publicKeyMultibase, publicKeyBase58, publicKeyJwk) reaches through the
0xed 0x01 multikey without a length check. The small-order and encoding
check now reads the key from that JWK and runs for an Ed25519 multikey of
any length, not only a 34-byte one. Tests cover Multikey,
Ed25519VerificationKey2020, Ed25519VerificationKey2018 and JsonWebKey2020.

Go test labels: 00..0080 is the second order-4 point (y = 0, sign set), not
an x = 0 case; ec..ff (order 2, sign set) is added as one.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(vta/dids): key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the `vta/dids/*` family to the VTI specification's **key assurance levels** (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#82). Every service DID now has a level its operator chooses, and each verifier's policy decides which level it accepts:

| Level | Name | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | single key | Today's shape. Not created or managed by this family, except by `upgrade` |
| 2 | role-separated | `keyRoles`, with the VTA holding the `attestation` and `update` keys. The VTA may derive them and back them up. **There is no recovery key** |
| 3 | recoverable | The 1.0 design: keys generated and kept out of every backup, a recovery custodian outside the VTA, and **a witness is now required** |

The design note, with the reasoning in prose, is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2352.

### Versioning: what is amended in place, what gets a new version, and why

`vta/dids/*/1.0` merged in #986 and **was released in `trust-tasks-rs` v0.36.3**. CI's *published schemas change only additively* check therefore forbids any in-place change that the generated types can see. That holds even though the specs are `draft`, and even though the design is unpublished for review. So:

| Item | How it changes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **`vta/dids/create/1.1`** | **New version folder** | `assuranceLevel` becomes required, and `recoveryCommitment` becomes optional. Both are breaking changes to a released schema. At `draft`, SPEC §5.2 lets a breaking change be a MINOR, so it is 1.1, not 2.0. It has no `extends`, because it does not only add. 1.0 becomes superseded, so the libraries mark it deprecated, and it is withdrawn in the quarterly batch. Nothing pins it: the VTI workspace has no code against it |
| **`vta/dids/upgrade/1.0`** | **New task** | Raises a level in place. It is the only task in the family that accepts a level-1 identity |
| `_shared/0.1/key-roles.schema.json` | In place, additive | New `$defs` (`KeyAssuranceLevel`, `RecoveryCustodian`, `RecoveryCustodianKind`), a new optional member `RecoveryCommitment.custodian`, appended enum values (`declareAssuranceLevel`, `roleKeysInBackups`), and descriptions. All of these are allowed in place. A new shared-folder version would have forced a new version of every task in the family, through the stale-reference check |
| `_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md` and method profiles | In place | Prose that the generated types cannot see. The shared folder is `draft` |
| `keys/rotate/1.0` | In place, additive | New optional members `useRecoveryKey` and `recoveryProof`; appended error codes |
| `keys/list/1.0` | In place, additive | New optional response member `assuranceLevel` |
| `keys/revoke/1.0`, `recover/1.0`, `update/1.0` | In place | Prose, descriptions and appended error codes. Level-scoping is a refusal they now state |

`npm run check-published-schemas` passes: 10 changed spec files, all released, and every one changed only additively.

### What changes on the wire

- **`create/1.1`**:
  - `assuranceLevel` (2 or 3) is required.
  - `recoveryCommitment` is required at level 3 and refused at level 2 (`vta/dids:assuranceLevelMismatch`).
  - At level 3, a method with witnesses must name one (`vta/dids:witnessRequired`).
- **`upgrade/1.0`** takes:
  - `toLevel`;
  - `previousKeys` (`retire` or `revoke`). This is required, because the two have opposite effects on every credential in force;
  - `compromisedSince`;
  - `layout` (from level 1 only);
  - `recoveryCommitment` (at level 3).

  It mints fresh keys for every role whose custody tightens, moves the update authority, declares the level, and re-signs status lists. A level is never lowered.
- **`keyAssurance` in the document** (CONVENTIONS §3.4.2): `{ "level": 2 }` or `{ "level": 3, "recoveryCommitment": "<the recovery hash, as in nextKeyHashes>" }`. It is absent at level 1. This is how a verifier and a witness tell the levels apart. A recovery hash in `nextKeyHashes` is otherwise indistinguishable from a routine one.
- **`RecoveryCommitment.custodian`**: `separateKey`, `vta` (with the custodian VTA's DID), or `thresholdGroup`. It is custody data only, never published. A threshold custodian is offered as a `ThresholdRecoveryCommitment` `{ threshold, members }`: n members, each holding one whole recovery key of its own, t of whom must authorize; `keyAssurance.recoveryCommitment` is then `{ threshold, commitments }` (VTI-KEY-197, VTI-KEY-210–221).
- **`keys/rotate` `useRecoveryKey` plus `recoveryProof`**: the current recovery key authorizes its own replacement, so no VTA-side quorum is needed. With a threshold custodian, the t member proofs make this the two-approver rule, counted by the witness and verifiers. The quorum path remains only for a lost recovery key.
- **New family codes**: `vta/dids:assuranceLevelMismatch` and `vta/dids:witnessRequired`. There is also one task code, `vta/dids/upgrade:compromiseTimeInFuture`.

### Threshold custodians: a condition over whole keys, no ceremony tasks

After review, the threshold custodian is not a threshold signature scheme (FROST was dropped). It is n members, each a `separateKey` or `vta` custodian with a whole key, of which t must sign; a recovery entry carries a proof set of at least t member proofs, which the witness and VTI verifiers count (VTI-KEY-210–221). FIPS-approved signatures only. No ceremony tasks are needed: the only VTA-to-VTA message is the existing `RecoverySigningRequest` (CONVENTIONS §19).

### Ease-of-use changes (loosened, each with its reason)

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Level 2 needs no recovery key, witness, KEK or new party. Role keys may be derived and backed up | Level 2's protection is against compromise of the service process. That needs the keys in the VTA, not out of its backups. The recovery key was only ever needed because generated keys are in no backup |
| A level-1 identity is raised in place by `upgrade`, rather than replaced by a new DID, re-issue and deactivation | Relying parties keep the DID. The level of an artefact is fixed by its signing key, so the old key's artefacts stay level 1 |
| A bound step-up is SHOULD for a level-2 `create` (CONVENTIONS §6.5) | Level-2 creation commits nothing outside the VTA, and a MUST would push operators to level 1, which has no step-up at all |
| The witness may be run by the recovery custodian | Level 3 adds one party, not two |
| The level-2 restore path needs no `recover` | Restore brings the keys back |

### Tightened (it was weaker than it looked)

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| **Witness MUST at level 3**, up from a `noWitnesses` warning | Without one, a compromised VTA holding the routine successor drops the recovery commitment, and level 3 protects against loss only |
| The witness checks only the log: no lower level; a named recovery commitment present in `nextKeyHashes` and distinct; continuity unless the entry is signed by the previous recovery key | 1.0's "the VTA declares the recovery hash to the witness, as the second element" was a profile convention invisible to verifiers |
| The recovery key authorizes its own replacement (`useRecoveryKey`) | A VTA-side quorum is disarmed by a compromised VTA |
| A level is never lowered (`assuranceLevelMismatch`) | Lowering is the disarming attack |
| `keys/list` reports the level a verifier would establish, not merely the declared one | A defect gets reported, not hidden |

### Checks run locally

- `npm run build`: clean.
- `npm run build-bundles` and `npm run check-bundles`: clean.
- `npm run check-bindings`: Rust, TS, Go and Dart all agree; the error codes match.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: additive only.
- Bindings regenerated with `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings` and `build-dart-bindings`.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`: clean (only the macOS linker's `__eh_frame` and the pre-existing example filename-collision warnings). `go build`/`go vet` of `specs/vta/dids/...`, `tsc --noEmit` and `dart analyze` of the new modules: clean

### Needs review

1. How a witness checks the approvals for a quorum replacement when the recovery key is lost. It cannot know who is eligible to approve (webvh profile §4).
2. Whether `create` should also accept level 1 (it does not; level 1 stays on `vta/webvh/dids/create`).
3. ~~Whether the threshold ceremony tasks belong in a `vta/threshold/*` family~~ — moot: threshold custodians need no ceremony tasks (§19).

### Updated 2026-11-12: rebased, and brought in line with what merged since 2026-11-09

**Rebase.** Squashed onto current `main` as three commits: the PR's original content (five commits, one of them a merge of `main`), the content update below, and a fix for the red compatibility checks. No spec source conflicted. The generated files (`trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/**`, `schema_index.rs`, conformance tests, TS/Go/Dart modules, `component-names.lock.json`) were taken from `main` and regenerated.

**Fix for the red checks.** The previous head failed four checks: `published schemas change only additively`, plus `go`, `ts` and `Dart API compatibility`. The cause was the threshold-custodian commit. It pointed the released `keys/rotate/1.0`, `keys/revoke/1.0` and `recover/1.0` `recoveryCommitment` at the new `RecoveryCommitmentOrThreshold` union, which renamed a generated type in every library. The fix:
- `recoveryCommitment` is a single key there again.
- `keys/rotate` and `keys/revoke` take a threshold custodian in a new optional `thresholdRecoveryCommitment`, never together with `recoveryCommitment` (`malformedRequest`).
- `recover/1.0` cannot gain an alternative in place, because its `recoveryCommitment` is required. It stays as released, and the new **`recover/1.1`** takes either form (`RecoveryCommitmentOrThreshold`, as `create/1.1` and `upgrade/1.0` do), so an identity recovers straight back to a threshold custodian. 1.0 is now superseded.
- `create/1.1` and `upgrade/1.0` keep the union.
- CONVENTIONS §5.7 says which task takes which form.

The table above that says `keys/rotate` "gains `useRecoveryKey` and `recoveryProof`" now also covers `thresholdRecoveryCommitment`.

**Content updates:**
- **`vta/webs/dids/create/0.2`** linked `vta/dids/create/1.0`, which this PR supersedes; it now links `create/1.1`. The stale-references check failed on it after the rebase.
- **`vta/webs/_shared/0.2` §1.1** said the VTI spec "is being amended" (dtgwg-vti-spec#120). It now cites what merged in dtgwg-vti-spec#121: optional and alpha (VTI-KEY-001, VTI-KEY-003), the `resolvedMethods` declaration (VTI-KEY-008) and `methodNotDeclared` (VTI-KEY-009).
- **Changes to the `webs` method profile:**
  - The reference implementation is now `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.1, on KERI 2.0 (`affinidi-keri` 0.8). It replaces 0.9.1, here and in the README.
  - It states the optional/alpha position, with VTI-KEY-008/009 and the VTI-KEY-173 open issue.
  - The record is now an ACDC 2.x credential, of schema `EBMCaUhH…`. That schema adds `critical: true` and `keyAssurance`. The 1.x schema `EPulJFl5…` is still read.
  - `keyAssurance`: the 2.x schema has the attribute, but 0.13.1 neither issues nor renders it yet. Until an implementation does, a key-role did:webs is judged level 1 (VTI-KEY-199).
  - Each role's use: `attestation` → `assertionMethod`; `operational` → `authentication`, the key Trust Task documents and DIDComm senders prove with; `messaging` → `keyAgreement`. A sealed-transfer producer assertion is signed by the `attestation` key (VTI-KEY-072).
  - Planned role-key rotation (`keys/rotate`) is `Change::KeyRoles`, a new designation anchored by an `ixn` and signed by `k`. Compromise is `Change::RevokeRoleKey`. Role keys are never KEL keys (VTI-KEY-071).
  - Role-key ids are key-derived (`#<CESR key>`).
  - It explains how a raise in level is rendered (VTI-KEY-147, VTI-KEY-172). A committed successor whose custody is too weak for the new level needs a second rotation.
  - Templates: a key-role template's `@context` and `resolvedMethods` are **ignored, not refused**. This matches #1170 for `vta/webs/_shared/0.2` §9.2. Any other member that cannot be rendered is `templateNotKeyRole`, whose meaning now says so.
- **CONVENTIONS §5.4, §3.4.1, §4 item 5, create/1.1 item 5, `witnessRequired`:** a profile's next-key threshold that requires the recovery key for every rotation **MAY stand in for the witness** (VTI-KEY-129). Before this change, the `webs` profile said it did, while §5.4 still refused every unwitnessed level-3 identity.
- **CONVENTIONS §3.1, §4, §9:** the did:webs counterparts of the level-1 tasks are named (`vta/webs/dids/create/0.2`, `update/0.1`, `rotate-keys/0.1`), with the refusal that family uses for a key-role identity: `vta/webs/dids/<task>:notFound`.
- **`keys/rotate/1.0`:** a non-normative note. Rotating the role keys of the VTA's *own* identity changes the key ids it signs and decrypts under (under did:webs, the key itself), so a VTA may need to reload or restart.

**Checks (local, on the head commit):** all clean.
- `npm run build`
- `check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `check-published-schemas`: 10 released files, all changed additively.
- `build-bundles` and `check-bundles`
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`
- the `vta/dids` conformance tests: 24 pass.
- the TS, Go and Dart API compatibility scripts: none breaking.
- `go vet`, `tsc --noEmit` and `dart analyze` over the regenerated modules.

**Maintainer decisions (2026-11-12), now applied:**
- **Open question 3** → `recover/1.1` was added. Every 1.0 payload is a valid 1.1 payload with the same meaning, but 1.1 declares no `extends`, because the member's generated type changes.
- **Open question 1** → VTI-KEY-184 will be narrowed in the VTI spec. CONVENTIONS §5.1 and §14 item 3 now say an X25519 key MUST NOT be computed from a published key or a key of another role, and that deriving it as X25519 in its own right is a SHOULD. They cite the amendment as pending.
- **Open question 2** → the proposed VTI-KEY-199 item 3 change. CONVENTIONS §5.4 and the webs profile now say that a method whose establishment rules make the custodian's signature necessary for every change of the change authority counts as witnessed for the level cap. Witnesses stay SHOULD, for duplicity detection.

**Open for review:**
1. **VTI-KEY-184 versus the VTI implementation.** CONVENTIONS §5.1 and §14 item 3 keep VTI-KEY-184 as written: no published X25519 key computed from an Ed25519 key. OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2685's role rotation designates the X25519 image of an Ed25519 key on its own unpublished path. The create path there derives X25519 directly. Either the implementation changes, or VTI-KEY-184 is narrowed to forbid only conversion of a published or role-bound key.
2. **VTI-KEY-199 item 3** caps an unwitnessed level-3 version at level 2 "where the method has witnesses". It does not carve out the VTI-KEY-129 threshold stand-in, which a did:webs level-3 identity relies on.
3. ~~recover/1.1~~ — done.
4. Role-key rotation of a did:webs identity is specified here (`vta/dids/keys/rotate`). The VTI implementation's commit message plans it as `vta/webs/dids/rotate-keys` "with roles". One family should own it. I think this one should, since `vta/webs/*` manages level 1 only.

title: feat(vta/dids): key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians (#993)
body:
feat(vta/dids): key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians (#993)

* feat(vta/dids): key assurance levels — create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, recovery only at level 3, threshold custodians

Key roles were all-or-nothing: every key-role identity needed an external
recovery key, and an identity without roles was not served at all. The VTI
specification now gives every service DID a key assurance level its operator
chooses (VTI-KEY-194): 1 single key, 2 role-separated, 3 recoverable.

- vta/dids/create/1.1: `assuranceLevel` (2 or 3) is required;
  `recoveryCommitment` is required at level 3 and refused at level 2; a level-3
  identity under a method with witnesses needs one (witnessRequired); a
  template MAY set a level floor (assuranceLevelBelowTemplate). create/1.0 is
  released, so the changed shape is a new version rather than an in-place edit.
- vta/dids/upgrade/1.0 (new): raise an identity's level in place, from 1 to
  2 or 3 or from 2 to 3, with fresh keys for every tightened role; never lower.
  `previousKeys` is retire (RECOMMENDED), revoke, or, from level 1, keep.
- _shared/0.1 (additive): KeyAssuranceLevel, RecoveryCustodian and its kind,
  ThresholdRecoveryCommitment (a condition over whole keys, VTI-KEY-210–221),
  the declareAssuranceLevel change, the roleKeysInBackups warning; CONVENTIONS
  §3.4 (levels and the `keyAssurance` member), §3.5 (raising), §5.6–§5.7
  (recovery custodians, threshold custodians), §19, two family error codes
  (assuranceLevelMismatch, witnessRequired), and level-scoped custody, witness
  and approval rules.
- 1.0 tasks, additively: keys/rotate gains `useRecoveryKey` and
  `recoveryProof`; keys/list reports `assuranceLevel`; keys/revoke
  `scope: boundary` and recover are level 3 only; update refuses
  `keyAssurance` and the removal of a level-3 identity's last witness.
- Method profiles: did:webvh names the recovery commitment in
  `state.keyAssurance`; did:webs maps the levels onto its next-key threshold,
  every rotation exposes K and commits a fresh K′.
- vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 now links vta/dids/create/1.1.

Rebased onto main as one commit (was five, including a merge of main).
Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vta/dids): bring the did:webs profile and cross-references in line with dtgwg-vti-spec#121 and affinidi-did-webs 0.13.1

- webs profile: the reference implementation is affinidi-did-webs 0.13.1 on
  KERI 2.0 (affinidi-keri 0.8); the record is an ACDC 2.x credential of schema
  EBMCaUhH… with `critical` and `keyAssurance` (1.x EPulJFl5… still read), and
  until an implementation issues the attribute a key-role did:webs is judged
  level 1 (VTI-KEY-199). States the optional/alpha position (VTI-KEY-001,
  VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008, VTI-KEY-009, VTI-KEY-173); what each role is used
  for, with the sealed-transfer producer assertion on `attestation`
  (VTI-KEY-072); planned role-key rotation as a new designation anchored by an
  interaction event (Change::KeyRoles), compromise as Change::RevokeRoleKey,
  role keys never KEL keys (VTI-KEY-071); key-derived role-key ids; how a
  raise in level is rendered (VTI-KEY-147, VTI-KEY-172); and a key-role
  template's `@context` and `resolvedMethods` are ignored, not refused, as
  #1170 has it for vta/webs/_shared/0.2 §9.2.
- CONVENTIONS §5.4 (and §3.4.1, §4 item 5, create/1.1, witnessRequired): a
  profile's next-key threshold that requires the recovery key for every
  rotation may stand in for the witness (VTI-KEY-129), as the webs profile
  already claimed.
- CONVENTIONS §3.1, §4, §9: name the vta/webs/dids level-1 counterparts and
  that family's notFound refusal for a key-role identity.
- create/1.1 templateNotKeyRole also covers a member the profile cannot render.
- keys/rotate/1.0: non-normative note that rotating the VTA's own identity's
  role keys changes the key ids it uses, so it may need to reload or restart.
- vta/webs/_shared/0.2 §1.1: cite the merged VTI amendment (dtgwg-vti-spec#121)
  rather than "being amended".

Bindings regenerated (Rust; TS, Go and Dart unchanged).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vta/dids): keep the released 1.0 schemas additive — thresholdRecoveryCommitment beside recoveryCommitment

keys/rotate/1.0, keys/revoke/1.0 and recover/1.0 are released (trust-tasks-rs
0.36.3), and pointing their `recoveryCommitment` at the new
RecoveryCommitmentOrThreshold union renamed a generated type in every library
— the `published schemas change only additively`, go and Dart API
compatibility checks failed on it.

- keys/rotate/1.0 and keys/revoke/1.0: `recoveryCommitment` is a single key
  again; a threshold custodian is offered in a new optional
  `thresholdRecoveryCommitment` (ThresholdRecoveryCommitment), never beside
  it (malformedRequest).
- recover/1.0: `recoveryCommitment` is required, so it cannot gain an
  alternative in place; it commits a single key, and an identity recovered
  by a threshold custodian's proofs returns to one with keys/rotate.
- create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, unreleased, keep the union.
- CONVENTIONS §5.7 says which task takes which form.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta/dids/recover): 1.1 recovers straight back to a threshold custodian; VTI-KEY-184 and the witness stand-in aligned

- vta/dids/recover/1.1: `recoveryCommitment` is RecoveryCommitmentOrThreshold,
  as in create/1.1 and upgrade/1.0, so a recovery can commit a threshold
  custodian directly instead of a single key followed by keys/rotate. Every
  1.0 payload is a valid 1.1 payload with the same meaning; `extends` is not
  declared, because the member's generated type changes. recover/1.0 stays as
  released (only its description points at 1.1) and is now superseded.
- CONVENTIONS §5.7 and the links that named recover/1.0 point at 1.1.
- CONVENTIONS §5.1 and §14 item 3 follow VTI-KEY-184 as it is being narrowed
  (amendment pending): an X25519 key MUST NOT be computed from a published key
  or a key of another role; deriving it as X25519 in its own right is a SHOULD.
- CONVENTIONS §5.4 and the webs profile: a method whose establishment rules
  make the recovery custodian's signature necessary for every change of the
  change authority counts as witnessed for the level cap (VTI-KEY-129, and
  VTI-KEY-199 item 3 as proposed); witnesses stay SHOULD, for duplicity.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).
