title: fix(vta-service)!: check a backup upload's token before reading its body, and read only its declared size
body:
`POST /backup/blob/{bundle_id}` read the whole request body, up to the 100 MB branch limit (`BACKUP_BLOB_BODY_SIZE`), before it looked the bundle up or checked the `X-Backup-Token`. Every request held its body in memory before it was checked. The per-address limiter allows a burst of 10, and the branch had no concurrency bound.

## Changes

- **vta-backup `ops::blob`** splits the upload into two steps.
  - `admit_import_upload(ks, bundle_id, token) -> AdmittedImport`: the bundle lookup, `enforce_token`, `enforce_import_pending` and `enforce_not_expired`. It reads no body.
  - `stage_import_blob(ks, dir, admitted, bytes)`: the size and SHA-256 checks, then a **second read of the record**. State, expiry and token are checked again before anything is written, so a bundle accepted, aborted or expired during the read is not written over.
  - `write_import_blob` stays, as admit followed by stage.
- **vta-service `routes::backup_blob::post_blob`**:
  1. Path and header parsing, then admission. A wrong token or an unknown bundle is refused before any of the body is read.
  2. A bundle whose declared size is over the 100 MB ceiling is refused, and so is a `Content-Length` that differs from `expectedSizeBytes`. Neither reads the body.
  3. It claims an upload slot: one upload per bundle, two across the VTA (`UploadSlots`, an axum extension built once per router). The slot set is a `std::sync::Mutex<HashSet<Uuid>>`, never held across an await (R1.3). The slot is freed on drop.
  4. The body is read chunk by chunk, up to the declared size and no further. A body that runs past it is refused at once. A 30 s gap between chunks is a 408. The router-wide 120 s request timeout still applies.
- `routes/mod.rs`: comments updated, and the slot extension is layered onto the blob branch.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- A wrong token, unknown bundle or wrong-state upload gets its 403/404/409/410 **without its body being read**. Before, a body over 100 MB got a 400 first.
- **Newly refused:**
  - a `Content-Length` that disagrees with the bundle's declared size (400);
  - a second concurrent upload for the same bundle (409);
  - a third concurrent upload across bundles (503);
  - an upload that stalls for 30 s (408).
- A body longer than declared is refused as soon as it passes the declared size (400, as a size mismatch was before), rather than after it has been read in full.
- No wire types change. The SDK's `upload_blob` sends the exact bytes with a matching `Content-Length`, so it is unaffected. No JS client uses this route (I checked `pnm-browser-plugin`).
- The OpenAPI annotation for the POST gains the 408, 409 and 503 responses.

## Tests

New tests in `routes::backup_blob::tests`:
- `post_blob_wrong_token_refused_before_the_body_is_read` and `post_blob_unknown_bundle_refused_before_the_body_is_read`: the request body is an endless stream that counts its polls. The handler answers 403 or 404 and the stream is polled 0 times. Against the old handler these hang, because it read the endless body.
- `post_blob_stops_reading_once_past_the_expected_size`: an endless body is refused after a few chunks, and the bundle stays `ImportPending` for a correct retry.
- `post_blob_refuses_a_mismatched_content_length_before_reading`
- `read_body_capped_drops_a_stalled_upload`
- `upload_slots_allow_one_upload_per_bundle_and_a_bounded_total`
- `staging_rechecks_the_bundle_after_the_body_is_read`: an abort while the body is in flight leaves nothing staged.

The existing blob tests (accept, size and hash mismatch, second upload refused, the GET cases) pass unchanged.

Local results:
- `cargo clippy -p vta-backup -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-backup -p vta-service --lib`: 54 + 2052 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a: no client. The inbound read now has a 30 s idle timeout under the existing 120 s request timeout.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The slot mutex guards only the in-memory set and is released before the body is read. The slot itself is a resource bound, not a lock.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a. A refused upload leaves the bundle `ImportPending`, so it can be retried within its TTL.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. New status codes are listed above, and the only consumer (the SDK) is unaffected.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). n/a. The bounds are constants.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Unchanged: "accepted" is logged only after staging.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). Unchanged. The bytes are written before the state flips to `ImportReceived`, and a crash between the two leaves the bundle `ImportPending` with a stray file, which the next upload overwrites.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vta-service)!: check a backup upload's token before reading its body, and read only its declared size (#2692)
body:
fix(vta-service)!: check a backup upload's token before reading its body, and read only its declared size (#2692)

`POST /backup/blob/{bundle_id}` read the whole request body, up to the
100 MB branch limit, before it looked the bundle up or checked the
`X-Backup-Token`. Every request held its body in memory first, whatever
its token.

The upload now runs in this order:

- `vta_backup::ops::blob::admit_import_upload` looks the bundle up and
  checks the token, the kind, the state and the expiry. No body is read.
- A `Content-Length` that differs from the bundle's `expectedSizeBytes` is
  refused (400) without reading the body. So is a bundle whose declared
  size is over the 100 MB ceiling.
- The body is then read chunk by chunk and refused (400) as soon as it
  passes the declared size. A client that sends nothing for 30 s is
  dropped (408).
- At most two uploads are read at once, one per bundle: a second upload
  for the same bundle is 409, a third concurrent one is 503. The slot set
  is a plain mutex that is never held across an await.
- `vta_backup::ops::blob::stage_import_blob` checks the size and SHA-256,
  then reads the record again and re-checks the state, expiry and token.
  So a bundle accepted, aborted or expired while the body was being read
  is not written over.

`write_import_blob` remains as admit-then-stage for callers that already
hold the bytes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(room-host): warn when no room creator is named, log refused registrations, recount after room changes
body:
Follow-up to #2683, from review of that PR.

## Changes

- **Startup.** A host started without `--room-creator` or `--any-room-creator` now logs at **warn**, with `rooms_held`. It still serves those rooms and registers no new ones. An upgraded host whose owners register rooms finds out from the first lines of its log, not from refused requests.
- **Refused registrations are logged.** A refused `rooms/create` (signer not named, owner at its limit, host at its limit) logs one warn line naming the signer and the limit.
  - At most one line a minute (`REFUSAL_LOG_INTERVAL`); each line carries `also_refused_since_last_line`.
  - The answer to the caller is unchanged.
- **Kept room counts follow changes made elsewhere.** #2683 kept registration's room counts and recounted them every 5 minutes or after an ownership transfer. Now:
  - A generation counter, bumped by `HostState::rooms_changed()`, makes the next registration recount.
  - Handing out `HostState::rooms()` counts as a change. That keyspace is how an embedder seeds, restores or removes rooms (for example `vti_rooms::storage::purge_room_rows`). Ownership transfer and claim bump it too.
  - A removed room frees its slot at the next registration, instead of up to 5 minutes later.
  - room-host itself has no room-removal path. Purging is only the VTC's (`community_lifecycle.rs`), and the VTC does not use these counts.
- New `room_host::rooms_held`. Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` §8.1.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- New warn-level log lines: one at startup when no creator is named, and the rate-limited refusal line.
- No change to any answer, wire shape or limit.

## Tests

- `a_room_removed_by_the_embedder_frees_its_slot_at_once`: at a 1-room ceiling, a second registration is refused; after `purge_room_rows` through `rooms()`, it succeeds.
- `refused_registrations_are_logged_at_a_bounded_rate`: three refusals inside a minute write one line and count two.

Local results:
- `cargo clippy -p room-host --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p room-host --features didcomm --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p room-host --no-fail-fast`: 102 + 3 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The log limiter is a std mutex held for a field update only. The counts lock is unchanged.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire changes.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Unchanged (closed by default). The closed state is now loud.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Refusals are logged as refusals, with the rule.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). n/a: in-memory counters only.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: site: render prose through an allow-list, pin marked by hash, and drop the tweaks panel (#1173)
body:
site: render prose through an allow-list, pin marked by hash, and drop the tweaks panel (#1173)

* site: render prose through an allow-list, pin marked by hash, drop the tweaks panel

Spec, binding and framework-spec prose now renders through
website/assets/markdown.js, a dedicated marked instance that keeps raw HTML
only for an allow-list of inline tags and attributes, drops HTML comments,
and keeps a link or image only when its URL is relative, a fragment, or
http(s)/mailto. Everything the prose uses today renders as before. A
`carries.reference` becomes a link only when it is http(s).

The marked script tag now carries an integrity hash, like the other three
CDN scripts.

The design-tool tweaks panel and its message protocol are removed; the
values it defaulted to are now fixed in index.html.

The dev server (npm run serve) listens on 127.0.0.1 unless --host or
SERVE_WEBSITE_HOST names another address.

npm run test:website covers the renderer's allow-list, and deploy.yml runs it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* site: escape text after an unclosed inline tag, refuse protocol-relative prose links

marked's inline tag tokenizer switches to a raw mode after an opening
<code>, <kbd>, <pre> or <script> tag and emits the text that follows
unescaped, even when the renderer escapes the tag itself. The renderer now
wraps that tokenizer so the mode stays off and such text is escaped like
any other.

isSafeUrl also refuses URLs starting with two slashes (or backslashes, which
browsers read as slashes), since those name another host.

test:website now renders markdown end to end through the marked build the
page loads, fetched from the URL pinned in index.html and checked against
its integrity hash (MARKED_JS=<file> runs it offline), and checks every
element, attribute and URL in the output.

The dev server's startup log prints the address it actually bound.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(site): check the missing-renderer error in a fresh context

Deleting the global from the shared test context does not remove it on
Node 24, so the case now loads markdown.js into a context with no marked.

received wherever a pipeline holds it, so two documents under one id that
differ only in a member the payload type does not model, or in the spelling
of a timestamp, are an idConflict rather than a duplicate:

- Go ConsumeInbound digests ConsumeOptions.Received when set.
- Dart consumeInbound digests `received` whenever it is passed (it did only
  for a forward read), and the HTTPS server, DIDComm and TSP consumers pass it.
- Rust consume_inbound / consume_dispatched digest the received JSON under
  ProofPolicy::VerifyReceived, with or without a proof; the HTTPS server
  digests the body. New received_document_digest.

TypeScript consumeInbound now checks the envelope before anything reads it:
member types (string id/type and string-valued optional members, object
payload/proof/ceremony, @context string/array/object) and a nesting bound of
128 levels, refused malformedRequest and addressed only from string members.
validateEnvelope and MAX_NESTING_DEPTH are exported.

Dart consumeInbound refuses a document nested beyond maxNestingDepth (128)
with malformedRequest instead of overflowing the stack, and the new
parseTrustTaskDocument decodes a received value without throwing, returning
a malformedRequest reason for a mistyped member.

Shared vectors in fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json run in all four
runtimes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(runtime)!: received-document digest in every binding, and JCS number form

- Rust: ProofPolicy gains RejectIfPresentReceived and
  AcceptUnverifiedReceived; with_received maps all three policies, so every
  binding digests the received document whatever proof policy it is given.
- Go: digest Received only when Doc is a reading of it; the didcomm and tsp
  consumers pass Received and require core v0.9.6.
- Rust and Dart canonical forms read numbers as RFC 8785 doubles (1 and 1.0
  are one number), matching TypeScript and Go; number vectors added.
- TypeScript: a refusal with no string type carries no inResponseTo, and one
  with neither a string id nor type is suppressed.
- Dart: the nesting check runs before the payload validator.
- Tests for each, including the HTTPS server's digest over the body.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vti-witness): bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause
body:
A witness identity with no `allowed_parties` (the default) admits any opener. Three resource bounds were missing.

- **Session slots.** At `max_open` (default 1000) every new session was refused, and an open session lived for its whole TTL (default 600 s). With a per-opener cap of 4, 250 fresh DIDs filled an identity, and reopening every ten minutes kept everyone else out.
- **Per-submission work.** `witness/session/submit/0.2` verified every credential in `verifiableCredential` (and in `memberPresentation`), resolving each issuer's DID. Neither the count nor the issuers were bounded, and this ran before the session was taken.
- **Repeat submissions.** A submission whose presentation failed left the session open, so one session could be submitted to without limit for its whole TTL.

## Changes

### Opening (`witness::open_session`, `witness::evictable`)
- The per-opener cap (`max_open_per_party`) is unchanged. It also bounds each (opener, counterparty) pair. There is **no** cap on sessions naming one party as the counterparty: anyone can name anyone, so such a cap would let one opener keep everyone else from naming that party.
- At `max_open`, an identity **with no allow-list** makes room in this order (`EVICTION_MIN_AGE_SECS` = 60 s):
  1. surplus sessions over a minute old (of an opener holding more than one, every session but its newest), oldest first;
  2. then any other session over a minute old, oldest first;
  3. only then recent surplus sessions, oldest first.
- An opener's newest session, opened under a minute ago, is never closed for room, so a party's only session in progress survives. When every slot is one of those, the open is refused.
- An identity **with** an allow-list refuses at `max_open`, as before.
- Refusals keep the single `witness/session:refused` message; the rule is logged locally.

### Submitting (`presentation::verify`, `witness::submit`)
- A presentation carries at most `MAX_CREDENTIALS` = 8 credentials. More is refused before anything is resolved.
- Only credentials that could count are resolved and verified: the submitter's relationship credential, or a membership credential from an accepted community naming the holder. The same rule applies to the member presentation. Any other credential is ignored and its issuer is not resolved. The independence check (no credential issued by an excluded DID) still covers every credential.
- Failure counting:
  - A submission that **definitely** fails counts toward `MAX_FAILED_SUBMITS` = 3.
  - One that failed because a signer's key **could not be retrieved** (no resolver for the method, or the DID did not resolve: `vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::is_unretrievable`, now public, observed by wrapping the resolver) may be the network rather than the party. It counts toward `MAX_INCONCLUSIVE_SUBMITS` = 10 instead. Every other resolver refusal is a verdict on the proof and counts as definite: a key not under the proof's purpose, a `did:key` fragment that is not its own key, a malformed method, an unsupported key type.
  - Either limit closes the session. Both counts are on `SessionRecord` (`#[serde(default)]`) and are updated under the `opening` lock, which guards only local store calls.
- `presentation::verify` takes any `PurposeVmResolver`.

The new `affinidi-data-integrity` dependency entry (moved from dev-dependencies) is not a new crate; it is already in the graph through vta-sdk. It is needed for the resolver trait's types.

Docs: `docs/06-witness/README.md`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6), and what they still allow

- **A full open identity closes a session to make room instead of refusing:** aged surplus first, then other aged sessions, then recent surplus. A party whose session was closed gets `challengeMismatch` on submit and opens a new one.
  - Remaining trade-off: an opener with many DIDs, one session each, can keep every slot full. A newcomer is refused while every slot is someone's newest session under a minute old, so sustained churn can refuse a newcomer repeatedly. A newcomer who retries gets in once any session is over a minute old, or as soon as a churning opener holds more than one session.
  - A party holding several recent sessions keeps them while an older session exists; if none does, its surplus goes first.
  - Under sustained churn, a legitimate flow that takes longer than a minute between open and submit can be closed.
  - A per-source rate limit would need the transport's sender identity before the DID, which this service does not see; not done here.
- **A presentation with more than 8 credentials is `presentationInvalid`.**
- **A credential that could not count no longer fails a presentation, even if its proof would not verify; it is ignored.** Before, it was refused. The VWC still names only the verified relationship credential.
- **A session closes after 3 definite, or 10 inconclusive, `presentationInvalid` submissions.** Remaining trade-off: a submitter whose own DID never resolves gets 10 attempts, not 3. The counts are checked after verification, so up to the host session's `MAX_INFLIGHT_INBOUND` (16) verifications can run concurrently on one session before the counters close it.

Wire shapes and error codes are unchanged. No consumer outside this repo sends `witness/session*` (cierge, vti-didcomm-js, pnm-browser-plugin, pnm-relay, vti-message-bridge and affinidi-trust-registry-rs were checked).

## Tests

- **Integration (`vti-witness/tests/witnessing.rs`):**
  - `a_third_party_cannot_lock_a_counterparty_out`
  - `at_capacity_an_open_identity_spares_a_partys_only_recent_session`: a single-slot party's in-progress session survives churn; once aged, it makes way
  - `at_capacity_an_allow_listed_identity_refuses`
  - `a_session_closes_after_repeated_presentations_that_do_not_verify`
  - `a_presentation_with_too_many_credentials_is_presentation_invalid`
  - `a_credential_that_cannot_count_is_not_checked`
  - `verification_resolves_only_the_issuers_that_can_count`: a counting resolver records every VM asked for, and the third party's issuers never appear
  - `the_caps_bound_open_sessions_in_total_and_per_party`: refused when full of single, recent sessions
  - `a_wrong_verification_method_counts_as_a_definite_failure`: a `did:key` fragment that is not the key's own increments `failed_submits`, not `inconclusive_submits`
- **Unit (`witness.rs`):**
  - `room_is_made_from_aged_sessions_before_recent_surplus_never_a_recent_newest`
  - `a_recent_surplus_session_outlasts_an_aged_one`
  - `only_an_unretrievable_key_marks_a_submission_inconclusive`: an `unretrievable` error is inconclusive; a resolver verdict ("not listed under assertionMethod") is not

Local results (head 5cccacdf6, on top of the coordinator's rebase onto main with #2688):
- `cargo clippy -p vti-witness -p vta-sdk --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p vti-witness --no-fail-fast`: 56 unit and 34 integration tests passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client --lib trust_task_proof`: 53 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). No new clients.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). Eviction and failure counting run under `opening`, which guards only local store calls. Verification runs under no lock.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a: local session state only. The session is still taken after verification and restored on a failed mint.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Submissions per session are now bounded (3 definite, 10 inconclusive).
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a. A failed count update is logged and does not fail the reply.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire changes. The stored `SessionRecord` gains two defaulted fields.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). No new config. Eviction applies only where the operator chose to admit any opener.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Closing for room and after failures is logged with the identity name, not the parties' DIDs.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). Room is made before the insert; a crash in between leaves fewer sessions, never more.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

Not covered here: whether a deployment's mediator ACL already limits who can message a witness DID. The fix does not depend on it.

title: fix(vti-witness): bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause (#2682)
body:
fix(vti-witness): bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause (#2682)

* fix(vti-witness): bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause

An identity that admits any opener (`allowed_parties` unset, the default)
refused new sessions once `max_open` were open, and a session stayed open for
its whole TTL. Openers with fresh DIDs could therefore hold every slot and keep
members out by reopening. A submission's presentation was verified credential
by credential, each resolving its issuer's DID, with no limit on how many
credentials it carried. A failed submission left the session open, so the same
session could be submitted to any number of times.

- Opening: besides the per-opener cap, at most `max_open_per_party` open
  sessions may name one party as the counterparty. At `max_open`, an identity
  with no allow-list closes its oldest open sessions to make room. One with an
  allow-list still refuses (`witness/session:refused`, same message).
- Submitting: a presentation carries at most 8 credentials, refused before any
  is resolved. Only credentials that could count are resolved and verified: the
  submitter's relationship credential, or a membership credential from an
  accepted community naming the holder. Any other credential is ignored, not
  resolved. The independence check still covers every credential.
- After 3 submissions whose presentation does not verify, the session is
  closed (`SessionRecord.failed_submits`, defaulted for stored rows).

Behaviour changes: a full open identity closes its oldest session rather than
refusing; a second session naming the same counterparty is refused at the
default per-party cap; a presentation with more than 8 credentials is
refused; an extra credential that could not count no longer fails the
presentation; a session closes after 3 failed submissions.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-witness): spare a party's only recent session, drop the counterparty cap, count only definite failures

- No cap on sessions naming one party as the counterparty. Anyone can name
  anyone, so that cap let one opener keep everyone else from naming a party.
  Per (opener, counterparty) pair the per-opener cap already holds.
- At `max_open`, an identity with no allow-list makes room from surplus
  sessions first: those of openers holding more than one, each one's oldest
  first. Then it takes any session older than `EVICTION_MIN_AGE_SECS` (60 s).
  A party's only session, opened under a minute ago, is never closed for room;
  when every slot is one of those, the open is refused. Before, the oldest
  session was closed whoever held it, so churning openers could close a
  session in progress.
- A failed submission counts toward `MAX_FAILED_SUBMITS` (3) only when no DID
  resolution failed during it. One that failed while a DID could not be
  resolved, which may be the network, counts toward `MAX_INCONCLUSIVE_SUBMITS`
  (10) instead (`SessionRecord.inconclusive_submits`, defaulted).
- `presentation::verify` takes any `PurposeVmResolver`. A test now observes,
  at the resolver, that a credential that cannot count is never resolved.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-witness): count only unretrievable keys as inconclusive; close aged sessions before recent surplus

- A failed submission is inconclusive only when a signer's key could not be
  retrieved (`vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::is_unretrievable`). Every other
  resolver refusal is a verdict on the proof and counts toward the definite
  limit of 3: a key not under the proof's purpose, a `did:key` fragment that
  is not its own key, a malformed method. Before, any `Resolver` error was
  inconclusive. vta-sdk makes `is_unretrievable` and `unretrievable` public for
  this.
- Making room at `max_open` now closes, in order: surplus sessions over a
  minute old, then any session over a minute old, and only then recent surplus
  sessions. A party holding several recent sessions no longer loses them to a
  newcomer while an older session exists. An opener's newest recent session
  is still never closed for room.
- Tests: the ordering (aged surplus, aged, recent surplus, never a recent
  newest), a recent surplus outlasting an aged single, an unretrievable key
  versus a resolver verdict, and a wrong `did:key` fragment counted as a
  definite failure.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vta-service)!: outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client
body:
When the VTA sends a Trust Task over REST, it posts to `{endpoint}/trust-tasks`. The endpoint comes from the recipient's DID document, which whoever controls that DID writes. For room tasks the caller names the recipient (the room host's DID), and persona-signed documents only go over REST, so this is the normal path.

`Outbound::send_rest` had three problems:
- **No address check.** It posted through `vta_sdk::http::rest_client()`: timeouts and same-origin redirects, but no resolver guard and no `no_proxy`. The only endpoint check was `is_https_or_loopback`, which accepts `https://10.0.0.5` and `http://127.0.0.1:…`.
- **No size limit.** The reply was read with `response.text()`, with no cap.
- **Echoed body.** A reply that was not JSON was copied into the 502 error text the caller sees.

`vti_common::trust_task_push::RestPushTransport` (VTA and VTC member pushes) had the same endpoint rule. It used the foreign-fetch client, but never checked the URL, and that client's resolver never sees an IP-literal host.

The workspace already had the right pieces (`guard_foreign_url`, `foreign_fetch_client_for`, `read_body_capped`, `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`). This PR wires them in.

## Changes

- **vta-sdk `http::guard_peer_endpoint(url, policy)`**: the check for a peer-advertised Trust-Task endpoint that a *service* is about to dial.
  - `https://` is decided by `guard_foreign_url`: private-network, loopback and local names only with the opt-in; link-local, metadata and reserved addresses never.
  - `http://` passes only for an exact loopback host **and** only with the opt-in.
  - Userinfo is refused without being echoed.
  - It is stricter than `guard_vta_endpoint`, which admits loopback by default because it vets a VTA that a *client* chose.
- **vta-service `operations::outbound`**:
  - `send_rest` delegates to `send_rest_to(recipient, endpoint, document, policy)`, called with `EndpointPolicy::process_default()`.
  - URL guard, then `foreign_fetch_client_for(policy)`: no proxy, no redirects, a guarded resolver. The 30 s total budget is kept per request; the connect timeout is the foreign-fetch one.
  - The reply is read with `read_body_capped` at `MAX_REST_REPLY_BYTES` = 4 MiB. The largest legitimate reply is a `rooms/keys/read` batch, about 512 KiB plus one record of up to about 1.4 MiB base64url.
  - A non-JSON reply is reported as status, byte count and serde class/position. A 256-character excerpt goes to the debug log only.
  - This covers every `Outbound` caller (room tasks, `webvh_host`, room owner/profile/key-watch), since they all send through `Outbound::send`.
- **vti-common `trust_task_push`**: `RestPushTransport::new(pushes, http, guard)`. The `RestEndpointGuard` is checked before every dial; a refusal is `MessagingError::NoEndpoint`. vti-common does not take on the HTTP client stack: the VTA (`messaging/push.rs`) and the VTC (`messaging.rs`) pass `guard_peer_endpoint` and a client built for the same policy.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- **Loopback and private-network peers need `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`.** That covers room hosts, a DID-hosting `https_base`, and REST push recipients, on the VTA and on the VTC's member push. `docs/03-vtc/data-rooms-quickstart.md` already sets it for local development. Production peers on public HTTPS are unaffected.
- A public peer hostname whose DNS answer is non-public is refused at connect time.
- A peer's redirect is no longer followed. Before, a same-origin redirect was.
- A reply over 4 MiB is refused as a bad gateway.
- A non-JSON reply's body no longer appears in the error.
- **API (breaking, vti-common):** `RestPushTransport::new` takes a third argument. Both in-repo callers are updated.
- **API (additive):** `vta_sdk::http::guard_peer_endpoint`.
- No wire or error-code changes, so no JS consumer is affected; the JS clients do not drive the VTA's outbound sends.
- The VTA's policy is carried as `AppState.endpoint_policy`, set from `AppStateParts.endpoint_policy` and defaulting to `EndpointPolicy::process_default()` at startup. `Outbound::from_app_state` passes it to `send_rest_to`. `AppStateParts` gains a field (it is `#[non_exhaustive]`). `Outbound::from_parts` (the webvh hosting path) reads the process policy.
- **Test harness:** `MockVta` / `TestAppContext` and `build_signing_test_app_state` state `EndpointPolicy::private_allowed()`, because their stand-in peers listen on loopback. External users of `MockVta` (openvtc-core) can therefore reach loopback peers from it. `StubWebvhHost::start` still enables private endpoints process-wide, because the webvh path does not go through `AppState`.

## Tests

- vta-sdk `http`: `guard_peer_endpoint` cases (public https; opt-in for loopback and private; refusals the opt-in does not lift, including look-alike names, metadata, link-local, plaintext to a private IP, userinfo).
- vta-service `outbound::tests::send_rest_guard`:
  - a loopback peer is never contacted under the default policy (`expect(0)`)
  - non-public peers are refused
  - a JSON reply round-trips
  - a non-JSON body is not echoed
  - an oversized reply is refused
- vti-common: `rest_push_refuses_an_endpoint_its_guard_refuses_before_dialling`.
- The policy is passed explicitly wherever that was simple: the room tests (`room_act`, `room_owner_group`, `room_profile_tests`) and `tests/e2e/tests/room_key_watch.rs` run on harness states that say `private_allowed()`, and no longer touch the process switch. The process-wide switch remains in two places, with comments saying why:
  - `StubWebvhHost::start`: the webvh seam is built from parts, not from `AppState`; threading the policy through `WebvhDeps` is a larger change.
  - `vtc-service/tests/it/member_push_didcomm.rs`: set before the VTC starts, because the VTC's push transport reads the process policy then.

Local results (rebased on origin/main, after the policy-on-AppState commit):
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service -p vti-e2e-tests --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --features transport-harness --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib`: 2025 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test it`: 381 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --features transport-harness transport_harness_tests`: 13 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vti-e2e-tests --test room_key_watch`: 11 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --features transport-harness --test it member_push`: 12 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0
- From before the rebase, files unchanged since: `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client --lib http::` 37 passed, exit 0; `cargo test -p vti-common --lib trust_task_push` 21 passed, exit 0

Not covered: DID resolution for `did:web` recipients goes through the external resolver crate, which this PR does not change.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). Peer sends use the shared foreign-fetch client: 30 s per request, 10 s connect.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a: the check runs before the send.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Unchanged. A guard refusal on a push is `NoEndpoint`, bounded by the existing attempt window.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire changes. Rust API change listed above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Without the opt-in, only public `https://` peers are dialled.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). A refused push endpoint is logged at warn with the reason.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

body:
fix(vta-service)!: outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client (#2687)

* fix(vta-service)!: outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client

A REST send's URL comes from the recipient's DID document, which whoever
controls that DID writes, and the recipient of a room task is named by the
caller. `Outbound::send_rest` posted to it with the ordinary REST client
(timeouts and same-origin redirects only), so the endpoint could name a
loopback or private-network service, the reply was read with no size limit,
and a reply that was not JSON was copied into the error the caller saw. The
push transport (`vti_common::trust_task_push::RestPushTransport`) had the
foreign-fetch client but no URL check, and that client's resolver never sees
an IP-literal host.

- vta-sdk: `http::guard_peer_endpoint(url, policy)`. `https://` is decided by
  `guard_foreign_url`. `http://` passes only for an exact loopback host, and
  only with the private-endpoint opt-in. Userinfo is refused unechoed.
- vta-service: `send_rest` (now `send_rest_to`, taking the policy) checks the
  URL with `guard_peer_endpoint` under `EndpointPolicy::process_default()` and
  sends through `foreign_fetch_client_for` with the same policy (no proxy, no
  redirects, a resolver that refuses non-public answers). The 30 s total
  request budget is kept. The reply is read under a 4 MiB cap
  (`read_body_capped`). A reply that is not JSON is reported by status, size
  and parse position; its text goes to the debug log only.
- vti-common: `RestPushTransport::new` takes a `RestEndpointGuard`, run on each
  URL before it is dialled; a refusal is `MessagingError::NoEndpoint`. The VTA
  and VTC pass `guard_peer_endpoint` and build the client for the same policy.

Behaviour changes: loopback and private-network peers (room hosts, DID
hosting, push recipients) are reached only with `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`
(the data-rooms quickstart already sets it); a peer's redirect is no longer
followed; a reply over 4 MiB is refused; a non-JSON reply's body is no longer
in the error.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vti_common::trust_task_push::RestPushTransport::new` takes a
third argument, the URL guard.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-service): carry the peer endpoint policy on AppState instead of the process switch in tests

`AppState.endpoint_policy` (from `AppStateParts.endpoint_policy`, defaulting to

The test harness states its own: `MockVta` / `TestAppContext` and

title: fix(go-didcomm)!: validate and bind the JWE header, and take the local DID from the opening identity (#1169)
body:
fix(go-didcomm)!: validate and bind the JWE header, and take the local DID from the opening identity (#1169)

* fix(go-didcomm)!: validate and bind the JWE header, and take the local DID from the opening identity

UnpackTrustTask now checks the authcrypt JWE before opening it, following
DIDComm v2 and RFC 7516:

- apu must be base64url(skid) and apv base64url(SHA-256 of the sorted
  recipient kids). The per-recipient kids are unprotected; apv is what binds
  them to the protected header. A base64url error in either is refused
  instead of becoming an empty KDF input.
- Every recipient entry must carry a kid, and only the entry whose kid is
  exactly the identity's Kid is opened. The single-unlabelled-entry fallback
  is gone.
- Transport.Local is the DID of the identity the envelope was opened with,
  never the kid read from the envelope.
- crit and zip are refused, as is a typ other than
  application/didcomm-encrypted+json, a shared unprotected header, aad, the
  flattened header/encrypted_key form, a per-recipient header repeating a
  protected parameter, and JSON member names differing only by case.
- After decryption, a plaintext from that is not the authenticated sender is
  FailDecrypt, and a to that does not name the recipient is
  FailNotForThisRecipient.

Envelopes packed by this module and by affinidi-messaging-didcomm (the
interop fixture) still open.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(go-didcomm): open an affinidi-packed two-recipient envelope

A JWE packed by affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.8 to bob and carol (carol's
entry first, so the entries are not in apv's sorted order) now opens for
each recipient. The test also checks that affinidi's apv is SHA-256 of the
sorted kids, and that dropping an entry fails the apv check, so the check is
pinned against another implementation's computation rather than only
against computeAPV.

The README states that an empty "to" is refused. The harness source is in
testdata/README.md; the scripts/gen-didcomm-interop-fixture path an old
comment named never existed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(proof, ts-proof, dart-proof, dart-didcomm, ceremony): bound multibase decoding of unauthenticated values
body:
## Summary

The TypeScript, Dart and Rust counterparts of the Go change in #1166, plus two places nearby that decode unauthenticated multibase input. Each proof verifier decodes a proof's `proofValue` and its `did:key` multikey before any signature check, using decoders whose cost grows with the square of the input length. Measured before this PR:

| Where | Decoder | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Rust `trust-tasks-proof` | `multibase::decode` (upstream `affinidi-data-integrity`; base58btc, and also `Z`/`k`/`K`/`9`) | `verify_raw` on 1 MiB, release build: ~53 s (`proofValue`), ~50 s (`did:key`); a 64 KiB `Z` value ~218 ms |
| Dart `trust_tasks_proof` | `ssi` → `base_codecs` | 32 KiB ≈ 1.5 s, quadratic → roughly 25 min at 1 MiB |
| Dart `trust_tasks_didcomm` | `package:didcomm` resolves the authcrypt `skid` before decrypting | P-256 `did:key` skid: 8/16/32 KiB → 0.11/0.39/1.5 s |
| TS `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof` | `@scure/base` | 2.4.0 refuses over 4096 characters itself (~1.2 ms worst case); 2.0.0–2.3.0, which `^2.0.0` admitted, take 64 KiB ≈ 5.6 s |
| Rust `trust-tasks-ceremony` | `multibase::decode` of a receipt's salt | uncapped |

### What each package now does

- **proof** (Rust): new `pub fn affinidi::check_proof_bounds(&DataIntegrityProof)`, called by `Verifier::verify_raw` before the Affinidi crates run. It refuses a `proofValue` or `did:key` multikey that is not in its cryptosuite's base (base58btc `z`; base64url `u` for `bbs-2023`'s `proofValue`), and one longer than the cryptosuite's bound, checked **before decoding**:
  - `eddsa-*`, `ecdsa-*`: 128 bytes / 175 characters, the bound every runtime uses.
  - `mldsa44-*` (upstream `ml-dsa` feature): signature up to 4627 bytes (ML-DSA-87), multikey up to 2594 bytes.
  - `slhdsa128-*` (upstream `slh-dsa` feature): signature up to 7856 bytes, multikey up to 2594 bytes.
  - `bbs-2023`: base64url `proofValue` up to 48 KiB (linear decode).

  Failures are `VerificationError::MalformedProof("proofValue: …" / "verificationMethod: …")`. The `PurposeBound` docs tell callers who use `DataIntegrityProof::verify` directly to call `check_proof_bounds` first. A new `ml-dsa` crate feature turns on the upstream one so this crate's own tests cover the post-quantum bounds.
- **ts-proof**: `fromMultibase` and `publicKeyFromDidKey` go through one bounded decoder (175 characters / 128 bytes) and still report `signatureInvalid`. `@scure/base` is now required at `^2.4.0`.
- **dart-proof**: `verifyDetailed` checks `proofValue` and a `did:key` verificationMethod (175 characters / 128 bytes) before `ssi` sees them, and reports `signatureInvalid`. The constants are private, so there is no API change.
- **dart-didcomm**: `unpackTrustTask` refuses an envelope whose protected `skid` is over 4096 characters, or names a `did:key` multikey over 175 characters, before `package:didcomm` resolves it. Failure: `EnvelopeFailure.undecryptable`, no new enum value.
- **ceremony**: a receipt salt over 1024 characters is refused (`Error::Salt`) before it is decoded.

No new dependencies in default builds. `Cargo.lock` gains `ml-dsa`, `module-lattice`, `keccak`, `shake` and `sponge-cursor`, which `affinidi-crypto`'s own `ml-dsa` feature resolves. They are built only with the new opt-in `ml-dsa` feature, or `--all-features`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- **Ed25519 / NIST proofs (all runtimes):** nothing that verified before is refused. Over-long values always decoded to more bytes than any supported key or signature.
- **Rust, other bases:** a `proofValue` or `did:key` id in any base other than base58btc (base64url for `bbs-2023`) is now refused. Upstream signs only base58btc, or base64url for `bbs-2023`, so this refuses only values no Affinidi signer produces. A third-party signer using another base for these suites would now be refused.
- **Rust, post-quantum suites:** ML-DSA and SLH-DSA proofs within their parameter sets' sizes keep verifying. The first revision of this PR applied 128 bytes to every suite and would have refused them; there is now a test for that.
- **Rust, error variant:** an over-long `proofValue` now gives `MalformedProof` with a detail, where it used to give `SignatureInvalid`. Both reach the wire as `proofInvalid`.
- **dart-didcomm:** a 4096-character cap on the claimed sender key id. That is well above any `did:key`, `did:web` or `did:webvh` key id; a `did:peer:2` with very many services could in principle exceed it.
- **ceremony:** a salt is at least 16 bytes (22 base58 characters); 1024 characters is the new cap.
- **TS:** the `@scure/base` floor moves from 2.0.0 to 2.4.0.
- No `!`: no public signature changed. `check_proof_bounds` and the `ml-dsa` feature are additions.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Direct `DataIntegrityProof::verify` callers in other repos should call `trust_tasks_proof::affinidi::check_proof_bounds` first (e.g. `vti-push-gateway/src/proof.rs`), once this is released.
- dart-didcomm: only the top-level authcrypt `skid` can be checked before `package:didcomm` runs. An authcrypt layer inside an anoncrypt wrapper, and a signed layer's `kid`, are resolved inside `package:didcomm` after the outer layer is opened, and this binding has no hook there. That needs either a bounded resolver passed to didcomm or a change upstream.

## Tests

New test files only, apart from one test appended to `trust-tasks-ceremony/src/tests.rs`:

- `trust-tasks-proof/tests/base58_bounds.rs`: a signed document still verifies; refusal at 176 characters, at 175 characters that decode to 129 bytes, and at 129 leading zero bytes, for both fields; `Z`, `9`, `k`, `K`, `u` and `f` prefixes refused at 8 characters and at 64 KiB; `check_proof_bounds` called on its own; 180 one-MiB values (`z`, `Z`, `k`) refused in under 1 s. Under `--features ml-dsa`: a real `mldsa44-jcs-2024` did:key proof verifies (its `proofValue` is over 3000 characters), values just over the ML-DSA bounds are refused, and 100 one-MiB values are refused in under 1 s. Unit tests in `src/affinidi/bounds.rs` check that the largest values and all-zero values at each bound pass.
- `trust-tasks-ts-proof/test/base58.test.ts`: round trip up to 128 bytes, the same refusal cases, and 200 one-MiB refusals in under 1 s. The bounds test fails on `main`.
- `trust-tasks-dart-proof/test/base58_bounds_test.dart`: the same cases through `verifyDetailed`, including a 1 MiB `z6Mk…` did:key; 200 refusals in under 1 s. 6 of these fail on `main`.
- `trust-tasks-dart-didcomm/test/sender_kid_bounds_test.dart`: a real envelope still opens; an over-long `did:key` skid and a skid over 4096 characters are refused as `undecryptable`; 20 envelopes with a 1 MiB `zDn…` skid are refused in under 2 s.
- `trust-tasks-ceremony` (`src/tests.rs`): a salt at 1024 characters decodes, one over it is refused, and 100 one-MiB salts are refused in under 1 s.

Results:

- **Rust:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-proof -p trust-tasks-ceremony --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with default features and with `--all-features`; `cargo test` for the same crates, default and `--all-features`; `cargo doc` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`. All exit 0.
- **TS:** `npm test` (39 pass), `typecheck:test`, `build`. All exit 0.
- **Dart:** `dart analyze --fatal-infos`, `dart format` at language version 3.6, and `dart test` in `trust-tasks-dart-proof` (65 pass, on ssi 4.3.0 and ssi 3.9.6) and `trust-tasks-dart-didcomm` (29 pass). All exit 0.

## Checklist (dev guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a, no clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): n/a, no state
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire type changes; behaviour changes listed above (R3.6); the classic-suite bound is the same in all four runtimes as in #1166
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): out-of-bounds values fail closed; an unknown cryptosuite gets the tightest bound
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): each failure's detail names the field and the bound
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(vta)!: serve vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 — DID classes, did:webs service DIDs, templates
body:
Pin vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 beside 0.1 (0.1 is now marked superseded
upstream and stays served) and serve it.

- Every 0.2 create states a DID class (relationship | persona | service,
  VTI-KEY-190 – 193), which WebsDidRecord now keeps (`didClass`, serde
  default; a 0.1 create records none and none is inferred). Setup records
  this VTA's own did:webs identity as `service`.
- A level-1 did:webs service DID is enabled separately from creation by
  the new `[dids] webs_service_dids` (default false,
  VTA_DIDS_WEBS_SERVICE_DIDS), the name the specification's example uses;
  off refuses `service` with serviceDidNotPermitted (CONVENTIONS 0.2 §1.1).
- didClassConflict (§1.2): a persona/relationship DID made primary of a
  context whose primary is a service DID (this VTA's own DID, or a service
  did:webs it created) — details.requiredClass "service"; a service DID
  replacing a persona did:webs primary. The MAY rule is implemented too:
  a template whose kind names only a node (mediator, dtg-witness,
  push-gateway, trust-registry, vtc-host, room-host, ballot-box,
  did-host-*) under a class other than service.
- DID templates (§9): template/templateContext/templateVars resolve
  context → global → built-in (the webvh resolver), variables are checked
  (templateVarsInvalid with missing/unknown), and the document is checked
  against §9.2 by a new pure checker in vta-sdk
  (`did_templates::webs::{check_key_shape, map_webs_document}`, returning
  the first failing reason and the JSON Pointers it refused, or the
  designations). The template is rendered and checked once with
  placeholder keys before any key is derived, then again with the real
  DID and keys after the inception: create_did_webs now computes the
  inception (and so the AID and DID) before writing the designations, and
  still publishes before recording anything (R2.1).
- `resolvedMethods`, carried by VTI's node built-ins, is refused as
  documentMember as §9.2 is written (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1164);
  the fix, should the specification honour it, is one line in
  DOCUMENT_MEMBERS, and a test pins today's behaviour. `ai-agent` and
  `room` are representable today.
- SDK: TASK_VTA_WEBS_DIDS_CREATE_0_2, retry-safety Keyed,
  VtaClient::create_did_webs_classed, fixes for the new codes.
  pnm webs create gains --class (sends 0.2; without it, 0.1), --template,
  --template-context and --var.

Specification choices (conservative readings):
1. 0.2 with didClass service and setPrimary on the context holding this
   VTA's own DID: 0.2 declares no code for "a create cannot re-identify
   this node", and its serviceDidNotPermitted now means only the switch,
   so it is the framework's permissionDenied. 0.1 still answers
   serviceDidNotPermitted.
2. A templateContext the caller may not act in is permissionDenied
   (CONVENTIONS §8), not a silent fall-through to the global scope.
3. An unresolved placeholder is reported in templateVarsInvalid's
   details.missing (the details schema has only missing and unknown).
4. #1164: the specification's own dtg-witness example is refused under
   §9.2 as written.
5. Setup's own key-role identity is recorded as class service; the service
   switch gates level-1 service DIDs only (key roles are not this family).
6. A context provisioned for a VTC, VTN or host service carries no marker,
   so §1.2 item 1's second case is not refused (gap documented in
   docs/02-vta/did-webs.md).

The designated aliases of a did:webs also carry its did:web twin and
did:keri form (affinidi-did-webs designates them, as for 0.1), beyond the
specification's example responses.

Also fixes two clippy findings on this stack (Option::replace in role-key
rotation, an item after a test module in webs_store).

Refs: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1164
Refs: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#120
Refs: VTI-KEY-190, VTI-KEY-191, VTI-KEY-192, VTI-KEY-193
(cherry picked from commit eb68452f046cded02a02158fa1b54362fb287f98)



Note: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1170 (open) resolves #1164; once it merges, the §9.2 checker stops refusing a template's `resolvedMethods` (one line, `DOCUMENT_MEMBERS`) and VTI's own node templates become usable here.

title: feat(vtc)!: a VTC finds its own keys by role, and derives from a stable root
body:
Prepares vtc-service for a VTC whose own DID is a key-role did:webs
(VTI-KEY-001; S7 of docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md) without
changing anything for today's did:webvh VTCs.

Keys by role. `VtcKeyBundle` gains `authentication_key` (the operational
key of a key-role identity, VTI-KEY-072) and `key_role_ids`, which names
each key by the id its document gives it, as `NodeKeyIds::from_document`
reads a key-role document. `LocalSigner::for_own_keys` signs credentials
and attested responses as the attestation method, and Trust Task
requests/responses and sign-in proofs (`proofPurpose: authentication`)
with the operational key. DIDComm, mediator login and `vtc status` hold
the operational key under the authentication id; `messaging::vtc_key_ids`
uses a key-role bundle's local ids instead of resolving.

Stable derived keys. The storage key, install-token signer, initial audit
key, hidden-vetting and voting keys, tag mask and storage-credential
fingerprint all derived from the current Ed25519 signing seed, so a
signing-key rotation would make the at-rest store unreadable. They now
derive from `VtcKeyBundle::derivation_root`: the stored
`derivation_root_multibase`, or (absent, as for every VTC to date) the
Ed25519 seed, so existing values are byte-identical (golden test).
`carry_derivation_root_to` writes the root into a successor bundle and
refuses one carrying another root.

No local log for a did:webs: `/.well-known/did.jsonl` answers 404, the
DID self-check and did-log register name the VTA that publishes it, and
the setup wizard says it mints did:webvh only (did:webs not yet here).

Breaking: new public fields on `VtcKeyBundle` and a new parameter on
`SealedCredentials::new`. A bundle written with the new fields cannot be
read by an older binary (`deny_unknown_fields`).

title: fix(proof, ts-proof, dart-proof, dart-didcomm, ceremony): bound multibase decoding of unauthenticated values (#1167)
body:
fix(proof, ts-proof, dart-proof, dart-didcomm, ceremony): bound multibase decoding of unauthenticated values (#1167)

* fix(proof, ts-proof, dart-proof): bound base58 decoding of proofValue and did:key

The Rust, TypeScript and Dart proof verifiers decode a proof's proofValue
and its did:key multikey with base58btc decoders whose cost grows with
the square of the input length, and they do so before any signature is
checked. A 1 MiB value took about 50 s per field in trust-tasks-proof
(release build), and would take minutes in the Dart package and in the
TypeScript package on @scure/base 2.0-2.3 (2.4 refuses over 4096
characters itself).

Each verifier now refuses a base58btc value longer than 175 characters
before decoding it, or one that decodes to more than 128 bytes - the
bounds the Go module adopts in #1166. The largest value any of them reads
is a 96-byte P-384 signature; a did:key multikey is at most 51 bytes;
175 = ceil(128 * log 256 / log 58).

Nothing that could verify before is refused: a value over the bounds
always decoded to more bytes than any supported key or signature.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(proof, dart-didcomm, ceremony, ts-proof): per-cryptosuite proof bounds, sender kid and salt caps

trust-tasks-proof: the bound now applies to the whole encoded value, not
only to base58btc. affinidi-data-integrity decodes proofValue and a did:key
id with multibase::decode, which also accepts base58flickr, base36 and
base10, whose decoders cost the square of the input length as well. A
proofValue or did:key multikey in a base its cryptosuite does not use is
refused (base58btc everywhere, base64url for bbs-2023's proofValue), and the
length is checked before anything is decoded.

The bound is per cryptosuite: 128 bytes for the Ed25519 and NIST suites, as
before and as the Go, TypeScript and Dart verifiers apply; for the
post-quantum suites, available when affinidi-data-integrity's ml-dsa or
slh-dsa feature is on, the largest signature (ML-DSA-87 4627 bytes,
SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s 7856 bytes) and the largest public key (ML-DSA-87, 2594
bytes with its multicodec header), so an ML-DSA proof that verifies keeps
verifying. A new `ml-dsa` feature switches the upstream one on for this
crate's tests.

The check is public, as `affinidi::check_proof_bounds`, and `verify_raw`
calls it. A caller verifying through `PurposeBound` and
`DataIntegrityProof::verify` directly should call it first; the
`PurposeBound` docs say so.

trust-tasks-dart-didcomm: `unpackTrustTask` refuses an authcrypt envelope
whose protected `skid` is over 4096 characters, or names a did:key multikey
over 175 characters, before package:didcomm resolves it. didcomm resolves
the sender before decrypting, and a long P-256 did:key took 1.5 s at 32 KiB.

trust-tasks-ceremony: a receipt salt over 1024 characters is refused before
it is multibase-decoded.

trust-tasks-ts-proof: require @scure/base ^2.4.0, whose base58 decoder
refuses over 4096 characters itself.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(proof): lock the ML-DSA crates the opt-in ml-dsa feature resolves

The new trust-tasks-proof ml-dsa feature switches on affinidi-crypto's
ml-dsa support, which resolves ml-dsa, module-lattice, keccak, shake and
sponge-cursor. They are built only when that feature is on; default builds
are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

requests/responses and sign-in proofs (`proofPurpose: authentication`)
with the operational key. DIDComm, mediator login and `vtc status` hold
the operational key under the authentication id; `messaging::vtc_key_ids`
uses a key-role bundle's local ids instead of resolving.

Stable derived keys. The storage key, install-token signer, initial audit
key, hidden-vetting and voting keys, tag mask and storage-credential
fingerprint all derived from the current Ed25519 signing seed, so a
signing-key rotation would make the at-rest store unreadable. They now
derive from `VtcKeyBundle::derivation_root`: the stored
`derivation_root_multibase`, or (absent, as for every VTC to date) the
Ed25519 seed, so existing values are byte-identical (golden test).
`carry_derivation_root_to` writes the root into a successor bundle and
refuses one carrying another root.

No local log for a did:webs: `/.well-known/did.jsonl` answers 404, the
DID self-check and did-log register name the VTA that publishes it, and
the setup wizard says it mints did:webvh only (did:webs not yet here).

Breaking: new public fields on `VtcKeyBundle` and a new parameter on
`SealedCredentials::new`. A bundle written with the new fields cannot be
read by an older binary (`deny_unknown_fields`).

title: ci: pin actions to commit SHAs and publish only from main
body:
Two changes to the release workflows.

**Actions pinned to commit SHAs.** All 129 `uses:` references now name a full commit SHA, with the release it corresponds to in a trailing comment (`# v6.1.0`). The `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` steps now pass `toolchain: stable` explicitly, since that action took the toolchain from its ref. Tool installs in the release jobs are versioned too: `npm@12.2.2` (was `@latest`), `git-cliff@2.14.2` and `cargo-semver-checks@0.51.0` (were unversioned). A new `.github/dependabot.yml` updates the `github-actions` pins weekly, grouped into one PR.

**Named runner image.** Every job now runs on `ubuntu-24.04` instead of `ubuntu-latest`. `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04, whose package mirrors aren't answering from the runners, so every job that installs a system package (`libdbus-1-dev`) fails — open PRs #1162 and #1163 are failing on exactly that step. A named image also keeps the build environment from changing underneath pinned actions.

**Publishing only from `main`.**
- In `publish.yml`, `release-plz-release`, `publish-npm`, `publish-go`, `tag-dart` and `release-pr` run only when `github.ref` is `refs/heads/main`. A `workflow_dispatch` on any other branch now skips every job instead of publishing that branch's versions.
- `publish-dart.yml` checks that the pushed tag's commit is on `main` (GitHub compare API: `identical` or `behind`) before publishing.

Checked with `actionlint` (clean) and a YAML parse that every `rust-toolchain` step has a `toolchain` input.

Not in this PR (repository settings): moving the AWS and `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` secrets into GitHub environments restricted to `main`, naming those environments in the crates.io / npm / pub.dev trusted-publisher configs, and a tag ruleset for `trust-tasks-*` tags.

title: fix(status-list): bound every size read from a fetched Bitstring Status List
body:
A fetched `BitstringStatusListCredential` is someone else's document, and the VTC sized its decode from it. It read `credentialSubject.statusSize` as the list length, with no upper bound, and passed it to the `affinidi-status-list` decoder, which allocates in proportion to that size.

In W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0, `statusSize` is the number of bits per entry and belongs on the `BitstringStatusListEntry` (§2.1). It is not a list length. So a list carrying the conformant `"statusSize": 1` was also read as a one-entry list and refused for any index above 0.

## vtc-service (`recognition::verify`: recognise, join presentation, invitation checks)

- The bit is now read by `read_status_bit`, which bounds everything before decoding:
  - the index: the largest accepted is 4,194,303 (an index of 4,194,304 or more is refused), also checked before the fetch
  - the `encodedList` length
  - the decoded length: the larger of `index + 1` and the spec minimum of 131,072 entries

  Nothing the list declares about itself sizes a buffer.
- A list shorter than 131,072 entries, or too short to hold the index, is refused. This follows §3.2 steps 9 (STATUS_LIST_LENGTH_ERROR) and 10 (RANGE_ERROR).
- `statusSize` on an entry, or on a list, must be 1. Only 1-bit entries are read, which §1.3 allows ("Conforming processors MAY choose to only support bitstring entry sizes of 1"). Any other value is refused rather than read as one bit.
- A multibase `u`-prefixed `encodedList` (§2.2) is now read.

## The same reads in other crates

- **vta-sdk** `vetting::status`: this path was already bounded (it decodes only as far as the index). `MAX_STATUS_LIST_BITS` drops from `1 << 26` to `1 << 22`, because the decoder allocates about one byte per entry read. An entry whose `statusSize` is not 1 now reads as `Unknown`.
- **vta-vault** `status`: the resolver-supplied list size is now checked to be within `1..=1 << 22` before decoding, and so is the `encodedList` length. The index is checked against the size first, and an entry whose `statusSize` is not 1 is refused. The HTTP resolver already used a fixed 131,072 size, so this is a guard on the `StatusListResolver` trait boundary.
- **vti-vtn**:
  - `VtnClient::get_url` (the status-list fetch) reads the body under a 2 MiB cap (`MAX_FETCHED_BODY`). It used to buffer the whole body through `res.json()`.
  - `StatusChecker` refuses an index past the end of the list. Such an index used to read as a clear bit, so the credential came back `Valid`.
  - `StatusChecker` also refuses an entry whose `statusSize` is not 1.
  - `Bitstring::decode` refuses a list shorter than 131,072 entries (§3.2 step 9), matching vtc-service.
  - New: `Bitstring::len_bits`.

Unchanged: fetch timeouts and body caps for vtc-service, vta-vault and vta-sdk callers already came from the shared `vta_sdk::http::foreign_fetch_client` (10 s) and `read_body_capped` (2 MiB).

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- An entry declaring a `statusSize` other than 1 is refused everywhere: `StatusListFailed` / `Malformed` in vtc-service (`Unknown` on the join path), `Unknown` in vta-sdk, `Validation` in vta-vault, an error in vti-vtn. Before, such entries were read as a single bit at the index, which gave the wrong position.
- vtc-service:
  - A list carrying `statusSize: 1` is now read in full; any other value is refused.
  - A list longer than 131,072 entries is read past that point. It used to be read only up to entry 131,072.
  - `u`-prefixed lists now decode.
- The largest accepted index is now 4,194,303 in vtc-service and vta-sdk: an index of 4,194,304 or more is refused (vta-sdk's limit was 67,108,864).
- vti-vtn `StatusChecker::check` returns an error, not `Valid`, for an index past the end of the list. `get_url` errors on a body over 2 MiB. `Bitstring::decode`, and so `StatusChecker`, refuses a list shorter than 131,072 entries.

Wire shapes are unchanged. These are consumer-side read rules only, so there are no JS consumers to update.

## Tests

New regression tests in each crate:
- `recognition::verify::status_bit_bounds_tests`
- `join_requests::present` (multi-bit entry)
- `vta-sdk vetting::status` (statusSize cases)
- `vta-vault status` (size, encodedList and statusSize bounds)
- `vti-vtn` (body cap against a local server, bounded decode, minimum list length, statusSize, and `StatusChecker::check` erroring on an index at or past the end of a signed, locally served minimum-size list)

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). No new clients. vti-vtn's existing client has a 20 s timeout and now also a body cap.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). Unchanged; `StatusChecker` takes its cache lock only around the map.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a: no new state. vta-vault still writes only after a definitive read.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change; behaviour changes are listed above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). An absent `statusSize` means 1, as the spec requires. Every new refusal fails closed (not `Valid`).
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). vti-vtn no longer reports `Valid` for an index it could not read.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). No mutations touched.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vta/webs/_shared): a template's resolvedMethods is ignored, not refused (0.2 §9.2)
body:
Closes #1164.

**Change.** `vta/webs/_shared/0.2` CONVENTIONS §9.2 gains a row: a template's `resolvedMethods` member is **ignored, not refused** as `documentMember`. This is how `@context` is already treated.

**Why.**
- VTI-KEY-008 (dtgwg-vti-spec#121) puts `resolvedMethods` in every VTI node's own DID document, and VTI's built-in node templates carry it (`vtc-host`, `room-host`, `dtg-witness`, `ballot-box`, and `did-host-*` via `RESOLVED_METHODS`).
- As written, §9.2 refused all of them, including this family's own `dtg-witness` example in create/0.2.
- A did:webs document cannot render the member anyway: a did:webs node declares `did:webs` by using it (the open issue under VTI-KEY-009). So the refusal protected nothing.

**Also.** A note that a post-quantum second signing key has no did:webs representation. `vtc-host`'s ML-DSA-44 `pq-signing` slot is refused as `keyAlgorithm` / `verificationMethod` at level 1, and the key-role designation registers no PQ attestation key. An identity that needs one stays did:webvh for now.

Prose only: no schema, binding or error-code change. `npm run build` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and generate no further diff.

title: fix(room-host)!: the operator names who may register rooms, and rooms and storage are bounded
body:
`rooms/create` is the one room task no room-issued credential can authorize. `vti_rooms::authz::authorize_create` checks only that the signer is the owner it names, and its own doc comment says bounding registration "is quota and access control … and belongs to whoever hosts". room-host supplied no such bound:

- Any signer, including a freshly minted `did:key`, could register any number of rooms.
- `--storage-capacity-bytes` was unset by default, so up to 5 GiB of files per room (the default per-room cap) had no host-wide ceiling.

The VTC is not affected: its creation path is `govern_creation`.

## Release notes: operator-visible changes

1. **A `room-host` started without `--room-creator <DID>` or `--any-room-creator` refuses every `rooms/create` (`permissionDenied`).** Rooms it already holds, and mirrors, are served as before. Add `--room-creator` for each owner that registers rooms on the host. That is the DID that signs `rooms/create`; through a VTA's `rooms/owner/register`, it is the caller's DID or the `ownerDid` it names.
2. **`--storage-capacity-bytes` now defaults to `50GiB` of room files** across every room, deleted files awaiting collection included. A host past that refuses new uploads until it is raised. `unlimited` restores the old behaviour.

Also: `--max-rooms` (default 10 000) and `--max-rooms-per-owner` (default 100). For embedders, `room_host::open_state` is closed by default too (see below).

## Changes

### `room-host/src/creation.rs`
- `RoomCreation { creators, max_rooms_per_owner, max_rooms }`, where `creators` is `Creators::None`, `Only(set)` or `Any`.
- `RoomCreation::default()` is **`None`**, so the library is closed by default (R5.1). Opt in with `RoomCreation::any_creator()` or `RoomCreation::only(dids)`.
- DIDs are compared without a `#fragment` or `?query`, both when named and when checked.
- `max_rooms_per_owner` is documented as a **courtesy limit**. It counts rooms by their current owner, so more DIDs or an ownership transfer step around it. The bounds are who may register and `max_rooms`.

### `room-host/src/lib.rs`
- `HostState::set_room_creation` sets the policy. The `create` handler, after the existing `authorize_create`, checks in this order:
  1. the presenter is a creator (`permissionDenied` if not);
  2. the room is not already registered. If it is, the answer is "already registered", ahead of the ceilings;
  3. the ceilings (`taskFailed`, `details: { "limit": "roomsPerOwner" | "rooms", "max": N }`).
- **Room counts are kept**, not recounted by a scan on each create:
  - built on first use and advanced by each registration;
  - dropped after an ownership transfer or claim;
  - recounted when older than five minutes, to catch mirrors, embedder writes and removals.
  - The check, the write and the count update happen under one mutex, so concurrent creates cannot overshoot.
- Opted in to `any_creator()`: the room-host tests, the `data_room` example, `vta-service`'s `room_profile_tests`, and `tests/e2e/tests/room_key_watch.rs`.

### `room-host/src/main.rs`
- `--room-creator <DID>` (repeatable; fragment ignored), and `--any-room-creator` (exclusive with it).
- `--max-rooms-per-owner` (100, documented as a courtesy limit) and `--max-rooms` (10 000, mirrors included).
- `--storage-capacity-bytes` defaults to `50GiB` of room files; `unlimited` lifts it.
- Startup logs the policy in force.

Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` §8.1.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- Binary: the two release-note items above, plus the room ceilings.
- Library (`open_state`): an embedder that registers rooms over `rooms/create` must now call `set_room_creation`. This is breaking for room-host (`publish = false`); in-repo users are updated.
- Consumers: `pnm-browser-plugin` reaches hosts through the VTA's `rooms/owner/register` and does not send `rooms/create` itself; its wire is unchanged. cierge, vti-didcomm-js, pnm-relay, vti-message-bridge and affinidi-trust-registry-rs do not send `rooms/create`. No script, compose file or Dockerfile here starts the `room-host` binary.

## Not in this PR: needs a product decision

A blob whose last reference is released is credited back to its member and room at once (`vti-rooms` `blobs.rs`, `adjust_refs`), but its bytes stay on storage for the 7-day orphan grace. A writer can upload to quota, release, and repeat. The storage ceiling now bounds that host-wide; nothing bounds it per member.

Recommendation: keep crediting the member at once, but count orphaned-and-uncollected bytes against the **room** scope until collection. This changes what `vtc/rooms/limits` and usage report on both hosts (vti-rooms is shared with the VTC), so it is left for a decision.

## Tests

- `creation::tests`: closed default; named creator, with a fragment; owner and host ceilings.
- `lib.rs` (through the router):
  - `a_host_registers_no_room_until_told_who_may`
  - `a_host_that_names_no_creator_registers_no_room`
  - `only_a_named_creator_registers_rooms`
  - `an_owner_holds_at_most_its_ceiling_of_rooms`
  - `the_host_holds_at_most_its_ceiling_of_rooms`
  - `a_repeat_registration_is_already_registered_even_at_the_ceiling`
  - `concurrent_registrations_never_overshoot_the_ceiling` (two creates race for the last slot; exactly one wins and one room is stored)
- `main.rs`: flag parsing (closed default, named creators with a fragment, the exclusive flags, the 50 GiB default, `unlimited`, an explicit size).

Local results (rebased on origin/main):
- `cargo clippy -p room-host --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0, also 0 with `--features didcomm`
- `cargo test -p room-host --no-fail-fast`: 100 + 3 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p room-host --features didcomm --no-fail-fast`: 113 + 5 + 3 passed, exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service -p vti-e2e-tests --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- room`: 311 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vti-e2e-tests --test room_key_watch`: 11 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The registration mutex guards local store reads and writes only.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. Refusals use existing framework codes.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Closed by default in both the binary and the library. Storage has a finite default. Unbounded needs the explicit `--any-room-creator` / `unlimited`.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Startup logs the registration policy.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). One room insert after the check. The kept counts are in memory and rebuilt on restart.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.
