title: fix(room-host)!: the operator names who may register rooms, and rooms and storage are bounded (#2683)
body:
fix(room-host)!: the operator names who may register rooms, and rooms and storage are bounded (#2683)

* fix(room-host)!: the operator names who may register rooms, and rooms and storage are bounded

`rooms/create` is the one task no room-issued credential can authorize, so
`vti_rooms::authz::authorize_create` checks only that the signer is the owner
it names, and leaves bounding registration to whoever hosts. room-host had no
such bound: any signer, including a freshly minted `did:key`, could register
any number of rooms, and the host's storage ceiling was unset by default.

- New `room_host::creation::RoomCreation`: who may register (`Creators::None`,
  `Only(dids)` or `Any`), and how many rooms one owner and the host may hold.
  Set with `HostState::set_room_creation`. The count and the write happen
  under one lock, so concurrent creates cannot overshoot.
- The binary: `--room-creator <DID>` (repeatable) names the parties it
  registers rooms for. With none named, and without `--any-room-creator`, it
  registers no new rooms; existing and mirrored rooms are served as before.
  `--max-rooms-per-owner` (default 100) and `--max-rooms` (default 10000)
  bound the count. A refusal is `permissionDenied` for a creator not named,
  and `taskFailed` with `details.limit` (`roomsPerOwner` / `rooms`) at a
  ceiling.
- `--storage-capacity-bytes` defaults to `50GiB` across every room, deleted
  files awaiting collection included; `unlimited` keeps the old behaviour.
- The library default (`open_state`) admits any signer within the default
  ceilings, so embedders and tests keep working; the binary is closed by
  default.

BREAKING CHANGE: a `room-host` started without `--room-creator` or
`--any-room-creator` refuses `rooms/create`, and one without
`--storage-capacity-bytes` stops accepting uploads past 50 GiB stored.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(room-host): close the library default, keep room counts, answer repeats first

- `room_host::open_state` now registers nothing until told otherwise
  (`RoomCreation::default()` is `Creators::None`). Embedders opt in with
  `HostState::set_room_creation(RoomCreation::any_creator())` or
  `RoomCreation::only(dids)`. The room-host tests, the `data_room` example,
  vta-service's room profile tests and the e2e room watch test do so.
- Room counts are kept, not recounted by a full scan on every create. They are
  built on first use, advanced by each registration, dropped on an ownership
  transfer or claim, and recounted when older than five minutes (to catch
  mirrors, embedder writes and removals). They are checked and advanced under
  the same lock as the write.
- A repeat of a registration that already happened is answered as already
  registered, before the ceilings are checked.
- `--room-creator` values and `RoomCreation::only` drop a `#fragment` or
  `?query`, so they compare as the signer is compared.
- Docs: `max_rooms_per_owner` is a courtesy limit (it counts by current owner);
  `--storage-capacity-bytes` is described as room files.

title: fix(vta-service): vault proxy-login posts only to a vetted login URL, through the guarded client
body:
The `vault/proxy-login` password driver POSTs an entry's username and password to the entry's `loginConfig.loginUrl`. Two things were off:

- Whether a plain `http://` URL was loopback was a string test, `host.starts_with("127.")` (plus `localhost`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`). A DNS name such as `127.example.net` passed it, so the password could go out in clear text to a remote host. The type's own doc says `https://` is required for any non-loopback host.
- The POST used a bare `reqwest` client: timeout and no redirects, but no address checks and no `no_proxy`. An `https://` login URL could name any private-network or loopback service.

## What changes (vta-service `operations::vault::password_post`)

- `validate_login_url` now parses the host. `http://` passes only for an exact loopback host, using the shared `vta_sdk::protocol::matching::is_https_or_loopback` (which already refuses `http://127.0.0.1.evil.com`). `0.0.0.0` is not loopback.
- `https://` URLs are checked with `vta_sdk::http::guard_foreign_url` under `EndpointPolicy::process_default()`. The POST goes through `foreign_fetch_client_for` with the same policy: no proxy, no redirects, a resolver that refuses non-public DNS answers. The 15 s request timeout stays; the connect timeout is the foreign-fetch one (10 s).
- Loopback and private-network targets, over either scheme, need `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`. Link-local and cloud-metadata targets are never accepted. A URL with userinfo is refused, and the userinfo is not echoed.
- New `validate_login_url_for` / `run_password_post_with_policy` take an explicit policy, which is how the tests reach a loopback mock server without touching process state.

## vault/upsert (`trust_tasks::vault`)

A newly sealed `password` secret with a `loginConfig` has its `loginUrl` checked the same way. A bad one is refused under the existing code `vault/upsert:sealedSecretInvalid`, with `details.reason = "login_url_invalid"`. A metadata-only update (no `sealedSecret`) keeps the stored secret and is not re-checked; the driver checks again at use.

`loginConfig` lives inside the sealed secret, so changing it means re-sealing the whole secret, password included. A writer cannot point an existing entry's password at a new URL without also supplying that password.

## Release notes

- **Already-stored entries are checked at use, not migrated.** An entry whose `loginConfig.loginUrl` is `http://0.0.0.0`, a loopback host while `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` is unset, or `https://` to a private-network host now fails its next `vault/proxy-login` with `invalid_login_url`. Fix it by re-sealing the entry with a public `https://` login URL, or by setting the opt-in where a local target is intended. The rule is also in the `password_post` module docs.
- **Local development against a loopback login page needs `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1` on the VTA.** That includes `pnm-browser-plugin`'s `demo-rp` (`http://127.0.0.1:4040/api/login`), which is being handled in that repo separately.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- proxy-login and upsert refuse loopback and private-network login URLs unless the VTA runs with `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`. Before, `http://` to `127.*`/`localhost`/`::1`/`0.0.0.0` and `https://` to any address were accepted.
- `http://0.0.0.0/...` and look-alike names such as `http://127.example.net/...` are refused under any policy.
- A public login hostname whose DNS answer is non-public now fails as `targetUnreachable`.
- Consumers checked: `pnm-browser-plugin` builds `loginConfig` in `packages/core/src/vault/upsert.ts`; its `demo-rp` uses `http://127.0.0.1:4040/api/login`. That still works, as long as the VTA it talks to sets `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`, which local development already uses for loopback DIDs. No error code changes. cierge, vti-didcomm-js, pnm-relay, vti-message-bridge and affinidi-trust-registry-rs do not reference `loginUrl`.

## Tests

- `password_post` unit tests:
  - exact loopback only under the opt-in
  - look-alike names refused under both policies
  - private `https://` needs the opt-in
  - metadata and link-local never accepted
  - userinfo not echoed
  - a loopback mock server is never contacted under the default policy (`expect(0)`)
- The wiremock round-trip tests run under an explicit private policy.
- `tests/it/vault_release_didcomm.rs` sets the process opt-in, because its stand-in login server listens on loopback.

Local results (rebased on origin/main; after the docs commit, clippy was re-run (exit 0) along with `--lib password_post`, 24 passed, exit 0):
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib vault`: 86 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test it vault`: 63 passed, exit 0
- `cargo test -p vta-service --features transport-harness --test it vault_release`: 1 passed, exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). A per-call `reqwest::Client::builder()` was removed. The shared foreign-fetch client is used, with a 15 s per-request timeout and a 10 s connect timeout.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a: the upsert check runs before anything is written.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire type changes. The new upsert refusal uses an existing code. Consumers are listed above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). With the opt-in unset, only public `https://` targets are accepted.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vta): build the vta binary without the webs feature
body:
#2679's `vta setup` validation calls `operations::did_webs::check_path`, which only exists with the `webs` feature. The non-TEE Docker image builds with `--no-default-features` and does not include `webs` in its features, so the image failed to build (the `Docker image (non-TEE)` check on #2686).

Without `webs`, setup already refuses `vta_did` kind `create_webs` outright, so the path check is now gated together with the module it calls.

title: feat(vta)!: a did:webs VTA provisions integrations from its key event log, and rotates its role keys
body:
feat(vta): rotate a key-role did:webs's role keys

S6 slice 5, operation layer (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md
§4): planned rotation of a node identity's attestation, operational or
messaging key, by a new key-role designation anchored in its key event
log (Change::KeyRoles). Roles not named keep their key; the log's own
keys are rotate_did_webs_keys'.

A replaced attestation or operational key is retired (record revoked); a
replaced messaging key stays held to decrypt what was sent to it. New
keys are minted on fresh paths (VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-184). Published
before it is recorded (R2.1).

When the DID is this VTA's own identity the result says so
(own_identity): its keys' ids change with a role rotation, and only a
restart loads them into every component that holds them — the caller
restarts the VTA. A key-event-log rotation changes no role key, so it
needs none.

The wire (vta/webs/dids/rotate-keys with roles) needs a specification
version first.

Not breaking: new public items only.

Refs: VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-072, VTI-KEY-173, VTI-KEY-184
(cherry picked from commit a929311fd723a9cdc962e297c7a2f9440192b328)


---

fix(vta)!: a did:webs VTA provisions integrations from its own key event log

A did:webs VTA could provision nothing: provision-integration read the
VTA's keys from its did:webvh log only, so it fell back to the webvh
convention (#key-0, #sealed-transfer-0) for key records a did:webs VTA
does not have, and built the trust bundle by resolving the VTA's DID over
the network, which before its first-boot publication does not resolve.

ProvisionIntegrationDeps (and the DIDComm router's VtaState) carry the
webs keyspace: the VTA's keys are found by role in its key event log's
document, and its trust bundle carries that document, derived locally as
its host serves it.

Breaking (vta-service): ProvisionIntegrationDeps and VtaState gain
webs_ks.

Refs: VTI-KEY-150
(cherry picked from commit bfcc284f56524657c32e3b30a8ab07b9604c1b8b)

title: feat(core)!: mark OpenVTCError #[non_exhaustive]
body:
## Why

`OpenVTCError` is exhaustive, so adding a variant is a breaking change (`cargo-semver-checks` `enum_variant_added`) and fails the patch-line semver check on `release/*` PRs. #590 added `UnlockCodeRejected` and could not be backported as it stood; #592 had to carry it as `OpenVTCError::Decrypt` with a reason string instead.

`#[non_exhaustive]` is itself a breaking change, so it has to land on `main` before 0.8 is cut. From then on, a new error variant can be backported unchanged.

## Change

- `#[non_exhaustive]` on `OpenVTCError`, with a doc comment saying why.
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased] / Changed`: breaking for code that uses `openvtc-core` as a library; a `match` on it outside the crate needs a wildcard arm.

No code in this workspace needed changing: every match on `OpenVTCError` outside `openvtc-core` already has a wildcard arm. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo test --workspace` are clean.

Not for backport: it is breaking, and the patch line doesn't need it.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: feat(vta)!: manage the runtime services of a did:webs VTA
body:
A VTA whose own DID is a did:webs (VTI-KEY-001, alpha) can now enable,
update, disable and roll back its TSP, DIDComm, REST and WebAuthn services
and list them, as a did:webvh VTA does (did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4, S6).

- `preconditions::load_vta_doc_state` switches on the DID's method.
  `VtaDocState` now holds `vta_did`, `current_doc` and a
  `VtaDocBacking { Webvh { scid, did_log, record }, Webs { record } }`. For
  a did:webs, the document is derived from the stored key event stream. An
  identity that first boot has not published yet is refused
  (`VtaDidNotPublished`, which each op reports as its `VtaDidLogMissing`).
- `service_lifecycle::publish_patch` is now the only publish step, used by
  every family including DIDComm. For a did:webs it designates the patched
  `service[]` as the whole designated service set (`update_did_webs`)
  through the host named by the record's `server_id`. It leaves services
  that KERI endpoint data supplies to KERI, then reseeds this VTA's
  resolver entry for itself. The version is the log's `<sn>:<said>`. When
  the designated set is already the patched one (`noChange`), nothing is
  published and the version in force is returned.
- The patchers find DIDComm as `#vta-didcomm`, but a did:webs designates
  `#didcomm`. Load gives the patchers `#didcomm` as `#vta-didcomm`, and
  publish designates it as `#didcomm` again.
- Order (TSP > DIDComm > REST): the resolver renders designations in the
  order they are listed. A create and an update now sort designated
  services by type, which fixes setup designating `#didcomm` before
  `#tsp`.
- WebAuthn is designated as an ordinary service. Passkey VMs are only
  ever added to did:webvh DIDs the VTA manages, never to its own document.
- `list_services` reports a did:webs VTA's services from its document.

BREAKING CHANGE: `ServiceOpDeps` gains `webs_ks` and `webs_host`;
`VtaDocState` is reshaped around `VtaDocBacking`; `load_vta_doc_state` and
`list_services` take a `webs_ks`; `VtaState` gains `webs_ks`.

title: feat(vta)!: a VTA whose own DID is a key-role did:webs — setup, first-boot self-registration
body:
S6 (design note `docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md` §4): a VTA whose own durable identity is a **did:webs** (alpha; VTI-KEY-001 admits it as an optional method). It builds on #2675, which made the VTA authenticate with its authentication key and resolve itself as a did:webs. Two commits:

**1. Create a key-role did:webs (decision 2)**
- `CreateDidWebsParams::key_roles` mints a key-role identity (VTI-KEY-070, VTI-KEY-173):
  - distinct attestation and operational Ed25519 keys and a messaging X25519 key, each on its own path;
  - designated through the did:webs key-role extension;
  - the key event log's own key in no relationship (VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-184).
- Each role key's record is named by the id its document gives it, so the VTA finds it by role.
- `delete` refuses this VTA's own DID.

**2. Setup and first boot (decision 3)**
- `vta setup` has a new VTA DID kind, `create_webs`, in TOML and in the wizard. It needs `[dids] webs_enabled`. It runs offline:
  - registers the hosting server;
  - mints the key-role identity as the `vta` context's primary DID and `vta_did`;
  - records it unpublished.
- At first boot, before messaging starts, `publish_own_webs_identity` registers the DID at its host on its own authority.
  - This is a self-certifying `did/register/0.1`, signed by the operational key the key event log establishes.
  - affinidi-webvh-service accepts it from a did:webs outside its ACL, on a domain whose operator allows it (`[[hosting.webs_self_register]]`, affinidi-webvh-service#411).
  - A failure is logged with what the host must allow; the next boot retries.
- The `did-host-*` templates take `RESOLVED_METHODS` (default `[]`, with the term in `@context`). A host built with `method-webs` sets it to `["webs"]`, which a did:webs VTA needs before it can register there (VTI-KEY-008).
- `serviceDidNotPermitted` now tells the operator how to make the VTA a did:webs (through setup).

Tests:
- the key-role document and records;
- an offline mint followed by a first-boot publish, done once;
- setup from TOML end to end;
- refusal without `webs_enabled`;
- the host templates' optional declaration.

Follow-ups, already on a stacked branch: runtime services, role-key rotation, provisioning from a did:webs VTA, `vta/webs/dids/create/0.2`.

* feat(vta)!: create a key-role did:webs, and keep this VTA's own DID from being deleted

S6 slice 2 (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4, decision 2):
a node's durable identity is a key-role identity (VTI-KEY-070,
VTI-KEY-173), so create can mint one.

- CreateDidWebsParams::key_roles: two more Ed25519 keys, each on its own
  path, designated as the attestation and operational role keys, and the
  independently derived X25519 key as the messaging key, through the
  did:webs key-role extension; the key event log's own key is in no
  relationship (VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-184). Each role key's record is
  named by the id its document gives it, so the VTA finds it by role.
- WebsDidRecord and CreateDidWebsResult carry the attestation and
  operational key ids.
- delete refuses this VTA's own DID (permissionDenied): a node's identity
  is retired by re-identifying it.

Off by default: personas and relationship DIDs are minted as before. The
wire does not expose it yet (vta/webs/dids/create/0.2's didClass, S7);
setup will (slice 3).

Breaking (vta-service): new fields on WebsDidRecord (serde-defaulted) and
CreateDidWebsResult.

Refs: VTI-KEY-070, VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-072, VTI-KEY-173
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta)!: set a VTA up as a did:webs, published at first boot by self-registration

S6 slice 3 (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4, decision 3).

- vta setup: vta_did kind create_webs (TOML and the wizard) mints the
  VTA's own did:webs offline: it registers the hosting server, creates a
  key-role identity (attestation, operational and messaging keys) as the
  vta context's primary DID and vta_did, and records it unpublished.
  Needs [dids] webs_enabled (the wizard's choice turns it on).
- First boot: publish_own_webs_identity registers it at its host before
  messaging starts, through operations::did_webs::publish_own_identity —
  a self-certifying did/register/0.1, signed by the operational key the
  key event log establishes, which the host accepts from a did:webs
  outside its ACL on a domain whose operator allows it
  (affinidi-webvh-service [[hosting.webs_self_register]]). A failure is
  logged with what the host must allow; the next boot retries.

  (serde default true); NoHost stands in for the host setup cannot reach.
- The did-host-* templates take RESOLVED_METHODS (default [], the term in
  @context): an operator whose host is built with method-webs sets
  ["webs"], which a did:webs VTA needs before it can register there
  (VTI-KEY-008).

title: fix(messaging): handle peer messages only as the authenticated sender; check received VRCs in full
body:
## Problem

Two gaps in how inbound peer messages are handled.

1. **Sender binding.** `dispatch_inbound` computed the transport-authenticated sender, but `process_inbound` decided who sent a message from `message.from`. When the transport bound no sender (anoncrypt DIDComm, or an authcrypt whose `from` its sealing key does not back), the plaintext `from` was used anyway. Handlers with no proof check therefore acted on it: VRC request (inbox task showing that DID's verified name), VRC request rejection, trust ping (pong sent to it) and pong (removed the task named by `thid`, of any type, including for a pong with no `from` at all), relationship reject and finalize, and notifications (`Received.sender`, which gets the signed receipt).
2. **Received VRCs.** A VRC from an established peer was offered for storage after its proof and issuer checks only. Nothing checked that its subject is us, its validity window, or its `credentialStatus`. The community-issued credential path (`issued_credential.rs`) already does all of these and fails closed. `accept_vrc` also filed it under `vrc.issuer()`, which is the peer's relationship DID. The relationship view and `Relationships::remove` both key on the remote persona DID, so for a relationship that uses a relationship DID the credential was not listed and was left behind on removal.

## Fix

Two commits.

**`fix(messaging)`: handle as the authenticated sender**
- New `openvtc_core::didcomm::bound_sender(claimed, authenticated)`. It returns the sender only when the transport authenticated one and `from` (if present) names the same DID. It compares by DID, so a did:scid `?src=` locator still matches.
- `process_inbound_message` takes `authenticated: Option<&str>` and drops any message that `bound_sender` refuses, before any handler runs. Every caller passes it: the TUI loop, `restore_kept` (the kept sender), headless `join` / `repos` via `apply_inbound`, and the `repos` reply matcher.
- `TrustPingReceived` / `TrustPongReceived` now carry the authenticated sender only. The pong reply goes only to it, and the log no longer credits an anonymous pong to the last DID pinged.
- `TrustPong` removes only a `TaskType::TrustPing` task of ours, to the answering party (or that party's relationship). The no-`from` pong shortcut is removed.

**`fix(vrc)`: check received VRCs**
- `vet_vrc_issued` (local) adds a check that `credentialSubject.id` must be the DID we use in that relationship (`our_did`, the DID the peer's issuing code targets).
- `verify_inbound_vrc` (off-loop job) checks the validity window, then the proof, then `credentialStatus` where present. It reuses `issued_credential::check_validity_window` / `check_status`, which are now `pub(crate)`. A status that cannot be established refuses the credential (fail closed).
- `accept_vrc` re-checks the window, so a credential that expired while waiting in the inbox is not stored. It files the credential under the relationship key (remote persona DID). With no relationship it refuses.
- Migration: at load (after the VTA state sync), `Relationships::rekey_received_vrcs` moves entries filed under a relationship's remote R-DID to its key. `Relationships::remove` also clears that old key.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- A peer message whose `from` its sealing key does not back, or that arrives anoncrypt, is no longer acted on. This includes pings (no pong is sent) and notifications (no receipt is sent). Everything in the stack I checked sends authcrypt with `from` set: VTC, VTA, room host, `host_session`, and this client's own sends. Proof-gated types were already refused unauthenticated by `queue_for_check` in the TUI, so this extends the same rule to the rest, and to the headless commands.
- A pong with no authenticated sender no longer closes a ping task. That task stays in the inbox until dismissed.
- A received VRC that is about someone else, is outside its window, or whose status cannot be established is refused on arrival. The refusal is logged and no inbox task is created.
- Received VRCs move to a new storage key. The VTA sync projection keys records by that map key, so an R-DID relationship's received VRC records are re-keyed on the next sync.
- No wire types changed.

## Testing

New tests:
- `didcomm::bound_sender_tests`: unauthenticated, mismatched and did:scid locator cases; ping/pong events carry only the authenticated sender.
- `message_dispatch::tests::sender_binding`: for VRC request, VRC rejection, pong, relationship reject, finalize, trust-ping task and notification, a message with a claimed `from` and either no authenticated sender or a different one produces no task, no removal, no state change and no hand-over. Each has a positive control. The pong test also covers a thread naming a non-ping task, and a sender we did not ping.
- `messaging::tests`: third-party subject refused; expired and not-yet-valid refused; an unreachable status list refused; a current signed VRC with no status accepted.
- `relationships::tests`: removal clears VRCs under the old key; re-keying moves only R-DID-keyed groups and is idempotent.
- `inbox_actions::r14_tests`: filed under the relationship key; expired-in-inbox not stored; no relationship, not stored.

Not covered: a VRC whose status list is reachable and says revoked. That would need a status-list server in the test. The revoked branch is the shared `check_status` that the community-credential path already uses.

Local, all exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`, `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. The first commit also builds on its own. Not tried against a live stack.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the status check reuses `vetting::status::status_client` with `STATUS_FETCH_TIMEOUT`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): checks run before any state change; the re-key is local and idempotent
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a refused message is logged and dropped; the loop continues
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire types changed; peer senders across the stack checked for authcrypt (R3.6, see above)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no authenticated sender means no action; a status that cannot be established refuses (R7.1, R5.3)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): ping/pong logs name only an authenticated sender; refusals say why
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): the re-key at load runs in memory and is written on the next save; re-running it is a no-op
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(messaging): handle peer messages only as the authenticated sender; check received VRCs in full (#594)
body:
fix(messaging): handle peer messages only as the authenticated sender; check received VRCs in full (#594)

* fix(messaging): handle peer messages only as the authenticated sender

The inbound dispatcher decided who sent a message from its `from` header
when the transport bound no sender to it. Pass the transport-bound sender
into `process_inbound_message` and handle a message only as that sender
(`didcomm::bound_sender`): a message with none, or whose `from` names
another DID, is dropped before any handler runs. This covers VRC
requests and rejections, trust ping and pong, relationship reject and
finalize, and notifications (whose receipt goes to the sender).

Trust ping/pong events now carry only the authenticated sender. A pong
closes only a TrustPing task of ours, on its thread, to the party that
answers; the no-`from` pong shortcut is removed. The headless join and
repos commands pass the authenticated sender through as well.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vrc): check subject, validity window and status of a received VRC

A VRC received from a peer was offered for storage after its proof and
issuer checks only. The arrival checks now also require its subject to
be the DID we use in that relationship and, off the loop, that it is
inside its validity window and, where it names a `credentialStatus`,
not revoked or suspended; a status that cannot be established refuses
it, as for a community-issued credential (`verify_inbound_vrc`).
Accepting it from the inbox re-checks the window.

A received VRC is now filed under the relationship key (remote persona
DID) instead of its issuer's relationship DID, so the relationship view
lists it and removal clears it. Existing entries are moved at load, and
removing a relationship also clears any left under the old key.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(messaging): check the sender before the replay cache; re-key synced VRCs

- Run the sender check before the replay cache, so a message handled as
  nobody does not take up the id of one that is.
- `join --wait` reports a verdict only from its authenticated sender.
- Re-file received VRCs under the relationship key after every sync
  apply, not only at load, so one pulled live from a device on an older
  build is listed and cleared with its relationship.
- Compare the VRC issuer, and relationship lookups by remote DID, with
  `same_reference`, so a did:scid `?src=` locator does not make a party
  someone else.

title: fix(go): bound base58 decoding and refuse a nil sender key in didcomm
body:
## Summary

Two robustness fixes in the Go nested modules. No exported API changes.

### `trust-tasks-go/proof` — bounded base58btc decoding

`base58Decode` did big.Int multiply-add per input character with no length limit, so its cost grew quadratically with the length of a `verificationMethod` multikey or `proofValue` (measured on `main`, one core on an Apple-silicon laptop: 100 000 characters 0.13 s, 400 000 characters 2.1 s, 1 000 000 characters 13.3 s). Both are decoded before any signature check.

- Refuses input longer than 175 characters, or input that decodes to more than 128 bytes, before doing any work that scales with input size. The largest value this package decodes is a 96-byte P-384 signature; a did:key multikey is at most 51 bytes (2-byte header + 49-byte compressed P-384 point). 175 = ceil(128 · log 256 / log 58).
- Decodes into a fixed-size byte accumulator rather than `big.Int`.

### `trust-tasks-go/didcomm` — nil key from `ResolveSender`

`UnpackTrustTask` (and `Receive`, which wraps it) dereferenced the returned `*PeerKey` without a nil check, so a resolver that answers `(nil, nil)` for an unknown DID panicked on an envelope naming that DID. Now a nil `*PeerKey`, or one not built with `NewPeerKey` (no key inside), fails with `FailSenderUnresolved`. The JWE layer also refuses a nil resolved key. The `ResolveSender` doc comment says so.

`PackTrustTask`, and `PackReply` which calls it, also dereferenced their `sender` / `recipient` without a check. `PackReply`'s recipient comes from the same kind of resolver, so a `(nil, nil)` answer reached it too. Both now return an error for a nil value, or one not built with `NewIdentity` / `NewPeerKey`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- proof: multibase values over the new bounds are refused with an error. Nothing that could verify before is refused: an over-long value always decoded to more bytes than any supported key or signature length, so it already failed later (multicodec header or signature length check). No `!`, because no previously accepted input is now refused.
- didcomm: what used to panic now returns `*EnvelopeError{Failure: FailSenderUnresolved}`. `PackTrustTask` / `PackReply` with a nil or empty sender or recipient now return an error instead of panicking.
- Consumers: `base58Decode` is unexported. `ResolveSender` is used only within the Go didcomm module and its README; its signature is unchanged. The TS, Rust and Dart packages are not affected.

## Tests

- `proof/base58_test.go`: round-trip (including leading zeros and max-size values), standard vectors, length/size bounds, invalid characters, and a timing bound: refusing 200 one-MiB values through `fromMultibase` / `publicKeyFromDidKey` must finish in under 1 s.
- `didcomm/resolve_test.go`: a `(nil, nil)` resolver, a zero `PeerKey`, and a nil key at the JWE layer each give `FailSenderUnresolved`. `TestPackWithoutRecipientKeyIsError` and `TestPackWithoutSenderIdentityIsError` cover the pack side. Checked against `main`: the first test panics there.

The new tests are in new files, so they don't touch the test files in other open Go PRs.

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, `go test -race ./...` in `trust-tasks-go/proof` and `trust-tasks-go/didcomm`: all exit 0.

## Checklist (dev guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a, no clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a, no state
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a resolver returning nil now gives an error instead of a panic
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire type changes; behaviour change described above (R3.6)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — a nil key fails closed
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: fix(messaging/mux): revoke-all ends session attaches; accountBlocked covers ACLs below scope
body:
Brings the `messaging/mux` drafts in line with a decision on session attaches and with how mediators treat a member's account standing. No wire change: only prose and one shared-schema description.

**`messaging/mux/revoke-all` 0.1 (draft)**
- Revoke-all now ends the member DID's **session attaches** admitted before it, as well as voiding its grants. It does so on every connection, before answering, with a `detached` event giving reason `epochBumped`. Rule 6 used to say attaches were unaffected. Revoke-all is the hand-over switch, and an attach can last up to its statement's lifetime (24 h at the reference mediator), so leaving attaches alive kept the previous controller's live traffic flowing after the switch.
- Rule 3: the clustered-mediator text now covers attaches. They have no stored state, so other nodes rely on the published detach.
- Rule 5: a principal that carried the DID only through an attach gets the live `detached` event and no `grantsRevoked` notice. The notice goes to principals whose grant was voided.
- Rule 6: attaches ended this way are not counted in `revokedGrants`. Nothing is ended when the epoch did not advance.
- Summary, side-effects rationale and consequences updated to match.

**`messaging/mux/attach` 0.1 (draft)**: the side-effects rationale lists revoke-all and a blocked or removed account among the ways an attach ends.

**`messaging/mux/_shared` 0.1 `DetachReason`**:
- `accountBlocked` also covers a member whose access-control capabilities no longer cover its scope. The member leaves rather than being narrowed.
- `epochBumped` notes that it ends attaches too.

Bindings regenerated (TS, Go, Dart, Rust). Only doc comments change. `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `check-published-schemas` (additive only) and `check-bindings` pass.

The reference mediator implements this in affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#222.

title: fix(go)!: refuse member names that differ from a declared one only by case
body:
Go's `encoding/json` matches object member names to struct fields without regard to case. A document carrying both `"issuer"` and `"Issuer"` therefore decodes in Go with the second, while a proof verifier, a JSON Schema validator, and the Rust, TypeScript and Dart runtimes all read the exact-case `"issuer"`. The same holds inside payloads (`{"subject":"alice","Subject":"bob"}` is `bob` in Go and `alice` everywhere else). A document must mean one thing to every reader, and the Go reading has to be the one the other checks saw.

## What changes

**`trusttasks` (core module)**
- `Document[P].UnmarshalJSON` and `Proof.UnmarshalJSON` refuse a member whose name is not one the envelope, the proof or the payload type `P` declares but which `encoding/json` would match to one. Folding is exactly `encoding/json`'s (v1, which is also what the v1 API does on the v2 implementation): ASCII case and Unicode simple case folding (`ſ`/`s`, `K`/`k`). `_` and `-` are significant, so `"thread_id"` is an ordinary unrecognised member, kept as everywhere else. The walk follows `P` into nested structs, pointers, slices, arrays and map values, with `encoding/json`'s field precedence (a shallower field wins a name over a promoted one); types with their own `UnmarshalJSON` are left to themselves.
- New `CheckMemberNames[T any](data []byte) error` exposes the check for a payload decoded outside a `Document` (a binding's payload decoder).
- Verify-then-decode path: `ConsumeInbound` decodes `Received` to confirm `Doc` is a reading of it, so a `Received` carrying such a member is now refused `proofInvalid` rather than vouching for a differently-decoded `Doc`.

**`trust-tasks-go/didcomm` and `trust-tasks-go/tsp`**
- `Consume` refuses, `malformedRequest`, a document in which any object (envelope or payload) holds two members whose names differ only by case, *before* the caller's payload `decode` runs. A signed `{"role":"reader","Role":"admin"}` can no longer verify as `reader` and reach the handler as `admin`. These modules require the published core (`v0.9.3`), so the check is a self-contained one in each module (`memberfold.go`) that needs no type information; `Receive`/`Consume` docs say so.

**`trust-tasks-go/proof`**
- The verifier refuses (`malformedProof`) a document or proof object carrying such a member, since its issuer binding reads the exact-case `issuer`.

Unrelated extra members (`issuerNote`, `x-vendor`) still round-trip through `Extra`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
**Breaking (`!`):** a Go consumer now refuses documents it used to accept.
- **Stricter than the other runtimes, by design:** Go refuses `{"issuer":"a","Issuer":"b"}`, which Rust, TypeScript and Dart accept with issuer `"a"` and the second member ignored as unrecognised. Refusing is the only reading in which Go agrees with them about `issuer`. Documented in `trust-tasks-go/README.md` and on `CheckMemberNames`.
- A Go consumer now refuses, at decode, documents whose member names differ from declared ones only by case/delimiter. Every conforming producer emits lowerCamelCase exact names (SPEC §4.10), and the other three runtimes never read such members as the declared ones, so no interoperable document is affected. The binding consumers report a decode failure as `malformedRequest`.
- **Follow-up once this core is released:** move the `didcomm` and `tsp` modules' core requirement to it. Their envelope decoding then gets the full exact-name check (a lone `"Issuer"` with no `"issuer"` is still read as issuer by core v0.9.3 today), and their payload decoders can wrap `CheckMemberNames[P]`; the self-contained duplicate check can then go.

## Tests
- `trusttasks/membercase_test.go`: case, upper-case, Unicode-fold and delimiter variants in the envelope, payload and proof are refused; unrelated members survive; nested types are followed; a `Received` with a case-variant `issuer` yields `proofInvalid` and the handler does not run.
- `didcomm/didcomm_test.go`, `tsp/tsp_test.go`: case-duplicate members in the payload and the envelope are `malformedRequest` and the handler does not run; `"text_note"` beside `"text"` is still handled.
- `membercase_test.go` also: `"thread_id"` survives in `Extra` and is not read as `threadId`; shallowest-field precedence.
- `proof/proof_test.go`: a signed document with a case-variant `issuer` (or a folded-rune spelling), and a proof with a case-variant member, are `malformedProof`; an unrelated member still verifies.

Run locally:
- `trust-tasks-go`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go test -race ./...` — all exit 0
- `trust-tasks-go/proof`, `trust-tasks-go/didcomm`, `trust-tasks-go/tsp`: `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go test -race ./...` — exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack development guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a, decode-time refusal
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a

title: fix(go)!: refuse member names that differ from a declared one only by case (#1161)
body:
fix(go)!: refuse member names that differ from a declared one only by case (#1161)

* fix(go): refuse member names that differ from a declared one only by case

encoding/json matches object member names to struct fields without regard
to case, so `{"issuer":"a","Issuer":"b"}` decoded with Issuer "b", while a
proof verifier, a JSON Schema validator and the Rust, TypeScript and Dart
runtimes all read the exact-case "issuer" and see "a". A document must mean
one thing to every reader.

- trusttasks: Document and Proof decoding now refuse a member whose name is
  not one the envelope, the proof or the payload type declares but which
  encoding/json would match to one (case, Unicode simple folding, and the
  '_'/'-' insensitivity of encoding/json/v2's matcher). The check follows
  the payload type into nested structs, slices, arrays and map values.
  CheckMemberNames[T] exposes the same check for a payload decoded outside
  a Document.
- Because ConsumeInbound decodes Received when checking that Doc is a
  reading of it, a Received carrying such a member is now refused
  proofInvalid instead of vouching for a differently-decoded Doc.
- proof: the Data Integrity verifier refuses a document or proof object
  carrying such a member (malformedProof), since the issuer binding reads
  the exact-case member.

The didcomm and tsp modules pick the envelope check up when their core
requirement moves to a release containing it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(go): match member names as encoding/json does, and check the DIDComm and TSP consumers

- Member names now fold as encoding/json's v1 matcher compares them (ASCII
  case and Unicode simple case folding). '_' and '-' are significant, so a
  member such as "thread_id" is again an ordinary unrecognised member, kept
  as Rust, TypeScript and Dart keep it. Same in the proof verifier.
- The member walk follows encoding/json's field precedence: a shallower
  field wins a name over one promoted from an embedded struct.
- didcomm and tsp: `Consume` refuses, malformedRequest, a document in which
  any object holds two members whose names differ only by case, before the
  caller's payload decoder runs. A signed {"role":"reader","Role":"admin"}
  no longer verifies as one value and reaches the handler as the other.
  These modules require an earlier core, so the check is self-contained;
  the full exact-name check (CheckMemberNames) is available to their payload
  decoders once their core requirement moves.
- Documented that Go refuses {"issuer":"a","Issuer":"b"}, which the other
  runtimes accept with the unrecognised member ignored.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: fix(vtc-service): a badge group changes only through its badge, and by its owners' own key
body:
A community badge is backed by a badge group, and that group belongs to the badge (VTI-BDG-012).
- `vtc/badges/update` keeps the group's name, `joinPolicy` (from `requestable`) and `showMembers` (from `holdersVisibleTo`) in step with the badge.
- `vtc/badges/retire` is admin-only and takes a bound step-up. It deletes the group and revokes holders, shares, claim codes and the registry record.

`vtc/groups/update` and `vtc/groups/delete` checked only that the caller manages the group. They never looked at `badgeId`, so a badge owner (who holds `vtc.groups.manage` on the group) could:
- **delete it.** The badge stayed active with no group and no owners, and its awards and shared credentials stayed unrevoked.
- **set `joinPolicy: open`.** Any member who could see the badge could then join and get the credential, with no offer and no owner decision.

Separately, `standing()` in `group_tasks` accepted the member portal's delegated sign-in key for every group task. That let owner acts on a badge group be signed with the portal key, which the badge tasks' own owner acts deliberately refuse (VTI-BDG-095).

## Change (vtc-service `trust_tasks::group_tasks`)

- **`vtc/groups/update` and `vtc/groups/delete` refuse a badge group** with `permissionDenied`, whoever signs, administrators included.
  - The refusal names `vtc/badges/update` or `vtc/badges/retire`.
  - It is checked after the existing not-found / not-a-manager answers, so what a caller can learn about which groups exist is unchanged.
  - `members/add` and `bindings/add` already refused a badge group this way.
- **The portal's key is refused for owner acts on a badge group.** `standing_signed` reports whether the document was signed with the portal's delegated key. On a badge group, `requests/decide`, `members/remove`, `managers/add` and `managers/remove` refuse that key with `permissionDenied`, and the owner signs with their own key.
  - Other groups are unaffected.
  - `join`, `leave`, the reads and every other group task still accept the portal key.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/badges.md` states both rules.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- `vtc/groups/update` and `vtc/groups/delete` on a badge group: `permissionDenied`. Both used to succeed.
- `vtc/groups/{requests/decide,members/remove,managers/add,managers/remove}` on a badge group, signed by the portal's delegated key: `permissionDenied`.

Consumers checked:
- The admin console (`admin-ui/src/lib/groups.ts`) reaches badge-group owner acts through the console, signed with the owner's own key, as `docs/03-vtc/badges.md` describes. The member portal offers no owner acts on badges.
- `vtc-mcp` and the CLIs sign with the caller's own key.

No wire shape changes.

## Tests

`vtc-service/tests/it/badges.rs` `a_badge_group_is_changed_only_through_its_badge_and_by_its_owners_own_key`:
- `groups/update` to `open` is refused and the stored join policy is unchanged.
- `groups/delete` is refused and the group is still stored.
- With a portal key armed for the owner's session (scope `vtc/groups`), `requests/decide`, `managers/add`, `managers/remove` and `members/remove` are each refused, and no badge is held.
- The owner's own key then approves the request, and the member holds the badge.

Local results:
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --no-fail-fast`: 3613 passed, 0 failed, exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The refusals happen before any write.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. The new refusals use the standard `permissionDenied`. Consumers are listed above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Refused whoever signs, with no configuration that loosens it.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). No mutation paths added.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(vtc-service): keep no copy of a token-bearing response for redelivery
body:
The Trust Task spine (`vti-trust-task-server`) keeps each successful response in the duplicate-id record, so a redelivery of the same document `id` gets the first result back. A response that carries a bearer secret is left out of that record. vtc-service's list of those (`records_response`) had invite claim codes, invitations and the event-stream grant, but no session tokens.

So a redelivered `auth/authenticate/0.3` or `auth/refresh/0.2` got the recorded access and refresh tokens back, and the handler never ran:
- the single-use challenge was not checked
- the refresh was not rotated or checked for reuse
- no audit row was written

The tokens also sat in the record in plaintext for the acceptance window.

## Change

Now unrecorded. A redelivery within the window is answered `204` with no body, as invite creation already was:

| Task | Secret in the response |
|---|---|
| `auth/authenticate/0.3`, `auth/refresh/0.2` | access + refresh tokens |
| `vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3`, `vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish/0.1` | setup session token |
| `vtc/auth/recognise/0.3` | cross-community access token |
| `backup/initiate-export/0.1`, `backup/initiate-import/0.1` | transfer transport token |

- `trust_tasks::records_response` is a free function now, and the `Dispatcher` impl calls it.
- **New census** (`trust_tasks::response_record_census`):
  - It walks every served version's published response schema, following `$ref`s from the root. Unreferenced `$defs`, such as a sealed cleartext declared only for bindings, are skipped.
  - It fails if a response that can carry `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `setupSessionToken`, `sessionToken`, `claimCode`, `secretAccessKey`, `privateKeyMultibase`, `sealedSecret`, `transportToken` or `resumeToken` is still recorded.
  - The backup rows above came from this census.
- The `Dispatcher::records_response` docs in `vti-trust-task-server` now name session and setup tokens.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- A redelivery (same `id`, same content) of one of the tasks above is now `204`, not a copy of the first response. A client that lost the first answer has to start again with a new document:
  - a new challenge for `authenticate`
  - a new claim for install
  - a new recognise
  - a new transfer for backup
- For `refresh`, the next refresh with the old token is now seen as reuse. Before, the redelivery returned the successor tokens without going through `handle_refresh`.
- The first execution is unchanged. Wire shapes are unchanged. A client that resends a stored document after a lost answer now gets `204` and must send a new one. I did not audit every client's retry path for this.

Not changed: vta-service's pre-session `auth/*` family does not pass through its accepted-id record, so it never kept these tokens.

## Tests

- `vti-trust-task-server/tests/spine.rs` `an_unrecorded_response_is_not_handed_to_a_redelivery`: the first send gets the token, the redelivery is `204` with no body, and the handler runs once.
- `vtc-service` `trust_tasks::response_record_census`:
  - the census over every served response schema
  - the reference walk
  - the token-bearing URIs are not recorded

Local results:
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vti-trust-task-server --no-fail-fast`: 3648 passed, 0 failed, exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vti-trust-task-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The claim is still completed after a success, just without a body, so the effect happens once (§7.2 item 11).
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a. Redeliveries of these non-idempotent tasks no longer hand back a result.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. The `204` on a duplicate is the existing disposition; see R3.6 above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). n/a. The census fails the build for any new token-bearing response that is recorded.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). Unchanged ordering: dispatch, sign, then complete the claim.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None.

title: fix(voting-service): resolve a signer on the HTTPS door only where the box knows it
body:
The ballot box's HTTPS door proves no sender. Verifying a request's proof resolves the DID that the proof's `verificationMethod` names. Only casts had to be signed by a `did:key`, so a signed read, a trustee step or a registration could name any `did:web` / `did:webvh` and the box would fetch it, once per request. Signed community and trustee requests were also accepted at any age.

## vti-voting-service (`dispatch::answer`)

- **Verification method before resolution.** The proof's verification method must be the issuer's before anything is resolved. Before, it was compared only after verifying.
- **Which resolver** (`resolver_for`):
  - `did:key` / `did:peer`: resolved locally with no I/O (`TrustTaskVmResolver::did_key_only()`), on any binding.
  - TSP / DIDComm: unchanged. The transport proved the sender, and the sender must be the issuer.
  - HTTPS, any other DID: resolved only when `[communities] allowed` names it, or when the election the request names (held here) lists it as its community, an auditor or a trustee. Otherwise the request is refused `permissionDenied` before anything is fetched. An open box (`allow_any`) names no community.
- **Acceptance window.** A request from a community or a trustee (register, close, cancel, enrol, deal, confirm, justify, decrypt, authorize) is refused `expired` when its `issuedAt` is older than the VTI acceptance window (VTI-OPS-024: 10 minutes plus 60 s skew). The window and skew are read from `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW`.
- **Casts keep their current rule.** Their key is made for one cast, the voter's agent may resend a cast until voting closes, and the box answers a resend as it did the first time.

## vti-voting

- New `BallotBox::names_party(community, election_id, did)`.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)

- On HTTPS, a signed request whose signer is neither a `did:key`/`did:peer`, nor in `[communities] allowed`, nor a party to the named election held here, is now `permissionDenied` (403). It used to be resolved.
  - The documented clients are unaffected:
    - The VTC sends registrations, closes, cancels, authorizations and its reads over TSP/DIDComm (`elections::link`).
    - Trustees post their steps and signed reads over HTTPS, but they are named in the manifest.
    - Auditors are named in the manifest too.
  - On an open box (`allow_any`), a registration over HTTPS signed by a non-`did:key` is now refused. Registrations go over TSP or DIDComm.
- A proof whose verification method's DID is not the issuer is `proofInvalid` without being resolved. This was already refused, after resolution.
- A community or trustee request issued more than 11 minutes ago is `expired` (400). The VTC builds a new document for each exchange, and `pnm elections trustee step` signs each step when it runs, so neither resends an old document.

Wire shapes are unchanged. Docs updated: `docs/07-voting/README.md` (what the service refuses) and the threat-model table (row 21).

Not in this change:
- A duplicate-id record for these tasks. Every community and trustee handler already answers a repeat as it did the first time, and the window now limits how long a copy is accepted.
- The HTTPS door's request rate. This is still left to the reverse proxy, as the threat model's "Still open" says.

## Tests

`vti-voting-service/tests/http.rs`:
- `the_https_door_resolves_only_a_signer_it_has_a_reason_to_know`:
  - a stranger's DID and an election not held here are both `permissionDenied` before any fetch
  - an auditor named by a held election passes the gate
  - a verification method that is not the issuer's is `proofInvalid`
  - a `did:key` signer still reads
- `an_allowed_community_is_resolved_on_the_https_door_and_an_open_box_names_nobody`
- `a_communitys_request_older_than_the_acceptance_window_is_refused`: 20 minutes old is refused, 5 minutes old is accepted.

Local results:
- `cargo test -p vti-voting-service -p vti-voting`: 95 passed, exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p vti-voting-service -p vti-voting --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). No new clients. Fewer DIDs reach the existing resolver, which is the one `vta_sdk::resolver::build_did_cache_config` builds, with its public-host policy.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The gate takes the ballot-box `std::sync::Mutex` only for a synchronous `names_party` lookup and releases it before any resolution.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). n/a: the new refusals happen before any state is read or written.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire types change. Consumers checked: VTC `elections::link`, `vta-cli-common` `elections_trustee` and `elections` (votes, inclusion).
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Without `[communities] allowed`, no unknown DID is resolved on HTTPS. A poisoned ballot-box lock refuses.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). No mutations touched.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None. Behaviour changes are listed under R3.6.

title: feat(rooms): a live watch while a conversation is open (rooms/watch 0.2, rooms/keys/watch 0.2)
body:
Stacked on #2667; retarget to main once it merges.

Implements **live room watches** from the Trust Task specs (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1087): `rooms/watch/0.2` at both hosts and `rooms/keys/watch/0.2` at the VTA. 0.1 is still served everywhere.

## Pins
`rooms/watch` and `rooms/keys/watch` are pinned as `["0.1", "0.2"]` in `vti-specs-rooms` with the `trust-tasks` CLI. The registry's in-place draft updates to the two 0.1 bundles come too: they mark 0.1 deprecated and change nothing else. Nothing else is re-pinned: the in-place updates `update` also fetched for `records/list`, `keys/browse` and `keys/list` were reverted to keep this PR to watches. `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-rooms check` passes.

## Hosts (`vti_rooms::watch`, served by `room-host` and the VTC)
- `live: true` is allowed only on a room whose signal delay is `none`. Any other room is refused `rooms/watch:liveNotPermitted` before anything is touched, so a watch at that address stays as it was (Host item 6).
- The lease is at most 120 s from each request, whatever was asked, and the answer says `live: true` (item 7).
- A renewal without `sinceVersion` keeps the watch's watermark, which is the version last signalled. A renewal with it replaces the watermark and signals at once if the room is above it (item 3). A request without `live` makes the watch one-shot again.
- The host sends one signal each time the room moves past the watermark, then moves the watermark to that version. Signals are paced per watch at least 1 s apart (`LIVE_SIGNAL_SPACING`). A change inside the spacing sets one timer, and that timer's signal carries the latest version. There is no queue per change and no resend (item 5).
- Setting a room back to `randomised` ends its live watches at once, sending nothing: both hosts' `rooms/signal-delay/set` call `end_live_watches`. As a backstop, `fire` drops any live watch it finds on a randomised room.
- The watch key is unchanged. Records written before this PR read as one-shot (`live` is absent, which means false).

## VTA (`rooms/keys/watch/0.2`)
- Each room is armed at the host with `rooms/watch/0.2` live. One-shot watches are still armed with 0.1, so they work with hosts that lack 0.2.
- **Every** signal is passed on. The record is kept after each one and holds nothing more than item 6 allows (`live` only): no watermark, version or time.
- A live renewal keeps the address. A switch between one-shot and live mints a **new** address and moves the old record under its own key (`WatchRecord::retiring`), where it still receives. Once the host has armed the new watch, the VTA cancels the old one at the host and forgets it. If the host refuses the new watch, the old record is put back, so a refused live watch leaves the one-shot watch in place (item 5).
- The host's `liveNotPermitted` becomes `hostRefused` + `hostCode`. There is never a fallback to one-shot (item 3). A refused renewal forgets the watch (item 7). `live` appears in the outcome only when the host answered it.
- Reachability of a new address: as with any fresh arming, the record (and so the address's connection) is written before the host is asked. A signal sent before the connection opens waits in the mediator's queue for that DID. `tests/e2e/tests/room_key_watch.rs` already covers this case.
- Plumbing: dispatch, policy subject, operation budget (charged like 0.1) and the conformance sample.

## SDK, clients, CLI
- `vta_sdk`: `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_WATCH_0_2` (in `ALL_URIS`, classified `RetrySafe` in `retry_safety`), `VtaClient::room_watch_live`, `LIVE_NOT_PERMITTED`, `LIVE_RENEW_EVERY`.
- `vtc_client`: `RoomsClient::watch_live` (`rooms/watch/0.2`).
- `pnm rooms watch --live` tails the room. It prints each `rooms/keys/changed` from the operator's own VTA, renews every 60 s, cancels on Ctrl-C, and stops after two renewals in a row fail. On `liveNotPermitted` it prints `pnm rooms signal-delay set --room … --host … --none --reason …`. A watch answered without `live` is cancelled and reported as one-shot.

## Docs
`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`: the *Watching a room* row, a new live-watch passage under *Watching instead of polling*, and both reference tables. `vta-service/CLAUDE.md`: the *Watching rooms for a client* flow entry.

## Tests
- Host (`vti-rooms`): live is refused on a randomised room and the existing watch stands; each change signals and a burst coalesces into one signal with the latest version, at least the spacing apart, without disarming; the lease is capped at 120 s; a renewal keeps or replaces the watermark; `randomised` ends live watches silently and the backstop drops a stray one; a request without `live` makes the watch one-shot; a cancelled live watch's pending timer sends nothing; the schema accepts only `live: true`. The existing 0.1 tests are unchanged and pass.
- VTA, against a real `room-host`: every signal is passed on and nothing more is kept; the address is kept across renewals; the switch arms a new address first, with the host's order pinned (arm 0.2, then cancel 0.1, and the reverse); `liveNotPermitted` becomes `hostRefused` with no fallback and the one-shot watch left in place; a refused renewal forgets the watch; a cancel ends a live watch.

title: feat(vta)!: a VTA authenticates with its authentication key, and can resolve itself as a did:webs
body:
S6 slice 1 (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4): the plumbing
a did:webs VTA identity needs, with nothing changed for a did:webvh VTA,
whose authentication and signing key are both #key-0.

- SelfKeys gains the authentication key: a key-role identity's
  operational key (VTI-KEY-072), which is the key every request,
  response and DIDComm sender of this VTA proves with (proofPurpose
  authentication). The VTA's resident key at boot, the offline CLI
  bridge's signer, vta status's DIDComm profile and the operational-
  secret fallback now load it; attestation artefacts (credentials, the
  VtaAuthorization VC, room-owner registration) keep the signing
  (attestation) key. load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store takes the SelfKey
  to load.
- A did:webs VTA preloads its own document into the resolver from the key
  event log it stores; readiness probes did:webs over the network and
  names its keri.cesr URL.
- didcomm_light and url_from_did handle did:webs;
  vta_sdk::resolved_methods::is_durable_identity is webvh, scid or an
  optional durable method (did_scid::is_durable keeps meaning "has a
  webvh log").

Breaking (vta-service): DIDCommBridge::signing_only and
preload_self_did_document take the webs keyspace;
load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store takes a SelfKey; SelfKeys has an
authentication field.

Refs: VTI-KEY-001, VTI-KEY-072

title: feat(vta)!: a did:webs node acts only toward peers that declare did:webs
body:
VTI-KEY-008 / VTI-KEY-009, sending side. A node initiating an exchange
as its own durable identity, when that identity is of an optional method
(did:webs), first holds the peer's verified current DID document to its
resolvedMethods declaration; without it the node sends nothing and fails
with methodNotDeclared, never acting under another identifier.

Checked where a node initiates as its own DID and already resolves the
peer's document to choose a transport:

- the VTA's Outbound::send, when the VTA's DID is the document's issuer
  or the TSP/DIDComm sender (a persona issuing over HTTPS is not the
  VTA's durable identity). Outbound now reads the VTA's DID from the
  live config, or from_parts' caller;
- the VTC's PeerTasks::select (its VTA, git bridge, ballot boxes, watch
  addresses) as PeerError::MethodNotDeclared, and its trust-registry
  selection as a permanent registry failure;
- room-host's watch signals.

Not checked, by the rule's own exception: the Trust-Task push engine,
whose every recipient addressed the node under its identity (an enrolled
approver device, a holder that asked, a joined member). The sends that
bypass a resolving seam (push-gateway calls, the VTC hook writer, VTN
requests, mediator login) are recorded in the design note for S6/S7,
when a node can first be a did:webs.

No node's own DID is a did:webs yet, so every send passes today.

Docs: the design note records S1-S5 done and where the declaration is
made and checked; the operator guide's "Not a node's identity" becomes
"A node's identity: not yet".

Refs: VTI-KEY-008, VTI-KEY-009

Breaking (vta-service): `operations::outbound::Outbound::from_parts` takes the node's own DID (`node_did: String`), which the declaration check holds every send it acts in to.

title: feat(pages): build and deploy the toolkit front door to GitHub Pages
body:
## What changed

This adds a front door for the toolkit on GitHub Pages: a redesigned site in the Trust over IP style, built straight from `data/`, `method/` and `review/examples/`, plus a workflow that builds it on every PR and deploys it when we merge to `main`.

The site has 18 pages: a home page with the review journey (who does each step: people, AI or a machine), step-by-step guides with and without AI, examples with their review state, and plain-language pages for people, situations, risks, safeguards, who is affected, the lifecycle, decisions and a glossary. Codes like RK- and CT- are still there, but tucked into each item's details.

## Why

When I used the toolkit for the first time as a non-technical reviewer, I found it really hard to get into without AI, and there's no front door (my notes are on #50). This is a first go at fixing that: different ways in for different people, honest about what's draft and what's AI-drafted, and accessible by screen reader and voice.

@sankarshanmukhopadhyay, I've built this on your Pages pipeline from the fork: PRs build and check without publishing, `main` deploys, and the standard Pages actions are pinned to SHAs like `validate.yml`. I haven't brought over Just the Docs, because the redesign has its own design system, or the post-deploy route observer. That could come later if we want it.

## Scope

- `tools/build_pages.py`: generates the site into `_site/`. Every page shows the commit it was built from.
- `tools/check_pages.py`: fails the build on a broken internal link or anchor, or a page without a title or language.
- `site/`: the front door template, plus example inputs that aren't review records in this repo:
  - the **Linux case** findings, an **AI draft, not yet reviewed by me**, labelled that way on every page;
  - **Arthur and Margaret**, the public version of a persona-led implementation review. The stack it reviewed is deliberately not named.
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: build, check, upload; deploy on `main` only.

Not in scope: no changes to `data/`, `method/`, the review contract or `tools/build.py`. The older `build/site` pages stay as they are.

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 tools/build_pages.py          # 18 pages into _site/
python3 tools/check_pages.py _site    # 18 pages checked, 0 problems
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests # 118 tests OK (unchanged)
```

Or download the `pages-preview` artifact from this PR's "Build and deploy the toolkit pages" run and open `index.html`.

## Assurance / review questions

1. **Layer:** publication and reader-facing docs only.
2. **Evidence:** it consumes the canonical corpus and the upstream example review records; it doesn't produce assurance evidence.
3. **Judgment it enables:** helps people, including non-technical reviewers, find who could be harmed and where a fix belongs.
4. **Judgment it avoids:** it doesn't score, accept or decide anything. Passing the checks is stated as "well formed, not right" wherever it appears.
5. **Affected:** none of the risks, controls, vocabularies or records change.
6. **Open, and for the TF to decide:**
   - **Review states for the upstream examples.** TEA, TRQP and VRC are shown as "checked by a person" and the worked adoption as "training only". This is my reading of their READMEs, and the pages say so. @sankarshanmukhopadhyay, can you check these are right?
   - The proposed mapping of the journey steps onto the five lifecycle stages.
   - The routes for sharing a finding, including a protected route. They're shown as still being designed.
   - Whether this front door becomes the official page.
7. **To reproduce:** run the commands above and compare the pages with `data/`.

## Compatibility and limitations

- **Pages has to be switched on once:** Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions. Until then, the deploy job on `main` will fail.
- The site will be at https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-rahp-tf/ and is public.
- The status bar says it's a draft and not an official Trust over IP Foundation page until approved.
- The Linux case review records (SR-301 to SR-303) aren't in the repo yet. Only their themes and findings are used.
- The fonts load from Google Fonts.

## AI assistance or agent execution, if applicable

Claude (Anthropic) designed and drafted the pages and the generator, and ported them into the repo and the workflow. I'm the responsible human. I've decided the content, structure and wording, and reviewed the pages as a draft artifact. The Linux case findings are an AI draft that I haven't reviewed yet, and they're labelled that way. The checks above were run locally, and they'll run again in CI on this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] The PR explains why the change exists and what remains outside scope.
- [x] Reproduction or validation steps are sufficient for a reviewer who did not author the change.
- [x] Reported validation results were actually observed; missing evidence remains visible.
- [x] Compatibility or migration impact is stated when semantics or contracts change.
- [x] No generated file under `build/` was edited by hand.
- [ ] If canonical corpus records changed, `python3 tools/validate.py` exits 0. *(No corpus changes.)*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.2

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 7.30.1 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

In Undici 7.x, the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

Undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] fix(decompress): join a repeated content-encoding header (#5664) by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6026
  • ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6087
  • fix(h1): backport ignore type of service errors to v7.x (#5547) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6076
  • [Backport v7.x] extractBody fixes 2 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#6093

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.30.1...v7.30.2

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.
