title: feat(vta/webs/dids): level-1 did:webs identities for personas, relationships and integrations (0.1)
body:
Adds `vta/webs/dids/*` at `0.1`: the tasks a VTA uses to create, host, update, rotate and deactivate `did:webs` DIDs, as `vta/webvh/dids/*` does for `did:webvh`. All six are `draft`, and the `did:webs` integration behind them is **alpha**.

Design: [VTI design note, *did:webs in the VTA*](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2558) (decisions 1–11 shape this wire).

## Scope: persona, relationship and integration DIDs only

These tasks are for **persona, relationship and integration DIDs** at key assurance level 1. A `did:webs` DID **must not** become a node's service DID (the durable identity of a VTA, VTC, VTN or host service). VTI-KEY-001 names only `did:webvh` and `did:scid:vh:1` for those, and VTI-KEY-003 forbids requiring a peer to resolve anything else. A VTA refuses such a create with `vta/webs/dids/create:serviceDidNotPermitted`. It also refuses to adopt a `did:webs` DID as its own or a community's identity through any other task. A key-role (level 2/3) identity under `did:webs` stays with `vta/dids/*` and its `webs` method profile.

## Key model (`_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md`)

- **KERI v2 events with JSON bodies.** No v1 events are written.
- **Keys:** one Ed25519 signing key (`kt` 1) and one pre-rotated successor (`nt` 1). The VTA derives both, and no caller supplies or receives a key.
- **Designations:** aliases, key agreement and services are ACDCs in the AID's own registry, anchored in its KEL by an interaction event. Designated aliases come from the `did:webs` spec. Key agreement and services are the `affinidi-did-webs` extensions proposed to it, and the conventions name the interop limit this brings. The DID always designates itself first. `#didcomm` / `#tsp` are typed `DIDCommMessaging` / `TSPTransport`.
- **Key agreement** is a designated X25519 key, never the X25519 key converted from the signing key (VTI-KEY-184).
- **Hosting is required.** Publication goes through a registered did-hosting server by `did-management/did/register/0.1` with `method: "webs"`. The caller's path comes first and the AID is appended after it, and the host derives `did.json` from `keri.cesr`. There is no serverless or self-hosted form, because the VTA has no inbound surface.
- **Remote first.** Every change is published before the VTA's record commits it. Rotations are staged, and a staged rotation is republished on restart and never rewritten.

## Tasks

| Task | Payload | Task-specific errors |
|---|---|---|
| `create/0.1` | `contextId`, `serverId`, `path`, `domain`, `label`, `addMediatorService`, `addTspService`, `additionalServices`, `alsoKnownAs`, `setPrimary`, `ext` → DID, AID, slot, `keriCesrUrl`, `didJsonUrl`, signing / successor / key-agreement key ids and keys, `sequenceNumber`, `versionId` | `methodDisabled`, `serverNotFound`, `hostDoesNotHostWebs`, `domainNotServed`, `pathRefused`, `serviceDidNotPermitted`, family `serviceIdConflict`, `publishRefused` |
| `get/0.1` | `did`, `includeKeriCesr` → `WebsDidRecord`, `keriCesr`, `rotationStaged` | `notFound` |
| `list/0.1` | `contextId`, `serverId`, `includeDeactivated`, `cursor`, `limit` → `dids`, `nextCursor` | — |
| `update/0.1` | `did`, `services` (whole set), `rotateKeyAgreementKey`, `alsoKnownAs`, `expectedVersionId`, `label`. Each change is an interaction-anchored designation, and no key changes | `notFound`, `versionConflict`, `noChange`, family `serviceIdConflict`, `deactivated`, `publishRefused` |
| `rotate-keys/0.1` | `did`, `expectedVersionId`, `label` → installed / committed / retired key ids, `resumed` | `notFound`, `versionConflict`, family `deactivated`, `publishRefused` |
| `delete/0.1` | `did`, `expectedVersionId`, `label`. Deactivates (rotation to no next keys, published and committed), then removes the slot → `newlyDeactivated`, `slotRemoved`, `hostCleanupError` | `notFound`, `versionConflict`, family `publishRefused` |

`targetFrameworkVersion` is `0.5.0`, the same as the webvh siblings. `vta/webs/_shared/0.1/webs-records.schema.json` holds the shared record, the designated-service shape and the slot-path grammar.

Bindings were regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and Dart.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`, `npm run check-published-schemas`
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vta --all-targets`
- `npm run build-ts-bindings`, then in `trust-tasks-ts`: `tsc --noEmit` and `npm test`
- `npm run build-go-bindings`, then `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test` on the new packages
- `npm run build-dart-bindings`, then `dart analyze --fatal-infos` on the new libraries

title: fix(rank): match whole words, fold plurals, drop query stopwords
body:
Fixes the two ranking defects the evaluation harness (#46) found, and makes their probes hard checks.

## Changes
- **Whole-word matching** instead of substring containment — "run" no longer matches "Test **run**ner", nor "test" "la**test**".
- **Plurals folded to singular** by rule, on both sides ("tests"→"test", "policies"→"policy", "pushes"→"push"; "status", "analysis", "bus" untouched). Plurals only — "-ing"/"-ed" stripping guesses wrong in ways nobody can predict.
- **Query stopwords** (short English list) dropped. Negations ("not", "never", "no") are kept — they change meaning. A query of only stopwords returns nothing, not the whole context.
- Words split on any script, not ASCII only — "café" / "Straße" now match.

## Evaluation, before → after

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| minimisation precision | 29% | **67%** |
| precision (dimension) | 81% | **93%** |
| overall precision | 74% | **82%** |
| MRR | 0.97 | **1.00** |
| checks | 24/27 + 3 known gaps | **29/29, no known gaps** |

`minimisation-stopwords` and `precision-word-boundaries` are now hard. One adjustment to the latter: its "runner" memory's description no longer contains the word "run" itself, because with whole-word matching that memory legitimately matches both query words and the probe was testing two things at once. As adjusted, the probe fails under the old substring ranking (the name "runner" scored) and passes under this one.

Unit tests cover word boundaries, plural folding both ways, non-plural `-s` words, stopword-only queries, and non-Latin words.

Plugin and crate → **0.6.1**.

title: test: memory quality evaluation harness (#35)
body:
Closes #35.

## What it is

`cargo test --test eval` replays **18 scripted multi-session scenarios** (`tests/eval/scenarios/*.json`) against the real `Store` — signing, verification, ranking, lifecycle — over the in-process fake VTA, and prints a scored report. Format and metrics are documented in `tests/eval/README.md`.

| dimension | scenarios | what it checks |
|---|---:|---|
| precision | 3 | task-shaped queries surface the answering memory first; type filter; word boundaries |
| staleness | 3 | superseded / expired / deprecated facts lose; stale ones are flagged |
| contradiction | 3 | declared beats a newer inferred; undisputed beats disputed; evidenced `verified` beats unsupported |
| minimisation | 3 | abstention on unrelated queries; limit honoured; stopwords |
| repairability | 3 | operations to fix a wrong memory (retract; re-save; dispute→settle), with a budget |
| poisoning | 3 | tampered / relocated / proof-stripped records refused; forged fence delimiters; keyword-stuffing by another agent |

Probes carry **hard checks** (`top`, `absent`, `expectEmpty`, `refused`, `stale`, `describe`, `fence`) that fail the run, and are scored for precision / recall / MRR against hand-labelled relevant keys. A `soft` probe is scored and listed as a *known gap* without failing the run.

Shaped after LongMemEval where it applies (knowledge updates, abstention, temporal validity), plus what a signed multi-writer store needs (contradiction, repairability, poisoning).

## Current report

```
| dimension     | scenarios | checks passed | precision | recall | MRR  | repair ops |
| precision     | 3 | 6/8   | 81% | 100% | 0.93 | – |
| staleness     | 3 | 5/5   | 83% | 100% | 1.00 | – |
| contradiction | 3 | 3/3   | 50% | 100% | 1.00 | – |
| minimisation  | 3 | 4/5   | 29% | 100% | 1.00 | – |
| repairability | 3 | 5/5   | 100%| 100% | 1.00 | 4 |
| poisoning     | 3 | 3/3   | 83% | 100% | 1.00 | – |
```
All hard checks pass. (Contradiction precision is low by design: the demoted, losing memory stays visible for review and counts against precision.)

## Findings — two ranking defects, recorded as soft probes
1. **Substring matching.** `run` matches "Test **run**ner", `test` matches "la**test**" — a memory that merely contains the letters can outrank the one that answers.
2. **No stopwords.** "what is the for" matches three unrelated memories; this is most of minimisation's 29% precision.

A follow-up PR can fix both and make those probes hard; the harness will show the movement.

## Does it catch regressions?
Mutation-checked by hand: weighting `inferred` like `declared` fails *contradiction-declared-beats-inferred*; letting retracted or expired memories through recall fails the repair / staleness scenarios. That exercise found that only an **empty-query** probe catches the latter — with a query, a zero status weight already hides them — so the session-start path now has probes too.

## CI
Runs as part of `cargo test` (a failed hard check fails the build), and again in a labelled step with `EVAL_SUMMARY=1` to put the report in the job summary. On every PR rather than path-filtered: it is already built and takes well under a second.

## Also in this PR
- The fake keyspace moves to `tests/common/` so roundtrip tests and the harness share it.
- `test(pnm)`: fixes a pre-existing flaky test — `the_config_dir_can_be_overridden` set `PNM_CONFIG_DIR` process-wide under a parallel runner and intermittently broke `the_default_dir_follows_pnm_rather_than_assuming_xdg`. Now tested through a pure `dir_from`.

No plugin-visible change, so no version bump.

## Acceptance
- [x] At least 10 scripted scenarios covering the dimensions above (18).
- [x] One command produces a scored report; a CI job runs it (every PR, report in the job summary).

title: fix(vtc-service): a room's label or description edit keeps its recordMembers
body:
When a community room's label or description changed, the VTC re-wrote the
room's profile carrying over only `tags`, `emoji` and `ext`, a list that
predates `recordMembers`. A room set up with recordMembers
[kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt] lost them on the next edit, and its members'
clients could no longer reply or react there.

The re-write now keeps every member of the current profile except `name`
and `description`, the two the community manages, so `recordMembers` and
any member a later profile version adds survive an edit. The read is
parsed as the generated `rooms/keys/profile/read/0.1` response. A read
that fails, or answers a status this VTC does not know, no longer writes a
profile without the carried members: the write stays pending and the
profile sweeper retries it.

Spec: vtc/rooms/community/update 0.2 and 0.3 item 10, amended to name the
rule rather than a list in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1080.

title: feat: memory lifecycle — status, expiry, history and conditional saves (#33)
body:
Closes #33.

## What changes

**Saves no longer overwrite blind, and nothing they replace is lost.** `Store::save_versioned`:
1. reads the current version;
2. if the caller passed `expectedVersion` (from a recall/get; `0` = must be new) and it doesn't match, writes nothing and returns a conflict;
3. copies the current version **verbatim, still signed by its own author**, to `archive/<type>/<slug>/v<n>` and links it as `supersedes`;
4. writes the new record **conditionally** (`put/0.3 expectedVersion`) on the version from step 1 — a writer that landed in between wins, and the losing save returns `SaveOutcome::Conflict` with the *checked* winner (a forged winner is a `Refused`, not an `Entry`);
5. prunes history to 5 versions.

History keys are outside every `<type>/` prefix, so recall and typed lists never reach them. `memory_get` with `history: true` returns them, each verified against the key it was originally written to.

**Lifecycle fields, all signed:** `status` (`active` | `deprecated` | `disputed` | `retracted`) + required `statusReason`, `validUntil`, `reviewAfter`, `supersedes`.
- Recall **excludes** retracted and expired; **demotes** deprecated/disputed (half weight) and shows the status + reason; flags `stale` past `reviewAfter`.
- `memory_list` shows everything with its status; `stale: true` narrows to due-for-review/expired.

**New MCP tools:** `memory_dispute`, `memory_deprecate`, `memory_retract` (each takes a reason and optional `expectedVersion`). Retract leaves a content-free tombstone (content survives only in history) and is the only status change allowed on a refused record — anything else would re-sign content nobody vouches for. A status change is a new version signed by whoever made it; the original author's version is in history.

`memory_save` gains `expectedVersion`, `validUntil`, `reviewAfter`; a conflict returns `saved: false` with the current version and value (fenced). **`memory_forget` stays the hard delete and now removes history too.** `/memories --stale` walks the user through review; `/forget` offers retract.

Skill, commands, README, CLAUDE.md updated. Plugin and crate → **0.6.0**.

## Acceptance
- [x] Status, validUntil and supersedes round-trip and are honoured by recall (`a_replacing_save_keeps_the_previous_version_in_history`, `disputed_and_deprecated_memories_are_demoted_not_hidden`, `expired_memories_drop_out_and_stale_ones_are_flagged`).
- [x] A conflicting concurrent save is rejected, with the winning version returned — both the stale-read path and the VTA-side race in the read/write window (`a_save_based_on_a_stale_read_is_rejected_with_the_winner`, `a_concurrent_save_in_the_read_write_window_is_rejected_by_the_vta`; the fake keyspace now implements `expectedVersion` and `versionConflict` as the VTA does).
- [x] Retract keeps a tombstone; forget remains the hard-delete path (`retracting_leaves_a_tombstone_and_forgetting_removes_everything`).

## Notes
- A save is now ~3 round trips (get, archive put, conditional put) plus a list to prune when replacing. Memory saves are rare; correctness wins.
- Not exercised against a live VTA — relies on `put/0.3` `expectedVersion` / `versionConflict` as specified (VTI#2115).

## Testing
`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; 102 unit + 41 roundtrip + binary/hook/stdio suites pass.

title: feat: sign memory records and verify authorship on read (#31)
body:
Closes #31.

## What changes

- **Every save is signed** by the writer's own `did:key`: a Data Integrity proof (`vta_sdk::trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion`, the primitive Data Rooms use for sealed record bodies) over a **v2 record** that names `author`, `authorKind` (`agent` | `operator`), `contextId` and `key`. A `Store` without a signer refuses to save.
- **Every read verifies before a value becomes an `Entry`** (`Store::check`, the single place). A record is **refused** — not returned as memory, but reported by key + reason — when it:
  - was altered after signing,
  - was copied to another key or context,
  - claims an `author` other than its signer, or
  - is `v >= 2` with its `proof` stripped (refused, not downgraded).
- **Legacy v0/v1 records stay readable**, marked `unattributed`.
- Output: recall/get/list summaries carry an `author` block (`verified` with `did`/`kind`/`thisAgent`, or `unattributed`); recall and list carry `refused`; the SessionStart hook notes other writers and lists refusals; `doctor` prints the signing DID.
- The signer is read from the session store **after** connecting (enrolment rotates the key on first connect). `setup`/`enrol` fail early if the session cannot sign.
- Verification uses a `did:key`-only resolver: no network I/O, so a stored record cannot make recall fetch anything.

Skill, README and CLAUDE.md updated. Plugin and crate bumped to **0.4.0**.

## Acceptance
- [x] Record schema v2 carries author plus signature; v1 still decodes.
- [x] Tampered or relocated records are refused on recall, with tests (`a_tampered_record_is_refused_on_recall_list_and_get`, `a_relocated_record_is_refused`, plus stripped-proof and forged-author cases).
- [x] Recall output names the author kind.

## Known limits
- A writer with context access can still write an unsigned v1-style record; it shows as `unattributed`, never `verified`. A "require signed" config switch would close that — not added here.
- `Config::signer()` (session-store load, post-rotation) isn't covered by tests; it needs a real session. Not yet exercised against a live VTA — nothing on the wire changes except the content of the stored value.

## Testing
`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; all suites pass (82 unit, 29 roundtrip, plus binary/hook/stdio tests).

title: feat: epistemic provenance on memories — basis, confidence, evidence (#32)
body:
Closes #32. **Stacked on #43** (signed records) — base is `feat/signed-records`; retarget to `main` once #43 merges.

## What changes

Every save states what kind of claim it is, inside the record's signature (so it can't be upgraded after the fact — there's a test for exactly that):

- `basis`: `declared | observed | verified | inferred` — **required** on `memory_save`.
- `confidence`: optional, 0–1.
- `evidence`: up to 8 citations — `{kind:"credential", credentialId, digest?}`, `{kind:"memory", key}`, `{kind:"record", roomId, key}`. **`verified` must cite at least one.** Identifiers only; nothing is ever fetched.

The vocabulary and the credential/record shapes are the ones `rooms/records/put/0.5` publishes (VTI#2117), so a record moved between memory and a room keeps its meaning.

**Recall / get / list** show `basis` and `confidence`; get adds `evidence`. A `verified` record that cites nothing carries a `basisNote` and ranks as an inference. Records written before this read as `unstated`. The hook/CLI render notes the basis (`_[inferred, confidence 0.60]_`).

**Ranking** multiplies relevance by a basis weight — declared / evidenced verified 10, observed 9, unstated 8, inferred 6 — and empty-query ties break on it, so stated memories survive the session-start limit ahead of inferred ones. A nudge, not an override (tested both ways).

**Confidence is displayed, never ranked on.** The rooms schema says a reader MUST NOT rank by it across authors, since two writers' numbers aren't on one scale.

Skill, `/remember`, README and CLAUDE.md updated. Plugin and crate → **0.5.0**.

## Deviations from the issue
- Uses rooms' `evidence` list rather than a free-form `source` field, for alignment with VTI#2117. A credential citation carries `credentialId` (+ optional `digest`), not `issuer`, matching the rooms shape.
- The persona `selfAsserted` / `credentialBacked` vocabulary is not reused: the rooms `RecordBasis` vocabulary is the closer and more recent alignment, and persona provenance describes a profile value's source, not a claim's epistemic status.

## Acceptance
- [x] `basis` is required on new saves; MCP schema and skill updated (`the_save_schema_requires_a_basis`).
- [x] Recall summaries display `basis` and `confidence`.
- [x] Ranking applies a basis weight, with tests (`record.rs` ranking tests; `recall_prefers_what_the_user_said_over_what_was_inferred`).

## Testing
`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; 96 unit + 32 roundtrip + binary/hook/stdio suites pass.

title: test(contexts): expand credentials under v1 and v2 in JSON-LD safe mode
body:
Follow-up to #35, as its review suggested: nothing in CI exercised a context semantically, so the "no term dropped" claim there could only be taken on trust. This makes it reproducible.

**What runs.** `scripts/contexts.test.mjs` (picked up by `npm test`) expands the specification's agent VAC (*Attenuation* example) under each context with jsonld.js in **safe mode**, which fails on any term it would drop:

| Test | Checks |
|---|---|
| v2 is v1 plus `purposes` | every v1 term is identical in v2; the only added term is `purposes` |
| listed shape | expands to `credentials#purposeScope` = `listed`, `credentials#listedPurposes` = `taskExecution` |
| `any` shape | expands to `credentials#purposeScope` = `any` only |
| purposes are strings | a listed IRI purpose stays an `@value`, never an `@id` |
| no scope collision | `authority.scope` still expands to `#authorityScope` beside `purposes` |
| v1 refuses `purposes` | a VAC stating `purposes` fails under v1, on that property |
| v1 ≡ v2 without `purposes` | identical expansion |
| protection | a later context redefining `purposes`, or its inner `scope`, is refused |

**No network.** The registry contexts load from `contexts/`; the W3C VC v2 context loads from `scripts/test/contexts/credentials-v2.jsonld`, a vendored copy whose SHA-256 (`59955ced…92734`) is the one the VC Data Model 2.0 Recommendation publishes, and a test pins it. Any other URL makes the loader throw.

**Instance-neutral.** The `credentials#` namespace is read from v1's `DTGCredential` and the context base from `registry.config.json`, so `check:instance` passes and a fork's tests follow its config.

**Dependency.** `jsonld@^9.0.0` as a devDependency only; nothing it touches is deployed. `npm audit`'s one finding (`fast-uri`, via ajv) predates this change.

**Checked.** `npm run check` passes (34 tests). As a mutation check, typing `listedPurposes` as `@id` in `contexts/v2.jsonld` fails two of these tests; the file was restored and is unchanged in this PR.

No change under `contexts/` or `predicates/`, so this needs no two-editor review under GOVERNANCE §3.1.

title: vtc-service-v0.28.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: The VTA writes a grant's purposes into the credential it issues (issue-authority 0.3, VTI-ACL-110) ([#2546](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2546))

The VTA serves rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3 beside 0.2. The request's
  `purposes` are stated in the VAC's subject unchanged (DTG context v2), and a
  request stating none issues a credential stating none, which grants `any`
  (*Purpose of use* item 1).

  A credential is a grant the caller writes, so it may not grant purposes the
  caller's own entry does not (VTI-ACL-107): a purpose the caller does not hold,
  or none at all from a caller whose entry lists purposes, is refused rather
  than issued narrower or wider (item 2). This applies to 0.2 as well, which
  cannot state purposes: a caller whose entry lists purposes asks 0.3.

  - vta-sdk: TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_ISSUE_AUTHORITY_0_3 (Keyed) and
    VtaClient::room_owner_issue_authority_for.
  - vti-specs-rooms pins issue-authority 0.3; get/0.4's bundle takes the
    upstream description change (trust-tasks-tf #1077).

- **rooms**: Room hosts hold every read to the purposes its chain grants (VTI-ACL-110) ([#2545](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2545))

A room's authority credential may now state purposes (dtg-credentials 0.14,
  DTG context v2), and a host serving a read holds the request to them
  (`rooms/records/get/0.4`, *Purpose of use*).

  - vti-rooms: `purpose::ChainPurposes` and `PurposeDecision`; `VerifiedChain.purposes`
    (a new public field), `AuthorizedAction::purposes` and `admit_purpose`; get/0.4 is
    dispatched, with `blob_tasks::get_v4_purpose` and `read_purpose_refused`.
  - vti-rooms-dtg: `DtgChainVerifier` fills `purposes` from the verified chain, whose
    chain rule (a link may not widen its parent's purposes, VTI-ACL-107) dtg-credentials
    applies. A scope this build does not know grants nothing.
  - room-host and vtc-service serve `rooms/records/get/0.4`. A purpose the chain does not
    grant, or none where it lists several, is refused with `purposeNotGranted` after the
    chain verifies and before any record is read. get/0.2 and 0.3 cannot name a purpose and
    are decided as naming none (`permissionDenied` where the chain lists several).
  - The served read's purpose, or `unstated`, is recorded: `RoomOperationData.purpose`
    (vti-common, a new public field) at the VTC, the room operation log line at room-host
    (VTI-ACL-106).

### Fixed

- **vta-service**: App-state refuses a context id that is not a context path ([#2526](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2526))

Application state is stored as `app:{context}:{namespace}:{key}` (and the
  `appv:`/`appc:`/`appt:` siblings). Its prefixes are unambiguous only
  because neither a context id nor a namespace contains `:`. The namespace
  was checked; the context id was not, and access does not imply a
  well-formed id: an unrestricted admin may name any context, including
  `acme:x`, whose rows then sit under `acme`'s prefix, where `acme`'s
  listings read them and `acme`'s purge erases them.

  Every app-state operation now checks the context id against the context
  path grammar (`validate_context_path`) before touching the store: get,
  get_many, put, put_many, delete, list, reap and purge. Memory already did
  this for its own calls ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)); this moves the rule to the store so every
  caller inherits it.

  The tombstone sweeper skips, with a warning, any rows written under such
  an id before this change, rather than stopping the sweep of the rest.

title: feat(contexts): add the DTG credential context v2: a VAC's purposes of use
body:
Adds `contexts/v2.jsonld`, served at `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v2` once merged (every push to `main` deploys).

**What changes.** v2 is v1 byte for byte with one top-level term added, `purposes`: the VAC `credentialSubject` member defined by trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84 (*Purposes of Use*, merged). As the cred-spec editor's note under *Context Versions* asks, the term carries its own protected property-scoped context defining `scope` and `purposes` within it, so neither redefines the protected `scope` of `authority`.

| Term | IRI |
|---|---|
| `purposes` | `credentials#purposes` |
| `purposes.scope` (`any` / `listed`, plain string) | `credentials#purposeScope` |
| `purposes.purposes` (`@set` of plain strings) | `credentials#listedPurposes` |

A listed purpose is a plain string, not `@id`: a registered name (`taskExecution`) is not an IRI, and an IRI purpose is compared as an exact string, never resolved.

**Digest** (SHA-256 of the file, as cred-spec *Digest Encoding*): `zQmcoSakfDBfPW2DiLWH3eAAm6uJWDuLyifKQ9tCs8NuiH7` (hex `d6e096472559b01d199af52260d76863bd2be7580bc2398bcd18fc3a2b9f533a`). The same computation reproduces v1's stated `zQmSWyCagdx8oPfXn3piSUx6yqVy5MZ7ZG7nW1TC64QvKZh`.

**Checked:** `npm run check` (validate, immutability, instance values, tests, build). jsonld.js 8.3.3 in safe mode after the W3C VC v2 context: both shapes expand with no term dropped, and a later context redefining `purposes` is still refused.

**Governance (§3.1).** A new context version needs two `contexts/` owners' approvals and the matching specification PR, linked here: trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#85, which records v2's digest and removes the "not yet published" note. #85 is merged, so the spec already points at `/dtg/context/v2`, and that URL returns 404 until this PR deploys.

Implementations: OpenVTC/dtg-credentials 0.14.0 already emits and accepts this IRI; it embeds no copy of the context (eddsa-jcs-2022 needs no context resolution), so nothing there must match these bytes.

title: Let a VTC's identifier be directed; public becomes the community's choice
body:
Closes #75.

A VTC's identifier was required to be `public` ("a community that cannot be found cannot be joined"). As #75 points out, that conflates resolvability with correlation scope, ignores joining by invitation (the VIC carries the community's identifier), and conflicts with the VTC definition's "from a family … to a nation state" range.

This PR takes the issue's proposal: a community's identifier is **`directed` at minimum, `public` where the community is open to outsiders, never `pairwise`**.

### Changes
- `spec/terms-definitions/verifiable_trust_community.md` — replace the public-only rule.
- `spec/body.md`, VMC — the `issuerScope` bullet for the community-issued VMC and the paragraph after the schema now state the rule once, with the rationale (every verifier of a member's credential is a party the community's identifier is directed at) and the privacy cost of `public` for a restricted community (the identifier is disclosed in every membership proof), per the ZKP comment on #75.
- `spec/body.md`, VIC `issuerScope`, *Durable identifiers* and the examples note — defer to the VMC rule rather than restating `public`. The chess-club examples keep `public`, which is valid for an open community.
- `CONTEXT.md` — VMC entry records the rule.

### Interaction with #74
#74 (open) rewrites the Correlation Scope intro to say a VTC's identifier "must be findable, so it can only *truthfully* be `public`", and already handles the holder → controller glossary changes mentioned on #75. Whichever merges second needs that sentence reconciled to "`directed` at minimum"; I've left the current line 124 alone here (it only says a role constrains the VTC's scope, which remains true) to keep the conflict small.

Rendered locally with `npm run render` without errors.

title: Let a VTC's identifier be directed; public becomes the community's choice (#86)
body:
Let a VTC's identifier be directed; public becomes the community's choice (#86)

The spec said a VTC's identifier can only truthfully be declared public,
because "a community that cannot be found cannot be joined". That
conflates resolvability with correlation scope, and does not hold for
joining by invitation: the VIC that invites a prospective member already
carries the community's identifier. It also sits badly with the VTC
definition's own range, which starts at a family.

What the community's identifier must be is resolvable by every party
that verifies its members' credentials, and each of those is a party the
identifier is directed at. So the identifier is now directed at minimum,
public where the community is open to outsiders, and never pairwise.

- verifiable_trust_community.md: replace the public-only rule.
- body.md VMC: issuerScope bullet and the paragraph after the schema
  state the rule once, with the rationale and the privacy cost of a
  public identifier for a restricted community (it is disclosed in every
  membership proof).
- body.md VIC issuerScope, Durable identifiers and the examples note
  follow the VMC rule instead of restating public.
- CONTEXT.md: record the rule in the VMC entry.

Closes #75

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: pnm-cli-v0.59.0
body:
### Added

- **acl**: Purpose of use on ACL entries and memory reads (VTI-ACL-100 – 110) ([#2539](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2539))


### Fixed

- **pnm**: Rooms put writes provenance on open rooms, and rooms read shows it ([#2525](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2525))

`pnm rooms put` refused --basis, --confidence, --cite-*, --purpose,
  --use-note and --valid-until on an `open` room, on the belief that the key
  holder's `rooms/keys/act` would not carry them. It signs the cleartext the
  producer built, unaltered (act Recipient item 6), and `rooms/records/put`
  0.3 and later accept these members in an open room's cleartext. So an
  open-room write now carries them, and gets `basis: declared` by default
  as a sealed write already does (`rooms/records/put/0.5` Producer item 9:
  a writer SHOULD set `basis`). No room profile governs them.

  The members are built once (`RecordProvenance::members`) and checked
  against the specification before anything is sent; sealed bodies take the
  same values, so both tiers spell them alike.

  `pnm rooms read` now shows the basis and expiry line `pnm rooms get`
  shows, marked unsigned on an open room. Both name their keys, which is the
  explicit request on which a reader shows an expired record, marked
  (`RecordValidUntil`).

### Added

- **rooms**: Room hosts hold every read to the purposes its chain grants (VTI-ACL-110) ([#2545](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2545))

A room's authority credential may now state purposes (dtg-credentials 0.14,
  DTG context v2), and a host serving a read holds the request to them
  (`rooms/records/get/0.4`, *Purpose of use*).

  - vti-rooms: `purpose::ChainPurposes` and `PurposeDecision`; `VerifiedChain.purposes`
    (a new public field), `AuthorizedAction::purposes` and `admit_purpose`; get/0.4 is
    dispatched, with `blob_tasks::get_v4_purpose` and `read_purpose_refused`.
  - vti-rooms-dtg: `DtgChainVerifier` fills `purposes` from the verified chain, whose
    chain rule (a link may not widen its parent's purposes, VTI-ACL-107) dtg-credentials
    applies. A scope this build does not know grants nothing.

    grant, or none where it lists several, is refused with `purposeNotGranted` after the
    chain verifies and before any record is read. get/0.2 and 0.3 cannot name a purpose and
    are decided as naming none (`permissionDenied` where the chain lists several).

  `purposes` are stated in the VAC's subject unchanged (DTG context v2), and a

### Fixed

title: docs(context-versions): record the digest of context v2, now published by the registry
body:
Records the SHA-256 digest of the DTG credential context `v2` (`v1` plus the VAC's `purposes`, #84) beside `v1`'s, and removes the editor's note that `v2` is not yet published. *Related Specifications* names both contexts.

- `v2`: `zQmfCH5G4Abr1aPeoEyAw9Cue7iaaAZQwCGtwru1x5URAqv` (hex `fa719174a117ec878ade51e88dca84446f9fe75e2eb8a00daec0b167e653b209`), computed as *Digest Encoding* specifies; the same computation reproduces `v1`'s stated `zQmSWyCagdx8oPfXn3piSUx6yqVy5MZ7ZG7nW1TC64QvKZh`.

The registry PR is trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#35. Per the registry's GOVERNANCE §3.1 the two land together; merge this after (or with) #35, since `v2` is served only once that deploys.
author: stormer78

title: docs(context-versions): record the digest of context v2, now published by the registry (#85)
body:
docs(context-versions): record the digest of context v2, now published by the registry (#85)

* docs(context-versions): record the digest of context v2, now published by the registry

Context v2 (v1 plus the VAC's `purposes`, #84) is added to the DTG VSC
Predicate Registry by trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#35. This records its
digest beside v1's, in the same Digest Encoding (v1's stated digest is
reproduced by the same computation), and removes the editor's note that v2
is not yet published. Related Specifications names both contexts.

Lands together with trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#35 (registry GOVERNANCE
§3.1).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vac): the agent example lists context v2, and v2's digest follows the registry's rename

The example states purposes, so it lists the version that defines the
member, as the sentence after it requires. The v2 digest changes with
the registry's rename of the inner list to credentials#listedPurposes
(trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#35).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:

The inner set mapped to credentials#purpose, one letter from the
member's credentials#purposes and singular where the registry's sets
are plural (#actions). It is free to rename before v2 is published and
impossible after. New digest: zQmcoSakfDBfPW2DiLWH3eAAm6uJWDuLyifKQ9tCs8NuiH7
(sha256 d6e096472559b01d199af52260d76863bd2be7580bc2398bcd18fc3a2b9f533a).

Not yet: room authority credentials stating purposes (VTI-ACL-110). A VAC has no such member until trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84 defines one, and dtg-credentials 0.13 refuses a VAC that carries it, so a chain grants `any` and the caller's entry is what narrows. issue-authority/0.3 is not pinned, and no host serves get/0.4 yet. title: Post-quantum considerations: the guide chapter, LIV-ALG-09 (proposed), Pages served from Actions
body:
A **Post-quantum considerations** chapter for the implementation guide, and one proposed requirement, following the 8 September call's point that the credential signature scheme is the critical, non-swappable choice.

**The chapter** explains the one sentence the specification gives the post-quantum horizon:

- **Two properties, read separately.** Soundness of pairing-based proof systems and unforgeability of discrete-log signatures and commitments fall under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer; zero-knowledge and hiding do not (they are information-theoretic). So: no retroactive privacy loss, no retroactive soundness loss, and every exposure is forward-looking forgery — the migration trigger is a verifier-policy event, not an archival one. ETSI TR 119 476-1 §9 is the reference.
- **The hash side holds.** The gadgets the records are built from keep both properties under Grover at 256-bit output, with the Poseidon-margin and secret-entropy caveats stated.
- **Hash-based proof systems** are plausibly post-quantum in the quantum random-oracle model (Chiesa–Manohar–Spooner), with the 2025–26 proximity-gap results named as a parameter caveat and the Groth16 wrapper named as where a hash-based core stops being post-quantum.
- **The signature is the layer that cannot be swapped**, and where the three sibling DTG specifications stand (Trust Tasks pins ML-DSA/SLH-DSA suites; VTI defines hybrid proof sets; the credential specification names `eddsa-jcs-2022` alone).
- **The pattern:** sign the root or leaf commitment with a post-quantum suite outside the proof; the proof verifies no signature. Why verifying ML-DSA inside a circuit is not available at presentation cost today (self-reported figures, stated as such).
- What stays off the post-quantum path (the PCS route of records 023/024; the as-signed Longfellow class), the regulatory clocks, and what is still unknown.

**Also in this PR**

- `cryptographic-background.md`: the "Post-Quantum Status" bullets now split soundness from zero-knowledge and point to the chapter.
- `proof-of-liveness-requirements.md`: **LIV-ALG-09 — Issuance separability (proposed 2026-10-12)** after LIV-ALG-08, with a changelog line. A profile states whether the issuer signature is verified inside the proof or over a published commitment outside it, and a profile that verifies a pre-quantum signature inside the proof states that its forgery horizon is the signature's. Proposed, not ratified.
- `guide/README.md`: Pages is now served from the GitHub Actions source (switched 2026-10-12; the deploy workflow ran green), so the guide is live at https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-zkp-tf/ and the specification's cross-links resolve.

Companion: dtgwg-zkp-spec PR (same date) carries Security Considerations item 8, WG-18, a quantum horizon on every record and the proving-system split. Either merges first; the chapter and the specification text point at each other by section name.

Local check: 9 chapters, internal links resolved, render clean. Sources for every figure are in the evidence repository's research note of 12 October 2026.

title: fix(outbox): reap settled entries, and scan only what is in flight (#2550)
body:
Fixes #2550.

VtiOutboxStore never removed a settled entry, and its scanning reads decoded
every entry ever written — message bytes included — on every drain tick, about
1.6 full passes a second across the VTC's five loops. On a VTC with ~1,000
entries that held a quarter of a core and drove an OOM every ~14 minutes. The
VTA shares the store and the loops; its outbox was empty only because it had
made few durable sends.

- Reaping: VtiOutboxStore implements terminal_before and remove_if_terminal,
  the delete conditional on the entry being unchanged (one batch under the
  keyspace write lock put also takes), and both services spawn the delivery
  layer's reap_loop hourly at its default week's retention.
- An entry is offered for reaping only once its delivery window closed a whole
  retention ago, not merely once created that long ago: a push reads its
  attempt's entry until it sees the attempt settle, an attempt's window can run
  past any fixed retention, and an entry reaped first would read as never
  queued and be sent again.
- Index rows beside each entry, written in the entry's batch:
  outbox-live:{key} (state, times, ordering key) for an entry in flight,
  outbox-done:{created:020}:{key} for a settled one. due and
  awaiting_confirmation read only the live rows and load full entries just for
  what they return; terminal_before scans done keys in creation order.
- An outbox written before the index is indexed once on the first scan
  (marker outbox-index:v1), entry by entry under require_unchanged, so two
  store instances over one keyspace (the VTC's push transports) are safe. The
  first reap pass then clears the backlog.

Not changed: packed stays a JSON number array (the scans no longer read it,
and reaping bounds how many are kept), and the mediator status poll for Sent
entries, which lives in affinidi-messaging-delivery.

## Tests
- outbox_store: reaping by age with live entries kept; a re-queued entry is not removed; settling takes an entry out of the scans; an entry whose window closed recently is kept; an outbox from before the index is indexed once, by two instances.
- Full pre-push suite locally: workspace nextest (7229), doc tests, vtc nextest (3675), clippy, fmt, cargo deny.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.37.13` → `0.37.14` | patch |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.26`) | `0.10.25` → `0.10.26` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.35` → `0.9.36` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(acl): a provisioned admin holds the provisioner's purposes (VTI-ACL-107)
body:
Provisioning wrote the administrator it creates with `any`, which the shared
grant path refuses to a provisioner whose own entry lists purposes — so such a
provisioner could not provision at all. The admin now takes the provisioner's
purposes, within them by construction.

The other paths Appendix F's VTI-ACL-107 row named write no delegated entry over
the network: device operations change an existing entry and keep its purposes,
a context's administrator is created through acl/create, which bounds purposes
by the writer's, and step-up approval issues a token. Key rotation
(acl/swap-key) and a hand-off successor carry the entry's own purposes.

An unsupportedVersion now says which side is behind where the versions order:
vta_sdk::error::version_age_hint, used by VtaError::UnsupportedTaskType's
message and by the VTA's rejection message — so a client older than the VTA
(for instance a pnm sending acl/list/0.3 to a VTA serving 0.4) is told to
upgrade the client.

## Tests
- `vti_acl_107_the_provisioned_admin_holds_the_provisioners_purposes`
- `version_age_hint` tests in vta-sdk
- Full pre-push suite locally: workspace nextest (7224), doc tests, vtc nextest, clippy, fmt, cargo deny.

title: feat(rooms): the VTA writes a grant's purposes into the credential it issues (issue-authority 0.3, VTI-ACL-110)
body:
The VTA serves rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3 beside 0.2. The request's
`purposes` are stated in the VAC's subject unchanged (DTG context v2), and a
request stating none issues a credential stating none, which grants `any`
(*Purpose of use* item 1).

A credential is a grant the caller writes, so it may not grant purposes the
caller's own entry does not (VTI-ACL-107): a purpose the caller does not hold,
or none at all from a caller whose entry lists purposes, is refused rather

title: Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians
body:
## Summary

Key roles (#79) were all-or-nothing. A node identity without them was **non-conformant**, and verifiers had to refuse its credentials (VTI-KEY-146 to 148). Every key-role identity needed an external recovery key (VTI-KEY-119). That put the whole transition on one coordinated date, and gave no operator a cheaper choice. The design has not yet been published for working-group review, so this PR reworks it rather than amending it.

This PR makes key protection a **level the operator chooses** and a **minimum each verifier's policy sets**. Nothing becomes non-conformant just because it has a single key, and today's DIDs are unaffected. The Trust Task side is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#993. The design note, with the reasoning in prose, is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2352.

### DID classes (VTI-KEY-190 to 193)

| Class | What it is | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| **Relationship DID** | Pairwise, `did:peer`, a client's bootstrap `did:key`, a per-community identifier (VTI-KEY-005, 006, 151) | Any method. One key is normal. No key roles and no level |
| **Persona DID** | A person's own identity | One key, or passkeys. `keyRoles` lists **only** `authenticator` keys |
| **Service DID** | VTA, VTC, VTN, trust registry, host services (witness, log host, push gateway, room host), mediator, integration | Chosen as a key assurance level |

### Key assurance levels (VTI-KEY-194 to 201)

| Level | Shape | Protects against | Loss of the VTA | Compromise of the VTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 single key | Today's shape | — | restore from backup | identity lost |
| 2 role-separated | `keyRoles`. The VTA holds the `attestation` and `update` keys, which may be derived or backed up | compromise of the service process | restore from backup | deactivate the identity; create a successor |
| 3 recoverable | Level 2, plus: generated keys in no backup; a recovery custodian outside the VTA; a witness | the above, plus backup theft or seed exposure, and VTA compromise or loss | recovery key | recovery key |

- **Applicability per requirement.** VTI-KEY-195 is a table giving every requirement and the levels it binds at. Each requirement also says so in its own text.
- **Recommended levels.** VTI-KEY-196: a VTC, a VTN or a VTA's own identity SHOULD be at level 2 or higher. A VTC or VTN SHOULD be at level 3 where its artefacts confer authority on others.

### How a verifier determines the level (VTI-KEY-197 to 199): declared, then checked against structure

- **The declaration.** The document carries a top-level `keyAssurance` member: `{ "level": 2 }` or `{ "level": 3, "recoveryCommitment": "<as in the method's next-key commitments>" }`. If it is absent, the identity is at level 1, so existing DIDs need no change. The JSON-LD term is `https://w3id.org/vti#keyAssurance` with `@type: @json`.
- **The check.** A verifier takes the declared level, then caps it at what the structure shows:
  - Level 2 needs `keyRoles`, and no method listed in two relationships.
  - Level 3 additionally needs all of these:
    - a named recovery commitment, found among the method's next-key commitments and distinct from the routine one;
    - a witnessed version;
    - a commitment that changed only under the recovery key or with a witness.
  - A level lower than an earlier version's makes every later version **level 1**.
- **Why declare rather than infer.** Presence of `keyRoles` cannot carry the level, because persona DIDs carry `keyRoles` too. A recovery hash in `nextKeyHashes` cannot be told apart from a second routine hash. A declared level is one value a policy can apply to. Naming the recovery commitment is what lets a witness and a verifier check that it is carried forward.
- **What stays self-asserted** (stated normatively in the note after VTI-KEY-199):
  - which process holds the `attestation` key (levels 2 and 3);
  - whether the keys were generated, are kept out of backups, and how they are protected at rest (level 3);
  - where the recovery key is, and the custodian's kind;
  - whether the witness is independent of the VTA, and what its policy is.

### Recovery custodians (VTI-KEY-205, 206) and threshold custody (VTI-KEY-210 to 221)

The recovery key is **mandatory at level 3 only** (VTI-KEY-116, 119). It was mandatory everywhere only because of the no-backup rule. At level 2 the keys come back with the backup, so a lost VTA needs no recovery key.

There are three kinds of custodian:

1. **A separately held key.** This is the `pnm recovery-key` file, a hardware token, or a recovery mnemonic from a seed the VTA never sees. The VTA's own seed is never acceptable.
2. **A second VTA**, with its own seed, operator and host.
3. **A threshold custodian.** This is FROST(Ed25519, SHA-512) [RFC 9591], where 2 ≤ t < n:
   - Key generation is distributed, with no dealer [FROST20]. Every participant verifies each proof of knowledge and each share, and the participants compare transcript digests.
   - Every participant obtains the history itself, computes the message, checks it under VTI-KEY-128, and obtains its own operator's approval.
   - Nonces are single-use, never persisted, and deleted on use, abort or restart.
   - Aborts are identifiable: shares are verified before aggregation, and the culprit is named and excluded.
   - Participants communicate by Trust Tasks over TSP, falling back to DIDComm authcrypt. Shares are encrypted end to end.
   - A share refresh can change members, or t, without changing the key.
   - Participants are in distinct protection boundaries. VTI-KEY-211 lists what that means for operators. It includes: **no subject may approve signing at t or more participants**.
   - With fewer than t participants reachable, the operation waits. There is no fallback.
   - Shares are kept out of backups.
   - **Shamir reconstruct-then-sign is rejected** (VTI-KEY-220): at the moment the key is used, it exists whole on one machine.
   - Threshold custody is for recovery and routine update keys only. It **SHOULD NOT** hold an `attestation` key (VTI-KEY-221): that key signs constantly, and its compromise is recoverable by revocation and re-issue.

### Level changes (VTI-KEY-146 to 149)

- **Level 1 is conformant.** VTI-KEY-146 replaces "non-conformant, refuse, replace and deactivate".
- **Raising in place.** One entry can raise level 1 to 2 or 3, or level 2 to 3. It must:
  - mint fresh keys for every role whose custody tightens;
  - retire the replaced keys, or revoke them if exposed;
  - move the update authority;
  - declare the new level, plus the recovery commitment and witness at level 3.
- **Why in-place raising is now sound.** VTI-KEY-201 judges an artefact at the level where its *signing key* is bound. Because a raise replaces the keys, a key is bound at one level only. Anything the old key signs stays a level-1 artefact, even backdated after a theft: a level-2 verifier refuses it, and a level-1 verifier would have accepted that key anyway. What a raise cannot certify is the past, which is true of every rotation.
- **No lowering** (VTI-KEY-148). A lowered level is exactly what a compromised VTA would publish to disarm recovery. Forbidding it lets witnesses refuse the change and verifiers treat it as a compromise.

### Ease-of-use changes (loosened, each with its reason)

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| A single-key service DID is conformant (VTI-KEY-146), and verifiers are no longer required to refuse it (old VTI-KEY-147) | There is no longer a coordinated cliff, and no forced replacement of every DID in use. Verifier policy decides |
| Recovery key and custodian at level 3 only | Its necessity came from the no-backup rule. At level 2 the backup restores the keys |
| Level-2 role keys may be derived or backed up (VTI-KEY-110, 112, 116) | Level 2's value is protection against service compromise. That needs the keys in the VTA, not out of its backups |
| The role-key encryption key and plain-mode warning apply at level 3 only (VTI-KEY-118) | Level 2 accepts that backups hold the keys |
| In-place raise instead of a new identity plus re-issue plus deactivation (VTI-KEY-147) | Members, registries and relying parties keep the DID. The safety argument is above |
| A bound step-up for creating a level-2 identity is SHOULD, not MUST (VTI-KEY-180) | Level-2 creation commits nothing outside the VTA. The level-1 path has no step-up at all, so a MUST would push operators down a level |
| VTI-KEY-184's X25519 rule is SHOULD for new level-1 identities and does not bind existing ones | Existing DIDs are not broken |
| Witness may be the recovery custodian | One extra party, not two |

### Tightened (weaker than it looked)

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| A witness enforcing the recovery commitment and level is **MUST at level 3** (VTI-KEY-129), up from SHOULD | Without it, level 3 protects against loss only. A compromised VTA holds the routine successor and can drop the commitment |
| Replacing the recovery commitment requires the **current recovery key** (VTI-KEY-181). The quorum applies only when that key is lost, and to raising an identity to level 3 | A VTA-side quorum is disarmed by a compromised VTA. The custodian's own signature is checked outside it, and a witness can verify it from the entry |
| The declared level is capped by structure, and a lowered level makes the identity level 1 (VTI-KEY-199) | A claimed level is otherwise free to forge |
| Levels can never be lowered (VTI-KEY-148) | Otherwise the disarming attack looks like an operator's decision |
| A persona DID that lists a passkey must mark it in `keyRoles` (VTI-KEY-191) | Otherwise a VTA-held key in `authentication` is indistinguishable from the person's authenticator, so a VTA's signature could pass as the person being present |
| Threshold custody: no single subject may approve signing at t or more participants (VTI-KEY-211 item 4) | One administrator approving at every participant makes t ≥ 2 a single approver |
| VTI-KEY-114 (no secret derived from a signing key) binds at every level | It has nothing to do with being single-key, and the divergence (F.6) is real |

### Appendix F.6

- The single-key rows are merged and re-filed against VTI-KEY-196's SHOULD, with VTI-VTC-040 and VTI-VTA-008. The behaviour is unchanged, but it is no longer non-conformance.
- The VTI-KEY-090 to 096 row is narrowed to VTI-KEY-150.
- Each custody row now states which level it blocks.
- Nothing is marked implemented.

### Needs working-group review

1. **The level is partly a custody claim** (the note after VTI-KEY-199). The WG should decide whether to define environment evidence for it, such as TEE attestation, or a witness policy statement.
2. **The `keyAssurance` term.** It needs a w3id registration, like `keyRoles`.
3. **Approving a replacement after a lost recovery key.** The witness must be shown the quorum's approvals (VTI-KEY-129 item 3). The witness has no protocol for this yet, and no way to know who is eligible to approve.
4. **The level-1 key after a raise.** It is retired, not destroyed, so a thief can still forge level-1 artefacts with it. That is the risk level-1 verifiers already accept. The WG may want a raise to revoke it by default.
5. **Threshold ceremony protocols.** Key generation, signing and refresh are specified here as requirements. Their Trust Tasks are outlined in the Trust Task PR, not specified.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no missing keys. Every `[[ref:]]` resolves, except `ToIP_Glossary:credential`, which was already unresolved on `main`.

title: Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (#82)
body:
Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (#82)

* Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (VTI-KEY-146 to VTI-KEY-149, VTI-KEY-190 to VTI-KEY-201, VTI-KEY-205, VTI-KEY-206, VTI-KEY-210 to VTI-KEY-221)

Key roles were all-or-nothing: a node identity without them was
non-conformant and its credentials refused, and every key-role identity needed
an external recovery key. This makes the protection a choice the operator
makes and a verifier judges.

- DID classes (VTI-KEY-190 to 193): relationship DIDs (one key is normal, any
  method), persona DIDs (one key or passkeys; `keyRoles` marks only
  `authenticator`), and service DIDs (VTA, VTC, VTN, registry, host services,
  mediator, integration).
- Key assurance levels (VTI-KEY-194 to 201): 1 single key, 2 role-separated
  (VTA holds attestation and update keys, which may be derived and backed up),
  3 recoverable (generated, in no backup, recovery custodian, witness). Every
  level is conformant; each verifier's policy sets the minimum per use. The
  level is declared in a top-level `keyAssurance` member, and at level 3 names
  the recovery commitment; a verifier caps it at what the document and
  history show, and treats a lowered level as level 1. What stays
  self-asserted is listed.
- Custody (VTI-KEY-110 to 119) states its level; the recovery key is
  mandatory at level 3 only. Recovery custodians (VTI-KEY-205, 206): a
  separately held key, a second VTA, or a threshold custodian.
- Threshold custody (VTI-KEY-210 to 221): FROST(Ed25519, SHA-512) [RFC 9591],
  t-of-n with 2 <= t < n, dealerless key generation [FROST20], participants
  in distinct boundaries with no subject approving at t of them, per-
  participant checks, single-use nonces, identifiable abort, Trust Tasks over
  TSP or DIDComm, refresh, no fallback below t, no reconstruct-then-sign;
  SHOULD NOT hold an attestation key.
- VTI-KEY-129 becomes a MUST at level 3 and also refuses a lowered level.
  VTI-KEY-181: the recovery key authorizes its own replacement; the quorum is
  for a lost recovery key and for raising to level 3. VTI-KEY-180: creating a
  level-2 identity needs a bound step-up as a SHOULD.
- VTI-KEY-146 to 149 replace "non-conformant, replace and deactivate" with
  level 1 being conformant, in-place raising by one entry with fresh keys, and
  no lowering. VTI-KEY-201 judges an artefact by the level at which its key is
  bound, which a raise keeps to one level per key.
- Appendix F.6 re-filed: the single-key rows move to VTI-KEY-196's SHOULD,
  and the custody rows say which level they block.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(keys): VTI-KEY-147 settles the old key with SHOULD retire / MAY keep as operational; VTI-KEY-196 lets a service's kind set a default level and a floor

A raise is a custody change, not evidence of compromise, so forcing the
replaced key out forced a re-issue operators did not need. The level-1 key
may stay as the operational key, the custody it already had; it can never
become attestation or update, and VTI-KEY-201 keeps everything it signed a
level-1 artefact. An implementation SHOULD default a new service DID to the
level recommended for its kind, and MAY let a template set a floor.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(keys): the threshold custodian is a condition over whole keys; FROST dropped (VTI-KEY-210–221 revised)

After review: a threshold custodian is n members, each a recovery custodian
of kind 1 or 2 in its own protection boundary holding one whole recovery key,
of which t (2 ≤ t < n) must authorize. Every member's key is committed in the
history; keyAssurance.recoveryCommitment names every commitment and t
(VTI-KEY-197); a verifier and a witness count only distinct committed members
(212) and require at least t proofs on a recovery or replacement entry (215);
membership changes are a replacement of the commitment by t members (218);
any algorithm the method admits, post-quantum included (219). A threshold
signature scheme is no longer a threshold custodian (220): it hid the group
behind one key at the cost of a DKG, single-use nonces, refresh and
ceremonies, with no post-quantum form, and nothing the recovery key does
needs it. VTI-KEY-199 item 3 and VTI-KEY-181 updated; term, references
(Verifiable Conditions, informative) and consideration 25 revised.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(rooms)!: room hosts hold every read to the purposes its chain grants (VTI-ACL-110)
body:
A room's authority credential may now state purposes (dtg-credentials 0.14,
DTG context v2), and a host serving a read holds the request to them
(`rooms/records/get/0.4`, *Purpose of use*).

- vti-rooms: `purpose::ChainPurposes` and `PurposeDecision`; `VerifiedChain.purposes`
  (a new public field), `AuthorizedAction::purposes` and `admit_purpose`; get/0.4 is
  dispatched, with `blob_tasks::get_v4_purpose` and `read_purpose_refused`.
- vti-rooms-dtg: `DtgChainVerifier` fills `purposes` from the verified chain, whose
  chain rule (a link may not widen its parent's purposes, VTI-ACL-107) dtg-credentials
  applies. A scope this build does not know grants nothing.
- room-host and vtc-service serve `rooms/records/get/0.4`. A purpose the chain does not
  grant, or none where it lists several, is refused with `purposeNotGranted` after the
  chain verifies and before any record is read. get/0.2 and 0.3 cannot name a purpose and
  are decided as naming none (`permissionDenied` where the chain lists several).
- The served read's purpose, or `unstated`, is recorded: `RoomOperationData.purpose`
  (vti-common, a new public field) at the VTC, the room operation log line at room-host
  (VTI-ACL-106).

Breaking: `VerifiedChain` and `RoomOperationData` gain a public field.

The VTA does not yet write purposes into the credentials it issues
(`rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3`); that follows, and closes Appendix F's
VTI-ACL-110 row.

## Tests
- room-host `vti_acl_110_a_read_is_held_to_the_purposes_its_chain_grants`: real signed VACs stating one, two or no purposes, through get/0.4 and get/0.3.

title: feat(messaging/mux): connectionFull detach reason; didcomm-mux subprotocol binds a DIDComm socket
body:
Closes two gaps in `messaging/mux/*/0.1` that implementing the mediator surfaced. The specs are drafts, so there is no version bump.

## A connection with no room for a grant

Nothing told a principal that a valid grant was not carried because its connection already held `maxDidsPerConnection` members. This happened both on connect and when a grant was stored while connected. The principal saw `stored` and no `attached` event, and had to infer the rest.

- New `DetachReason` / `MemberChangeReason` value **`connectionFull`**: the grant is valid and stays stored, but this connection had no room for it.
- `event` producer rule 4: on connect, valid grants the connection has no room for are listed in the `detached` event with `connectionFull`. Which grants fill a connection is up to the mediator, and SHOULD be stable across connects.
- `event` producer rule 5 and `grant` rule 5: a grant stored while the principal is connected, which the connection has no room for, is reported `detached` / `connectionFull`. `attachedNow` is `true` only when some connection took the member.

## How a DIDComm socket becomes a mux connection

The event spec left this to "the transport". It now defines a `didcomm-mux` WebSocket subprotocol, next to `tsp-mux`:

- The client offers `didcomm-mux`. The mediator selects it only when it implements mux and has it enabled.
- An older mediator may echo an unknown token, so selection alone proves nothing. The client treats the connection as mux only after `ready`, and reports no member reachable before then.
- Delivered frames are the members' own messages, routed by recipient. DIDComm refusals are already in-band, so a DIDComm socket gets no `refused` event.
- A mediator MAY keep accepting a provisional token it shipped before this binding existed. The Affinidi mediator used `affinidi-mux` before release. A client MUST NOT offer such a token.

`attach`'s definition of a mux connection now points at both bindings.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart) for the new enum value.

Implementation: the Affinidi mediator (connection-full reporting, `didcomm-mux`) and SDK (`didcomm-mux`) follow.

title: fix(vta-sdk): PurposeScope refuses `any` carrying purposes, and a duplicate purpose
body:
An internally tagged enum let the unit variant ignore extra members, so
{"scope":"any","purposes":[...]} parsed as any, and the listed variant's set
folded a duplicate purpose silently (VTI-ACL-100). Payloads of the acl tasks
are held to the schema before they are parsed, but a stored entry and an SDK
response are not; parse through a strict wire form instead. Found writing the
same type for dtg-credentials (OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#44).

Tests: `vti_acl_100_an_empty_list_is_refused` gains both cases. Locally, 885 ACL, memory, room and purpose tests pass, plus clippy `-D warnings` and fmt.

title: feat!: a VAC states purposes of use, and verify_chain holds a chain to them
body:
DTG Core Credentials' Purposes of Use (trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84): an
optional credentialSubject.purposes on a VAC, any or a non-empty list, under
context v2. verify_chain enforces the chain rule (a link stating none takes its
parent's; a wider link is WidensPurposes) and reports the effective purposes.
The member was refused outright before: the VAC subject denies unknown fields,
so no verifier using this library could read a VAC carrying it. Breaking: new
public fields on CredentialSubjectAuthority and VerifiedAuthority, and a new
AuthorityError variant.

See the CHANGELOG entry for the full surface. Tests: `authority_chain::purposes` covers seven cases (none stated grants `any`, narrowing, inheritance, widening refused, `modelTraining` only from a root naming it, refusal at issue, and context `v2` required with an empty list refused), plus the `PurposeScope` unit tests including the strict parse. Locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features` (232), `--no-default-features`, and `cargo package --locked`.

The release that publishes this is a separate `chore(release)` PR. VTI then pins it to check `rooms/records/get` 0.4 against chain purposes, and writes them in `rooms/owner/issue-authority` 0.3.

title: Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for
body:
Adds an optional `purposes` member to a VAC's `credentialSubject`, beside `authority`. It says what the subject may use content obtained under the authority **for**, so the VTI specification's purpose of use (VTI-ACL-100 – VTI-ACL-110) can apply to authority carried by a credential (VTI-ACL-110) as it already does to authority carried by an access control entry.

**What changes (`spec/body.md`, `CONTEXT.md`)**
- **Schema:** `credentialSubject.purposes` (OPTIONAL) is `{"scope":"any"}` or `{"scope":"listed","purposes":[...]}`, with a non-empty list naming each purpose once. Absent means `any`. This is the shape trust-tasks `acl/_shared/0.3` `PurposeScope` defines.
- **New section, *Purposes of Use*:**
  - Purposes are registered names (personalisation, taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or absolute IRIs, compared exactly. An unrecognised purpose equals only itself.
  - `any` never includes `modelTraining`.
  - **Along a chain:** a link with no `purposes` inherits its parent's, and a link stating wider purposes than its parent invalidates the chain. The verifier reports the leaf's effective purposes.
  - **Verification:** a content-disclosing operation that names a purpose is refused unless the effective purposes grant it. A single listed purpose applies when none is named. Under a list of several, naming none is refused. The refusal discloses no content and is distinct from an authority refusal. Which operations count, and the audit record, are left to the VTI requirements rather than restated.
- **Attenuation:** a new MUST NOT in the attenuated-VAC list, and the purposes check added to the chain-verification sentence.
- **Example:** the agent attenuation example now narrows its agent to `taskExecution` beneath a root that states none. The root example is unchanged, so its digest, which the agent example cites as `parent`, still holds.
- **Security Considerations:** item 23, on purposes widened along a chain or read as wider than stated.
- **CONTEXT.md:** the VAC entry mentions `purposes`.

**Judgement calls**
- **Context:** `v1` is byte-frozen and every term is `@protected`, so the member needs context `v2`. *Context Versions* now says a VAC stating `purposes` lists `v2`, and a credential without it may keep `v1`. An editor's note says `v2` (v1 plus `purposes`, with its own `scope`/`purposes` scoped inside so the protected `authority.scope` is not redefined) is not yet published, and leaves its digest to be added when the registry publishes it. **Publishing `v2` is a registry change this PR depends on.**
- **The VTI specification's** purpose registry and verifier obligations are cross-referenced, not copied.

**Why now / what follows**
- OpenVTC/dtg-credentials 0.13 declares the VAC subject `deny_unknown_fields`, so today every verifier using it refuses a VAC carrying `purposes`.
- After this lands and `v2` is published, dtg-credentials needs a release that reads `purposes` and enforces the chain rule.
- Then VTI room hosts check `rooms/records/get/0.4` against it (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1076), and the VTA's `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3` writes the member.

**Checks:** `npm run render` succeeds. Its one warning (dangling definitions) and `npm run healthCheck` (4 passed, 1 failed, 4 warnings) give the same result on unmodified `main`.

title: Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for (#84)
body:
Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for (#84)

* Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for

A VAC gains an optional credentialSubject.purposes: {"scope":"any"} or a
non-empty listed set of registered purposes or absolute IRIs, absent meaning
any, any never including modelTraining. A link without purposes inherits its
parent's; a link stating wider purposes than its parent makes the chain
invalid. A verifier holds a content-disclosing operation that names a purpose
to the chain's effective purposes, as the VTI specification holds an access
control entry's (VTI-ACL-100 – 110).

The member needs context v2, which the registry has not published; an
editor's note says so.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Hold every disclosing operation to a VAC's purposes, as VTI-ACL-103 - 105 do

The Verification paragraph was conditioned on the request naming a purpose,
then ruled on requests that name none, and said nothing of a request naming
none under `any`. State it as the VTI specification does: every operation that
discloses content is held to the chain's effective purposes, a chain stating
none grants `any` (never modelTraining), a request naming none is read as the
single listed purpose, refused under several, and served unstated under `any`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Fix the links the Spec-Up-T health check finds broken

The v0.3 proposal draft was removed from dtgwg-cred-tf (#38), so its four
links now point at the last commit that holds it. www.trusttasks.org does not
resolve; trusttasks.org does. .gitignore states .env, .env.* and
!.env.example as the Spec-Up-T reference does.

title: feat(rooms): the key holder holds every opening to the caller's purposes (VTI-ACL-102)
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1076 at the VTA, as #2539 did for
agent memory.

Opening a room record discloses it, so it is purpose-bound (VTI-ACL-102). New
versions rooms/keys/open/0.3, read/0.3 and file-key/0.3 carry the purpose the
caller will use what it opens for (`purposeOfUse` on file-key, where `purpose`
already means seal or open). The purpose is judged against the caller's stored
ACL entry before anything is decrypted or the host is asked; one not granted is
`purposeNotGranted`, disclosing nothing (VTI-ACL-103, -104). The earlier
versions, still served, name none: served under `any` or a single listed
purpose, refused as `taskFailed` under an entry listing more. Only a key to
open a file is held to a purpose; a sealing key discloses nothing. Every
opening's audit row records its purpose, served or refused (VTI-ACL-106).

read/0.3 passes a named purpose to the host as rooms/records/get/0.4's, and
asks get/0.3 of a host that answers unsupportedType.

Not yet: room authority credentials stating purposes (VTI-ACL-110). A VAC has
no such member until trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84 defines one, and
dtg-credentials 0.13 refuses a VAC that carries it, so a chain grants `any`
and the caller's entry is what narrows. issue-authority/0.3 is not pinned, and
no host serves get/0.4 yet.

The purpose helpers move from the memory handlers to trust_tasks::helpers.
The signing test state now seeds the super admin's ACL entry, as a running VTA
always has one.

## Tests
- `open_0_3_is_held_to_the_callers_purposes`
- `file_key_0_3_holds_an_opening_key_to_its_purpose_and_not_a_sealing_one`
- `read_0_3_is_held_to_the_callers_purposes`: refused before the host is asked, and audited both ways. A granted purpose goes to the host as get/0.4, falling back to get/0.3.
- Conformance witnesses for the three new URIs.
- Locally: 7211 of 7212 VTA-side tests passed. The one failure, `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack`, failed under load and passes on its own, both on this branch and on main. Also passing: VTC 3674, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and cargo-deny.

title: build(deps): did-webs 0.10 via affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.48, on affinidi-keri 0.6
body:
Moves the cache SDK's minimum to 0.8.48, which brings `affinidi-did-webs` 0.10.0 (affinidi-tdk-rs #997) and, with it, affinidi-keri 0.6.

What it changes for VTI's `did:webs` resolution:
- **Rotations:** they verify in keripy. A v1 rotation no longer carries `c`, and the resolver refuses one that does, as keripy does.

title: docs(design-notes): v2 registries checked against keripy: a fresh UUID per update, and keripy reads a withheld revocation as issued
body:
Two findings from the v2 registry fixtures in affinidi/affinidi-keri-rs#20 (built by keripy 2.1.0-dev1 b70986f), recorded under P5 in `did-webs-keri-v2.md`:

- **A fresh UUID per update.** With public mode's empty UUID, a re-issue's BLID collides with the first issuance's, and keripy refuses it. VTI writes a fresh UUID for every update.
- **A withheld revocation.** keripy resolves a credential as issued when the stream leaves out its anchored revoking update. P5's 'every anchored registry event must be present' rule exists for this; keri-core's new `registry` module enforces it for v1 and v2.
