title: cnm-cli-v0.52.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-mcp**: Act as yourself — wallet sign-in for members, a signing-key delegation for administrators ([#2483](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2483))

* feat(vtc-mcp): sign the bridge in as yourself through your wallet

  The bridge becomes the starter of the trigger-link wallet sign-in the member portal and the operator console use (auth/oob/request, redeem, cancel), so a person's own assistant acts with their standing instead of an enrolled agent entry: no new ACL row, no duplicate member. vtc-client gains the starter side (signin: the portal's sign-in config, the trigger link, request, redeem polls with the match number, cancel; always over the HTTPS door, presenting the portal's origin and naming the starter; VtcError::SignIn), and a session client now keeps its own key for that door. vtc-mcp gains vtc_sign_in, vtc_sign_in_finish (answers with the match number for the person to compare in their wallet, then the session) and vtc_sign_in_cancel; vtc_status reports signedInAs. A member sign-in arms the portal's delegation for the bridge's key; an admin sign-in is a console session only, and administrative writes still need a signing-key delegation the bridge cannot obtain yet (operator page section 11). The starter's three auth/oob steps are ReadOnly in the shared table: nothing happens without the person's approval. Also fixes a phase 3 defect: the bridge now enables the SDK's acl-setup, as cnm and vta-mcp do, so a freshly minted did:key's mediator ACL is set on connect instead of the mediator silently dropping its messages.

- **pnm**: Memory commands use vta/memory 0.2; the 0.1 client methods are deprecated ([#2521](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2521))

The registry marked vta/memory/{put,list,delete}/0.1 superseded when 0.2
  was published ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) and will withdraw them. `pnm memory` moves to 0.2:

  - `plant` is an unconditional 0.2 put and prints the version it took.
  - `recall <key>` uses `vta/memory/get/0.1`. A bare `recall` pages through
    `vta/memory/list/0.2` instead of loading the whole context in one
    response. The `--json` output keeps 0.1's `{ items: [{ key, value }] }`
    shape, so scripts keep working.
  - `delete` / `forget` is a 0.2 delete. 0.2 answers a key holding nothing
    with `existed: false`, but pnm still fails on it, as it did on 0.1's
    `notFound`, so a mistyped key is never reported as forgotten.
  - `wipe` deletes each item conditional on the version it listed, so an
    item another writer changed after the operator confirmed stops the wipe
    with a `versionConflict` instead of being deleted with the rest.

### Added

- **vtc-mcp**: A VTC as MCP tools, over the transport its DID document advertises ([#2476](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2476))

Phase 3 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md ([#2470](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2470)). vtc-client gains VtcClient::connect_resolved: connect as a did:webvh secrets bundle (a member's persona) or a did:key over TSP, else DIDComm, else signed documents over the advertised VTCRest endpoint — a session the community advertises is never silently replaced by HTTPS (VtcError::NoTransport; TransportChoice::Rest is the explicit diagnosis path). vtc-mcp (publish = false) is a stdio MCP server that is a native Trust Task client: vtc_list_operations catalogues every pinned request Type URI from vti_specs::schema_index with risk, policy and served-by-the-community; vtc_call sends any pinned operation through send_task and returns a parked write as a status: parked outcome; vtc_supported_tasks, vtc_whoami, vtc_status; three resources; a two-rung identity ladder with no fall-through and no operator-login rung; every call through the shared guard (node VTC) and recorder, with community record identifiers added to the redactor's safe keys. Never runs cnm or pnm.

- **vtc-client**: Send any pinned Trust Task by Type URI, report the transport, and discover what a community serves ([#2472](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2472))

* feat(vtc-client): send any pinned Trust Task by Type URI, report the transport, and discover what a community serves

title: vti-rooms-v0.33.0
body:
### Fixed

- Hash canonical JSON, so digests don't depend on serde_json's map order ([#2500](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2500))

Idempotency hashes, list cursors' filter digests, the election ticket
  digest, the git namespace role digest, the admin-events change digest and
  the collection fingerprint all hashed `serde_json::to_vec` output. That is
  sorted only while serde_json's `preserve_order` feature is off, and any
  dependency can turn it on for the whole build (cargo unifies features).
  With it on, the same request with its members in another order hashed
  differently: a retry was refused as a different request, and a page cursor
  failed against the filters it was minted for.

  Each now hashes RFC 8785 canonical JSON (serde_json_canonicalizer, already a
  workspace dependency). For these inputs — ASCII keys, compact, integer
  numbers — the canonical bytes equal today's sorted output, so stored
  idempotency records and open cursors stay valid across the upgrade.

  The room file vectors test compares JSON values rather than text, since key
  order is not part of the vectors.

  dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and
  acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any
  unknown-schema task until then).

  Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG)
  to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from
  credential signing.

- **vtc**: Member badges — the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family, badges backed by badge groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos (VTI-BDG-001 – 095) ([#2477](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2477))

The backend of member badges (phase 1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md):
  the 24 pinned `vtc/badges/*` tasks served on the dispatch spine.

  - A community badge is a badge group: `create` mints the group as
    `vtc/groups/create` does and records `badge_id` on it; its managers are the
    badge's owners, its members the holders; requests and owners reuse the groups'
    own tasks; retiring deletes the group. A badge group never carries authority
    and is not listed among the community's groups (VTI-BDG-010 – 014).
  - An award is an offer until accepted: `awards/offer` and `kudos/give` record
    `offered` and admit, issue and show nothing; `mine/accept` has the VTA sign
    an Open Badges 3.0 `OpenBadgeCredential` as the group's DID, with the
    community as the Achievement's creator and one evidence entry per award,
    before the membership is recorded (VTI-BDG-020 – 024, 060). The groups'
    credential issuer branches to it for any badge group, so admission by
    request, by rule and renewal issue the same profile.
  - Hidden is portal-only (VTI-BDG-030): walls, holder lists and counts leave a
    hidden holder out while owners see the mark and nothing is revoked.
  - Kudos: any active member gives a kudos badge to any other within the
    community's limits, each giving counted (VTI-BDG-040 – 044); `promote`
    turns one into a community badge, offering every holder.
  - Settings (`settings/show`, `settings/update`: `vtc.config.admin` + a bound
    step-up); a community badge's `retire` takes the step-up too.
  - Pictures reuse the directory's picture pipeline over a `badge_images`
    keyspace. New keyspaces `badges` and `badge_images` (backed up), capability
    `vtc.badges.admin`, audit event `BadgeChanged`, `vtc/badges` in the portal
    signing scope, departure and sweep hooks.

  Inside-only credential regime only: `shareableOutside` is refused until the
  community-owned status set is served (VTI-BDG-062). Console and portal pages
  follow in the next PR.



### Fixed

- Did:webs (and any JWK-published DID) in approver distinctness, re-rotation and SIOP login ([#2519](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2519))

An audit of the places VTI decides which DID methods it accepts, or how it
  finds a DID's key, after did:webs resolution and rotation landed.

  - Step-up approver distinctness read a subject's keys with
    `get_public_key_bytes`, which reads only Multikeys. A subject publishing
    its keys as JWKs (did:webs, did:jwk, a JWK did:web) had them all dropped,
    so every approver looked distinct: a subject could enrol its own key as
    its approver. Keys are now read with `decode_public_key` (Multikey or
    JWK); a method with no key (a ConditionalProof2022) is skipped, and one
    whose key cannot be read fails closed.
  - Member rotation verified the old DID's signature as a did:key only, so a
    member who had rotated onto did:webvh, did:scid or did:webs could never
    rotate again. Both signatures now go through one per-method verifier
    (VTI-MEM-041).
  - SIOP id_token login read only `publicKeyMultibase`; it now reads a JWK too,
    keeping the Ed25519 codec check (an X25519 JWK is refused).

  Left as they are, by the spec: node identities (VTI-KEY-001), client
  bootstrap and ephemeral keys (VTI-KEY-002), key-role identities
  (VTI-KEY-173), and foreign protocols (swiyu, BBS).

- **store**: Flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory ([#2492](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2492))

* fix(store): flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory

  fjall 3.1 (3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only flushes a keyspace once that one
  keyspace holds 64 MiB of unflushed writes. Its database-wide
  max_write_buffer_size is stored but never read, and max_journaling_size
  is only checked while a flush runs. The VTA spreads its writes over ~37
  keyspaces, so it never flushes: every write it has ever made, including
  every overwritten version of a record, stays in memory and is replayed
  from the journal at startup. On staging this OOM-killed the keyring
  runner VTA vta-78 461 times (84 MB journal, under 1 MB of live data).
  STORAGE_FJALL_WRITE_BUFFER and STORAGE_FJALL_MAX_JOURNAL had no effect.

title: vta-sdk-v0.86.0
body:
### Added

- **pnm**: Memory commands use vta/memory 0.2; the 0.1 client methods are deprecated ([#2521](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2521))

The registry marked vta/memory/{put,list,delete}/0.1 superseded when 0.2
  was published ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) and will withdraw them. `pnm memory` moves to 0.2:

  - `plant` is an unconditional 0.2 put and prints the version it took.
  - `recall <key>` uses `vta/memory/get/0.1`. A bare `recall` pages through
    `vta/memory/list/0.2` instead of loading the whole context in one
    response. The `--json` output keeps 0.1's `{ items: [{ key, value }] }`
    shape, so scripts keep working.
  - `delete` / `forget` is a 0.2 delete. 0.2 answers a key holding nothing
    with `existed: false`, but pnm still fails on it, as it did on 0.1's
    `notFound`, so a mistyped key is never reported as forgotten.
  - `wipe` deletes each item conditional on the version it listed, so an
    item another writer changed after the operator confirmed stops the wipe
    with a `versionConflict` instead of being deleted with the rest.

- **vta-service**: Versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) ([#2520](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2520))

Serves the memory versions specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1067.
  0.1 keeps working against the same store.

  The store. Memory 0.2 has application state's semantics with one
  namespace: a per-context counter that is both the `expectedVersion` token
  and the `sinceVersion` watermark, conflicts that carry the winner's view,
  tombstones reaped behind a watermark, and a version index that makes the
  change feed paginatable. `operations::memory` therefore stores items as
  application-state records, under a fixed namespace in the MEMORY
  keyspace, instead of keeping a second copy of that machinery. The
  keyspace stays memory's own, so backup, purge-on-context-delete and the
  memory capabilities are unchanged.
  - `app_state::put_measured` with `ValueMeasure`: memory measures the
    UTF-8 text of a value (as `put/0.2` says), not its JSON encoding, so a
    note full of quotes or newlines does not hit the 64 KiB cap early.
  - 0.1 rows (`mem:<ctx>:<key>`) move into the versioned layout at boot
    (`memory::migrate_legacy`). The migration is idempotent and never
    drops data: an over-cap value (0.1 had no cap) moves uncapped, and a row
    it cannot place stays where it is. Context-delete purges both layouts.
  - Memory tombstones are reaped on app-state's retention window.
  - A memory call naming a context id that is not a valid context path is
    refused, keeping the layout's prefixes unambiguous.

  The tasks.
  - put/0.2: `expectedVersion`; `versionConflict` carries `currentVersion`
    and `currentValue`, but the value is withheld from a caller holding
    `memoryWrite` without `memoryRead` (a conflict is a read).
  - delete/0.2: tombstone; optional positive `expectedVersion`; deleting
    nothing succeeds with `existed: false`.
  - list/0.2: a snapshot (prefix, cursor/limit, values by default) or the
    change feed with tombstones; `highWatermark`, `watermarkTooOld`,
    `cursorInvalid`, `filterConflict`.
  - get/0.1: up to 256 named items, answered in `items` / `missing` /
    `deferred`.
  - An access refusal is the declared `contextForbidden` on 0.2 and `get`.
    0.1 still answers `permissionDenied`.
  - 0.1 on the new store: put is an unconditional put, delete leaves a
    tombstone and still answers `notFound` when nothing was live, and list
    drains every page.

- **contexts**: Context-create capability so an agent gateway can provision sub-contexts ([#2302](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2302))

* feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types

  Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over
  a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike
  `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the
  `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under
  `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than
  as a VTA opaque-signing payload.

  The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or
  issuer artifact:

  - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT
    profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`);
    anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before
    the key is touched;
  - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request
    a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one;
  - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go
    through the opaque oracle, not here.

  Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same
  context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the
  dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and
  acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any
  unknown-schema task until then).

  Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG)
  to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from
  credential signing.

- **resolver**: Resolve did:webs (VTI-LNK-052, VTI-KEY-003) ([#2505](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2505))

Turns on the cache SDK's did-webs feature and raises its floor to
  0.8.47. From 0.8.46, did:webs resolution obeys the host policy did:web,
  did:webvh and did:scid already do; 0.8.47 is on did-webs 0.9 and keri
  0.5, which no longer turn on serde_json's preserve_order for the whole
  build (that broke idempotency hashes, page cursors and the VTI-08 stack
  budget here; #2500 hardened the hashes regardless).

  A contact's or peer's did:webs verifies when its KERI key event log
  verifies (VTI-LNK-052). A node's own identity stays did:webvh or
  did:scid:vh (VTI-KEY-001), and key-role identities are still never
  created under did:webs (VTI-KEY-173); resolving another method is
  VTI-KEY-003's MAY.

  A test holds the guard through the construction path every VTA and CLI
  resolver uses: a loopback, .local or metadata-address did:webs is
  refused by the host policy, not as an unsupported method, and its host
  is never contacted.

- **vtc**: Badge claim codes for events and the automatic badge counts (VTI-BDG-015, 025 – 027) ([#2494](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2494))

Phase 4 of member badges, from the chapter (dtgwg-vti-spec #108) and the wire
  (trust-tasks-tf #1059), pinned here.

  Claim codes (`vtc/badges/claims/{create,list,withdraw,redeem}/0.1`,
  `badges::claims`):
  - An owner (or `vtc.badges.admin`) issues a code for a community badge with a
    label, a time (at most 90 days ahead) and a claim limit. The code is 256 bits
    from the CSPRNG, answered once; the community keeps only its SHA-256 digest
    (`bcdig:`), the record (`bclaim:`, indexed by badge) and a marker per member
    who redeemed it.
  - A member redeeming it is admitted as on an approved request (VTI-BDG-024):
    the claim is reserved - counted and marked under the badges lock - before the
    credential is issued, and released if the key holder fails, so a limit is
    never exceeded; then `credential::issue_with_new_award` issues the badge
    credential with a new accepted award (giver = the code's issuer) as evidence,
    offers it, and records the membership. Unknown, expired, exhausted,
    withdrawn and retired-badge codes answer `codeInvalid` alike;
    `alreadyClaimed` and `alreadyHeld` refuse a second claim.
  - Withdrawing stops a code; claims made stand. Retiring a badge withdraws its
    codes. `claims/list` never answers a code.

  Rule counts (VTI-BDG-015): an automatic badge's rule may read
  `kudosReceived`, `ideasSelected` and `electionTickets` with `atLeast` and
  `count`. `groups::check_badge_rule` admits them; `check_rule` (any other group)
  refuses them. `badges::rule_counts` counts from the community's own records at
  each recompute - accepted kudos awards, selected ideas by proposer entry,
  tickets by the member's current DID (never whether a ballot was cast).
  Accepting kudos, selecting an idea and issuing a ticket kick the dynamic
  sweeper (VTI-DIR-072).

- **vtc**: A holder shows a badge award outside the community — share, unshare, the verification location and the baked picture (VTI-BDG-070, 071) ([#2489](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2489))

* feat(vtc): a holder shows a badge award outside the community — share, unshare, the verification location and the baked picture (VTI-BDG-070, 071)

  Serves `vtc/badges/awards/share/0.1` and `unshare/0.1` (pinned in #2487) and
  answers the holder's own awards on `vtc/badges/show/0.1` (`myAwards`,
  trust-tasks-tf #1057, refreshed here).

  Sharing is the holder's own choice, award by award, for a badge marked
  `shareableOutside`:

  - `badges::share`: a 256-bit token generated for the share and derived from
    nothing (`bshare:<token>` -> award, `Award.shared` with the locations and
    `since`); a repeat share answers the same locations; `unshare` discards the
    token, revokes nothing, and a later share answers new ones.
  - What is served is the holder's credential exactly as issued: each time
    `credential::issue` signs one in the outside regime it is kept at
    `bcred:<badge>:<entry>`, so a repeat award or a renewal is served at the same
    location (share item 10). A holder whose credential predates that is issued
    it again on their first share (outside the lock, as every issue is).
  - `GET /badges/shared/<token>`: the credential (`application/vc+ld+json`) to a
    verifier; to a browser, a page saying what the community verifies of it
    (issued by it, in its validity period, its slot in the community's
    revocation list clear), with its own CSP. `GET .../image.png`: the badge's
    picture as a PNG with the credential baked into an `iTXt` chunk
    (`openbadgecredential`, Open Badges 3.0 baking). Unauthenticated,
    parent-root, let through the host-surface gate; neither names another
    holder or a count (VTI-BDG-071).
  - A share ends with `unshare`, a take-back (`awards/revoke`), retiring the badge
    and the holder's departure (`badges::on_departure`); `share::resolve`
    re-checks the award, the token and the badge on every request, so a stopped
    share answers the same `404` as a token never issued.
  - Refusals as declared: `badgesOff`, `notFound` (unknown, another's and not
    accepted alike), `notShareable` (`insideOnly` | `kudos` | `retired`),
    `publicLocationUnavailable` (no `public_url`).
  - `settle_after_revoke`'s re-issue is factored out as `reissue`, which now
    re-reads each award under the badges lock before recording the credential on
    it, so it never writes back a stale award (and its share) over a newer one.

- **vtc**: Member badges in the console and the member portal (VTI-BDG-001 – 095) ([#2479](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2479))

The pages over the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family #2477 serves.

  Console (Community → Badges, `plugins/badges.tsx` over `lib/badges.ts`):
  every badge the administrator or owner may see; the settings — on or off,
  who may make a kudos badge (nobody, chosen roles and groups, every member),
  the limits — behind vtc.config.admin and a bound step-up; defining a
  community badge (vtc.badges.admin) with its picture, credential regime,
  rules, who sees its holders, an automatic rule where the settings allow it,
  and its owners; and one badge's page: edit, give to chosen members or to a
  group, decide requests for it and appoint its owners (the badge group's
  requests and managers, through the groups' tasks), every award given and
  taken back with a reason, a kudos badge's givings and its promotion, and
  retiring it (step-up for a community badge). Every act is signed by the
  console key (VTI-BDG-095).

  Portal (`#/badges`, `members/Badges.tsx` over `members/badges-api.ts`):
  offers accepted or declined one by one (a decision surface drawn out of the
  community theme's reach); the wall — order, pins within the limit, hide and
  show again, who sees it; every badge to browse; one badge with its holders,
  asking its owners for it (vtc/groups/join on the badge group), giving a
  kudos badge; making a kudos badge with a picture uploaded from the browser.
  A member's directory card shows their wall, pinned first, with the kudos
  total where the community shows it, and lets another member give them a
  kudos badge from there. The home page gets a Badges tile and an attention
  line for offers waiting. Every act is signed by the portal's delegated key.



### Fixed

- **vta-sdk**: Reconnect a TspSession whose websocket the mediator closed ([#2503](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2503))

The mediator closes every websocket when the access token it was opened
  with expires (close 1008, "authentication token expired"; 900 s by
  default). `TspSession::request` reconnected only after a reply timeout, so
  a long-lived session kept the dead socket and every later request failed
  at once with "TSP websocket closed by the mediator". vtc-mcp, which holds
  one session for the life of the MCP server, stopped working after a
  quarter of an hour.

  A request that finds the socket closed or broken now reconnects once (a
  fresh authentication, so a fresh token) and keeps waiting on the same
  waiter until its own deadline, or STRANDED_REPLY_GRACE if that is later.
  The request went out over the TSP transport's HTTP post, so its reply is
  in the inbox and the new socket's flush-on-connect delivers it; nothing
  is resent.

  Concurrent requests failing on the same close share one reconnect: the
  session numbers its sockets, and a waiter reconnects only if the socket
  it saw die is still the current one. Each opening its own would evict the
  one before, losing any reply already flushed onto an evicted socket
  (raw-TSP mode deletes a frame once written).

  tests/e2e/tests/tsp_reconnect_on_close.rs drives both cases against a
  TestMediator with a 5 s access token; both fail on the previous code with
  the production error.

title: vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.3
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A member can rotate onto a did:webs (VTI-MEM-041, VTI-KEY-003) ([#2517](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2517))

Member rotation accepted did:key, did:webvh and did:scid. It now accepts
  did:webs. A did:webs document has no `#key-0`: its keys are the KERI key
  state's, identified by their CESR encoding, all in `authentication`. The
  document resolves only when the key event log verifies (VTI-LNK-052), so the
  new-DID signature is accepted from any key the document authorises for
  authentication (at most 16 are tried), each through the same purpose and
  controller check as the did:webvh path (VTI-MEM-041). A ConditionalProof2022
  entry is skipped; it is not a key.

  its response `method` enum in place (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1064).

  as an internal error.

title: vti-specs-vta-v0.7.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-service**: Versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) ([#2520](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2520))

Serves the memory versions specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1067.
  0.1 keeps working against the same store.

  The store. Memory 0.2 has application state's semantics with one
  namespace: a per-context counter that is both the `expectedVersion` token
  and the `sinceVersion` watermark, conflicts that carry the winner's view,
  tombstones reaped behind a watermark, and a version index that makes the
  change feed paginatable. `operations::memory` therefore stores items as
  application-state records, under a fixed namespace in the MEMORY
  keyspace, instead of keeping a second copy of that machinery. The
  keyspace stays memory's own, so backup, purge-on-context-delete and the
  memory capabilities are unchanged.
  - `app_state::put_measured` with `ValueMeasure`: memory measures the
    UTF-8 text of a value (as `put/0.2` says), not its JSON encoding, so a
    note full of quotes or newlines does not hit the 64 KiB cap early.
  - 0.1 rows (`mem:<ctx>:<key>`) move into the versioned layout at boot
    (`memory::migrate_legacy`). The migration is idempotent and never
    drops data: an over-cap value (0.1 had no cap) moves uncapped, and a row
    it cannot place stays where it is. Context-delete purges both layouts.
  - Memory tombstones are reaped on app-state's retention window.
  - A memory call naming a context id that is not a valid context path is
    refused, keeping the layout's prefixes unambiguous.

  The tasks.
  - put/0.2: `expectedVersion`; `versionConflict` carries `currentVersion`
    and `currentValue`, but the value is withheld from a caller holding
    `memoryWrite` without `memoryRead` (a conflict is a read).
  - delete/0.2: tombstone; optional positive `expectedVersion`; deleting
    nothing succeeds with `existed: false`.
  - list/0.2: a snapshot (prefix, cursor/limit, values by default) or the
    change feed with tombstones; `highWatermark`, `watermarkTooOld`,
    `cursorInvalid`, `filterConflict`.
  - get/0.1: up to 256 named items, answered in `items` / `missing` /
    `deferred`.
  - An access refusal is the declared `contextForbidden` on 0.2 and `get`.
    0.1 still answers `permissionDenied`.
  - 0.1 on the new store: put is an unconditional put, delete leaves a
    tombstone and still answers `notFound` when nothing was live, and list
    drains every page.

## [0.6.3](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.2...vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.3) — 2026-11-09 ### Added - **vtc**: A member can rotate onto a did:webs (VTI-MEM-041, VTI-KEY-003) ([#2517](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2517)) Member rotation accepted did:key, did:webvh and did:scid. It now accepts did:webs. A did:webs document has no `#key-0`: its keys are the KERI key state's, identified by their CESR encoding, all in `authentication`. The document resolves only when the key event log verifies (VTI-LNK-052), so the new-DID signature is accepted from any key the document authorises for authentication (at most 16 are tried), each through the same purpose and controller check as the did:webvh path (VTI-MEM-041). A ConditionalProof2022 entry is skipped; it is not a key. Re-pins vtc/members/rotate/0.1, which gained `did:scid` and `did:webs` in its response `method` enum in place (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1064). That also fixes rotation onto a did:scid, whose successful reply (`method: "did:scid"`) failed the published schema and reached the member as an internal error. - **vtc**: Badge claim codes for events and the automatic badge counts (VTI-BDG-015, 025 – 027) ([#2494](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2494)) Phase 4 of member badges, from the chapter (dtgwg-vti-spec #108) and the wire (trust-tasks-tf #1059), pinned here. Claim codes (`vtc/badges/claims/{create,list,withdraw,redeem}/0.1`, `badges::claims`): - An owner (or `vtc.badges.admin`) issues a code for a community badge with a label, a time (at most 90 days ahead) and a claim limit. The code is 256 bits from the CSPRNG, answered once; the community keeps only its SHA-256 digest (`bcdig:`), the record (`bclaim:`, indexed by badge) and a marker per member who redeemed it. - A member redeeming it is admitted as on an approved request (VTI-BDG-024): the claim is reserved - counted and marked under the badges lock - before the credential is issued, and released if the key holder fails, so a limit is never exceeded; then `credential::issue_with_new_award` issues the badge credential with a new accepted award (giver = the code's issuer) as evidence, offers it, and records the membership. Unknown, expired, exhausted, withdrawn and retired-badge codes answer `codeInvalid` alike; `alreadyClaimed` and `alreadyHeld` refuse a second claim. - Withdrawing stops a code; claims made stand. Retiring a badge withdraws its codes. `claims/list` never answers a code. Rule counts (VTI-BDG-015): an automatic badge's rule may read `kudosReceived`, `ideasSelected` and `electionTickets` with `atLeast` and `count`. `groups::check_badge_rule` admits them; `check_rule` (any other group) refuses them. `badges::rule_counts` counts from the community's own records at each recompute - accepted kudos awards, selected ideas by proposer entry, tickets by the member's current DID (never whether a ballot was cast). Unlike `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than as a VTA opaque-signing payload. Console (Community → Badges, `plugins/badges.tsx` over `lib/badges.ts`): every badge the administrator or owner may see; the settings — on or off, who may make a kudos badge (nobody, chosen roles and groups, every member), the limits — behind vtc.config.admin and a bound step-up; defining a community badge (vtc.badges.admin) with its picture, credential regime, rules, who sees its holders, an automatic rule where the settings allow it, and its owners; and one badge's page: edit, give to chosen members or to a group, decide requests for it and appoint its owners (the badge group's requests and managers, through the groups' tasks), every award given and taken back with a reason, a kudos badge's givings and its promotion, and retiring it (step-up for a community badge). A request that finds the socket closed or broken now reconnects once (a fresh authentication, so a fresh token) and keeps waiting on the same waiter until its own deadline, or STRANDED_REPLY_GRACE if that is later. Concurrent requests failing on the same close share one reconnect: the session numbers its sockets, and a waiter reconnects only if the socket it saw die is still the current one. Each opening its own would evict the one before, losing any reply already flushed onto an evicted socket (raw-TSP mode deletes a frame once written). tests/e2e/tests/tsp_reconnect_on_close.rs drives both cases against a TestMediator with a 5 s access token; both fail on the previous code with the production error.

## [0.62.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.61.0...vti-common-v0.62.0) — 2026-11-09 ### Added - **vta-service**: Memory reads are audited per item, and the trail names items by commitment, never by key ([#2116](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2116)) ([#2522](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2522)) #2116 asked which agent saw which memory. Answering it showed a problem with what the trail already held: the chained sink commits a DID-shaped resource but keeps any other resource in the clear inside the hashed event, on the rule that only a DID is personal data. A memory key is not a DID and is personal (it names what was remembered, often a person), so every memory.put and memory.delete wrote one where no erasure can reach it without breaking verification (VTI-AUD-005). - `AuditSink::commit` (provided, default `None`) and `vti_common::audit::commit_reference`: a domain-separated HMAC under the active audit key, `hmac-sha256::`. The chained sink implements it. A sink with no key returns `None`, and the caller then records no reference: an unkeyed digest of a short name is a dictionary lookup away from the name. - Memory audit records now name each item by its commitment over (contextId, key): - put / delete: the commitment as the resource; - get: `items=N refs=…`, one per item returned (never a deferred or missing key); - list: `items=N keySet=…`, one commitment to the returned key set. - `pnm memory history --context … [--actor] [--from] [--to] [--limit]`: who read or changed a context's memory and when, newest first, from `audit/list` (one query per memory action, since the action filter is exact). - `MockVta` writes the chained trail production writes, not the flat keyless one. Three persona tests that read raw audit rows as flat entries now read both forms, as the VTA's own reader does. Records written before this change keep their keys until the retention sweep. That is recorded in the specification's divergence register (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#113). - **contexts**: Context-create capability so an agent gateway can provision sub-contexts ([#2302](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2302)) * feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than as a VTA opaque-signing payload. The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or issuer artifact: - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`); anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before the key is touched; - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one; - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go through the opaque oracle, not here. Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any unknown-schema task until then). Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG) to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from credential signing. - **vtc**: Member badges — the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family, badges backed by badge groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos (VTI-BDG-001 – 095) ([#2477](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2477)) The backend of member badges (phase 1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md): the 24 pinned `vtc/badges/*` tasks served on the dispatch spine. - A community badge is a badge group: `create` mints the group as `vtc/groups/create` does and records `badge_id` on it; its managers are the badge's owners, its members the holders; requests and owners reuse the groups' own tasks; retiring deletes the group. A badge group never carries authority and is not listed among the community's groups (VTI-BDG-010 – 014). - An award is an offer until accepted: `awards/offer` and `kudos/give` record `offered` and admit, issue and show nothing; `mine/accept` has the VTA sign an Open Badges 3.0 `OpenBadgeCredential` as the group's DID, with the community as the Achievement's creator and one evidence entry per award, before the membership is recorded (VTI-BDG-020 – 024, 060). The groups' credential issuer branches to it for any badge group, so admission by request, by rule and renewal issue the same profile. - Hidden is portal-only (VTI-BDG-030): walls, holder lists and counts leave a hidden holder out while owners see the mark and nothing is revoked. - Kudos: any active member gives a kudos badge to any other within the community's limits, each giving counted (VTI-BDG-040 – 044); `promote` turns one into a community badge, offering every holder. - Settings (`settings/show`, `settings/update`: `vtc.config.admin` + a bound step-up); a community badge's `retire` takes the step-up too. - Pictures reuse the directory's picture pipeline over a `badge_images` keyspace. New keyspaces `badges` and `badge_images` (backed up), capability `vtc.badges.admin`, audit event `BadgeChanged`, `vtc/badges` in the portal signing scope, departure and sweep hooks. Inside-only credential regime only: `shareableOutside` is refused until the community-owned status set is served (VTI-BDG-062). Console and portal pages follow in the next PR. ### Fixed - Did:webs (and any JWK-published DID) in approver distinctness, re-rotation and SIOP login ([#2519](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2519)) An audit of the places VTI decides which DID methods it accepts, or how it finds a DID's key, after did:webs resolution and rotation landed. - Step-up approver distinctness read a subject's keys with `get_public_key_bytes`, which reads only Multikeys. A subject publishing its keys as JWKs (did:webs, did:jwk, a JWK did:web) had them all dropped, so every approver looked distinct: a subject could enrol its own key as its approver. Keys are now read with `decode_public_key` (Multikey or JWK); a method with no key (a ConditionalProof2022) is skipped, and one whose key cannot be read fails closed. - Member rotation verified the old DID's signature as a did:key only, so a member who had rotated onto did:webvh, did:scid or did:webs could never rotate again. Both signatures now go through one per-method verifier (VTI-MEM-041). - SIOP id_token login read only `publicKeyMultibase`; it now reads a JWK too, keeping the Ed25519 codec check (an X25519 JWK is refused). Left as they are, by the spec: node identities (VTI-KEY-001), client bootstrap and ephemeral keys (VTI-KEY-002), key-role identities (VTI-KEY-173), and foreign protocols (swiyu, BBS). - **store**: Flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory ([#2492](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2492)) * fix(store): flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory fjall 3.1 (3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only flushes a keyspace once that one keyspace holds 64 MiB of unflushed writes. Its database-wide max_write_buffer_size is stored but never read, and max_journaling_size is only checked while a flush runs. The VTA spreads its writes over ~37 keyspaces, so it never flushes: every write it has ever made, including every overwritten version of a record, stays in memory and is replayed from the journal at startup. On staging this OOM-killed the keyring runner VTA vta-78 461 times (84 MB journal, under 1 MB of live data). STORAGE_FJALL_WRITE_BUFFER and STORAGE_FJALL_MAX_JOURNAL had no effect.
## `vti-rooms`
## [0.32.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-rooms-v0.32.0...vti-rooms-v0.32.1) — 2026-11-09 ### Fixed - Hash canonical JSON, so digests don't depend on serde_json's map order ([#2500](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2500)) Idempotency hashes, list cursors' filter digests, the election ticket digest, the git namespace role digest, the admin-events change digest and the collection fingerprint all hashed `serde_json::to_vec` output. That is sorted only while serde_json's `preserve_order` feature is off, and any dependency can turn it on for the whole build (cargo unifies features). With it on, the same request with its members in another order hashed differently: a retry was refused as a different request, and a page cursor failed against the filters it was minted for. Each now hashes RFC 8785 canonical JSON (serde_json_canonicalizer, already a workspace dependency). For these inputs — ASCII keys, compact, integer numbers — the canonical bytes equal today's sorted output, so stored idempotency records and open cursors stay valid across the upgrade. The room file vectors test compares JSON values rather than text, since key order is not part of the vectors.

## [0.38.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-config-v0.38.0...vta-config-v0.38.1) — 2026-11-09 ### Fixed - **vta-config**: Make the config attestation view canonical JSON ([#2510](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2510)) The view `vta/attestation/config-report` returns, and whose SHA-384 the enclave's evidence binds, was `serde_json::to_vec` of the config. The config holds `policy.approver_sets`, a `HashMap`, whose iteration order is seeded per map, so the same configuration produced a different view and digest in every process: two enclaves of one fleet, or one enclave before and after a restart, attested different digests for identical configurations. The task specification calls the view canonical. The view is now RFC 8785 canonical JSON (serde_json_canonicalizer), so equal configurations are equal bytes whatever their field types.
## `vta-support`
## [0.37.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-support-v0.36.0...vta-support-v0.37.0) — 2026-11-09 ### Added - **contexts**: Context-create capability so an agent gateway can provision sub-contexts ([#2302](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2302)) * feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than as a VTA opaque-signing payload. The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or issuer artifact: - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`); anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before the key is touched; - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one; - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go through the opaque oracle, not here. Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any unknown-schema task until then). Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG) to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from credential signing.
## `vta-service`
## [0.79.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.78.0...vta-service-v0.79.0) — 2026-11-09 ### Added - **vta-service**: Memory reads are audited per item, and the trail names items by commitment, never by key ([#2116](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2116)) ([#2522](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2522)) #2116 asked which agent saw which memory. Answering it showed a problem with what the trail already held: the chained sink commits a DID-shaped resource but keeps any other resource in the clear inside the hashed event, on the rule that only a DID is personal data. A memory key is not a DID and is personal (it names what was remembered, often a person), so every memory.put and memory.delete wrote one where no erasure can reach it without breaking verification (VTI-AUD-005). - `AuditSink::commit` (provided, default `None`) and `vti_common::audit::commit_reference`: a domain-separated HMAC under the active audit key, `hmac-sha256::`. The chained sink implements it. A sink with no key returns `None`, and the caller then records no reference: an unkeyed digest of a short name is a dictionary lookup away from the name. - Memory audit records now name each item by its commitment over (contextId, key): - put / delete: the commitment as the resource; - get: `items=N refs=…`, one per item returned (never a deferred or missing key); - list: `items=N keySet=…`, one commitment to the returned key set. - `pnm memory history --context … [--actor] [--from] [--to] [--limit]`: who read or changed a context's memory and when, newest first, from `audit/list` (one query per memory action, since the action filter is exact). - `MockVta` writes the chained trail production writes, not the flat keyless one. Three persona tests that read raw audit rows as flat entries now read both forms, as the VTA's own reader does. Records written before this change keep their keys until the retention sweep. That is recorded in the specification's divergence register (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#113). - **pnm**: Memory commands use vta/memory 0.2; the 0.1 client methods are deprecated ([#2521](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2521)) The registry marked vta/memory/{put,list,delete}/0.1 superseded when 0.2 was published ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) and will withdraw them. `pnm memory` moves to 0.2: - `plant` is an unconditional 0.2 put and prints the version it took. - `recall ` uses `vta/memory/get/0.1`. A bare `recall` pages through `vta/memory/list/0.2` instead of loading the whole context in one response. The `--json` output keeps 0.1's `{ items: [{ key, value }] }` shape, so scripts keep working. - `delete` / `forget` is a 0.2 delete. 0.2 answers a key holding nothing with `existed: false`, but pnm still fails on it, as it did on 0.1's `notFound`, so a mistyped key is never reported as forgotten. - `wipe` deletes each item conditional on the version it listed, so an item another writer changed after the operator confirmed stops the wipe with a `versionConflict` instead of being deleted with the rest. - **vta-service**: Versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 ([#2115](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2115)) ([#2520](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2520)) Serves the memory versions specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1067. 0.1 keeps working against the same store. The store. Memory 0.2 has application state's semantics with one namespace: a per-context counter that is both the `expectedVersion` token and the `sinceVersion` watermark, conflicts that carry the winner's view, tombstones reaped behind a watermark, and a version index that makes the change feed paginatable. `operations::memory` therefore stores items as application-state records, under a fixed namespace in the MEMORY keyspace, instead of keeping a second copy of that machinery. The keyspace stays memory's own, so backup, purge-on-context-delete and the memory capabilities are unchanged. - `app_state::put_measured` with `ValueMeasure`: memory measures the UTF-8 text of a value (as `put/0.2` says), not its JSON encoding, so a note full of quotes or newlines does not hit the 64 KiB cap early. - 0.1 rows (`mem::`) move into the versioned layout at boot (`memory::migrate_legacy`). The migration is idempotent and never drops data: an over-cap value (0.1 had no cap) moves uncapped, and a row it cannot place stays where it is. Context-delete purges both layouts. - Memory tombstones are reaped on app-state's retention window. - A memory call naming a context id that is not a valid context path is refused, keeping the layout's prefixes unambiguous. The tasks. - put/0.2: `expectedVersion`; `versionConflict` carries `currentVersion` and `currentValue`, but the value is withheld from a caller holding `memoryWrite` without `memoryRead` (a conflict is a read). - delete/0.2: tombstone; optional positive `expectedVersion`; deleting nothing succeeds with `existed: false`. - list/0.2: a snapshot (prefix, cursor/limit, values by default) or the change feed with tombstones; `highWatermark`, `watermarkTooOld`, `cursorInvalid`, `filterConflict`. - get/0.1: up to 256 named items, answered in `items` / `missing` / `deferred`. - An access refusal is the declared `contextForbidden` on 0.2 and `get`. 0.1 still answers `permissionDenied`. - 0.1 on the new store: put is an unconditional put, delete leaves a tombstone and still answers `notFound` when nothing was live, and list drains every page. - **contexts**: Context-create capability so an agent gateway can provision sub-contexts ([#2302](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2302)) * feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than as a VTA opaque-signing payload. The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or issuer artifact: - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`); anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before the key is touched; - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one; - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go through the opaque oracle, not here. Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any unknown-schema task until then). Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG) to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from credential signing. ### Fixed - **vta-service**: A webvh update that cannot reach its host keeps the typed NoMatchingProtocol refusal ([#2279](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2279)) ([#2514](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2514)) Publishing a webvh update to its hosting server wrapped every failure in `UpdateDidWebvhError::Publish(String)`, which maps to `AppError::Internal`. When the outbound seam shared no transport with the host, the typed `AppError::NoMatchingProtocol` was rendered to text: an online edit answered a retryable internal error instead of the refusal, so the SDK's `VtaError::NoMatchingProtocol` never reached the CLI, and the offline `vta webvh update-did` path detected the case by matching the rendered "no transport in common" text. `UpdateDidWebvhError` gains a `NoMatchingProtocol { step, refusal }` variant (additive; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`), built by `publish_failed` at every call that reaches the host: the reconcile re-publish, the publish of the new entry, agent-name operations, and the agent-name list and availability lookups. It maps to `AppError::NoMatchingProtocol` (502) at the boundary. Every other host failure is still `Publish` with the same text as before. The offline CLI now matches on the variant. `NO_TRANSPORT_MARKER` and the test pinning its wording are gone. The before/after-commit distinction from #2275 is unchanged. - Hash canonical JSON, so digests don't depend on serde_json's map order ([#2500](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2500)) Idempotency hashes, list cursors' filter digests, the election ticket digest, the git namespace role digest, the admin-events change digest and the collection fingerprint all hashed `serde_json::to_vec` output. That is sorted only while serde_json's `preserve_order` feature is off, and any dependency can turn it on for the whole build (cargo unifies features). With it on, the same request with its members in another order hashed differently: a retry was refused as a different request, and a page cursor failed against the filters it was minted for. Each now hashes RFC 8785 canonical JSON (serde_json_canonicalizer, already a workspace dependency). For these inputs — ASCII keys, compact, integer numbers — the canonical bytes equal today's sorted output, so stored idempotency records and open cursors stay valid across the upgrade. The room file vectors test compares JSON values rather than text, since key order is not part of the vectors. - **store**: Flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory ([#2492](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2492)) * fix(store): flush fjall memtables in the background so writes don't stay in memory fjall 3.1 (3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only flushes a keyspace once that one keyspace holds 64 MiB of unflushed writes. Its database-wide max_write_buffer_size is stored but never read, and max_journaling_size is only checked while a flush runs. The VTA spreads its writes over ~37 keyspaces, so it never flushes: every write it has ever made, including every overwritten version of a record, stays in memory and is replayed from the journal at startup. On staging this OOM-killed the keyring runner VTA vta-78 461 times (84 MB journal, under 1 MB of live data). STORAGE_FJALL_WRITE_BUFFER and STORAGE

title: docs(vta/dids): did:webs is eligible with the key-role designation extension
body:
## Why

The did:webs method profile declared the method **ineligible as published**. It fails criteria 4 and 6 of CONVENTIONS §3.2: there are no controller-chosen relationships, and there is no room for `keyRoles` or `revoked`. The profile recommended **extension A**: role keys anchored in the KEL and rendered into their roles' relationships with `keyRoles` and `revoked`, with the key-state keys in no relationship.

`affinidi-did-webs` 0.9.1 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#991) implements extension A as a *key-role designation*, an ACDC anchored in the KEL. It is proposed to the did:webs specification (ToIP KSWG) as a proof of concept.

## What

- **Status:** eligible with the key-role designation extension, ineligible without it. A VTA MAY create a key-role identity under did:webs only with the extension, and MUST refuse otherwise with `methodNotEligible` (`missing: [4, 6]`).
- **§1:** criteria 4 and 6 are met with the extension.
- **§4 Rendering, as built:**
  - the record's schema SAID and attributes (`roles`, `revoked`);
  - one standing record, with accumulated revocations so a key can't be un-revoked;
  - the document's members, with key-state keys and `ConditionalProof2022` in no relationship and not in `keyRoles`;
  - key-agreement designations give way to `messaging`;
  - the fail-closed checks, and never falling back to the key-state keys.
- **Interop caveat:** a resolver without the extension refuses the published `did.json`.
- **§8:** parameters schema still to follow the working group's review.
- The method-profiles README row is updated to match.

Companion VTI spec change: VTI-KEY-173 (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec).

`npm run validate` passes.

title: feat(keys): a party may encrypt to a KERI identifier with the key converted from its key state (VTI-KEY-185)
body:
KERI identifiers made outside VTI hold their key state and nothing else, and
their controllers decrypt with the X25519 key converted from the Ed25519 key
(KERI practice, and the did:webs reference implementation's DIDComm support).
Without the conversion a node cannot encrypt to any of them.

VTI-KEY-185 permits it for KERI key-state identifiers only (did:webs, did:keri),
only when the identifier has never designated key agreement keys or key roles,
and never for a key-role identity. VTI-KEY-184 is unchanged: a node never
publishes a converted key for its own identity.

Reference implementation: affinidi-did-webs 0.9.2 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#993).

title: feat(vta-service): memory reads are audited per item, and the trail names items by commitment, never by key (#2116)
body:
Closes #2116.

## What #2116 asked for, and what was already there

- **Hash-chaining:** already implemented since the issue was filed (VTI-AUD-004).
- **Item-level reads:** added here.
- **"Who read or changed my memory":** added here as `pnm memory history`.

## The problem it turned up (VTI-AUD-005)

The chained sink commits a DID-shaped resource, but keeps any other resource in the clear inside the hashed event, on the rule that only a DID is personal data. A memory key isn't a DID, but it is personal: it names what was remembered, often a person. So every `memory.put` and `memory.delete` wrote one where no erasure can reach it without breaking verification. Logging the keys a read returned, as the issue suggested, would have made that worse.

## Change

- **`AuditSink::commit`**, plus `vti_common::audit::commit_reference`: a domain-separated HMAC under the active audit key, `hmac-sha256:<key id>:<hex>`.
  - It's a provided trait method defaulting to `None`, so it's additive.
  - A sink with no key returns `None`, and the caller records no reference rather than an unkeyed digest, which a dictionary lookup would reverse.
- **Memory audit records** name each item by its commitment over `(contextId, key)`:
  - `put` / `delete`: the commitment as the resource;
  - `get`: `items=N refs=…`, one per item returned (never a deferred or missing key);
  - `list`: `items=N keySet=…`.
- **`pnm memory history --context … [--actor] [--from] [--to] [--limit]`:** who read or changed a context's memory, newest first, from `audit/list`. It runs one query per memory action, since the action filter is exact.
- **`MockVta` now writes the chained trail production writes**, not the flat keyless one. Three persona tests that decoded raw rows as flat entries now read both forms.
- **Docs:** `docs/02-vta/personal-ai-agents.md`.

## Not covered

- **Rows written before this change** keep their keys until the retention sweep. That's recorded in the divergence register: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#113.
- **Looking up "was item X read?" by key** needs an `audit/list` filter that recomputes the commitment, which is a spec change. Today, rows about one item can be matched by their shared commitment.
- **VTI-AUD-006** (reading the trail is itself audited) is still open. `memory history` reads the trail the same way `pnm audit list` does.

## Tests

- New: the commitment is deterministic, differs per context and never contains the value, and a flat sink commits nothing.
- New handler test: four memory rows, and no key anywhere in the trail.
- New end-to-end test (`memory_audit.rs`): over the wire, the `get` row names the item the `put` wrote, attributed to the agent.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7189 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3674 passed.
- Doctests, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check`: all clean.

title: docs(audit): record agent-memory keys held in the clear by earlier audit records (VTI-AUD-005)
body:
Adds an *observed* VTI-AUD-005 entry to Appendix F.4.

At one agent node, the chained audit trail committed actor and DID-shaped target identifiers, but kept any other resource in the clear inside the hashed event. Agent-memory writes recorded the item's key as that resource. A key names what was remembered (often a person), so those records embed personal data that no erasure can reach without breaking verification.

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2116 changes what new records hold: each item is named by a keyed commitment under the audit key, and reads record which items they returned the same way. The records already written can't be rewritten. They leave only at the retention sweep, and the entry says so.

The entry also records that the node's "a non-DID resource is not personal data" rule hasn't been checked for its other actions.

title: feat(pnm): memory commands use vta/memory 0.2; the 0.1 client methods are deprecated
body:
Follow-up to #2520 (#2115). The registry marked memory 0.1 superseded when 0.2 was published and will withdraw it, so `pnm memory` moves to 0.2:

- **`plant`:** an unconditional 0.2 put. It prints the version it took.
- **`recall <key>`:** `vta/memory/get/0.1`.
- **`recall`:** pages through `vta/memory/list/0.2`. `--json` keeps the 0.1 `{ items: [{ key, value }] }` shape.
- **`delete` / `forget`:** a 0.2 delete. It still fails on a key holding nothing, as before.
- **`wipe`:** each delete is conditional on the version the list showed. An item another writer changed after you confirmed stops the wipe with a `versionConflict` instead of being deleted.

`VtaClient::{memory_put, memory_list, memory_delete}` are now `#[deprecated]`, pointing at the 0.2 methods. Nothing in the workspace calls them any more.

## Tests

- New `mock_vta::versioned_memory_round_trips_through_the_client` drives the four 0.2 client methods against a running VTA, including the typed `versionConflict`.
- New unit tests: page decoding (tombstones skipped, cursor read), and a malformed page errors instead of shortening the list.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7184 passed.
- Workspace doctests, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check`: all clean.

was published (#2115) and will withdraw them. `pnm memory` moves to 0.2:

- `plant` is an unconditional 0.2 put and prints the version it took.
- `recall <key>` uses `vta/memory/get/0.1`. A bare `recall` pages through
  `vta/memory/list/0.2` instead of loading the whole context in one
  response. The `--json` output keeps 0.1's `{ items: [{ key, value }] }`
  shape, so scripts keep working.
- `delete` / `forget` is a 0.2 delete. 0.2 answers a key holding nothing
  with `existed: false`, but pnm still fails on it, as it did on 0.1's
  `notFound`, so a mistyped key is never reported as forgotten.
- `wipe` deletes each item conditional on the version it listed, so an
  item another writer changed after the operator confirmed stops the wipe
  with a `versionConflict` instead of being deleted with the rest.

`VtaClient::{memory_put, memory_list, memory_delete}` are deprecated in
favour of `memory_put_versioned`, `memory_list_page`,
`memory_delete_versioned` and `memory_get`. A new mock-VTA test drives
those four over the wire, including the typed conflict reaching the
client.

Refs #2115

feat: send vta/memory 0.2 — prefix-narrowed recall, a real get, tombstoned forget

The registry marked vta/memory/{put,list,delete}/0.1 superseded when 0.2
was published (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2115) and will
withdraw them. The store moves to the 0.2 client methods:

- save: `memory_put_versioned`, unconditional, still under
  `VtaClient::idempotent`. put/0.2 is classified Keyed, so the stable
  idempotency key now also stops a retried save taking a second version.
- list_of_type: `list/0.2` asks the VTA for `<type>/` only and pages by
  cursor, instead of fetching the whole context and filtering here.
- get: one `vta/memory/get/0.1` instead of a full list plus a lookup.
- forget: `delete/0.2` leaves a tombstone, so the user's other devices
  learn of the deletion. An absent key is still an error.
- Responses decode into the generated 0.2 types. A live item that comes
  back without its value is an error, not a skipped entry.

Needs vta-sdk 0.86 (with vti-secrets 0.35). That release carries the 0.2
client methods and `CreateAclRequest::handoff`, set to false here.
Cargo.lock is not updated in this commit because 0.86 is not published
yet.

title: feat(keys): did:webs meets VTI-KEY-170 with the key-role designation extension (VTI-KEY-173)
body:
## Why

VTI-KEY-173 refused did:webs for key-role identities, for two reasons. Its document is derived from the KEL with every key-state key in `authentication` and `assertionMethod`, and it has no member for `keyRoles` or `revoked`. Its open issue preferred a did:webs extension that anchors role keys in the KEL and renders the key-state keys into no relationship, over amending VTI-KEY-093.

That extension now exists as a proof of concept:
- **Reference implementation:** the *key-role designation* in `affinidi-did-webs` 0.9.1 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#991).
- **Method profile:** `vta/dids/_shared/0.1/method-profiles/webs.md`, updated in the companion trust-tasks PR.
- **Proposal:** it is being proposed to the did:webs specification (ToIP KSWG).

## What

- **VTI-KEY-173:** did:webs meets VTI-KEY-170 only with the key-role designation extension its method profile states. A node MUST NOT create a key-role identity under did:webs without it.
- **Open issue:**
  - **Interop caveat:** until the did:webs specification adopts the extension, a did:webs resolver without it refuses the published document. So such an identity is verifiable only by resolvers that implement it.
  - **Why the VTI-KEY-093 amendment isn't taken:** it would keep the change authority in two relationships.
  - **VTI-KEY-001 is unchanged:** it doesn't yet name did:webs for a node's durable identity. Naming it would oblige every peer to resolve did:webs (VTI-KEY-003), so that waits on adoption.

No divergence-register entry is needed. No VTI implementation creates did:webs key-role identities, which this text still forbids without the extension.

title: feat(vta-service)!: versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 (#2115)
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1067 for #2115. 0.1 keeps working against the same store.

## How

- **Store:** memory items are now application-state records under a fixed namespace in the existing `MEMORY` keyspace. Versions, tombstones, the change feed, cursors and reaping come from `operations::app_state`, not a second copy. The keyspace stays memory's own, so backup, purge-on-context-delete and the capability gates are unchanged.
- **Size measure:** memory measures a value's UTF-8 text, as `put/0.2` specifies, not its JSON encoding. This uses `put_measured` with `ValueMeasure`.
- **Migration:** at boot, `migrate_legacy` moves 0.1 `mem:<ctx>:<key>` rows into the new layout. It's idempotent and never drops data: an over-cap value (0.1 had no cap) moves uncapped, and a row it can't place stays put.
- **Write-only callers:** a `versionConflict` hides `currentValue` from a caller holding `memoryWrite` without `memoryRead`, since a conflict amounts to a read.
- **Access refusals:** 0.2 tasks and `get` refuse with the declared `contextForbidden`. 0.1 still answers `permissionDenied`.
- **0.1 on the new store:** `put` is an unconditional put; `delete` leaves a tombstone and still answers `notFound`; `list` drains every page.

## Also

- **App-state cursor errors:** `vta/app-state/list` now sends its declared `cursorInvalid`, not `malformedRequest`. This comes from the new `AppStateError::CursorInvalid`; the enum is `non_exhaustive`, so the variant is additive.
- **SDK:** new constants and retry classes (`put/0.2` is Keyed), plus four `VtaClient` methods.
- **Census:** conformance witnesses for all four tasks, and a test for every declared code. The error-code baseline shrinks by four.

## Things to know

- **Breaking (hence `!`):** `operations::memory`'s public functions changed signature.
- **0.1 is now superseded.** The registry marks it so automatically once 0.2 exists, and withdraws superseded versions about 90 days later. vta-agent-memory, `pnm memory` and vta-mcp still send 0.1 and need moving to the new client methods.
- **Not fixed here:** app-state has the same unchecked-context-id gap that memory now guards against.

## Tests

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7181 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3672 passed.
- Workspace doctests, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check`: all clean.
- I re-ran the SDK and memory tests after adding the client methods: 1455 passed.

Closes #2115

title: feat(vta-service)!: versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 (#2115) (#2520)
body:
feat(vta-service)!: versioned agent memory — vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.2 and get/0.1 (#2115) (#2520)

Serves the memory versions specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1067.
0.1 keeps working against the same store.

The store. Memory 0.2 has application state's semantics with one
namespace: a per-context counter that is both the `expectedVersion` token
and the `sinceVersion` watermark, conflicts that carry the winner's view,
tombstones reaped behind a watermark, and a version index that makes the
change feed paginatable. `operations::memory` therefore stores items as
application-state records, under a fixed namespace in the MEMORY
keyspace, instead of keeping a second copy of that machinery. The
keyspace stays memory's own, so backup, purge-on-context-delete and the
memory capabilities are unchanged.
- `app_state::put_measured` with `ValueMeasure`: memory measures the
  UTF-8 text of a value (as `put/0.2` says), not its JSON encoding, so a
  note full of quotes or newlines does not hit the 64 KiB cap early.
- 0.1 rows (`mem:<ctx>:<key>`) move into the versioned layout at boot
  (`memory::migrate_legacy`). The migration is idempotent and never
  drops data: an over-cap value (0.1 had no cap) moves uncapped, and a row
  it cannot place stays where it is. Context-delete purges both layouts.
- Memory tombstones are reaped on app-state's retention window.
- A memory call naming a context id that is not a valid context path is
  refused, keeping the layout's prefixes unambiguous.

The tasks.
- put/0.2: `expectedVersion`; `versionConflict` carries `currentVersion`
  and `currentValue`, but the value is withheld from a caller holding
  `memoryWrite` without `memoryRead` (a conflict is a read).
- delete/0.2: tombstone; optional positive `expectedVersion`; deleting
  nothing succeeds with `existed: false`.
- list/0.2: a snapshot (prefix, cursor/limit, values by default) or the
  change feed with tombstones; `highWatermark`, `watermarkTooOld`,
  `cursorInvalid`, `filterConflict`.
- get/0.1: up to 256 named items, answered in `items` / `missing` /
  `deferred`.
- An access refusal is the declared `contextForbidden` on 0.2 and `get`.
  0.1 still answers `permissionDenied`.
- 0.1 on the new store: put is an unconditional put, delete leaves a
  tombstone and still answers `notFound` when nothing was live, and list
  drains every page.

Also:
- `AppStateError::CursorInvalid`: `vta/app-state/list` now answers its
  declared `cursorInvalid` instead of `malformedRequest`.
- vta-sdk adds `TASK_VTA_MEMORY_{PUT,DELETE,LIST}_0_2` and `_GET_0_1`
  with their retry classes (put/0.2 is Keyed, like app-state put), and
  `VtaClient::{memory_put_versioned, memory_delete_versioned,
  memory_list_page, memory_get}`.
- Conformance witnesses for all four tasks, and handler tests for every
  declared code. The error-code baseline shrinks by four.
- vti-specs-vta pins `vta/memory/{put,delete,list}` at 0.1 and 0.2, plus
  get 0.1. The registry now marks the 0.1 versions superseded, so the
  memory clients (vta-agent-memory, pnm memory, vta-mcp) should move to
  0.2 before the registry withdraws 0.1.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_service::operations::memory::{put, delete, list}`
take the `NamespaceLocks` and the new versioned parameters and return the
application-state outcomes; `list_all_live` replaces 0.1's `list`.

Closes #2115

title: fix: JWK-published DIDs (did:webs) in approver distinctness, re-rotation and SIOP login
body:
An audit of every place VTI decides which DID methods it accepts, or how it finds a DID's key, now that did:webs resolution (#2505) and rotation onto did:webs (#2517) are in. Most code is already method-agnostic, because it reads keys through `TrustTaskVmResolver`. Three places were not.

## Fixed

**1. Step-up approver distinctness failed open (security).**
- `acl::approver::subject_keys` read the subject's keys with `get_public_key_bytes`, which only handles `Multikey`.
- A subject that publishes its keys as JWKs had every key dropped: did:webs always does, and so can did:jwk or a JWK did:web. The subject then appeared to hold no keys, so `check_distinct` accepted any approver, including the subject's own key. That defeats the separate-approver requirement (attest/0.1 consumer item 6, `redeem/finish/0.1` item 4).
- Keys are now read with `decode_public_key` (Multikey or JWK).
- A method that carries no key, such as a `ConditionalProof2022`, is skipped. One whose key can't be read fails closed.

**2. A member who had rotated off did:key could never rotate again.**
- The old DID's signature was verified as a did:key only.
- Both signatures now go through one per-method verifier: did:key, did:webvh/did:scid, did:webs (VTI-MEM-041).

**3. SIOP id_token login read only `publicKeyMultibase`.** It now reads a JWK too. The Ed25519 codec check stays, so an X25519 JWK is refused.

## Left alone, by design

- **Spec restrictions:**
  - node identities stay did:webvh/did:scid (VTI-KEY-001);
  - client bootstrap, ephemeral, delegated and approver keys stay did:key (VTI-KEY-002 and the flow specs);
  - no key-role identity under did:webs (VTI-KEY-173).
- **Foreign protocols:** swiyu issuers are did:webvh; BBS needs BLS12-381.
- **`display_name::shorten_did`:** does not special-case did:webs. Its vectors are shared with a TypeScript copy, so that change needs both sides.
- **Signatures made before a rotation:** VTI does not resolve a DID at a past version for any method, did:webvh included (see `routes/audit.rs`). did:webs supports `versionId`, but the resolver SDK does not expose version-addressed resolution yet. That's a separate piece of work.

## Tests

Each new test fails on the old code:
- `a_subjects_jwk_key_is_not_a_distinct_approver`: a did:webs subject's own JWK key is refused as its approver, and a different key is accepted.
- `a_member_on_a_did_webs_can_rotate_again`: rotate onto a did:webs, then rotate again signing as it. The test signing helper now signs as a non-did:key party through `HolderKey::new`.
- `an_ed25519_jwk_issuer_verifies` and `an_x25519_jwk_is_not_a_signing_key` (SIOP).

Full suite:
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7164 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3674 passed
- doc tests pass; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean
